And when we watch movies they are mostly from China, Japan, Europe anywhere but America. They have not been destroyed by shallowness of capitalism and feminism.

title: The Critics, Cast, Crew, and Disney executives need to be arrested for ruining film.
review: I thought after watching the first trailer, this 'thing' was going to be pretty mediocre. Only two days before the release, the critics on Rotten Tomatoes and YouTube gave the 'thing' an A. I thought I had to see this in theaters (I wasn't impressed with the audience's intelligence, and I'll start buying or renting instead.). Mediocre is an understatement. I'd rather have blood in my urine than watch this tripe again. Now I will give a review. "The Force Awakens" is a shameless, incoherent mess that does not deserve the word film. "Battlefield Earth" was more entertaining than this. I am not exaggerating. It lacks plot, character development, acting, cinematography, and, above all, inspiration. The plot is a dumb rehash of the very first Star Wars film. There is a third Death Star but this time it is a planet that is TEN TIMES BIGGER. Wow. A droid, BB-8, a Disney-fied version of R2- D2, has to bring a map to Luke Skywalker, who has vanished for no apparent reason, instead of blueprints of the new Deathstar, to the Resistance aka Rebels. This is beyond idiotic. Let's talk common sense. If you are going to vanish, are you going to leave breadcrumbs? Of course not unless you were my discrete mathematics professor. All the main characters run into each other by coincidence like I was watching "Independence Day" without the fun. This "Starkiller Base" is so IDIOTIC; including the name, ha! "Mega Maid" from Spaceballs actually is a better Death Star than "Starkiller". As the video game generation would say, LOL. This new base sucks energy from the closest sun while draining too, and, not just that, it has the exact same flaw as the other two Death Stars in which an X Wing can fire torpedoes down its shaft causing it to explode. This is unbelievably hilarious. Is this supposed to be a comedy? The characters lack any depth or development. Rey is a MARY SUE. She learns the Force within two minutes without the "film" giving any background to why she knows. By the way, she is not that hot! A solid 6/10! Finn, a black Stormtrooper, is a cowardly, idiotic buffoon who chases the white female protagonist trying to get laid. Did I mention he was a janitor?Wow, that is racially sensitive. Poe is wasted. Why include him in the movie. He only has 20 minutes of screen time. Oh yeah, to fill the diversity quota since he is Hispanic. This whole "film" was written by left-wing Disney executives. The original cast did not develop over the last 30 years. Han Solo is still a smuggler? WTF! He was a war hero! Leia is an idiot who gets Han killed. Chewbacca is there to sell toys. I saved the villain, Kylo Ren, for last. He is the biggest wimp I have ever seen in film history. He throws temper tantrums, murders a whole village like a mass murdering lunatic (how subtle), and wears a mask for fun. Awful. The acting is uninspired. Harrison Ford looks bored, confused, or embarrassed in almost every scene. I hope he enjoyed that money to fill his greed. The new "actors" need to go work at McDonald's especially the guy who plays Kylo Ren. Cinematography does not exist. Most of the locations used in the "film" look like golf courses. Jakoo is Tatoonine 2.0. CGI ranges from exceptional to laughable. The worst part is where Rey releases the god awful looking CGI monsters on the freighter ship. The cast and crew lied when they said they would use actual props as much as possible. Really, these people should be arrested. The editing is all over the place. The spaceships are uninspired and belong on Sci-Fi channel movie*. Everything happens in this "film" because... "Whatever, we need to make a movie so we can make a bazillion dollars!" None of this had a purpose but to make a quick buck. The original cast is way too old. That has already been stressed ENOUGH. John Williams score is so bland and that really breaks my heart. I cannot blame him. He is a gifted genius who at 87 really deserves better at his age. The guy was sick, and the "movie" already sucked so oh well. This "director" Jar Jar Abrams produces nothing rehash crap so he can make big bucks off of it. What a fuck1ng disgrace. The only saving grace for us all is Darwinism. Let nature eliminate those who are way too stupid including JJ Abrams. This is the 3rd highest grossing movie of all time. People are dumb and it is dragging society down! Edit #5

title: Mockbuster with expensive CGI
review: It is a "mockbuster" type of a movie - hi-budget knockoff of Star Wars: New hope. It looks like something that "The Asylum" has made, with expensive CGI. Nothing new, same old story taken from the first Star Wars movie. New actors were added to replace guys behind Dart Vader, Carrie Fisher and Harrison Ford. Unoriginal plot that added nothing to the Star Wars universe. The bad guys weren't intimidating, just funny. Rey was disappointing. Ray is a simple character that becomes highly trained pilot and then a master Jedi, just in a few days or even hours. This is like Assassins Creed 12 or Rocky 14 would look like. The Force Awakens = A New Hope. This is just a reboot.

title: Star Wars never looked so rewritten
review: There is almost nothing unique about this movie. Take a bit of A New Hope, with a dash of Return of the Jedi, throw in new characters and kill some others. Add a Death Star, planet-style and throw in just enough of the junked, unused Universe that Lucas created and you have this good-enough Sci-fi movie. It rates the same for me as Maximum Overdrive, Garbage Pail Kids, and Home Alone 5. Not the proudest of company there, but it is what it is. It IS a decent movie, but just a real disappointing Star Wars Movie. I liked some parts, which made me chuckle, but too many direct similarities to what was already in film make for a dry movie.

title: Star Wars could have been better
review:
After watching the 7th film of Star Wars, I came to the conclusion that George Lucas would have done better. It was good but it could have been better. Even I could have done better.

Seduced by the Dark Side of the Force, George sold Star Wars to Disney in 30/10/2012. Since then the fear was that the next films would not meet the expectations.

In 2015 the fears of the fans were confirmed by the release of the 7th episode: The Force Awakens, which impresses by the special effects but disappoints by the mediocre plot.

In the view of Disney, becoming a Jedi Knight should be easier, without much training. The images that can be found on the Internet give us an idea of what we can expect from Disney. Maybe I'll see Mickey Mouse becoming a Jedi Knight too so as to help Luke Skywalker in the fight against the Dark Side.

We can only hope that George come back to the Light Side and take Star Wars away from the hands of Disney. May the Force be with George!

title: Quite Disappointed
review:
We saw the movie yesterday. We got geared up to see The Force by watching the 3 originals in the series, and the first Chris Pine Star Trek which we really like (also by JJA). We were ready.

As the movie started, my first reaction was - why are the good guys who won the war, and survived the Emperor and Vader, now the resistance again? I guess that is too PC, since if the good guys were in power, and the bad guys were in the minority,...well you get it.

And the weak plot gets worse from there. Han Solo has not changed. Really?? Why not? He was a success at the end of VI, and would have parlayed that into even greater success--remember he was a 'scoundrel'. Instead he is again scruffy and in debt to mafia like bad trading partners. Very, very weak.

Finally, as mentioned by many, the overall plot is a weak remake of the original. I have not been more disappointed from a movie, perhaps ever, than I was by this. The crowd walked out of the theater in stunned silence, not the cheering I would have expected from a great Star Wars movie. I knew then my feelings were shared by many.

title: Last Star Wars movie I will ever watch.
review:
I went into this film with low hopes after seeing the destruction of Star Trek under J.J. Abrams' watch and it turned out even worse than I expected. The Force Awakens is just a remake with a more diverse cast and CGI. That's really all there is to it. And it's a bad remake too. I left the theater not really caring about any of the characters because we were given no time between the bang-bang boom-boom set pieces to really get to know them all that well. The plot of this film (no spoilers) basically makes everything that the heroes did in the original trilogy completely meaningless. Nothing changed and nothing improved. And what they did the the Han/Leia relationship is completely unforgivable.

After watching this movie with friends, we sat silently in a restaurant afterward and tried to figure out our thoughts and feelings about this film. Probably the only way to accept this movie is any way is to consider it J.J. Abrams' badly written fan fiction. Star Wars had only three films (six if we're going to be extremely generous, since at least the prequel trilogy was made by George Lucas himself) and then the series ended.

If you haven't seen this movie yet, don't waste your time. Just re-watch your DVD of A New Hope and save yourself a few bucks. If you have seen it, I'm sorry we both had to suffer through that garbage.

title: So Phantom Menace WAS a good movie anyway!
review:
OK people. You may be young. you may have no idea about decent storytelling. You may think today's ear-garbage which is called pop music is fine. You may connect with everything - everybody with your smart phones anytime. But you CANNOT say this is Star Wars. Far from it. Even if this wasn't an assault to original SW universe, it would still be a very BAD sci-fi movie.

Where to begin to tell how bad this movie is? All the actors (unfortunately even Harrison Ford & Carrie Fisher) are really bad, there is no meaning, no depth, no subtext in the script. If I say R2D2 is the best actor in this movie, you can guess the rest (no, this new droid BB-8something is also crap).

I'll try to forget this. Never expected such a huge disappointment from JJ Abrams, but it happened. This was really really bad movie..

title: The power of advertising and nostalgia
review: There is always an explanation...and many reviewers have given them. Indulge me and let me get this disappointment off my chest and into the universe. The extraordinarily high rating given this episode, Star Wars: The Force Awakens is surely linked in part to nostalgia and massive advertising. It is as if we couldn't dislike such a fixture of our childhood even if it is being served up again covered with crème chantilly and so many other frills designed to cover up the truth that the dish is tasteless. There is plenty of humanity in earlier episodes, the Nytimes.com review is a mystery here. And please tell me if I missed it but there is less than nothing new or original in this episode. The new young stars are compelling but the out of the vacuum storyline is not. The only humanity I saw in the film is that Carrie Fisher, Harrison Ford and Mark Hamill were allowed to age, graciously or not depending on your personal projections. We do have the generalized massacre of anything enemy, as well as defenseless planets. In sheer numbers these virtual deaths put practically every other high body count movie to shame. The carnage is rarely graphic however. The first 'moment of blood' is when John Boyega realizes that his fellow Stormtrooper is indeed flesh and blood, however, there are no indications that all these billions? of people being blown away, even though it looks so clean and spectacular, you know using the power of the sun to annihilate planets, are indeed people... This said, annihilating billions is a SF trope (see Dune, etc.) and the real problems with this film lie mostly elsewhere. Disney can make great films, using its name or one of its subsidiary studios but this film, which I am sure has already spawned many video games, was made to make money big time, and little else. Which is disappointing.

title: Epic Fail!!
review:
I can only echo the negative reviews that have come before this one. I really looked forward to this film as all the right ingredients were there. A new director, the original cast, a huge budget, how did this go so wrong?

When anyone sets out to make a sequel to such a massive and well known franchise the foundations and framework of the story must be respected. Having a character that can instantly and with no explanation perform mind tricks, use telekinesis, expertly wield a light sabre and do anything else that a Jedi Knight trains from an infant (adolescent in Luke's case, child in Anakin's) to achieve dismisses that framework.

I'm no fanboy, I've read nothing of the expanded universe and I congratulate Disney on not following those story arcs as it means something new for both hardcore and regular Star Wars fans. But this episode 4 rip-off was a joke. Another Death Star!?! C'mon!!!

JJ Abrams said "I can understand that someone might say, 'Oh, it's a complete rip-off!.' What was important for me was introducing brand new characters using relationships that were embracing the history that we know to tell a story that is new -- to go backwards to go forwards." Sorry JJ, but if you can't do that AND respect the story that you're continuing then you shouldn't be doing it!

It may be possible that there's two hours of deleted footage to go with the DVD release that makes all these plot holes and inconsistencies (I've just named the ones that annoy me most. There are plenty of others) more credible and in-line with the OT, maybe even episode 8 can salvage something, but as for the film I saw I can only say.......

EPIC FAIL!!

title: You could do anything in the universe and you redo A New Hope?
review:
THE PLOT A droid containing vital information escapes the imperialist First Order onto a desert planet where it is befriended by a young woman. The droid has to get back to the resistance forces. They escape the barren planet on a junked out smuggler's ship with the First Order in pursuit. A masked man in black wielding the force captures the girl and takes her to his giant battle station and interrogates her. Then the base fires its secret weapon destroying entire planets in one shot. A group of unlikely heroes both young and old band together on a rescue mission to save the girl and destroy the battle station before all is lost.

THE GOOD The actors. It really is amazing seeing Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher, Mark Hamill, Anthony Daniels, Peter Mayhew, Tim Rose, and Mike Quinn back in another Star Wars film. It was a great experience just seeing them again in the roles I've loved since my childhood. Then there is the new cast. Daisy Ridley delivered a great performance as the mysterious Rey (she reminded me of a young Keira Knightley). John Boyega and Oscar Isaac both make likable characters and ones you genuinely care for by the end of the film. Add into that veterans like Max Von Sydow (whom I swear hasn't changed in the last 20 years) and Andy Serkis and you've got an awesome team of actors. There was even a brief appearance by amazing martial arts actors Iko Uwais and Yayan Ruhian from the action epic THE RAID. Those two guys are extremely talented and it was a welcomed surprise to see them.

THE BAD A New Remake. When you read my plot synopsis above did it sound familiar at all? Basically this movie is a remake of A NEW HOPE. While that isn't a bad thing it certainly isn't what I wanted from a new Star Wars film. A New Hope is actually my least favorite of the original trilogy. It is also one of the most familiar films to the general populace, the last film in cinematic history that needs to be remade (in my opinion). The whole time I kept waiting for this movie to do something new, to really take off into a new direction, but it never did. Sure the genders are different for some of the roles but that's it.

The Scale. The whole time I'm watching the movie I'm waiting for the moment when things ramp up to the next level, that moment when the stakes gets really high. But it never happens. At one point Han Solo has a line that essentially says "Been there. Done that." Again, treading familiar territory isn't always a bad thing, especially when you're repeating a formula that so many people love dearly. But Star Wars should be setting the new standard, not going the safe route. The last three films, each of which taking new directions, have been panned and mocked by fans and none-fans alike, but at least they gave us something we hadn't seen before.

THE VERDICT I realize that this is the first film of a new trilogy and as such it is merely a set-up film. Set-up films have this feeling of just existing because it is necessary for the next films. It's like eating the vegetables on your dinner plate because Mom told us to. Some of us like vegetables. Some of us prefer our steak, mashed potatoes, and ice cream. I'm being harsh, but seriously this film should've upped the game. You know something is amiss when you find yourself thinking of going back and watching the prequels again.

All that said, I still enjoyed the film for the novelty that is Star Wars and the wondrous experience of seeing Han Solo, Chewbacca, Princess Leia, C-3PO, R2-D2, and my absolute favorite Star Wars character Luke Skywalker in a new film. I want to be excited for future films but it's hard to get stoked when it looks like we're going to be receiving a pound for pound remake of THE EMPIRE STRIKES BACK. Maybe this movie was intentionally blah to make the next two movies look even better. Maybe?

title: Not the chosen one
review:
On one level, I was pretty skeptical of the idea of a new Star Wars movie. The unfortunate Hollywood trend of rebooting and rehashing old franchises with sequels, prequels, and requels with only occasional success (Mad Max) has made me wary.

On the other hand, the menacing phantom of prequels past needed some sort of redemption. I was very cautiously optimistic that Disney's Episode VII would make good.

For the most part, the team working on this movie created a wonderful aesthetic that is referential to the original trilogy enough make it feel like a legitimate continuation of the saga. They also carefully created a droid in BB-8 that is cute and amusing enough to sell plenty of toys to children without being overly annoying to the adult audience.

Now for criticism. So much has been made of the problems with Episode VII that I want to just mention two.

C-3PO seems to be a pretty good metaphor for this movie. He is relatively unchanged from the original trilogy, and so is the plot of Episode VII. The only difference is that now he has a red arm for some reason, recycled from some other droid, a superficial change that is lamely put forward to indicate that this isn't just the same old movie. It now has a red arm!

Episode VII does something much worse than just 'remixing' older movies - it buries the heroes of the original trilogy in an attempt to establish the new ones. Han Solo, who shows the only really excellent acting performance to the movie, is now a failed parent who captains a mockery of a ship that Rey seems to know better than he does. Remember how Luke Skywalker engaged in painstaking training to finally return as a Jedi over three films? The new protagonist learns the ways of the force without tutelage, training, or effort, defeating a Sith Lord by the end of one film. JJ Abrams makes the critical mistake of elevating his protagonist too high and too quickly at the expense of the heroes of the films he intends to celebrate. Even the scale of the Starkiller Base makes the Death Star seem puny and weak in comparison.

Episode VII provides spectacle and fond familiar sights, but it really doesn't provide anything creative or new that justifies its existence beyond as a moneymaking venture. Unfortunately it tries to one-up the earlier movies instead of taking the story in new, interesting, worthwhile directions.

title: Worthless crap
review:
The Force Awakens is unoriginal, superficial and dull. The characters have none of the life or independence of those in the original trilogy. They just pant and stare at each-other with intense emotions. I'm not surprised J. J. Abrams scolded Daisy Ridley for being too wooden because he seems to like overacting rather than natural performances.

The plot is ripped off mainly from A New Hope but also episodes V and VI. Jakku is a desert planet just like Tatooine. The Starkiller (a reference to Luke's original surname before it was changed to Skywalker) is just a big Death Star. Even in the opening titles I became suspicious with references to the First Order (basically the Empire) and the Resistance (basically the Rebellion). Apparently nothing has changed since Return of the Jedi. Some plans are hidden in a droid. They need to deactivate the shields before they can do anything. The vehicles include the Millenium Falcon, Tie fighters and X-wings. One part is a direct imitation of the dogfight in Star Wars. Heavy sigh.

Kylo Ren is one of the lamest villains in movie history. He's an admitted imitation of Darth Vader. He wears a mask for no apparent reason. He casually takes it off at some point and reveals that he looks like a pouty teenager. He has no presence and isn't intimidating at all. The fact that he throws tantrums is a weakness, not a strength. It's a bad sign if I feel like I could easily beat a movie's main villain in a fight. Also, he's not conflicted. Near the start, he says "kill them, kill them all" in reference to innocent civilians. That's evil.

Finn is a dumb idea for a character. A storm trooper with a change of heart? What did he think he was getting into? And how can we continue to see other storm troopers as generic henchmen if we've now seen that some of them might be nice guys? There's no consistency. He's dull and only adds some mild comic relief.

Rey is a Mary Sue. She learns the ways of the force independently in no time at all. She makes Luke look like a moron. But more to the point, her character shows that Abrams and the writers don't understand Star Wars. Having Rey learn so quickly cheapens the force and the whole process of learning about it.

Captain Phasma is a throwaway bad guy. She's tall. She has about two lines. That's it. General Hux shouts until he froths at the mouth. Another sign of weakness. Tarkin was much more interesting in episode IV.

Harrison Ford is good, but wasted. One terrible scene involves him and others fighting some fake-looking CGI creatures. For whatever reasons, he broke up with Leia after they had a kid (her acting was pretty mediocre I thought, may she rest in peace). This isn't fleshed out. And he gets killed too easily. He's not that stupid. And we have nothing invested in his relationship with Kylo.

Abrams' direction is flat. Everything is shot in medium close-up. Most shots are focused on a character's face, heavy with overwrought emotion. There are few establishing shots and they are underwhelming. There's no sense of wonder, no mystery. Nothing that compares with Luke looking at binary Suns as the Force theme swells.

John Williams is amazing but this score is forgettable and somewhat empty. I suspect he was not as inspired as usual by the material. And perhaps the pace of the movie didn't leave enough room for the music to breathe, to develop. Kylo Ren has a 4-note motif. Rey's theme is weak as well. There's nothing that compares to the rich, brilliant, powerful scores of the original 6 films.

The ending is a joke. A slap in the face to fans of Star Wars but also movies in general. It's a cliffhanger at a literal cliff. The camera swirls around, blurring the background. Mark Hamill turns to look at the camera. How profound. But the real problem is that by this point - I simply don't care.

title: It is not a sequel, but a remake
review:
Sad but true. When the opening credits filled the screen (Episode VII... blah blah) I was already grinding my teeth because the plot sounded idiotic. Then the huge star destroyer filled the screen. The fun bit is that the star destroyer had some sort of antenna or whatever at the front and it looked liked the ship was showing the middle finger towards the viewers.

I have to congratulate the film makers as that was pretty much how the film worked from that point forward.

1) A droid has important information that must be delivered to the good guys (Episode IV, anyone?)

2) so the bad guys hunt for the droid on a desert planet (IV)

3) Storm troopers raid a village, killing everyone (IV)

4) A girl is captured by the bad guys and the good guys rush to the base to the rescue. (IV)

5) The girl and the boy have a friend zone relationship through the film (Ep IV, Luke & Leia, wouldn't be surprised to learn that they are siblings in Episode IX)

6) The stormtroopers, elite soldiers of the bad guys, still can't hit a barn door. On the other hand, the good guys always hit, even when they use a weapon for the first time in their life

7) Supreme Leader Snoke = Emperor with a silly name

8) The bad guys have a magnificent new weapon that can destroy planets (Ep IV)

9) They use it to destroy a planet loyal to the rebels (IV)

10) The weapon has shields that can be destroyed by going down on the planet and disabling the shield generator (VI)

11) The epic villain wears a mask that distorts his voice (IV) and sadly, looks better with the mask on than without it.

12) The good guys can only destroy the weapon with an attack by X-Wings on the exact target (IV)

13) The X-Wings have to fly in a tight trench in order to reach their target (IV)

The screen writers had absolutely no new ideas to show for their money. A bunch of monkeys could have written better dialogue. A 1st grader could have made a plot that had less holes in it. The special effects were pretty much of the same quality as in the first Star Wars movie that was released 1977. I'd expect something way better in 2015.

title: All is forgiven, George
review:
We have to give JJ Abrams credit here for he has done something that no Star Wars fan expected... he made the prequels look good.

If there was one stand-out aspect of Star Wars that made it so great it was its almost unparallelled imagination. Lucas created a hugely detailed and original universe with an epic story line. The prequels, whilst flawed in their over-use of mediocre CGI and themselves Disney'fied to a degree were still based on a deep, interesting and highly original story line. Abrams utterly failed in this respect with The Force Awakens.

It's hard to even know what TFA is even supposed to be. A complete and pointless rehash of Episode IV with bits of V and VI thrown in. Zero originality and by far and away the worst dialogue of any Star Wars film - absolutely cringe-worthy in places. Almost every scene or story aspect of any note is plagiarised from the original trilogy and reproduced in a hugely inferior way.

We all took George Lucas for granted when we saw the prequels. We saw the flaws and didn't appreciate the brilliant story beneath the surface, the original characters, ships and locations. TFA stands in stark contrast to this GL's brilliance... a pointless, corporate, plagiarised piece of unimaginative rubbish.

title: A lower quality remake disguised as a sequel
review:
If you never saw a Star Wars movie, then you could find this movie fun to watch, despite its shallowness and flaws. If you see this movie while really, really high then you might think its great. If neither of these conditions apply, then prepare to be disappointed.

There are tons of great visuals and the special effect are top notch, which is why I didn't rate this a 1. However, as an almost scene-for-scene remake of the first Star Wars trilogy all mixed together, it is a lesser quality film than the originals.

Typical of JJ Abrams' films, nothing makes any sense; it is all about visual clichés and absurd cliffhangers. Not that the Lucas' films had great acting or depth, but this movie's characters and drama are even worse. If they had bothered to come up with original space ships and robots like Lucas liked to do with each new installment, I would have given points for that, but instead they just reused the same old icons. This movie takes absolutely NO risk whatsoever. If you programmed a computer to generate a film based on cheap visual gimmicks and trope, this would be the result.

On the positive side: I never felt like walking out of the theater and it was fun to watch in a very superficial sort of way. As I already mentioned, the special effects were fantastic. You may not hate it, or even feel like it was awful (as long as you don't think too hard), but this is not a very good movie.

title: The Return of... the same old stuff
review:

Sad to say that this movie failed on so many levels. They basically rehashed plot elements from the previous movies and added special effects. Almost every line of the movie was a nod to a scene in the previous movies, which would have been nice once or twice but it's every single a character opens his/her mouth or interacts with an object.

In typical JJ Abrams fashion, they want to go "one up" on everything that has come before. The original trilogy has a Death star that can destroy planets? We'll have a Death Planet that can destroy solar systems.

You have huge star ships "Star Destroyers" so we'll have even bigger star destroyers.

You have an evil Empire trying to dominate the Galaxy, we'll have an even more evil Empire "The First Order" who want to cleanse the Galaxy? Your resistance is ill equipped but brave and skilled. Our resistance will be even worse equipped and even more skilled.

The comparisons go on and on (new more flashy light saber's, new more extreme evil Emperor) Why? Could you not move the plot forward without making things more extreme? Throw in some wooden acting (although not the worst i've seen) and you have some idea what you are dealing with.

title: It's not enough
review:
Aside from the most obvious, predictable and least suspenseful way of killing off an important character and the entire movie being pretty much a blatant copy-pasta of the original trilogy, the Force Awakens isn't all that bad. It's certainly an entertaining movie (especially for younger generations) all things considered, but is it enough for the old guard?

The big downfall of this movie are the characters. The characters in The Force Awakens are paper thin. And the reason why is because there are not enough meaningful dialogues. All the flashy pew'pew'ing is meaningless if there's not enough exposition. For example, what do we know about the lead character Rey? Well, the first half of the movie tells us that she lives alone on a sandy planet. She collects scrap. And... that's it for the most part. That's just not enough information! As a result it's impossible to form an attachment to this character. I mean there are a few other personality traits that we learn about her but overall it's just not enough. Compare that to when we first meet Han Solo in A New Hope. We instantly fall in love with this character not because he's a smuggler who owns a super fast ship (although that's cool in its own right), but because he instantly presents us with information - quirks, traits, characteristics, personality! He's arrogant, macho-type of guy with a shady past involving the Empire, isn't too slow to brag about his achievements, and a tendency to get entangled with local crime lords. That's an overload of information given to us through dialogues and interactions between the characters. See, that's where The Force Awakens falls flat. Not only is there not enough information about the lead characters, the dialogues that they engage in are short and woefully shallow... No amount of state-of-the-art graphics can make up for a lack of information. I guess we're supposed to grow and develop our attachment to the characters as the film progresses. But everything that happens to Rey is reactionary - stuff just happens and we're forced to watch her being forced to react by running away, fighting, and running away some more. In the end, none of her personality stands out as very unique or particularly interesting or has a chance to develop much.

Poe, played by Oscar Isaac, is by far the best and most charismatic character in this film. The moment he says "So who talks first? I talk first? You talk first?" when confronted by Kylo Ren, is when I instantly knew this character will not suck. Sadly, we don't get to see Poe very much after this scene which is a big shame.

I mean, I'd be lying if I told you I didn't enjoy watching the movie for its action sequences, beautiful cinematography and sets. Given today's standards, it's definitely an entertaining and fun movie. But this is STAR WARS. It's a goddamn religion for so many of the fans... As pretentious as it sounds - fun is not enough! The fans want more - more innovation, more interesting characters, more exploration of the mystery of the Force. Overall, it's just not enough.

Abrams and the rest of the writers should be ashamed.

title: Complete Trainwreck
review:
This film failed on every level. It's not a believable piece of the franchise and not even an acceptable movie. The cast is horrible and it's continually reinforced by moments of phenomenal acting by a few. There is very little story and it's mostly a rehash of the first three movies, yet it feels like i would have enjoyed it much more if i had never heard of Star Wars.

The acting by Harrison Ford and Daisy Ridley was superb and drew me in to the story but it was continually upstaged by the horrible performances of the scenes other actors. It may have been the writing but Finn who was supposed to be a serious battle trained storm trooper came off as a goofy teenager. Kylo Ren who is supposed to be a deadly and evil Sith trained by the galaxies most famous Jedi acted more like an angry kid who was only trained in temper tantrums. It summed it all up in the final 30 seconds when Rey and Luke Skywalker meet and without saying a word conveyed more emotion than i had seen throughout the film.

Throughout all the previous films and all the books and stories Lucas laid in political undertones and unsaid questions of morality but there was just nothing here. There was nothing to think about and no excitement. The scenes had no development or meaning. The characters were just inserted into the story with a brief line or two as to who they were and where they came from. There was never any climax. Even the light saber battles were boring and looked as though they were choreographed by a 4 year old playing with wrapping paper tubes.

Han Solo. Ran away from home and someone stole his ship. Rey. My parents left me but they'll be back. I think. Sand. Luke Skywalker. SHHH i'm hiding. Kylo Ren. I'm bad and evil because i said so. title: Another disappointing review :(
review:
*** Spoiler Alert *** I just wanted to start by saying, I am a true SW fan; I love all the previous SW films (including Episodes I-III, although I think the books are much better!); I have read over 50 SW novels (my favourite is Darth Plagueis by James Luceno, hands down); and I even enjoy watching SW the Clone Wars and SW Rebels on the weekend with my girlfriend. Saying that, I really wanted to enjoy this film, so I walked in with no expectations.

Initially, I thought it was a mistake for Disney to make Episodes VII-XI, largely because the storyline after Episode VI is rather weak. I actually hoped Disney would make a pre-Episode I trilogy. I also thought it was a huge mistake bring Mark Hamill, Carrie Fisher and Harrison Ford back into the mix (because I didn't think they could add anything more to the story). However, to spite all this, as I said above, I walked into the movie with no expectations. I only wanted to enjoy whatever Disney threw at me... and sadly I still walked out disappointed.

I thought the movie was a complete recycle of Episode IV, with a few scenes from Episode V and VI thrown in. The biggest disappointment, however, was the new villain, Kylo Ren. I thought he was nothing more than an emotional child, a pitiful example of a "wanna-be" Sith; well, well below the standards of a SW villain. I thought this character alone completely destroyed the film for me. I think I could have overlooked everything else I didn't like, providing this character alone lived up to the Sith legacy. What makes SW great are its villains, but Kylo Ren, was just an incredibly weak human being; throwing temper tantrums from one scene to the next. We're supposed to believe that Kylo Ren completely destroyed the new Jedi Order when he couldn't even defeat a single force-sensitive girl with no Jedi training of any kind? I don't remember Luke Skywalker defeating Darth Vader seconds after he picked up his lightsabre? Perhaps next time he better call for reinforcements before he faces a defenceless young girl (or a Jedi novice)? I really hope Disney kill off Kylo Ren before the next film (or at minimum, he grows a pair of balls the size of Death Stars, so he can at least swing a lightsabre. I'm really hoping for the latter!!)

SW the Old Republic (Knights of the Fallen Empire) has recently introduced some great villains into the game. Even the new television series SW Rebels has some great villains, Fifth Brother and Seventh Sister. Fifth Brother might not be the brightest Sith in the galaxy but at least he was well trained by Darth Vader... Kylo Ren on the other hand is an embarrassment to the SW series. Why couldn't Kylo Ren have lived up to anyone of these SW characters? I think even Jar Jar Binks could have easily struck Kylo Ren down. Disney please kill him off before the next movie!!

I also think the series needs to completely walk away from Death Stars. I mean seriously, how many times can the Rebel Alliance destroy a Death Star? This is 3 times now. Are we going to see another two more Death Stars in Episodes IIX and IX as well? There are hundreds of amazing SW novels out there that don't require a Death Star to finish off the story, but the movies seem unable leave them alone. Why couldn't Disney have made one of these books into a movie? I can only hope Disney is a little more imaginative next time. 4 out 10 from me... I also thought Harrison Ford completely carried the whole movie. Although, Daisy Ridley played her part exceedingly well.

title: The Manipulation Power of Nostalgia and Mass Appeal
review:
I want to start by stating I truly have enjoyed all Star Wars movies prior to this one. Even the prequels (which are obviously not as good) demolish this movie in plot, character building and EVEN action sequences. (there is only two lightsaber battles and they last seconds)

Anyone with a brain and knowledge of the original trilogy can see that Star Wars: Episode VII was a regurgitation of the first three film's plot condensed into two hours. Everything was the same with slight twists down to the famous "Luke, I am your father" scene except it's with Han Solo and his apparent Sith son who stabs and throws off of the new Death Star.

They added a bigger and badder Death Star, tossed Anakin's lightsaber around to whoever felt like using it to fight and did a terrible job of carrying on Star Wars essence. It was flooded with humor and half a**ed acting. There was no training or build up of power Rey is literally able to defeat the most powerful Sith Lord as a teenage girl who days before didn't even know she was a Jedi. Finn was able to wield and use a lightsaber although as far as I am concerned he is not a Jedi.

Han Solo and Chewbacca just happen to come across the Millennium Falcon after 30 years which just happens to have Luke Skywalker's daughter, Finn, and a droid carrying the map to Luke Skywalker on it. The film was pretty much downhill for me from this point on I spent most of my time watching this with a "What???" face and hands up in confusion as to how they could have made the film suck so bad.

This film literally spanned out the introduction of old characters we know and love in order to keep our attention and keep us excited to see the next only to disappoint us with no further elaboration in story and literally no emotion. Leia hardly even reacted to losing the love of her life Han Solo. The dialogue between the two of them was rushed and obvious that they were trying to explain 30 years of story in small talk.

What I take as the mentality for this film: MAKE A BIGGER DEATHSTAR, OH BIGGER EMPEROR TOO (srsly what was up with that), GIRL JEDI MAIN CHARACTER, BLACK GUY WHO MIGHT BE A JEDI TOO MAIN CHARACTER (I am African American so don't take this as racism) people are going TO EAT THIS UP. And congratulations, you all did and now they will keep milking the franchise and making terribly thought out films with nothing more than CGI and humor to make up for it.

Throughout this film I found myself wanting to walk out of the theater and just be done but I couldn't resist waiting for the punchline of this joke of a film and boy did I get it. After all of the humor riddled torture we are brought to the final scene. Rey is going to see her long lost dad who I guess spent all of this time standing on a random mountain looking at the beach. And then it happens, what we had all been waiting for. Luke turns around and sees the daughter he was forced to abandon and she hold out Anakin's lightsaber as some odd tribute to him (I don't see the symbolism in this) at this point I just burst out laughing at how bad this journey has been and that's it it's over. The next thing I see is JJ Abrams. I proceeded to scream "BOO" at the screen multiple times with the only response to it being "cmon it wasn't that bad" after that I walked outside and contemplated throwing up as the movie was so bad it caused me to feel nauseous.

This film took advantage of Star Wars fans and played into a hand of re-doing famous scenes with different characters and telling the same story over again. It's sad that people actually think this movie was good or acceptable because now they are going to once again shame the Star Wars name.

BOYCOTT EPISODE 8. THIS RENDITION NEEDS TO BE SCRAPPED AND REBOOTED THEY ARE JUST MILKING THIS FRANCHISE.

review: This film gets a 4 rating only because of the special effects, which were terrific - some of the best I've ever seen, even the rather badly-named Supreme Leader Snoke. Episode VII is sure to rake in the cash from hopeful moviegoers. But I doubt they'll be queuing around the block for Episode VIII.

title: The Remake Awakens & The Viewer Goes To Sleep
review:
If this movie didn't have Star Wars name on it, nobody would even remember it in less than a year. Well, maybe we would remember Abrams getting sued for plagiarism, but the movie itself IMO is ridiculously unremarkable.

To get the obvious out of the way, yes it's a remake pretending to be a sequel. It redoes New Hope with new characters taking the roles of the old ones. It doesn't have the guts to stray from the path in any significant way, and that makes it boring and predictable. If you've seen New Hope, you're up for no surprises whatsoever.

Other than that, everything about the movie screams generic. Everything, from it's heroes (female Luke and defector stormtrooper with lots of wasted potential) to it's villains. Take Emperor Palpatine, smash him together with Voldemort and Azog the Whatshisface, and you receive Supreme Leader Silly Name. His design is as unoriginal as it could be, and his lines don't help either. Kylo Ren is criticized for being whiny, but I couldn't even get annoyed with him, that's how little impression he made. This movie would need a Joker class villain to pull it's head above the sea of blandness, and instead it gave us these two.

Dialog, story, and character development take a backseat to the near constant action scenes. What little plot there is seems squeezed to fit the (too) fast pace.

It's not a bad movie per say. It's just a very, very mediocre one that seems to lack ambition to be anything more. It has nothing at all to distinguish it from dozens of similar blockbusters. Even John Williams seemed to understand that. His soundtrack suits the averageness of the movie perfectly, not giving us a single memorable track, which is really below his usual level.

This film made me miss the underrated prequels. Yes, they had their share of problems, but at least they prioritized the plot over explosions and presented some new ideas.

The Force Awakens may deserve four or five for what it does well (practical effects, CGI, diverse cast, acting) but it certainly doesn't deserve 82 it currently has on IMDb, so here is my score.

title: Really?
review:
Now before I go on, let me just say that I am a huge Star Wars fan. I grew up with and enjoyed both trilogies (yes, both) and like a lot of fans have dedicated a rather sizable part of my life to the franchise. After all these years of waiting since the last movie, I was so excited to see the new Star Wars. In some ways, I'm still waiting for a new Star Wars.

This movie has new characters, new actors, and new special effects, but at the end of the day, what I value most about sequels to movies I enjoy is when they bring a new story to the table and expand the fiction, which is exactly what this movie did NOT do. The whole story is literally A New Hope all over again. Now, A New Hope is one of my favorite movies ever, and there seems to be a lot of people who praise the movie for recapturing the feeling of the "old Star Wars". But there are so many ways this could be done without mimicking the story of an older movie. I understand that no movie ever made has been completely original, but when a movie is so unoriginal that you can predict almost everything that's going to happen before it does, there's a serious problem.

I also had a big problem with the new characters and the movie's acting. I honestly didn't find any of the new characters compelling. I can't find Rey that interesting because the whole orphan living on a desert planet has already been used in this series, twice. Finn was, no joke, one of the most annoying characters I have ever been exposed to. In my opinion, he is even worst than Jar Jar. The soccer ball that I refuse to name was also incredibly annoying. Captain Phasma was particularly infuriating. After all the hype surrounding her surrounding her leading up to the film's release, after how big a deal all the marketing made about her, you'd think she'd be in the movie for more than a total of two minutes of screen time and would actually do something important, but no, this is not the case. The only new character who had the potential to be interesting in any way was the highly anticipated Kylo Ren, but he is played by such a poor actor that it's ruined.

Which leads to my next point, which is the acting. People are always complaining about the acting in the prequel trilogy, and admittedly even though I enjoy the prequels as I stated before, I do think that a few of that trilogy's actors could have done a better job (although I do not think it was anywhere near as bad as what most people seem to think). The acting in this one was SO MUCH worse, though. Adam Driver was the worst one. He had one facial expression that he wore for most of his unmasked scenes and spoke in basically a monotone for most of the movie. John Boyega was another actor who stood out with how bad he was (the scene where he yells Rey's name when she is captured is SO overdone). The rest of the cast isn't that much better. The new actors all do a poor job, even Oscar Isaac and Domnhall Gleeson, who are normally excellent actors. Gleeson's "End of the Republic" speech seriously hurt me. The only new actor who was somewhat decent was Daisy Ridley, and she played such a boring character as I said before that it didn't matter much in the end. Even the older actors from the previous movies didn't seem like they were giving it their best effort in this installment of the saga.

There are a couple of other things I disliked, but they were significantly smaller things than what I have already discussed, so I won't keep you any longer, assuming anyone's still reading at this point. I know you're probably tired of listening to people complain about how unoriginal the new Star Wars is, and I'm sorry I added to that, but this is how I feel about the movie. I was honestly in shock when I left the theater the night I saw it. I could not believe what I had just witnessed. It took a couple days for me to get over my shock, which was then replaced by anger, and I couldn't help but wonder if this is what the generation before me felt like when they saw The Phantom Menace for the first time.

The one thing that made me give the movie two stars instead of just one was Han Solo. Even if Harrison Ford wasn't giving his best performance ever, just the fact that Han Solo was even in this movie made it somewhat better.

I hope to God Episodes 8 and 9 are a bit more original with their stories.

2/10

title: Disney makes a Star Wars movie
review:
There are so many negative reviews of this movie here that I doubt I could add anything new to them, so I'll just say that all the criticisms you've heard and read about The Force Awakens are correct. The problems fall into three categories:

1.) The story is mostly a copy of A New Hope, with characters, planets, droids, etc. simply having different names. Even some of the dialog is practically copied. There's a little The Empire Strikes Back in there, too. I guess it's a great film for kids who haven't seen the original, but for an adult like me it's a complete waste of time.

2.) The SJW component is pretty strong. The evil characters are almost all white men, and in fact all the males in the film are either weak, immature, or evil. The only exception is Poe, who's barely in the story. Even the great Han Solo himself is killed by his pathetic son.

3.) The "Luke" character is an extreme Mary Jane. She can do anything — repair spaceships, fly spaceships, talk to an R2 droid, do Jedi mind tricks, defeat a Jedi master with a light saber, etc. — all with no training, apparently without even having heard of The Force. This kind of character is outside the Star Wars universe, why is she in this movie? My impression is that problems 2. and 3. are common to Disney movies these days. I guess they're made for little girls, while little boys are instead playing violent video games.

Conclusion: Your nine year old daughter might love this movie. It's definitely not for adults, and quite a far cry from the great 1977 film that was once simply called Star Wars. The sad part is that it made a bazillion dollars so Disney will make many more just like it.

title: What new can I say?
review:
I guess I'll focus in this review on something I've always held as one of the best things about the Star Wars franchise: The soundtracks.

Every soundtrack through episode 1 to 6 have been super awesome. There have always been lots of recognizable melodies and harmonies in the tracks, something new and exciting. John Williams and George Lucas have been a really great combo when these pieces have become a reality. I believe really strongly this same kind of connection was not possible with Abrams and Williams. And maybe this fact contributed to this soundtrack being certainly the weakest of all the Star Wars soundtracks.

When I was watching the movie I felt the music was always pushed to the background, it had never enough room to carry the scene. And that was a shame because that has been the beauty of Star Wars: the music has played a big part carrying some big scenes, best of examples being the Binary Sunset.

What is the new super recognizable musical piece of this movie? There is no new "Duel of Fates" or "Across the Stars" in this movie. The most identifiable track is Rey's theme. I like to listen to it since there's something new there. But lots of other tracks miss that feeling of recognizability and originality. And I think that the lack of new things in the movie have contributed to this. When you have a new thing, you get inspired with experimenting what kind of music would suit this new world or new setting and have a good excuse to create an identifiable piece of music.

Overall the soundtrack is a bit boring and suffers from lack of inspiration. A good plot and new settings would have probably made the soundtrack more exciting. And of course it could have used a lot more room in the final mix.

And to conclude other things than the soundtrack, most of the nay guys out there have already said things I'd like to say about this film: It is unoriginal and uninspired and it's sad it was taken into this direction instead of creating something new.

title: A Horrible Rehash
review: This would have been one of the best Star Wars movies ever...if Episode IV did not exist. The plot is pretty much the same; I can't think of a single original element in the plot. Even the planets shown are copies from Episode IV and Episode V. The Prequels may be bad but at least it had an original story; the prequels had done quite well considering the outcomes were already decided before. But Episode VII had full freedom to steer it's plot in any direction but instead sadly they just decided to make an Episode IV clone to appeal to nostalgia and milk the cash cow. However, unlike episode IV the stakes weren't very high- the heroes' plans worked out more or less without a hitch. The new characters were highly unrealistic and the old ones are forced into the story. Rey is a mary-sue who is extremely good with machines; is able to understand droid language;can even understand wookie language even though wookies don't live in Jakku;is an ace- pilot who knows the Millennium Falcon better than even Han Solo himself and can use the force better than a fully trained Jedi without any Jedi training. Finn is a controversial character who refuses to kill for the First Order but is fully ready to kill his Stormtrooper brothers without any hesitation and remorse for the Resistance. Kylo Ren becomes an emo punk the second his mask comes off...This movie has stunning visuals and this is perhaps the only redeeming quality about the movie. The plot and characters however are grossly horrible. The dialogues were atrociously juvenile- "Do you have a boyfriend, a cute boyfriend?" and "Who talks first? Do you talk first or do I talk first?" are examples of cheesy dialogues scattered throughout the movie. Unless you didn't ever watch episode IV I don't believe you should watch this unoriginal trash.(This movie doesn't actually deserve 2 star, maybe 4 or 5, but the ratings have to be balanced)

title: Star Wars: The Profits Awakens
review:
Star Wars is one of the most beloved franchises from people of all ages. It started with its beginning roots telling the story of the evil Galactic Empire bent on ruling the galaxy while hindering the progress of the Rebel Alliance, to the backstory of how the Republic was deceived by the Sith who enacted war under the guise of the Trade Federation. This film, however, mocks the genius, the integrity, and the furious action packed thrills that existed in all the other films that preceded it. This film is the perfect example of 21st Century Hollywood capitalizing on a franchise name for pure profits while playing it safe. Disney had its eyes for years on this and knew to take advantage when they got the chance.

The Force Awakens felt like a mere reboot than an actual entry into Star Wars series. People loved the original trilogy (which I'm not actually a huge fan of, though I personally still enjoy it anyways), but when the prequels came out the fans bashed it harshly. All blame came out on George Lucas being a terrible Director and Writer. When this was announced, it was thought to be the "saving grace" from Episodes I-III. Unfortunately it was not, and turned out to be worse than the prequels. Let's analyze this movie:

Director and Writing: J.J Abrams, or Jar Jar Abrams, had some good movies before this such as Super 8 and Star Trek, but being handed down the mantle of Star Wars was not his strongest suit. If I wanted to watch a film about flashy lens flares and camera shake with sudden focus zoom following unconvincing CGI spaceships flying through space, I would stick to Star Trek. What really disappointed me was the "playing it safe" rule by telling a story that was pretty much the same thing from Episode IV, only this time it's bigger and/or has a different name. Why didn't they just put Rey on Tatooine instead of a planet that is called Jakuu which pretty much looked the same? I don't know maybe because the Director and Writers got lazy and decided it didn't need to be authentic. Same goes for bringing a oppressive regime to the picture, The First Order, which was born from the defeat of the Empire. Guys, the Empire was finished and done for, so there is no reason to doing a throwback at the Original Trilogy. The jokes in this film are childish and do not blend in with the situations at hand. It is written to entertain children who couldn't understand the babbling of space politics in the other films. Not one time did I feel that there was an actual threat at hand, it felt like a silly Marvel themed space journey like Guardians of the Galaxy.

Characters: I do have to hand it to JJ that the acting and character development was put forth quite well, except the fact that The Force Awakens traded this off for plot convenience. Rey, a lonely farm girl left of Jakku, seemed to know how to do everything from fixing machines, piloting space ships, using Force Powers, and engaging the main villain in light saber combat with no training whatsoever. What no faults at all? Hmm that characterization is very uninteresting and boring to say the least. Finn, and let's be honest, was tossed in to add diversity to the main characters. He is cowardly, obnoxious, and is there to save the girl even if she can already save herself. Poe Dameron and Finn's relationship was the only thing that seemed morally self-sub-staining (although rushed a bit) since Poe faced execution and Finn was able to escape the First Order while developing a friendship in the midst of danger. Kylo Ren was not convincing as a villain and was a heaping balloon of hot gas ready to explode when something did not go his way. The casting of this character was flawed and was more whinny than Anakin was in the prequel trilogy.

Music Score and Sound Design: If I'm not getting any of the aforementioned components above, then you are going to get the music down right? Wrong. John Williams knows how to score Star Wars and has been doing it for Lucas for over 30+ years. This time around, JJ sighed and said "okay fine I won't use Michael, I'll get John to do it." The pitch and tones are all off in this movie and have no memorable tunes in any form like Episode I did with "Duel of Fates" or the "Empire March" in Episode V. I felt the energy of Star Wars was not present in the Force Awakens much to many disappointed fans. Abrams himself did not even research the previous sound effects in any of the other movies and made every object in the film feel weak, foreign, and pathetic like the music.

Visual Effects: Nice use of practical effects on their part I won't lie about that. But other than that, it was still unconvincing. The space ships and fighters looked completely unreal with the preferred use of going absolutely CGI with every film production nowadays. All the other films used miniatures combined with practical effects like pyrotechnics and computer effects such as photo realistic rendering to get a real looking result printed onto film strips for the first entry in the prequels (yeah that was quite an ingenious method for visuals when film strips were still being used). In this case it was either one or the other, no mixing allowed.

Overall I am completely disappointed and felt no real external threat to this epic space tale. There didn't seem to be any continuity to the series and as stated before, felt more like a reboot than a sequel. Hopefully the other entries will try to fix the problems this movie had. If they don't, then I'm afraid the sequel trilogy will become the new prequels.

review:
The history of Star Wars ends in "The return of the Jedi" and that's all. all was said. No doubt about it. The rise and fallen of a hero, and his redemption across her son. there's no more in Star Wars movies.

title: Save your money
review:
I'd like to believe there are literally thousands of Star Wars fans sitting out there, desperately trying to like this film. Please stop, there's not that much here to like.

The storyline is almost a complete reiteration of the earlier films, has very little originality and is just...dull.

The acting is for the best part fairly wooden, in fact if the world was to turn too ridiculous for words and someone from this pathetic remake gets nominated, make it Chewy, who I suspect was actually saying "this is total cr*p" every time he spoke.

This film is overrated by about 4.5 points, it's unoriginal, badly scripted and badly acted, it's one redeeming feature is that eventually it ends.

I'm a fan of science fiction, and I know that the ratio between good and bad science fiction films is about 15:1, at least in my experience, so that's fifteen films ranging from "oh god" to "should never have been made" before I get a good one. title: Great first half then downhill. Recycled Star Wars.
review:
The Force Awakens did something quite unique. It made me feel excitement, confusion, sadness, boredom and then ultimately disappointment, probably in that order. It started off great, a new cast who were all top notch (apart from shouting Nazi officer guy), a story filled with adventure and so many possibilities, all set in the Star Wars universe. What's not to like? And I must admit. The initial First Order attack, while it did feel like something from a TV show, was pretty good. Kylo Ren was shaping up to be a menacing villain and Poe and Finn were great new introductions. Rey too was pretty great and seeing the Falcon with Han and Chewie was a lot of fun.

That's pretty much where I checked out. The rest was the most unoriginal uninspired bunch of Star Wars I have ever come across. I've watched all of the Clone Wars series and read the majority of the Expanded Universe books and comics and I've never felt so meh about a Star Wars story.

The breaks in logic took me right out of the movie as did the uninspired earth locales. They seemed so afraid of upsetting people who didn't like the prequels that the imagination that goes into the aliens and worlds that is usually present in a Star Wars movie was lacking. I was waiting during the bit on Jakku to see how they would introduce Han Solo and the Falcon but the lazy way that first the Falcon and then Han and Chewie were just there when the plot needed them to be was just lame. Next up was Maz and her castle, nothing about that felt like Star Wars, it felt more like a Lord of the Rings movie and was way too derivative of a New Hope.

Spoilers ahoy ########################

Rey just happens to find the Falcon, then Han Solo, then Lukes' Lightsabre. It's no fun when the film is constantly reminding you that there's a script behind the scenes telling everyone what to do.

We get a new death star, we get X-Wings, Tie Fighters, a Star Destroyer, a trench run, some X- Wings flying inside a big battle station, parental difficulties and lots of 'hey remember these things?' from earlier movies.

I was really confused when I left the cinema. Everything seemed pretty decent. Good cast, fun battles, decent characters and a fairly entertaining adventure. But then as I thought about it I realised the problem. I'd seen all of it before. JJ Abrams and Lawrence Kasdan just took what people loved and said, play it all again. Without seemingly any original ideas of their own.

Kasdan wanted Han to die and for Luke to walk off into the sunset back in Return of the Jedi. So guess what happens in this one. The extended universe of books and comics written over 30 years was done away with, only for one huge element of that to be ripped off. (Ben Solo, Jacen Solo) If Rey turns out to be Rens sister which I suspect will be the case it shows how bereft of original ideas they truly are.

It's a homage to Star Wars so it didn't feel like real Star Wars. Lucas thought thought it was too retro. George Lucas was right.

title: A poor story leads to a poor movie, such a disappointment.
review:
I saw TFA in 3D opening night and left feeling shocked. I didn't really believe what I just witnessed. So I went back a few days later again and watched it in IMAX 3D thinking I must have missed something. Well I didn't. I've since also read the TFA book and it only expands the story slightly, but basically goes hand in hand with the movie, with slight differences. The problem with this story is there is no emotional attachment to draw the audience in. When you watched episodes 4-6 you could feel that emotional attachment. Just think back to when the first teaser trailer came out for TFA, did you get so excited that you shed a tear?....:) Even the prequels had some of that feeling too, as long as "Ani" wasn't on screen whining about something...:) But the prequels had a great story, which I think a lot of people missed due to bad acting or whatever, and that was the story of how Darth Vader came to be.

So a little history of my overall Star Wars history. I've seen all the movies multiple times, read almost all the SW books and even played a few of the SW games, most of which have excellent stories. I was only 3 when SW came out, too young to remember it, but when I was 6 I was taken to the drive-in several times to watch Empire. It was a double feature with Empire and the Dark Crystal if anyone remembers that movie...:) So I went into TFA knowing that they were not going to use any of the previously written books and it was going to be a new story approximately 30 years after Return of the Jedi. So my problem started when i saw things in TFA taken from the the previously written books and inserted under different circumstances. For instance Han and Leia's son Ben aka Kylo Ren. That was Luke's son's name in the books. Also the Starkiller Base. They took the Starkiller name from Georges Lucas original concept of Star Wars. Luke Skywalker was originally going to be named Luke Starkiller. Simple changes they could of made but i think they did that so original fans could feel nostalgia, but it just comes across as lazy writing.

During the movie there are a few moments they put in to give the movie that "cool" factor which it shouldn't have needed if the story was there. the first one was when kylo froze the blaster bolt in mid travel, that was my first audible groan. Or when Finn looks up and sees Poe flying around shooting about 10 Tie fighters down in about 5 seconds, insert another groan.

So lets talk about the new lead villain Kylo Ren now. Pathetic. OK moving on then....:) Now we come to my main complaint about the movie besides the story, Kylo Ren, "Cool" story moments, the story again. Lets talk about Rey. Now first off I have no problem with a female lead character. My problem is with this character's abilities to do absolutely anything she wanted like fly the Falcon, extremely well even, figure out her force powers without training, and of course the light saber....wow. This is by far the most complained about subject about this movie. And with reason.

So lets talk about light saber battles. Back in the day and when I say back in the day I mean the prequel movies and before. both jedi and sith had training academies. At least until the Sith went to the "Rule of Two" strategy before episode 1. And they trained from early years until their adult life. I'm sure you noticed the light saber battles were very different from episodes 4-6 to episodes 1-3. Well that was from all the training. From episode 4 and beyond no one really had much training which helps explain the saber battle in TFA, partially. But, the fact that Kylo had been trained by Luke and should have been well trained. He was still hit by Finn, not a jedi at all, and overpowered by a girl with no jedi training at all. This was the part where everyone like me threw their hands in the air and screamed WTF??????????? And of course the final scene where they find Luke finally, and you see him as if he is a handicapped person in a wheelchair with slobber coming from the side of his mouth. To be fair, by this point I was way done with this movie...lol So in summary, poor story, nostalgia moments need to go, "cool" moments need to go. They knew before they made this movie people had extremely high expectations for this movie and they choose to make the quick buck instead of the everlasting buck.

Thats my 2 cents worth, enjoy it if you can...;)

title: Disappointed

title: Imitation. No substance. Like a cheap knockoff
review:

title: it's like a rich guy made a fan fiction movie
review:
A lot has already been written about the failings of this movie (and there are a lot and I only have 1000 words so I can't go into all of them) but there were a few specific things I'd like to address.

I feel like it's a bad piece of fan fiction. You know the one's where horrible things happen to the original characters and some random new characters are thrown in to fix it all. Also because the people who wrote this thing had no idea what the original characters were about in the first place ie loyalty and fidelity. Han had already transformed from smuggler to hero - we didn't need to see it done again. We needed to see how that character would have matured over 30 years, but he didn't mature. In true fan fiction style Disney is rewriting the Han Solo character from being lovable rogue to complete a**hole (so Poe Dameron can replace him in this new PC world), he's not the character written about in the pre-Disney books anymore where he's a leader and a hero and a brother-in-law, father, grandfather, husband and friend. Nope he's just a smuggler and a pilot and that's it.

I saw an interview with Harrison Ford where he said the old characters had been given, 'satisfactory' back stories and I thought at the time we could be in trouble with this film. Satisfactory is a very specific choice of words, it's like he wanted to say it's terrible but couldn't.

The people who are saying that it's like Episode 4 because that's what fans wanted...no we didn't we wanted a new story. We wanted new characters we could care about...seriously you could have blown up all the newbies and I wouldn't have given two hoots.

It's like Disney looked at what people hated about the prequels (that weren't that bad btw) and then what people liked about the Originals and just copied and pasted it. If there's 30 minutes of dialogue in this whole thing I'd be shocked.

In this new Hunger Games/Harry Potter/Avengers mash up you apparently have no life between 30 and 60. The characters are all either under 30 (and great at everything) or over 60 and just plain worn out and tired because apparently they made bad choices. Only wait a minute...they didn't, I saw the movies, they made great choices. They were loyal, heroic and brave not the husks we saw on the screen.

I wonder how much today's viewers will like it when in 20/30 years someone writes Ray as a bad wife and mother with an evil child whose husband has run away, when Fin and Poe abandon their friends and families and then die a pointless death? That's all Star Wars is now the ongoing saga of bad parenting...fan fiction at it's worst.

I won't be watching anymore Disney Star Wars. As others have said Star Wars is dead.

title: Epic let down to the first 6
review:
I am a huge fan of star wars and therefor placed the expectation of the 7th on a very high pedestal. But that's probably why it was such a let down.

Now the movie did hit certain points: the acting was pretty good, the visual effects were phenomenal, and it really is an action adventure.

However it missed quite a few major points.

1: No connection with the characters. Kylo Ren struggles with following good or evil, Han Solo feels the "loss" of his son throughout the movie, Rey has been abandoned at a very young age and has some sappy sad story, and Finn constantly is looking for his place in the world. All understandable stories. Yet, you don't feel any of it. No sadness, or understanding or anything. The only character that is some what relatable would be Han Solo. But that's not based on this movie, but from the love of the character in the 1st 3 movies (not chronologically).

2: Not realistic at all. Now I fully understand I'm watching a movie with Jedi, the force, aliens, space fighting, etc. I'm with you 100%. But, if I was to accept that what happened in the first 6 movies is the standard of what is realistic, than this movie is not realistic at all. This is based entirely around 1 character: Rey. She was abandoned at a young age, and has never really known what the force is. Yet somehow, after Han Solo gives her a brief 30 sec explanation of the force, she somehow manages to master the mind control and manipulate a storm trooper ... in a matter of minutes. So well actually, that the scene before, she resists the mind manipulation of Kylo Ren, a seasoned jedi. Somehow, manages to master the force and "summon" her lightsaber out of the snow with Kylo Ren attempting the same. Then, the really big "bullshit" scene, when she defeats a sith lord. Rey discovered the force yesterday, and somehow, in a day, masters it so well, she's able to defeat Kylo Ren: a seasoned, well trained, very powerful sith lord. Oh and she developed this ability in about half a second, mid way through the fight. Yeah, I don't buy it at all.

3: Originality. Yeah, this movie, is the exact plot of a New Hope. Character, abandoned by father, finds a droid with plans for the universe, joins up with a smuggler (the exact same smuggler in fact), travels across the galaxy, discovers they're a jedi, is taught very briefly how to be a jedi, loses that mentor later in the film to the villain, fights that villain and wins (without killing the villain, destroys a very large planet killing machine due to a convenient glitch in the killing machine's construction, and then leaves to go find a master jedi to learn the force... interesting.

4: Ending of the movie. I've already explained how the fight between Kylo Ren and Rey should have gone way differently. But even if Rey was that good, she should have killed Kylo. An earthquake, basically, separates them and they go there separate ways? Yeah no. Obi Wan and Anakin did force jumps like crazy in the first 3. If you're so powerful in such a short time with the force, then hop the damn canyon and go cut his head off. And then Chewy shows up to rescue her just before the planet size object blows up. And then she goes to find Luke Skywalker. Which I would have been OK with, except for the actor had 5 sec of screen time. The good parts about that ending, were the same good parts about the ending to A New Hope and therefor can't be attributed to this movie.

5: Kylo Ren. This character plays as the main antagonist in the film. He is following in his grand father's footsteps (Darth Vader) to becoming a very powerful sith lord. And he is very powerful. He stopped a blaster in mid air and then continued on with a conversation as if it took no concentration for him to hold it there. He also used a mind control interrogation technique rather successfully. And he took a hit from Chewy's crossbow which we have seen blow people up before, and continued moving. Yeah the character is powerful. But throughout the whole movie he continuously throws temper tantrums and cries like a little girl. Then, he gets his ass kicked by a little girl who learned the force yesterday. Oh yeah, that was very Dark Lord ish of you. After having fantastic villains in the 1st 6 movies, Kylo Ren was a major let down to this one.

For the rest of the Star Wars fans who haven't seen the 7th, don't waste your money at the theatre. Wait for Redbox.

title: The force flops

title: How did this fan fiction get so highly rated?
