title: The bubble popped, people are waking from a dream.
review:
In the previous Star Wars, all the major characters had flaws. They faced their own downfall and stood up stronger against it. Anakin Skywalker fell to the Darkside but overcame it thanks to the love of his son, daughter and wife. Obi Wan lost against Jango Fett, against Count Dooku and finally against his student, Anakin Skywalker. Han Solo was frozen in Carbonite, Leila got shot and the list goes on.

We do not however see any of these flaws in Rey, she is just perfect in every sense. She was living in isolation on a desert planet but still knows how to use the force, pilot a space ship, repair a space ship and eventually beat a previous student of Luke Skywalker. According to the lore of Star Wars, the Sith follows the rule of two. There is always a Sith teacher and his / her Sith student. If Rey can so easily overcome a student of Luke Skywalker, then WHY the need to learn from Luke ? As a trader. I know a financial bubble when I see one and The Force Awakens was a bubble. You can check it for yourself by sorting User Reviews on IMDb by Chronological. The madness of the masses implies that everyone follows the other fools until one by one they realized their own madness and wake up from their dreams. TFA was sold as a beautiful nostalgic dream and the audience bought it at first, but then slowly, they realized it was nothing new. Nothing new was added as canon to the Star Wars Lore.

title: Wooden Characters with no Complexion.
review:
While there were many problems with The Force Awakens such as it being a rehash of the original, the hurdle which I found the movie completely flops on was; - the characters

And more importantly the characters interaction with each other. There is no friction between them. When Poe meets Finn they take an immediate liking to one another. They know nothing about one another and don't even attempt to learn about each others character, it's just completely wooden because the writer wanted to create a band of heroes without any development to their relationship just so there could be time for the dull predictable action. Its the same with Rey and Finn, Rey at first distrusts Finn and then 3 minutes later they are best friends high-fiving and hugging and you wouldn't know they met each other only 10 minutes ago.

The characters themselves are also boring and full of holes. The director doesn't seem know how to create a connection between the characters on screen and the audience. I can't relate to any of the protagonists because I know nothing about them because nowhere in the movie do we get an interesting backstory or are we told about the characters interests or characteristics. They have zero personality.

In fact the only characters I found remotely interesting in the entire movie were the original trilogy characters. At least I knew a bit about them and their was a bit of tension between Han and Leia.

Overall the character department of this movie was weaker then both the Original and Prequel Trilogies. I wont even get into the plot- holes or how this movie was a complete rehash because everyone has already done that.

title: JJ Abrams is overrated
review:
I was pessimistic when I learned JJ Abrams was going to be taking on Star Wars. While he was "successful" in the reboot of the Star Trek films, he seems incapable of directing a film without a contrived plot that is about as coherent as something written by a 5th grader.

Okay, I had no problem having Finn crash land and run into Rey and BB-8. It's everything after that. Amazing that the Millennium Falcon just happens to be on the same planet in the same village that these two need to escape from. Amazing that they get picked up in space by non other than Han Chewy. Amazing that Han and Chewy decide to take them to the same backwater world where there is a wise ... individual who just so happens to have Anakin/Luke's lightsaber. Yeah, I get it, the Force works through everything, but come on. This isn't the Force at work. We've seen this sort of collection-of- coincidences-equals-plot in the Star Trek reboots. When looked at with a critical eye, this sort of plot is about as sturdy as a cardboard box in a hurricane.

The rest of the story was pretty simple. There's a giant planet- destroying base (quite original) and it's going to destroy the Resistance. This is the third such super-weapon plot device in the Star Wars franchise. They've ceased to become impressive, especially given how easily they are destroyed.

And the characters? Han Solo ... the best you could do was make the hero of the Galactic Civil War reverting back to a smuggler? It's like his character did absolutely no evolving in the 33ish years since we first met him at that cantina. Rey was fine, but I think we all sort of can predict her future. Why not giving us her full name or showing us who her parents were, that means you're hiding something. I wouldn't be surprised if she is a Skywalker. What a great story to pit two descendants of Anakin against one another? Finn. A bit over the top, and it didn't necessarily fit in with the Star Wars universe. They should have toned down his character a bit. Kylo Ren. Not bad. I think everyone was expecting a Vader clone and we got a guy who is still learning. Captain Phasma. Who? Everyone got excited about the chrome stormtrooper. All she did was walk around issuing orders and then get taken prisoner. That stormtrooper with the shock stick thing was more of a bada^^ than Phasma. General Hux. Definitely not on par with previous villains. Too young. They could have cast a much older actor and the role would have done better.

I'm glad that Abrams ISN'T running the next installment. Maybe we'll get more story--a more complete story

title: Sounds Legit
review:
My take? Nostalgia overload! I also agree that the plot is strikingly similar to 'A New Hope', but I won't re-write all the comments that other's have made to compare.

First: The Good

-Visually I thought it was great, very sleek and stylish (or the First Order did any way)

-I loved hearing the classic theme music once more, as it's been a while since I've watched Star Wars!

Second: The Bad

-I went to watch a NEW film, and ended up watching A New Hope

-I thought Kylo Ren was supposed to be a badass until he took off his mask, then he just came across as a problem child with temper tantrums and daddy issues

-Rey finds out she's a jedi, and instantly manages to use mind control, summon Luke's lightsaber AND completely own Kylo Ren the first time she used the damn weapon, even though Kylo had more experience? Sounds legit

-Finn magically knows how to fight with a lightsaber, and also manages to fight pretty well against Kylo? Sounds legit

-R2 D2 just magically gains battery power right when they need it most? I cringed at that moment.

-Seriously you would think after 2 Death Stars they would have built a weapon that can't be so easily destroyed... Let me guess, in the next film they're building another Star Killer?

-So Han Solo doesn't remember how to use his own ship, but a teenage girl who's never flown before does? Sounds Legit

OK, I'll stop there before I go on and on. I just sat there in the cinema and knew exactly what movie clichÃ© would happen next, I knew what the characters would quip about, and I just got a little bored at all the stuff that happened by the end. The director did a good job at providing nostalgic moments, but it was a little too predictable.

If you're looking for entertainment, go ahead and watch it, but you may find yourself rolling your eyes or laughing at how predictable it all is.

No wonder Luke wasn't in the movie until the end; if he'd have been there, Kylo would have been beaten in the first 10 seconds!

title: Horrible letdown
review:
WARNING spoilers below.

###############################

If I could give this movie a 0/10 I would, but 1 was the lowest available score.

I do not think I have ever been this disappointed in a movie, ever. I had so high hopes after really liking JJ Abrams reboot of Star Trek. But this... THIS?! I'm even having trouble writing a review due to being so upset.

It managed to be both a bad movie in itself, not care about the SW universe, and destroy so much of what the original trilogy and prequels spent years building.

The movie felt rushed, too busy, and with little character development. It didn't make me care about the new characters.

The plot was also extremely bad and without purpose. For example... Luke was hiding but left a map to where he was, with 95% left in his own droid? Why? Did he feel like staging a Treasure hunt but be quite easy to find anyway? 30 years after the Empire fell it is back in full power again but still cannot build a death star a handful of rebels/resistance fighters cant take down? The Force is now something you can learn to be really good at in like half a day or so and beat someone trained in it since childhood? How convenient.

The villain felt like an angry teenager. Not sinister, just angry and childish.

But what made me most sad and disappointed was to apparently kill off Han Solo just for shock value. Not to drive the story ahead, not for anything else than shock. I write apparently, since well, no one seemed to care much so from their reactions it seems like the character took a vacation or something and will return soon. Far from the reactions and impact when Han was frozen in the original movies. I was so upset at this point in the movie I wanted to leave and throw my popcorn at the screen. Han was the most important character to me in the original trilogy since he was the "regular guy" who was easiest to connect to. But sure, lets just kill him off without an afterthought. Shame on you! I want Han back.

To me, this is a complete slap in the face for anyone loving the original movies. I wish I had not spent my time or money watching this. I want my money back and I wish I could unsee this movie.

I wish episode 6 would still be the final movie of this saga,because all this movie did was destroy things. That is ALL it did.

I didn't think a movie could make me so disappointed, but this did.

title: They dare to call it STAR WARS!!!
review: I never write reviews, but this time I couldn't help it! What a disappointment! I don't even know where to start.... From the title, perhaps? STAR WARS they called it.... You gotta be kidding me!!!! This is no STAR WARS. It's a lame attempt of imitation, and a bad one, too! While I was watching this movie at the theater, all I could think was: the STAR WARS Saga, the real one, is dead. Which is very sad, because they have wasted a great opportunity of doing something really good. I am a great fan of STAR WARS. And I don't mean only the first three films, but even the last three ones, the prequels that so many people didn't like very much. STAR WARS has been the first film I ever saw in a movie theater when I was a child. Since then, that Saga has been my favorite, always. Therefore, I went to watch this movie with the best predisposition in the world. I had high expectations, too. After all this years, I thought, they will come up with something great and memorable. They have had enough time, money, and resources to do so. I have nothing against J.J.Abrams either. I had enjoyed the two Star Treks, alright. Besides, I have been reading lots of novels from the Star Wars Universe for a long time and I quite like most of them. There are tons of ideas and intriguing stories in those novels, even for bad screenwriters with no ideas at all of their own. So, there is no excuse! Instead, they just remade the same old story, again: droids carrying precious information stranded on a desert planet, pursued by storm troopers. A Death Star (again) but this time it is an entire planet, which doesn't make any sense, if you know just a bit of Astrophysics. And then what.... another Empire? After the other one has been destroyed a few years earlier??? Where does this new Emperor come from? And again the space station can be destroyed only by lowering the shields (this time by a team of people who have no plan and no idea on what they are doing) and by flying X-wings through the structure and placing a perfect hit to a specific target...... Same old story, we have seen all this already. But this time it was much, much worse because of bad actors, bad performance, no meaningful dialogue, no development of the characters whatsoever. Who are those guys, anyway??? For people like us, who know something of the Star Wars Universe, they make no sense at all. A girl, who knows nothing of the force, can beat a Sith Apprentice holding a light saber for the first time in her life??? You gotta be kidding me! A Black clone trooper? Weren't they all a perfect replica of the Bounty Hunter Jango Fett??? And weren't they programmed to obey orders without even thinking (order 66, for example)??? Not to mention that he is able to hold his ground against a Sith.... have Abraams even watched the old movies at all??? Please don't misunderstand me. I love black actors when they are up to the task. Mace Windu was great in his role and I liked him. It's the film and the story that are wrong. And what the heck is that silly red light saber???? The best way to cut off your own hands for sure, LOL! All in all, any of us could have done a better job. Even the old stars didn't make much of a difference. It was like they had nothing important to say or to do. There was no explanation or meaningful dialogue or feeling of any kind. Such a waste! If there had not been a Star Wars Saga before, and this movie had been the first of its kind, it would have been a complete failure. Nothing in common with the first Star Wars of Lucas that made history. When I got back home from the theater, I wanted to watch the true STAR WARS film once again to see the difference, and it was indeed like "long ago, in another galaxy far, far away...." another universe entirely. Am I going to watch the sequel next year? Definitely NOT. That is no STAR WARS. Not any more. They don't deserve my money.

title: ripped the heart out of Star Wars
review:
I was so excited to see this but my heart sank as soon as it started.

The premise is Luke has run and hid somewhere. The galaxy is in disarray, humans and non-humans are dying in their millions and he apparently doesn't care at all. He's left his friends/family and gone off to pout and be selfish. And so apparently the Rebell...oops Resistance is looking for him, although if he's become that big of a baby over the last 3 decades I can't think why they'd bother.

Forums debate why he ran off ie bad guy must have been really bad etc, but seriously who cares? We're talking about someone who faced Emperor Palpatine all alone at 23 and now he's left, all due to a really unconvincing bad guy. But more about Darth Cry-Baby later.

The whole point of being a hero is you don't just run off. EVER.

Han is a deadbeat dad who has abandoned his family too...very not-heroic from my usually favourite character. Abrams/Disney have turned him from lovable rogue to mid-life crisis guy. In the books (that Disney have decided are non-cannon) he's a leader,devoted father, grandfather and husband, but he retains his sarcastic wit and all the other elements that made him such a likable character. In this alternate reality (because that's all it could possibly be - it sure isn't Star Wars) according to the latest book, he basically became an intergalactic NASCAR driver and when everything went a bit wobbly he left Leia just as fast as Luke did.

Now let's get to Leia. She's not a Jedi or a member of the government, she's leading a Rebellion...again. It's like they couldn't even be bothered picking up after ROTJ they had to go back to before ANH.

In addition the new female lead is not only instantly great at absolutely everything she doesn't need any help from anyone, and I like independent female role models but we do all need help sometimes. I always really admired Leia because I thought she was independent and strong but I feel like Abrams/Disney have now cast her in a really bad light, not only is she apparently such a bad wife/mother that everyone leaves her but in her younger days she asked for help...and let Luke hold her hand...and let Han rescue her from Hoth. What was she thinking? How very un-PC of her.

The new villain is ridiculous, even his hostages make fun of him. No one ever made jokes at Vader. It's like even Abrams can't take him seriously. And then he throws tantrums like a child.

Lastly this movie makes the previous 3 and particularly ROTJ pointless. How can you watch that movie now and be remotely happy at the end? The victory made no difference, it would be better if they hadn't won at all and had all just died. The war just keeps going. None of our 3 heroes who got to even be a little bit happy. I always thought the 3 of them really loved each other (remember the Emperor's line to Luke about his faith in his friends being his weakness) but apparently not. And before everyone gets up in arms saying 'well that's how life goes' no it isn't, lots of couples/families survive tough times and are the stronger for it and secondly this is Star Wars, not Days of Our Lives, there are other ways to introduce conflict without completely destroying the whole back story of the characters we all loved so much. Such lazy writing in this movie, as other people have said it's just everywhere.

Looking back it seems like no main character in Star Wars ever gets a happy life, think about it, can you now name one main character (not the droids) that got to go on and have a decent life? They all either die young (usually murdered) or end up all alone on some forsaken planet...and then dead. I can get that from a midday movie, I don't want it in Star Wars.

This movie made me really sad and I can't work out why in an attempt to 'pass the torch' they had to destroy the old characters and the franchise.

I read an interview where Abrams said the character of Han had no point, but I feel he's the one that's missing the point, Han was the 'every man' through him we experience much of the movie, he's not a politician or a jedi he's just an average guy trying to get through life...but that's gone too now.

Movies just aren't about special effects they're about stories - if you take all the explosions and spaceships out of this you have a very hollow story. This movie will be forgotten in the not-so distant future, it will not be a classic and Disney will probably remake it every 10 years or so, just like Spiderman etc so they can sell toys.

I really can't see how anyone thought this was good but can only assume they got distracted by the flashy effects/characters or that professional reviewers have been paid for good reviews. They're used to the Avengers/Transformers/Jurassic Park format which has little or no substance. The Finn character is a bad stereotype and nothing more - he adds nothing to the story, if you killed him nothing would change, like I said it's not like Rey needs any help from anyone (including Jedi training because she can already do that too). It even seems like John Williams wasn't inspired by it because I can't remember the score,no twin suns or duel of the fates...just nothing.

If you are a Star Wars fan do not go and see this - it will destroy the story and characters for you. They ripped the heart out of the franchise and stomped all over it (and us).

Don't give Disney your money. BOYCOTT EPISODE 8

title: Star Wars fan: Is it a sequel? A remake? A parody? Is this even Star Wars?
review:
I am a mediocre Star Wars fan. This is not a hate review. But Ep VII really is not a good movie.

My review:

1. Key parts of the plot and the motives are just shameless 1 : 1 copies of the classic trilogy. Any fanzine story (let alone all the E.U. novels) could have delivered better and fresh ideas.

2. Really bad "bad guy" characterization:

  • The main villain is basically a Vader-rip-off with a far weaker mind and weaker powers. I can't take him serious at all, for me he's just Dark Helmet, the emo version. Surely Darth Maul was by far a better villain!


  • The big evil master-mind is an Emperor rip-off and nothing more than a one-dimensional CGI hologram. We know nothing about him. Who is he, how did he come to power?


3. Bad character development:

  • Waste of one of the best characters / actors of the entire franchise.


  • Although I like the character of Finn "as is" during the movie, its initial motives and development seems so illogical and contradictory to the overall back-story, I think it would have been better to just introduce him as yet another rebel guy from, whatever, Naboo.


  • What's the purpose of introducing BB the robot? Poe could just have taken R2 with him rather than BB, then it would also have been R2 to deliver the message, and there would have been no need for the ridiculous "R2-D2 is currently in hibernation, please try again later" thing.


4. The setting is really boring.

If there was one thing the prequel trilogy did right, then it was building up a big, deep, living galaxy which existed around the planets of the classic trilogy and which captured my imagination and fascination for the franchise as a kid. In VII, there's nothing more of that. We just visit a couple of planets which are either rip-offs of classic trilogy planets or just average sci-fi worlds. There's nothing special about these planets, and I forgot all of their names immediately:

  • a Tattooine clone


  • a wood planet


  • an alpine planet (turned into a battle station).


5. No mention of the events since IV which lead to the current situation, except for a few hints and the lead character's stories.

We can only guess that the Republic has been restored, but where does the 1st Order draw its power and its immense military resources from? How is it linked to the former Empire? Most importantly, where does the new super weapon come from? When did they build that? How? Why, if the Rebels are supported by the renewed Republic, do they still only have guerilla forces and fight with hit-and-run tactics? Also, what about the "Force Ghosts" concept? I thought these guys are somehow still around? Couldn't Anakin just tell his story to his grandson to make him stop the sh*t he's doing; and couldn't Obi-Wan contact Luke to tell him to come back to help his friends?

6. Awful plot holes:

  • Even though Star Wars isn't exactly well-known for its accuracy when it comes to the laws of physics, now the Star Destroyer is just way over the top. A planet which can suck the energy of a star, storing it in its core, wandering in between solar systems, and then shooting an energy bean which somehow magically splits up to precisely destroy multiple planets / moons in a system? Apart from the obvious break in "Death Star destruction" story continuity, this does not make sense in any universe.


  • With the first shot, they apparently "destroy the Republic". Isn't the Republic supposed to consist of thousands of Systems? Even if the Senate would get wiped out, there would simply be a re-election I suppose. Also, what were these planets / moons that got destroyed in that CGI explosion effect? Why doesn't any of the Rebel protagonists seem to be shaken by the loss of billions of lives?


  • I may have horribly missed the point here, but what actually is "the awakening" referred to in the title? Actually, the Force seems to merely play a marginal part in the movie. You can learn it without being taught by a Master, non-Force-users can use a light saber, and Force mind-reading tricks do hardly ever work.


  • Also, it remains a complete mystery (even more so for a new audience) why that old eremite named Luke is the only single hope now to restore peace and justice (once again) and why he didn't just leave an emergency address. Speaking of which, where does the new information about his whereabouts come from exactly?


Finally, there are a few things the movie does well: The movie score, the CGI / 3D effects, the Han Solo / Chewie team play.

Conclusion:

The more I think about this movie, the worse it becomes. I watched it back on day 2 after release, but I wasn't able to write down my impressions until now. I cannot imagine enjoying watching it a second time, let alone adding it to my annual Star Wars marathon. For me, this movie really destroyed the franchise. I'm not interested to learn more about the shaky, ridiculous storyline and the new characters they introduced with this movie. For me, Star Wars will just consist of George Lucas' parts from now on, pretending this last movie never happened. I will not watch VIII / IX when they hit the cinemas.

Rating:

I give this movie a rating of 1/10 in an attempt to "bring balance to the Force", opposing all the obvious fan-boy / buy-in 10/10 ratings. An honest rating would be 5/10 because its story is ripped off and flawed, and everything else really is just average.

title: I want my money back!
review:
After reading a bunch of positive reviews by the critics I expected this film to be pretty good. It was hard to do worse than the god-awful "Revenge of the Sith", with Frankenstein-like acting by Hayden Christensen and even the cool emperor Palpatine made look like the cartoon character Judge Doom in "Who framed Roger Rabbit". But "The Force Awakens" managed to take the Star Wars franchise to new lows.

As many others have noted, this movie is not so much a sequel to Episode VI, as a remake of Episode IV, and a much inferior remake at that. Has the Hollywood completely run out of original ideas??!

Let's see what we've got here: a wannabe emperor, a wannabe Darth Vader, yet another Death Star, and even a wannabe R2D2! P-l-e-a-s-e!

The new characters of Rey and Finn are likable enough, but they are too vanilla, and the film really suffers from the absence of a non-PC roguish character like Han Solo. Sure enough, Han Solo is present in this film but he is far too old, wise and venerable to be the Han Solo we loved in the original trilogy. "The Force Awakens" does have some jokes (which, I suppose, is an improvement compared to "Revenge of the Sith") but they are few and pretty lame.

The plot is incoherent and often nonsensical. Twenty years after the destruction of the Empire, with the Republic fully re-established, why does the Rebellion still even exist as a separate force?

Plot-wise, the least expected feature of the script is the decision to kill the Han Solo character at the end of the movie. Killing off a major positive character does take some guts, but really I would have preferred that they did away with a less entertaining and much more badly acted character, like Luke or Leia. (It looks like we are stuck with both of them for now).

And when will Star Wars actually deliver actual star wars? I mean huge opposing space fleets duking it out in some gigantic space battle? And maybe some new and original cool villain? (The last cool villain the franchise saw was Darth Maul in the "Phantom Menace", but he was taken from us all too quickly). Why do they keep rehashing old and tired plot lines and old and tires characters??

Arghhh!

title: Critical Failure

Hunting for droids in the desert just like the beginning of the episode 4. The x-wings barreling down the ravine like the first death star. Han and Chewie setting charges to lower the shield like the moon of endor. Black leader breaching the structure and flying around inside blowing up the interior like the 2nd death star. Walking into the strange bar just like Mos Eisley. /facepalm

Not to mention the entire movie is built on coincidences. Oh look, the first order shows up right when you are handed the map. Oh look, your droid just happens to pass by Rey. Oh look, the millennium falcon just happens to be sitting there. Oh look, Han and Chewie just happen to be there to find you. Oh look, Luke's lightsaber happens to be right there for you to find. Oh look, you learn how to use the force in 20 seconds flat and escape. How handy, Kylo just happens to be there. What a coincidence, Kylo doesn't remember that he is a dark Jedi and can simply burst Finn's organs with a single word. It just never ends.

It just makes my head hurt like you can't imagine. All they did was flip-flop content from the original star wars around. It isn't an orphaned boy named Luke, now it's an orphan girl named Rey. The desert planet is no longer tatooine, it is now Jakku. The droid sidekick isn't R2-D2, it is BB-8. Instead of fighting for the rebellion, now it is the resistance. It isn't Darth Vader killing the mentor Obi-Wan, now Kylo Ren killed Han. It just keeps going and going, the train wreck only gets worse the longer you watch.

title: Sacrifices the story for a bigger audience
review:
I'm not usually this critical about films but in recent years movies have had a tendency to pander to all audiences, and usually at the expense of the quality of the film. I'm not sure if this was meant to empower certain demographics, or if this was just a money grab (i.e. broader target audience), but the end result was predictable, unbelievable and almost laughable. All I saw throughout the movie was this "hidden agenda" in an otherwise simple and recycled plot.

Rey was a shallow character and was somehow proficient at everything despite being raised alone in poverty. Throughout the entire movie she was completely independent and not once was she ever in any real danger. NOTE: If the protagonist is always safe it's not much of an adventure/thriller. Rather than being drawn to the edge of my seat I just sat there raising an eyebrow.

Everybody knows women are just as capable as men (and those that don't are frankly not worth your time) but this sort of portrayal is just ridiculous. Rey was like an amalgam of Hans Solo, Leia and Skywalker but better than all three combined! Also, if you're going to empower women don't do it by putting men down (i.e. Fin, the male counterpart to Rey), was a coward whose few attempts to act gentlemanly or heroic were met with scornful remarks (i.e. I don't need you to hold my hand to run) or were entirely unnecessary (i.e. he flew halfway across the galaxy to rescue someone that escaped on her own because god forbid Rey get help from a man). Remember, Luke, Hans and Leia all needed rescuing at some point.

What made Indiana Jones such an amazing/believable character was because he often got beaten senseless and it was only thanks to his loyal companions that he got the edge he needed to survive. A strong character is one who is able to face his/her own faults and limitations, it's hard to do that when you're already perfect.

If you're looking for a fun flick for your kids then in that regard it delivers quite well.

title: Very boring and uninspired film
review:
This is an extremely boring and uninspired film. The boredom comes from the plot and also from the pacing which is completely off: This is a 2+ hours film, and the film seems very slow, and full of scenes which are not very original and clichés (IE: "Stormtroopers attacking village full of innocent people").

The plot itself is extremely bland and a recycled version of all past SW films. There is not a shred of originality or novelty in it.

The film feels like it was crafted to make dollars from the average movie-goer. Not that Starwars was ever a revolutionary franchise...In fact as a SW film I give it a 8/10, but as a original science fiction film it cannot go above 4/10 (which is generous), when we have seen what the likes of Christopher Nolan can produce.

> Weak unoriginal plot, with no risk taken to make dollars. > Intended for the nostalgic and/or low IQ film viewer. > Lots of beautiful shots, special effects, explosions/action, again intended to hide what is in effect a very weak film.

Again, of course, I did not expect StarWars to go in any different direction. To desire this and expect a mature or original Starwars film would be too much. So I do not blame JJ Abrams, who had lots of stress on his shoulders to say the least.

Yet I just felt so bored watching this film. The worst part I think being the script and characters being replicas of other characters in the series, with the inevitable "Good side" and "Bad side", the darth Vader character, the naive force sensitive character, the "Daring pilot", the "evil nazi Fascist Empire", you name it, they could not have been more unoriginal.

I feel that there was so much potential to do something new, if that was directed by a more intelligent (and daring) filmmaker, that it makes me angry. But then again, I understand, the average low IQ nostalgic film go-er would be angry and it would not work.

Here is where I would have gone with this film: - First Order are anti-hero in film. Since Empire was pretty much crushed beforehand, they should have been the resistance, with overwhelming Republic forces, not the new powerful force. - Resistance is new Empire. The flaws of the Republic (explored in the prequels) are shown. That doesn't mean that the Republic are the bad guys, just that they are the good but flawed guys. - Less quick succession of scenes/planets/etc. More focus on high quality dialogue and characters in individual scenes.

Finally there is one big problem with the entire script, being that almost the entirety of the film is a succession of deus ex machinas (random plot devices) to make the plot move forward, rather than logical successions of well thought out plot points: AGAIN, no low IQ SW film fan will notice this, but the more mature audience will (I have, it was awful).

So in conclusion all I can say about Force Awakens is: ITS A STARWARS FILM, plain as vanilla or chocolate icecream, or macdonalds hamburger, without any added flavour or sauce. Designed to make money on a long franchise, which many think should have died long ago.

ONE POSITIVE COUPLE OF NOTES: 1. The actors were excellent. Shout out to all of them. They were very very very great. Despite working with that awful script.

2. The other SW anthology films which will come out, seem much more daring and promising than this. I just have that feeling that everything could be salvaged by these films, lets pray and see!!!

title: Underwhelming

Main review: Similar to others, I was happy to hear that Abrams would be directing this sequel but I should've known better. Also, just like others, I became a fan of Abrams with Lost and Cloverfield. However, as time has gone by, I'm now of the opinion that he doesn't actually do anything special with any of the movies that he directs. And this is just the latest example.

I mean, how can you not get Star Wars right? The immensity of the lore gives you endless possibilities to work with. Unfortunately, it feels as if he just wanted to play it safe by using the same old formula and just not willing (Or able?) to think up anything original. Iconic characters from the original Trilogy just seemed so out of place in this movie. It's almost like he didn't have a clue as to what to do with them. Don't get me wrong, some of the scenery and effects in this movie were good to see. Kylo was okay and some of the sequences were good to watch but it just didn't save the movie. If you removed the Star Wars name and all lightsabers, this probably would've been seen as a terrible movie and be going at 2/10 on IMDb but, because it's Star Wars, it's rated highly. There was just something that.. I'm not sure what it was but something was missing. I still can't put my finger on it. The plot started off okay but seemed all over the place as the movie progressed. Okay, a planet got blown up - So what? I couldn't care less. Snoke? Don't care. Kylo? Apart from some stuff he did, who cares? The First Order? Don't care. Why even have Phasma there if you can't make her seem cool or do anything useful? To be honest, I had a hard time caring even when Han, Leia or even Luke made an appearance. Barely anything made me care about any of the characters, even the original ones - And I LOVED the Originals and Prequels. The whole thing seemed bland, dull and boring for the most part. And Abrams, in my view, is to blame. I have no idea why this is 8.4/10 on IMDb as I type this.

And that's excluding all the problems with the plot, some of which are below: - A planet-sized "Starkiller" was made within 30 years? Using what resources? How? Where did they get the people from given the size of the First Order? - Finn just happened to walk in the right direction in the desert and meet Rey? Er, okay. - Oh, how convenient that the Millennium Falcon was there to help them escape. - Oh, Poe died? Hmm. Oh wait, now he's not? Oh.. okay? - How convenient that Rey seems to fly the Falcon so well and take out the bad guys. - How convenient that Han finds their ship at the perfect time. - How convenient that Han has gone back to who he used to be and Leia is in a similar position as in the original movies (omg look! she is a born rebel!! omg). - How convenient that they find Luke's lightsaber. - Rebels save the day at the perfect time! - Let's blow up a planet that we don't care about to show how powerful this new weapon is. Oh, you were targeting the Senate.. Er, okay? Who cares? - How convenient that Finn et al sneak into the enemy camp ("Starkiller") and walk around without being caught. You'd think something of that size would have millions of troops. - Yes Rey, escape but not do the obvious and wear a Stormtrooper uniform to blend in. - Oh look, Rey can now climb walls and knows what button to press to go wherever she wants because.. Well, who cares. - Oh look, let's kill Han for shock value in one of the lamest ways possible. - Let's also shoot random stuff to blow up the Starkiller as Poe did. Because shooting at random stuff always works if you don't know what you're doing. Rest assured, as always, it's all good because the good guys will get away because that's how below average movies work.

Please.

All that I thought at the end of the movie was that Disney made a mistake by not allowing Lucas to work in some major capacity on the sequels. At least the prequels, even with problems, were good to watch. TFA wasn't good to watch but actually boring in various places.

I'm hoping Rian Johnson learns and improves on the below-average plot for Episode VII as he directs Episode VIII otherwise, if I were Disney, I'd seriously start reassessing how to proceed forward with the franchise.

review: The amount of poor dialogue makes the first half of the movie seem dull and poorly done. The movie seems to be a rip-off of A New Hope, the old heroes (in this case Han Solo, Chewbacca, Leia and Luke) must aid a new band of heroes in defeating a planet destroying system. Similarly to A New Hope, one of the old heroes must die to give the new heroes the strength to carry on. Finn's character is one of the worst I have seen developed in a very long time, and the actor rivals Anakin's poor actor from The Phantom Menace. Rey manages to unleash the power of the force while having NO prior training or knowledge. Kylo's character has NO facial recognition to Han Solo or Leia (the actor is very talented, however). Poe's character is unique, but they choose him to take Han's sarcastic and arrogant traits too early on in the movie and detract from the serious tone. title: Back to 1977
review:
After all those years, you learn that star wars will be back in 2015, you wait for one more year and guess what? you are back in 1977 instead of 2015!

Solo Han, Leia, Luke are all in the same place after 38 years. No, not played by young actors/actress but old folks. 65 year old grandma-looking princess and solo han with same mad attitude, portrayed as grumpy couple. And a meek Luke Skywalker, as if he has spent those 38 years watching his old movies. So living characters are easily copied in the new movie and what about the dead ones? gollum-faced Snoke replaces the emperor and Kylo Ren replaces Darth Vader. Yet both Snoke and Kylo do not have power to impress the audience. One might say Snoke's voice is striking, which is true but it is true for Kylo Ren only when his mask is on. This is another question that why Kylo wears this mask. Darth Vader needed it but what about Kylo, if he could easily put it off? Actually audience would have preferred him to keep it on his face because a teenager instead of a villain appeared under it. R2D2 is also put to second place after another smart ass droid BB. Producers are so obsessed with the idea that fans are rushing to theaters to see old fellows i.e: Luke, Leia, Solo. Old Luke is turning around in the final scene of the movie as if billions of fans were waiting for it. It is obvious that producers could not dare to put something new in order to avoid criticisms. This is why, not only characters but also what happens is so similar to episode IV-V-VI. Kylo Ren is son of Solo Han (remember Luke-Anakin), villain is trained by a scary master, dark side constructs another structure like Death Star to destroy the republic. Enough for the resemblance with Episode IV. And what about the movie itself? Visual effects are way too realistic compared to the scenes in Episode I-II-III. Also fight scenes are more unpretentious so we didn't see exaggerated light saber scenes similar to which 80 year old Christopher Lee jumps and flips all around. ships, stormtroopers are looking more real.

To conclude, Force Awakens made me feel like i am enough with Star Wars series. Producers may claim that this movie is a huge hit with more than 700 mio USD revenues only in US so far. However they should keep in mind that one may understand how much this movie sucks only after he sees it. so we'd better see the score after 2nd movie.

title: Disney took no risks and got no soul
review:
I'm greatly disappointed with Star Wars 7. OK, they wanted the movie to pay tribute to the earlier ones, but there isn't a single new idea in the whole movie.

It starts with the rebels yet again fighting a superior force , the "first order". OK, it took three movies to dethrone the emperor and now we are back at the same point.

After ten minutes , it was impossible to ignore the similarities. Take a look at the parallels:

There is one good old guy who sacrifices himself: Obi Wan Kenobi at Stars Wars IV and Han Solo at this one.

There is the Emperor who corrupts Darth Vader in the series , and Snoke (?) who corrupts Han's son at this one.

There is the ultimate weapon that is destroyed in the very last moment: death star and this new "solar" weapon.

And the list goes on and on. I could define Star Wars 7 as a "pout pourri" of the precedent movies with Disney's usual and great standards, but that's just it and nothing more.

In short, Disney paid U$ 4 billion for Star Wars rights and want their money back, so they decided to take no risks, and the result was a movie which is enjoyable, average, forgettable and with no soul at all.

title: The Force is Mediocre with this one
review:
The Force Awakens... I didn't hate it, but I certainly didn't love it either. It nails a few key elements that make action movies enjoyable, but it has a long list of failings to go with it (see my list of pros and cons below.) I found myself thoroughly enjoying the first 45 minutes only to feel my enthusiasm steadily drop for the next hour and a half as it became clear how paint-by-numbers this movie was turning out.

Its biggest problem is that it's instantly the most derivative Star Wars film ever made. The events are almost entirely a retread of things that happened in the original trilogy (OT) and it adds little of interest to the Star Wars mythos. It's the cinematic equivalent of a highly caffeinated soda: tastes good going down and gives you a nice energetic zing, but ultimately it's empty calories and will be harmful to the body in the long run.

Pros

1. Most of the new characters are likable, especially BB8 who is a genuinely endearing droid with lots of personality.

2. The action scenes looked and played out well on a technical level. (Hooray for competence!)

3. It successfully recreates the inherently dangerous but intriguingly exotic feel of the Star Wars universe from the OT.

4. Mostly well paced. (Hooray for competence part 2!)

5. Humor was hit and miss, but when it did hit (mostly BB8) it was good.

Cons

1. Poe / Rey / Finn bond WAY too quickly, almost to the point of incredulity.

2. It re-enacts too many scenes / scenarios from A New Hope (Storm Trooper slaughter on a desert planet, Cantina 2.0, Death Star 3.0 blows up planets, X-wing full scale attack followed by trench run attack, etc.)

3. With a couple beautiful exceptions (Jakku, night time light saber battle in the forest) the film's sets and locales really did not look that good.

4. No details about why "The First Order" or "The Resistance" emerged from the old Empire and Republic / Rebellion or how these new incarnations are even different from the original ones.

5. OT characters feel like cheap nostalgia distractions, because they are.

6. Kylo Ren becomes too vulnerable way too quickly, removing all sense of mystery and menace about the character before the first movie is even over.

7. The title of the movie is bull crap: The force does not "awaken" in any general sense. The force may have awakened in ONE character, but it was already awake in other characters, so this is clearly not what the title implied.

8. Rey's "awakening" is completely vague to the point of stuff just happening because the plot wants it to happen.

9. An untrained force initiate defeating a trained Sith is ludicrous to the point of breaking my suspension of disbelief. That was a cheap, unearned victory. Luke Skywalker, by contrast, spent three films learning, training and being battered down by the forces of darkness before emerging victorious in Return of the Jedi.

10. Highly derivative: What substance did this movie add to the Star Wars universe? For all the criticism the prequels get, at least a lot of new things were tried and an entirely different dynamic (the slow rise of evil instead of the hero's journey to fight evil) was presented to us. This movie showed almost no creative courage.

The Force Awakens will not age well, even in the short term. As the release hype dies and people who engage in thoughtful movie analysis realize how much of the movie was carbon copied, reviews will moderate and scores will drop. Given how much longer my list of cons is than my list of pros, I'm giving The Force Awakens a generous 5/10. It seems "the force" of nostalgia holds some sway over me as well. JJ Abrams and Disney benefit more from that nostalgia than they do from anything they've contributed to the franchise.

title: The bad taste in my mouth only got worse.
review:
This may contain spoilers.

A lot of things in life still amaze me, the most recent of which is the number of people giving positive or "10/10" reviews to Star Wars Episode VII. The only force that awakened in December 2015 was that of the dishonest critic and Disney's ability to manipulate audiences into making money. I left this movie with an unsettled feeling, similar to that which I had after leaving Star Wars Episode I. I was supposed to feel good - I wanted to feel good. But I didn't. The bad taste that I had in my mouth only got worse over the following weeks as I realized why. This movie was story telling at its worst, not to mention a complete rip-off of Episode IV.

Many YouTubers have rightly pointed out the obvious similarities between Episodes IV and VII. I won't belabor those points. But I will comment on the poor story telling.

For starters, everything seemed very rushed. This left the audience with dozens of unanswered questions and needing to accept absurd realities. It's probably better to list them as they come to mind than drone on in paragraph form:

1. The entire movie is catapulted forward by a lone storm trooper deciding that killing innocent people wasn't the right thing to do. They mention, almost in passing, that the new storm troopers were stolen from childhood rather than from a clone army. So how does Finn know right from wrong? At the very least they could have done some kind of flash-back, had dialogue or 5 minutes of additional screen time detailing why he felt so conflicted and decided to break from the mold.

2. There was far too much use of comedy - even Harrison Ford couldn't pull it off. The initial trilogy and even the prequels had an air of seriousness about it - the stakes were legitimate, lives were on the line, etc. This movie just had a degree of playfulness that seemed to break from the past movies and that which seemed appropriate.

3. Kylo Ren's character is made weaker and weaker throughout the film. It starts by the captured pilot talking trash to him (again, poor use of comedy) rather than being in fear. It continues as he rages out like a petulant child on numerous occasions. This is followed by his removal of his mask and near tearful state as he discloses his intentions to Rey. This, of course, is followed by him not being able to break Rey (more on this later), getting partially schooled by a light saber-wielding novice in Finn and then getting definitely schooled by a seemingly force-competent Rey. He's just a weak character. Not one to be feared in any capacity.

4. Rey has skills that seem to come out of nowhere. We have to assume she's someone who has innate skills and is force sensitive. But in her flashback we hear a voice that says something to the effect that "this is the start of your training" - to which she flees into the woods in tears. This is followed by a scene where she a) defies Kylo Ren (a trained Jedi/Sith/whatever) by not letting him into her mind and b) uses a Jedi mind trick twice to enable her escape. Then to top things off she overpowers Kylo Ren's use of the force to grab the light saber from the snow and best Kylo Ren in battle. This sudden ascendancy to greatness and Jedi-ism was perhaps the worst element of the entire movie. Zero development. It made no sense.

5. The entire plan and assault on the new Death Star is ridiculously rushed. Perhaps the worst moment in this series of events is where Han flippantly states "it's just bigger - it must have a weakness somewhere". Within 1 minute, Finn (who we now come to discover is a janitor, only making his besting of Kylo Ren even more implausible) tells them the weakness, a plan is hatched and everyone is off in space. Just seemed so rushed, not to mention a tired remake of the original Episode IV.

6. What the heck is C3PO doing with a red arm? This is just a stupid unanswered question.

7. R2D2 is in possession of this map the entire time and is sitting idol because Luke is not around. And yet we can't find Luke without R2D2's element of the map. So in theory we should never find Luke because R2D2 should never wake up. And why does an elderly man on Jakku have the additional piece of the map? And why does R2D2 come to life magically? I'm sure this will be explained in the next movie, but to leave so many holes and unanswered questions is just poor story telling.

8. Why did the Tie Fighter get sucked into the sand and explode in front of Finn? Zero explanation.

9. So you power the Death Star III by destroying a nearby sun? So you basically kill the entire solar system automatically. Why shoot a (slow) beam of destruction at those planets?

I could go on. If by some miracle you are reading this and haven't seen it, wait until it hits Red Box and rent it with a bunch of people so you don't have to spend more than 20 cents watching it. Disney doesn't deserve more than that for reproducing and old story and doing it so poorly.

title: Soulless, Assembly-Line Movie
review:
I wanted so badly to love this movie. But now I feel like I owe George Lucas a huge apology. At least Lucas tried to do an original story in his prequels. At least he allowed his characters to evolve.

Much has already been said about the repetitive, regurgitated nature of the "story" in Episode VII. This is not a crafted narrative. It's a Frankenstein movie--a stitched-together mess of JJ's favorite moments from the original trilogy. Starting with Luke 2.0, living on Tatooine 2.0, who runs into R2D2 2.0, carrying information critical to the Rebellion 2.0, then they run into Han and Chewy 1.0, visit the Cantina 2.0, eventually do battle with Vader 2.0 and the Empire 2.0 by blowing up the Death Star 3.0. Yes, we get a more politically-correct cast with a female lead and a black secondary lead, but those changes are purely COSMETIC. That doesn't make this movie fresh when the story itself is nothing more than a warmed-over, 38-year-old carcass.

JJ said his only criteria when putting together this story was, "What delights us?" So now we know that what "delights" JJ is repetition. That what he adored about the original trilogy was THINGS and SETPIECES, not the CHARACTERS.

Hey JJ, you know what delights me? A GOOD STORY! An original story that puts the CHARACTERS first. Where the characters have identifiable motives that drive what they do. Where the characters evolve and GROW over the course of the story.

Let's start with Rey the Wondergirl who is instantly good at every single thing she tries. Nothing against Daisy Ridley. She was the best thing about this film and did a great job with what she was given, which unfortunately wasn't much. Rey's only identifiable dramatic need is to find her family again. Which never happens--or if it does (assuming she is Luke's daughter or Han and Leia's) neither she, nor the audience ever finds out by the end of the movie. Because, you know, mystery box.

Without the family motive, which never gets resolved, Rey is nothing more than a tumbleweed floating through the events of this movie. For all her supposed girl-power, Rey spends the entire movie REACTING to events, tagging along, running from danger, all motion with no purpose. The moment when the force finally awakens within her rings completely hollow, because Rey never wanted it and has done absolutely nothing to EARN her sudden status as an insta-Jedi.

A film like this is only as good as its villain. Kylo, aka Ben Solo, has no character arc because the film never even hints at WHY he turned against his family. According to the novelization of the film (and it's pathetic that I need the novelization to tell me anything about the motivation of the film's main villain) the explanation is that Snoke has been watching over Ben since he was a baby and basically took him over from birth, while Han, Leia, and Luke all stood by. FEEBLE!!! This reduces Ben Solo to nothing more than a helpless puppet, and makes Luke, Han, and Leia into passive weaklings.

Which brings me to the heroes of the original trilogy, the characters that I (and so many millions of others) have loved for over 30 years. Han and Leia may look their age, but they are WRITTEN like they've been preserved in amber since 1977, with every bit of character growth from ESB and ROTJ wiped out like it never happened. Leia is still the exact same woman she was at the start of ESB, so wrapped up in the Rebellion/Resistance that she is incapable of maintaining a close relationship. But hey, Leia is a "general" now so I guess we're supposed to be so impressed with her new title that we don't care she failed as a wife and as a parent.

Han Solo fares even worse, as JJ and Kasdan are determined to shove Han in the wayback machine and fashion him back into the exact same rogue he was at the very beginning of the first movie. Again, all of Han's character growth in ESB and ROTJ vanishes in a puff of smoke. He is a failure as a husband and as a father; worse, Han ran out on his family like a coward when the going got rough. All because JJ and Kasdan fell in love with the early version of Han and god forbid they should let him grow or evolve.

Luke fares better, if only because he is barely in the movie at all. But we discover that Luke, too, ran out on his family and friends when the going got tough. And then inexplicably (and rather cruelly) he left behind pieces of a map so that his family and friends would have to risk their lives if they ever wanted to find him again.

As for the death of Han Solo, I was OK with the idea of him dying, but the WAY they killed him was lame. I thought Han would at least get a hero's death, sacrificing himself for someone he loved. Ha! Han's death on that catwalk served no dramatic purpose other than shock value, then Han gets mourned for about 10 seconds before he is forgotten for good, with no memorial whatsoever.

Why even bother bringing back the classic characters at all if you are going to treat them like this? Oh yeah: $$$$$.

If JJ and Kasdan had spent even half the time crafting a good original story as they spent lovingly re-creating moments from the original trilogy, THAT would have been a proper homage to Star Wars. This rehash won't stand the test of time. It may be raking in the great reviews and big bucks now (so did the prequels) but this movie is not going to age well. Years from now, it will be remembered as the lazy, cynical cash-grab that it is.

title: It all started here
review:
Think of all the directions they could have taken this film in, all the possibilities, and what did they do? Reset all timelines and wiped the achievements of the previous 6 films.

6 ended with the rebels celebrating the end of the empire and death star. So why on earth is 7 opening with the rebels being chased by an empire with a death star?

It's just shockingly unforgivable levels of amateurism, they didn't even bother attempting to come up with a narrative so rehashed everything. Were there writers for this film? What were they paid for? 98% of the film doesn't carry an ounce of creativity.

For some bizarre reason people tend to defend this film as a "safe entry" to rebuild the franchise for a new generation, for them to take it in new directions afterwards. What? This is episode 7 of a 9-length narrative for goodness sake.. You can't have episodes 4 and 7 telling the same story. The only remotely interesting aspect of the film is the mystery surrounding the search for Luke.

There was no excuse for TFA, they chose nostalgia over creativity and paid the price for it with the following train-wrecks when TLJ was forced to desperately trying something new. I suppose it made a lot of cash mind, and that was the sole objective.

title: Awkwardly forced
review:
This film was assuredly critic proof and having seen it that was certainly an advantage that it needed.

Why would you make the "next" Star Wars film like this? After a production hiatus and a change of franchise ownership. The first installment of a sequel trilogy? Episode VII of a nine part saga?

It's as though there was no confidence on the part of the film makers and financiers that Star Wars fans would go see it........and take their families and friends.......in some instances repeatedly.

They could have written, produced and released anything. Anything that their imaginations could conceive and their film making skills convey.

So.

Why this? Is this what they wanted to make?

A one paced remake. A prolonged slow, plodding, remake apology for touching the Star Wars brand? Why did they turn apologists for their own film making?

An entire movie of apologising for casting new actors in new roles in a new era of new stories. OK. We know it's not 1977 or 1999 or any part of the 20th century.

But there was no confidence that anything that these filmmakers would produce would be accepted by fans without a two hour apology on the part of the new management.

Perhaps because Disney had bought Lucasfilm simply because it was for sale and a desirable property to investing in.

Maybe.

As I watched this fresh in the cinema I realised that this film was bad because of how boring it was. Within thirty minutes of the opening scroll I was bored and getting increasingly so.

I wondered how professional filmmakers could produce a film so one paced. So incapable of telling a story in a manner that human beings naturally respond to, like a rhythm of life, like how almost every competent story teller does it. Modulation I believe is the term. Changes of pace and tone. Changes if emphasis and urgency. Things like that diminish the capacity for boring fiction. This film has a sky high over capacity.

Because the one paced storytelling is resolutely slow paced. Like a ship sluggishly responding to the helm at very low speeds. This film has a turning circle that never quits.

In part it is slowed down by the plethora of characters. The film sadly has two casts and that is far too many characters for this level of storytelling to carry.

You can almost see scenes getting out of the way so that the next character can introduce themselves. Then that scene stands aside so that a previously ponderously introduced new or reintroduced returning character can have a 'doing' scene. Then they, and their scene, step aside for the next introduction. Which repeats the formula once again. For ages this film keeps doing this.

Unfortunately I found the acting to be as awkward as the written filmplay must have read. New actors were awkward. Returning actors were awkward. Awkward individually. Awkward in concert. Generational difference doesn't have to produce an effect like this....an effect similar to one you may experience bumping into an old friend that you no longer have anything in common with. Or an ex partner.....

Harrison Ford seems as bored as I was watching his performance. I've since seen 'Solo: A Star Wars story' and I still think that this is the single worst performance of the role of Han Solo that I've ever witnessed.

Carrie Fisher and Harrison Ford's returning characters take the awkwardness analogy of exes too literally. Why and who even wrote that? And with them both being pretty severe victims of 'Hollywood face syndrome' I couldn't decide if they were too bored to emote or just too numbed.

I thought that the sound design was poor for a Star Wars film, not least the iconic lightsaber duel sound effect, which was ruined by the debatable decision to give the chief goon Kylo Ten a 'lightbroadsword' which had an unattractive sound effect best put down as a simple "bad creative decision".

Finally I suppose the believability of the drama was utterly lacking. After all these characters are introduced, given their own scene, moved around the galaxy in twos and threes, there's no build up of credibility in any one of them. No credibility means no involvement. No involvement means no suspension of disbelief. And that means no drama. No thrills. No suspense. No climax. No release.

It means boring.

This is compounded by the choice of premise for our dangerous motivating driver; the thing prodding our protagonist to protagonise: 'The First Order' and it's "armed forces".

Hhhmmmmmmmm. Boringly derivative nonsense that degrades the original trilogy not so much by underplaying the extent of the goodies win in that contest but denying the new generation a truly distinctive baddie of their own to best. It isn't the original generation of character heros being short changed........its the new ones who are expecting to carry on the thrilling action adventures in space!!!

What a way to start. With a total lack of confidence and conviction. A total disdain for the filmmakers own competency.

That's my reasoning to explain why this is so boring that it's just finally, frankly, really bad.

title: Predictable and unoriginal but isn't that exactly what the fans wanted?

I won't call 'Force' a bad movie, it isn't, but it stumbles and most of all it feels like a predictable fan-service production. 5 out of 10.

title: Suspension of disbelief vanishes under the weight of too many flaws
review:
--Too Many Coincidences--

Poe's contact for the map to Luke just happens to be on the planet where the Millennium Falcon was last sold AND where one of Luke's apprentices is in hiding AND where Han and Chewie just happen to be hanging out in orbit? On the whole sparsely populated planet, BB-8 just happens to bump into Luke's old apprentice? Finn bumps into her, too?

Han takes the heroes from Jakku to a backwater bar in the Outer Rim to hide, but that bar just happens to have spies from the rebels AND the New Order just sitting around waiting for the droid AND Luke's lightsabre just happens to be in the basement?

The New Order conveniently arrives 30s after the heroes land anywhere? Poe gets five lines on Jakku before the drop ships arrive. Han and the heroes barely get time for a drink at his so-called "hidden bar" before the New Order starts blowing the place up. How convenient that they always seem to be right where the heroes are, just after they arrive.

--Too Many Non-Sequitors--

Finn is separated from his family as an infant, put under harsh conditioning, given a designation and not a name ... to be made a sanitation worker?

New Order conditioning is so strong it gets defended vs. clones by Finn's commander, but Finn doesn't even show signs of any conditioning at all? Finn's commander says Finn has never been an issue before ... but this is first mission?

The Millennium Falcon hasn't flown in decades and is owned by a guy who clearly sells parts for a living but he doesn't take a single part off this ageing freighter, and the heroes can get in and start her up without an issue?

The New Order spends trillions of credits on a ridiculous super weapon that drains the sole source of light, heat, and gravity in the system? Don't get me started on the "beams across the galaxy" BS, or that two shots drain the star. How many trillion credit super weapons have to go up in flames before the baddies figure out this is a colossal waste of resources?

Rey stops in the middle of a duel on the edge of a precipice, closes her eyes, and spends 30s meditating on the force, and the baddie in front of her, who has just killed his own father, doesn't just force push her into the crevasse and walk away?

R2-D2 just sits in stasis waiting ... for what?

--Hello, Mary Sue, Good Bye Brain--

Rey is a Mary Sue, or a character that's too perfect.

She's a scavenger for parts, bartering parts for food and living in a lean-to in the desert, spending the overwhelming bulk of her days alone.

Despite this, she speaks multiple languages fluently, including both the languages she needs to understand Chewie and BB-8, despite no visible experience with either Wookies or Droids. She's a master of hand to hand combat, able to defeat multiple foes with a stick. Somehow, living alone out in the desert with no money or friends, she's figured out how to pilot a starship, and hops in the Millennium Falcon and takes a 50 year old ship she's never flown in before directly into combat manoeuvres. She only needs to experience the force one time before she starts using force powers herself, including ones she's never seen demonstrated at all (but which have been used in other movies, natch). The first time she picks up a lightsabre, she out duels a Knight of Ren who is so high in the New Order hierarchy that he speaks directly to Snokes and hangs around with generals.

JJ Abrams was clearly desperate for a girl power heroine, to the point where he used the schlocky, "Why are you holding my hand?" lines to specifically point it out. Blech.

--Odds and Ends--

The pacing is too quick and comes at the expense of the characters and story. Kylo Ren is a pretty non-scary antagonist. The dialogue around Han Solo's death was laughably bad. JJ Abrams uses deus ex machina events/characters too often.

title: They Didn't Even Try to be Original !!!
review:
Never have I been compelled to write a review for a movie before. It might deserve slightly more than 1/10 but that 8.6 average is a gross misrepresentation of the movie and an offense to the rest of the saga.

I came in with low expectations. I knew they would try to copy some elements from the original films. But I never expected them to simply copy them exactly. The minute I saw stormtroopers and a masked Sith Lord, I was kind of disappointed. I thought Darth Vader 2.0 would be the worst I would have to see. No, we also have R2D2 2.0, Darth Sidious 2.0, young Luke Skywalker 2.0 and Death Star 3.0.

The scene where Poe compares the new Death Star's size to the old one is the most horrible scene of the movie. That along with Han Solo's line "How do we blow it up? There's always a way to do that." felt like a spit in the faces of all loyal star wars fans. It was like JJ Abrams saying "We know we're bringing absolutely nothing to the table but we also know that you'll give us your money just for holding the Star Wars banner."

The one good element of the movie was the darkness of the few opening sequences. Kylo Ren seemed to be able to do things no other Sith was able to do before like stopping bullets and breaking into people's minds. However, this darkness abates more and more as the movie goes on. When the droid isn't caught, we're expecting Kylo Ren to take out his anger on the officer. Instead, he just pathetically destroys his own computers. The clip of the Death Star destroying five planets simultaneously is amazing however it's very quickly forgotten. Apart from Coruscant, we know nothing about the destroyed planets, and even less about the characters that died along with them.

The lightsaber battle was simply disgraceful. Even Anakin, who was supposed to be the Chosen One got destroyed by the first Sith Lord he faced (Count Dooku) and this was after many years of training as Obi- Wan's apprentice. Yet Rey manages beat an apparently very powerful (although unhinged) Sith first time she uses a lightsaber. When she says "Ah yes, the force" and closes her eyes right before she beats him, the cringe is too much to bear.

Of course there is an enormous amount of plot holes, and the more you think about the movie, the more you notice. No need for me to list them. To sum up, The Force Awakens was just a way to milk the nostalgia people have for the original star wars. DON'T WATCH THIS DISGUSTING GARBAGE!!!!

title: Fails to capture the imagination like the originals
review:
In a world where there are nuances and parodies of Star Wars everywhere from Spaceballs to Family Guy I would never have thought the franchise itself would fall victim to this trend. The similarities with A New Hope are endless but that's not what I'm going to write about. Star Wars always has an honest story to tell. This was more fan fiction than film yet even fan fiction can still be great. Some people don't understand that there's more to Star Wars than lightsabers and spaceships. The originals was a story about a revolution in a pirate themed sci-fi world with heavy Taoist philosophy and samurai. The prequels were sort of a cold war/medieval war blend, freedom vs fascism, and the originals being good vs evil. This film's themes were just so bland! I love a fun movie but in the end, it's completely worthless without proper context.

How you react to this movie depends on your need for instant gratification. If you like big-effects action to happen fast and keep happening, you'll love it. Unfortunately that's about the only thing that JJ Abrams has managed to do well. Everything else-and I do mean everything else has been botched. Frankly it's offensive to have an imaginative Universe and a work of art be re-manufactured into a Disney cash-cow. This is now a franchise trapped in its own fossilized iconography.

It's strange that there was nothing I can call original or a motif but only things that were rehashes. The film fails to have an identity of it's own. It isn't genuine or adventurous enough to be considered Star Wars. Many people have a positive attitude to the notion of Star Wars being a massive Universe with limitless possibilities. When I watch a Star Wars movie I always say to myself ''wow what an engaging story'' and if you summarize the plot into one sentence it would give me chills reading it. Sadly the newest instalment offers nothing interesting, nothing that captures the imagination. There's no context and Star Wars is often about context. There's no investment hence there is no pay-off, there's no stakes hence there is nothing to give a **** about.

A lot of people have complained that Rey is too powerful to invest in and they're right. She is essentially a super-hero. The film leaves behind the old concepts of fellowship since the lead can handle everything on her own. She doesn't depend on any other character for help and she doesn't accept guidance. All the characters actions just take place in a vacuum. Whereas Luke learns to become a hero, her story boils down to ''great power comes great responsibility.'' Not sure I buy into a super-hero in the Star Wars Universe.

Kylo Ren was a good villain with a brilliant performance by Adam Driver. He's extremely underdeveloped and is only left to a few short sentences of back story. I wish it was more clear how and why he became so evil. He had no turning point, he had no pain or fear in his backstory yet he was somehow seduced to the dark side.

I couldn't buy into Finn's character, he seemed like a guy who just walked into the film, though he was entertaining. Of the thousands of Stormtroopers, suddenly one of them happens to become morally conscious without introduction and has a story ''worth'' telling. Everything just takes place in a vacuum.

Han Solo is an archetype. He's a cowboy and archetypal characters deserve a fitting end. Why does his father-son relationship become the biggest plot point leading up to the events of the film? Yet there is barely any development or build up.

The film makes me question the genuinity of it's male and female characters. We have an instantly capable and completely independent female lead followed by a myriad of male losers, even Luke Skywalker.

Star Wars should have the most sophisticated techniques for maintaining continuity, and frankly it barely keeps the film together with its subtle tricks and the hidden clues. Part of it takes away meaning from the originals. 1-6 builds up a prophecy of bringing balance to the force and finally we have a film called Return of the Jedi. Luke is so hyped up by being a summation of all the greatest Jedi teachings and life lessons he learnt along the way. His effort to bring a new generation fails dramatically despite his wisdom and persistence that was developed in the original trilogy. Even after balance was restored everything became much worse shortly after with a more evil empire and a more powerful death star.

I thought the mid scene cut at the end was more of a slap to the face than a cliffhanger. The search for Luke story arc would've been the only thing worth investing in but there was no closure. It's one thing to depend on prequels for nostalgia and it's another thing to depend on a sequel for a more complete story.

From a sci-fi aspect, Star Wars is a fresh and vivid universe and it feels bigger in each instalment with new planets, cities, and also new ideas. Again there's none of that. Nothing that captures the imagination.

Star Wars isn't shallow and it definitely is not nuance. Like I've said before, Star Wars has a soul and an honest story to tell. Star Wars is a massive Universe with limitless possibilities yet one cohesive story. Star Wars has a mythology. Star Wars has a philosophy. Star Wars has strong roots, Taoism, Japanese Samurai, Akira Kurosawa, Joseph Campbell, Stoicism, Poetry, History, Technology. Star Wars is a rich tapestry of ideas, themes, philosophies and inspirations. I'm not saying Star Wars is overly referential to historic cultures, I'm saying Star Wars is epic in the way that it tells larger than life stories through genuine inspiration and imagination.
