title: So-so at best. Feels more like a cash-grab effort
review:
I watched this movie on the day it opened on the 18th. The theater was about half full. I got there early (about 1 hour earlier) thinking I would not be able to get good seat and will have to stand in line. I was surprised to see the entire empty theater upon my arrival so I choose my most favorite location for the seat. I also watched it in 3D. Although, it suffered from the typical cardboard cutouts standing next to each other type of feel for the converted 2D to 3D movies.

Back to the movie, it felt like JJ Abrams went back to the first 3 movies and created a template that gave him the formula of what made those movies favorite for the fans. Then, he used that template to design a storyboard for this movie by inserting new characters and new events. However, the overall theme is shockingly similar. For die-hard "Star Wars" fans, this might work. For someone like me who watches movies with objectivity, it looked like a rehash of the old formula.

The leading two characters had good chemistry, I must admit. Not having Yoda in the movie was definitely a surprise as I was expecting to see him in some capacity. The comic relief in the tense scenes every 2 - 3 minutes seemed funny at first, but became tiresome and the novelty wore off quickly. Even in the most tense and climactic scenes like the final fight scene between the British girl and Darth Vader's son, it looked unintentionally funny how the little girl was suddenly so overpowering compared to someone who has spent a good part of his life "with the force" and following in his father's footsteps. Hans Solo's character seemed more like a link to the first three movies, but did not further the story much. As a matter of fact, I felt the movie was heavy on action and running, but low on story content and character development. I never got to know the background of the leading two characters (the black guy and the British girl, whatever their names are).

The locations were very nicely filmed especially the final location where the British girl goes to find Mark Hamill. All in all, the movie is forgettable. I would say, I never felt bored for the 2 hours. Definitely, I watched the action closely, but nothing really was memorable in this movie. It is definitely like "Avatar". Another movie that was big on hype and a lot of focus on style and branding than substance. Lots of fluff without much content.

title: Am I taking crazy pills? Everyone needs to wake up, and smell what Abrams is cooking... it stinks.
review: As a warning, this "review" will contain spoilers. However, I hope that whoever may read this piece will continue on so as to see this movie through a different lens, rather than the emotional one I witnessed so many viewing this movie through during my first viewing of this film. I am aware that this is an overall negative review, and that it may turn some people off who have this unwavering passion for anything that says STAR WARS on it. However, I believe it is important to point out just how unsatisfying this film is, and that it is absolutely unacceptable to not scrutinize this film appropriately. First and foremost, have we not all seen this movie already? In preparation for this film I watched, and re-watched the "original trilogy" several times due to the excitement that was building for The Force Awakens. With The Force Awakens, we see a major repeat in the major story lines, and even specific scenes. Essentially, an evil force (The First Order) is threatening peace and freedom in the galaxy which is to be combated by an opposing righteous group (The Resistance). The First Order is The Empire all over again, just as The Resistance is The Rebellion all over again nothing new here. We even have yet another Death Star, although, this one can destroy 4-5 planets at one time rather than just one. The Death Stars just seem to be getting bigger and bigger. Again, nothing new here. How can we say that we are satisfied with the same story that was told in IV and VI? Similarities to the original trilogy were rampant throughout this movie even down to how a major character dies, and is disposed of down a never ending steel shaft. Even destroying the Death Star was done in the same manner, by crippling a major power source. The similarities go on and on, and frankly are just disgusting to see rehashed. Seriously people, why can't we all see this??? The characters within this movie were just as awful as the story line. My biggest issue lies with Kylo Ren. This character is by far the most unimpressive person to wield the dark side of the force I have seen in all of the Star Wars films. What we have seen in past films through other characters who are of the dark side, is an unwavering allegiance to the powers that the dark side hold. We see characters that strike fear into our hearts, are domineering, and make us wonder how their evil can ever be conquered. With Kylo Ren, we get an unassured, weak boy who is seen on several occasions crying to the Supreme Leader about how he's just not sure about this whole dark side thing (terrible). And by the way, Han Solo dies at the hands of this fool HAN SOLO. It would be more fitting for the BEST character in the Star Wars universe to go down in a blaze of glory in the heat of battle, rather he dies at the hands of his weak and unimpressive son. Rae and Fin are terrible as well. First, Rae, a scrapper who is found on yet another desert planet peaks at the end of this film with a light saber battle between her and Ren. Mind you, Rae was a scrapper an hour and a half prior to this light saber battle. She is a person who just discovered that she has the powers of the force, and at the end of the film goes toe-to-toe with Kylo Ren, a character who has had at least five more days of training than she at wielding the force. I'm not sure if this speaks to how weak and unimpressive Kylo Ren is, or how Abrams and the rest just needed to put a light saber battle in the end and essentially just said: "Rae discovered the force so she's got this, no training required." Even Luke Skywalker had some sort of visible training, but apparently Rae could do just fine without. Fin was just as terrible, more so in the acting than anything else. He also fought Kylo Ren in a light saber battle, and did pretty well again this is a testament to how awful the characters/ story is developed. As I am running out of words, I need to rap this rant/ review/ opinion up. Many others who were not impressed with this movie touched on a lot of the same issues I have, as well as many more. I suggest going to read those reviews as well. The last topic I want to touch on was the one piece of hope that I was given during this movie. This film could have been an absolute monster if it had taken the stance that The Empire Strikes Back did. The one time I remembered sitting up in my chair was during the speech that the First Order general was giving to the storm troopers prior to activating the "main weapon." This scene had such an eerie feeling to it, one which felt similar to Hitler's Third Reich. If the main story followed how the First Order rose from the ashes of the Empire, and became this sinister threat within the galaxy rather than just telling me via text at the beginning of the movie, I would be biting my fingernails right now waiting to see them be destroyed by the Resistance in the following movies. This movie should have broken our spirits by showing us that a new, even more sinister power in the universe controls it so that we could all cheer at the end subsequent films when the impossible becomes possible, and good prevails. Instead we just got IV and VI all over again OH! AND WHY IS CHEWY LETTING RAE DRIVE THE FALCON AFTER HAN DIES? FIRST HE LOST HIS BEST FRIEND, THEN ABRAMS WON'T EVEN LET HIM DRIVE THE FALCON HOME? POOR CHEWY.

title: YAWN (spoilers)
review:
There are many reasons to be disappointed with this pointless movie. But there are far fewer reasons to like it. I was most impressed with the expansive landscape shots of Jakku. And everybody loves the furball, as well as Carrie Fisher, who, it should be said, apparently overdosed on BoTox for the role. She somewhat resembled a mannequin in her own image, and then shows up on television to demand that we not discuss how she has aged (oh, the narcissism!).

It also deserves to be pointed out that as this film fairly accurately follows the plot track of the first movie, albeit with less finesse and suggestion of depth of thought. This is the most significant criticism of this mish-mash of beloved characters and contrived plot points: it will not stand the test of time. Is it fair to call it derivative, as Episode IV was essentially a western fairy-tale with Jedi warriors modeled on Samurai? Certainly.

But the pointless way this movie moves forward is simply odd: - When Ray ventures to the basement, called by...something?... - When planning the attack, "let's go!"... - Han Solo is killed, and we all know it is because Harrison Ford doesn't want to be in any more ridiculous films. - The denouement is a bearded Luke, standing silently. why? why can't he just die nobly like Obi Wan? This is such a pandering question mark leading into the next movie it is plainly ridiculous. - Why does everyone want to find Luke in the first place? - The idea of having two droids combine their maps to Skywalker is so contrived as to appear infantile. - Why use all these old characters anyway? Can't make a new movie with any substance?

So did Disney ask focus groups what characters, including the Millennium Falcon, they wanted in the new movie, and built a plot around them? Survey says...?!

Second to last comment: was there a single new science-"fictiony" idea in this movie? 50 points to anyone can identify one!

Last comment: Episode II was better.

title: The more water you add, the more Diluted it becomes....
review:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens. Wow. Lot's of Great effects, some pretty decent acting out of newcomer Daisy Ridley. Excellent cinematography.

If you're young (say.. under 35) and you haven't really hit the Star Wars sagas - hard, then this was probably AWESOME for you! Even if you have kept up... probably pretty cool for MOST of the younger crowd...

IF, however, you are older - and actually saw the original movies in the theater back in the 1970's - WOW. Harrison Ford - Who used to be greater or more Cool/Awesome? Handsome, with swagger, humor and great lines... in all of his parts, especially Star Wars! In this movie, he JUST LOOKS and ACTS: OLD. Very sad!

Carrie Fisher - What the heck happened to her voice? She was slurring and sounded very old in the parts of the movie that she was in. Not so great a choice even in the 70's (probably mostly because of her show business lineage), in this movie she was: Pitiful. Sadly.

Chewbacca - How do you screw that up? It's an outfit/effects deal.. This actor (Peter Mayhew) was fine. Had it down pat and hadn't aged from what I could see of the animal/alien. So this wasn't bad.

Mark Hamill - OMG. AGED and looking horrible!

So, to summarize, the film didn't need all the tie-ins and acting parts given out to Ford, Fisher, Mayhew and Hamill. The film would have been WAY BETTER to be a STAR WARS BEYOND all the others, and a stand alone. Having all the old characters AND ACTORS back screwed this film. Too bad, it could have been great.

Oh; and by the way - blowing up yet another death-star (this time: a "DEATH PLANET") - REALLY??? Can't we figure out something else to supply the main plot and objective? And bombing/destroying it in the same way as in the first movies? Really.

It was kind of a tired, re-heated leftover infused with modern effect technologies. A REAL RE-BOOT (since that seems to be all Hollywood can do these days....) would have hit hard, fast and been OUTSTANDING!!

Too bad. It was really hard to watch our heroes from the late 1970's reprise these roles, while clearly eligible for Social Security :-/

title: Worst film in the series!
review:
The latest Star Wars flick is the worst in the series.

It is a mixed bag. People are either raving about it or they're very disappointed, I'm with the latter. Me & my brother came out the cinema & both agreed it was terrible.

The original trilogy is quality, the prequel trilogy, not on par with the originals but they're still decent. There's still a decent plot with the prequels, there's depth in character, John Williams was still on top of his game doing the music score, there were bad ass Sith Lords like Darth Maul, Darth Tyranus & Darth Sidious. There was Yoda having light saber duels, Anakin Skywalker turning to the dark side.. It was sinister in places, it was Star Wars.

The latest film & the first of a new trilogy didn't grab me from the start. The acting was below average, it was predictable, I was nodding off half way through. The best thing about it was the new droid, BB-8.

I've given The Force Awakens a 4/10 because I loved little BB-8.. He made me smile & even laugh in some places.. I just wanted the droid to be safe!

Kylo Ren & The First Order were another big disappointment! When you see the film, you'll know what I mean! Darth Vader & the galactic empire were intimidating, there was something dark about them.. Kylo Ren is a no mark compared to Darth Vader.. I'm sure he'll get badder as the series goes on but we've already seen his face (no mystery there).. We know he's an emotional young man who seems to hate his dad for some reason?

I found the force awakens very predictable! I'm guessing Rey is Luke's daughter.. Also, in the next film we'll find out Rey & Kylo Ren are cousins or whatever!

I can't imagine the feeling of being at the cinema & seeing the Empire Strikes Back, I would've loved to have been a fly on the wall to see the audience gasp as Vader told Luke he's his father..

The Force Awakens is a big, big disappointment! I came out very let down to be honest.

Even the music is rubbish! In the Phantom of Menace when Qui Gon & Obi Wan are about to face Darth Maul, the music is amazing! It adds so much drama to what's about to kick off! During The Force Awakens there wasn't once I was on the edge of my seat.. I don't know if JJ Abrahams is to blame? I don't really know..

Star Wars has seemed to have done a WWE. If you grew up in the late 90's/early 00's watching WWF then you'll remember the attitude era.. The old Star Wars is like the attitude era. Episode 7 is like the PG era.. Great if you're kid.. Crap if you're an adult & seen a lot better!

I hope Episode 8 gives us something unpredictable because this film is dire!

title: I'm not exaggerating when I say this: This movie is terrible
review:
I'm just going to get right to the points that made this movie bad. In no specific order, here's what's wrong with Star Wars: The force Awakens:

1. Kylo-Ren, the main villain, is a wimp.

He seemed pretty bad*** until they ruined him by taking his mask off and revealing he was an insecure wimp (who even looked like a wimp). Obviously they wanted to get who he is out of the way before he did you know what to you know who, but it was just done so poorly. And BTW, his scene with Han Solo was WAAY too predictable.

Throughout the original trilogy, there wasn't a single time when you thought Vader wasn't a bad***. He only showed some emotion/weakness towards the end of Return of the Jedi when he's talking to captured Luke and then once he's defeated by Luke.

Also, Kylo-Ren idolizes Vader, but yet Vader turned good at the end of Return of the Jedi, and his ghost is actually around at the end of ROTJ, so he could have had direct contact with grandpa Vader. *scratches head*

Also, can I say HORRIBLE casting. That weak blank expression just doesn't do it for me, sorry.

2. Kylo-Ren can use the force to push people back or stop them from moving .... but only sometimes.

If he could actually just do that, why didn't he do it to Finn when they were fighting with sabers? Why did he allow Rey to regroup and get back to fighting him if he could just fling her across the forest again? No explanation ....

3. Captain-Phasma, another one of the main villains, is incompetent and weak.

Phasma is a storm trooper captain who oversees the invasion and slaughter of a village on Jakku at the start of the film, only she's not very villainous.

First, she fails to see the potential of Fin's insubordination, allowing him to escape. Then, she's quickly and easily captured by Han and the gang. She's then forced to lower the shields on the First Order's multi-trillion dollar new Death Star, which is their primary weapon against the resistance fighters, with LITTLE TO NO RESISTANCE.

The whole getting captured in two seconds completely zapped any potential of being a bad***/mysterious villain out of her. She should be a captain for a reason. Any real Imperial captain should be ready to die for what they're doing. The fact that she lowered the shields so quickly showed she had no real conviction for what she was doing, and her capture showed incompetence.

4. Harrison Ford just seems too old and his meeting with Fischer was awkward.

Throughout the movie, Han is involved in action scenes, but there's just this vibe that Harrison is just not up to it and he just seems too old. There's simply no vigor there. It's really noticeable and begs the question why Disney didn't buy the SW franchise in the 90's, so at least the original actors weren't pushing 80.

His meeting with Princess Leia, now General Leia, is awkward and just doesn't feel right. It could just be that they're too old, but I'd rather think that it's just BAD DIRECTING. *cough**Abraham*cough*

5. The directing is bad, and it's reflected in the bad acting.

John Boyega, Oscar Isaac, and Ford's acting were just not believable. Isaac throwing his voice to make himself sound like a tough guy is so obvious. When acting and directing is actually good, you don't really notice that actors are acting.

I feel like Harrison was simply playing himself, and they just labeled him Han Solo.

I will admit that Daisy Ridley did a great job as Rey, which indicates that if the movie had a better director she could have been an Oscar nominee.

6. A random storm trooper has a weapon that can fight/withstand a light saber.

Uh, OK? No explanation whatsoever ...

6. The Millennium Falcon's introduction was terrible, and .... it doesn't need keys ...

The way they threw the Falcon into the movie was done poorly. They couldn't have come up with something better than it just hanging out in the sand waiting for someone to hop into it and fly off in it? I don't know, but the alien dude who owned the Millennium Falcon seemed like a pretty shady character to me, which would indicate that he would be way too suspicious of others to leave the Falcon unattended, waiting to be flown off the planet by anyone who wanted to hop on board and fly away in it.

7. CGI ruins every movie, and Star Wars is no exception.

Come on, the original Star Wars had real set props and a real Millennium Falcon, could they not build another one? Dark Knight and Dark Knight Rises has spoiled me WAAAY too much. I HATED Maz Kanata because of the CGI.

8. The movie should have ended before they found Luke Skywalker.

Not showing Luke at the end would have left some mystery to the movie. They should have cut to the credits as Rey hit light speed in the Falcon. At the end of Empire Strikes Back, they don't just show Han frozen in Java's Palace.

I just feel like they had to show Luke to give him credit for actually being in the movie, but he's just some guy hanging out at the top of a mountain who looks like a confused homeless guy once they show his face. SUSPENSE ZAPPED.

-------------------------------------------

This movie was terrible from beginning to end. Any potential suspense was ruined and everything was revealed too quickly. The Falcon and Harrison's introduction were poorly thought out. The villains suck, the acting sucks, everything just sucked. I could literally keep going, huge disappointment.

title: Lacks energy and charisma of first three films, numerous plot holes, not even a good children's movie.
review:
Admittedly I've never been a huge fan of the Star Wars franchise, and when I went out to see The Force Awakens today, I kinda expected too see an overblown kid's movie wrapped in mind blowing CGI effects.

Instead, however, what I found was a film that managed to be completely predictable, even though it was riddled with plot holes to sink the Death Star! For example, if the Galactic Empire had been defeated thirty years earlier, then why did the First Order (presumably the direct successors to the Sith) still have legions of white armored storm troopers at their beckon call, and shouldn't these storm troopers have been serving the victorious Galactic Republic, instead of the evil First Order? Also, why is there still a Resistance Movement if the war ended thirty years ago, and the Republic has supposedly regained control of the Galaxy? At first I tried to dismiss the growing mountain of plot holes by telling myself to relax, and by reminding myself that The Force Awakens was just a kid's movie, but the straw that broke the camel's back came when the huge planet sized Starkiller (an upgraded Death Star) was introduced without any real explanation.

How did the First Order manage to build such a huge death machine under the collective noses of the victorious Galactic Republic, and how does the atmosphere on the surface of the Starkiller manage to stay in place, once the Starkiller moves away from its home star? (The surface of the Starkiller looks a little bit like the Sierra Nevada Mountains, with tall pine trees, and snow capped peaks in the background.) Seriously, what was the purpose in putting an Earth-like land mass across the surface of the Starkiller? It can't be meant as a form of camouflage, because the Starkiller has a huge yawning rectangular shaped chasm about the size of Indonesia spanning its equator? Anyway, C3P0 is reduced to only a minor character in the film, while R2D2 is hardly given any screen time at all, and instead a cute new robot named BB-8 is introduced just in time for Christmas. Also, too much time is spent focusing on a cootish looking Han Solo, and a disturbingly bloated raspy Princess Leia.

The long and short of it is that The Force Awakens is not a worthwhile kid's movie, it completely lacks the energy and charisma of the first three movies, and it also lacks the mind-blowing action and CGI effects found in the most recent films such as Revenge of The Sith.

title: Star Wars VII "I've Got A Bad Feeling About This"
review:
Where do I begin? Where do I begin indeed After a while you begin to notice commonalities between movies, plots, characters, themes and other nuances of the theatrical type. In a multi-movie run as long as Star Wars has been around you are bound to notice some of these similarities - most of which are minor in scope and detail. Overall though we expect originality to build our belief in the world being shown to us on the silver screen. It is this originality that we go back for, it is this newness that keeps us expecting more and it is this fresh take that make us excited about a movie that defines our generation.

SPOILERS AHEAD!

I sat in the theater by myself with other Star War Fans around me and I must admit I was really stoked to see this movie. It's been a few years since a new Star Wars movie came out and this was the first time Disney was at the helm guiding this franchise out of the harbor so to speak. What could go wrong? Disney bought Marvel and those movies were fantastic! J.J. Abrams rebooted Star Trek to great fanfare so see seems to know what he is doing. This had all the making of space opera perfection! The moment that Lucasfilm badge appeared on screen I felt my emotions well up, that music you all instantly know as the Star Wars theme song began and I leaned forward in anticipation, those words scrolled up the black space background and I was smiling ear to ear. It was actually starting! I sat back to enjoy the ride. But This movie seemed intent on destroying many of the previous conceptions of Star Wars (please keep in mind I don't' want to spoil it too much so I'll keep my review rather ambiguous). Female Stormtroopers - heck let's do a female Stormtrooper commander! Why? Because it's 2015 I guess. But let's limit her role to menacing lines and a then later as a cooperative prisoner to advance the plot. Let's throw in a black Stormtrooper as well - that will really shake things up! Except the black Stormtrooper runs away from his job a'la slave escaping it's master and is now on the run. And the main bad guy. Let's dress him in black, give him a mask for no reason and super cool funky sword that no one else has so he looks like a religious knight about to embark on a holy war. Let's make him mean! But unsure of himself and not completely trained yet - so people know he will be in training in the second movie. Let's make his current training so bad that a brand new user of the force can defeat him - in everything! I won't tell you the plot twist in all this but trust me, you'll see it coming. As much as the movie wants to destroy many of the previous conceptions of Star Wars, it also wants to hold many of the main plot points dear. A Droid holding secret plans, a droid abandoned on a planet, a droid finding friends to help it along. Let's have a Death Star, but not a Death Star, but bigger! NO! MUCH BIGGER! A wait for it A STAR KILLER! But let's not learn anything from the previous Death Stars instead let's make the same mistake of making an easily accessible guarded by laser cannons that rebel fights must fly through in a limited amount of time to the weak point that we can use as an attack point to blow it up. Just like the original Star Wars movie. How could it have been better? It's been 30 years since the end of the events in the The Return of the Jedi, new characters needed to be developed, new ships given a bigger role and a letting go of the past to the point of just allowing Han, Chewie, C-3P0 and Leia to be just background cameo characters - not the leads. Except for Mark Hamill, the movie connection could have just been Luke Skywalker and I think it would have been fine. Personally, I think the best part of the movie was the Mark Hamill reveal. Mirroring is one thing, but when you copy and paste the major plot points from one movie to the next - you're taking the fans for idiots J.J. Abrams, and trust me we are not. Finally, I predict that this "Star Wars IV A New Hope remake" will drop off the radar as many people realize just how bad it really is.

title: Mindless, unoriginal action sci-fi for the uncritical masses
review:
Imagine they make a continuation for Lord Of The Rings. We would have a dwarf named Fride, working in a mine in the beautiful mountains, who would be then visited by a shaman called Gindolf, who would tell Fride, that an evil being called Saurator has risen to destroy every good thing in the world. Fride would find a necklace in the mine recognized from Gindolf as the powerful necklace that Saurator lost once. Fride now has to go to the ice lake, defended by Saurator's hordes of goblins. The necklace has to be brought to this lake, because it would scatter this necklace to pieces by it's cold. It took me half a minute to come up with this, and 5 minutes to write it down.

I mean if they continued Lord Of The Rings like this, it would be a joke, am I right? And now to Star Wars - The Force Awakens...

When I came out of the theater after watching Disney's new Star Wars episode (without knowing anything about it beforehand, I made an effort to being able to do so), my first reaction was, that I never had a movie experience before, which involved so much deja vu. Other critical commenters already explained this, and I just can confirm: this new offering is painfully unoriginal, it's just a compressed mess of episodes 4-6. If you went to see "The Force Awakens" because you were eager and excited about, how the story would continue, what would happen next: so if you wanted a new, magical story, then you had no choice, but to be left very disappointed. Even the prequels with all their faults were light years ahead of this simplistic nostalgia mosaic. I'm also a bit sick of some of the pro arguments claiming the movie was "such an eye-candy, gorgeous, beautiful". First: it wasn't, the look was very average. Second: I don't want to have sex with the movie, that's not why I watch movies in the first place. For that I choose humans, I'm not the cybersex type. For me the biggest strength of Star Wars has always been the story and the storytelling. The storytelling is non-existent. And even what seems to be the "story" itself, is really just recycled stuff. This movie experience made me so sad. For a not Star Wars movie, I would give this a 4 out of 10, for being lightly and shallowly entertained. For a Star Wars movie it is a 1 out of 10. It would have been better, if it hadn't been made at all. We already have enough bad fan-movies of Star Wars... Even better ones!

title: Makes the prequels almost look good
review:
SPOILERS: I'm not going to bother giving a blow by blow of how bad this film is. I'll stick to the most ridiculous aspects.

1. The main character, a Luke Skywalker mish-mash named Ray (Rei, Reh, whatever) is able to learn everything that Luke learned in the first two movies in a matter of hours ON HER OWN with no help from anyone or any teacher. She is able to defeat the dark apprentice Darth Vader clone with a light-saber with NO TRAINING IN THE WEAPON while the dark apprentice has been training for at least since before the movie started. She is able to fix anything, fly anything, and defeat creatures far larger than herself in spite of having been living virtually alone on a desert planet since she was an infant. Essentially, she is Obi-wan Kinobi of the first movie, Han Solo, Luke Skywalker at the end of the second movie, and Anikan Skywalker combined (as far as her skills are concerned). This is absolutely idiotic.

2. There is nothing in this that wasn't done better in the other six movies. The music is cheesy digital rehash of the other movies' music with some entirely unnoticeable additions. The film is dark and has none of the clarity of previous films. All of the characters, and all of the plot-lines, are from the previous movies. The child-like innocence of the performances of the first movie are replaced with forced caricatures of child-like innocence. While the actors in this film may be better than Mark Hamil, they are far less convincing.

I don't feel like wasting anymore of my life with this. The movie was enough of a loss of time and money, and I felt cheated even though I paid less than 5.50 for it.

title: "I'm already on my way out." Out of the cinema....
review:
Oh come on, please...how can anybody rate this one more than five stars? So much has been said about the flaws and plot holes of this movie. I don't want to repeat it all. But I have to figure out some of my opinions because I just can't bare these 10 stars ratings made especially by professional "critics" (are these blind and deaf?) anymore.

I would describe myself as a Star Wars fan. I'm not a hardcore one, but I watched the six movies more than once, played enough computer games and read an amount of EU novels. At the moment I'm reading Timothy Zahn's THRAWN-trilogy again - I think just because I'm that disappointed with TFA.

I sat in the theater watching this movie and felt more and more bored and perplexed. When the end credits went on screen I felt some kind of emptiness. This was supposed to be IT? The long awaited an over-hyped new Star Wars? No. This movie is not Star Wars. It lacks everything that is so special about the original series and even the prequels. There is no magic in this movie, no character development, no build up of tension, no logical actions and backgrounds of the main characters, even no memorable score (and John Williams did this one again!).

What the hell has happened since ROTJ?? Nothing is explained. You can find it in Jedipedia oder a source book, but come on - I am supposed to buy a source book to understand what is going on on screen? Really?? Even worse the main plot totally fails to understand the character of Luke Skywalker. Never (!) would he have let down all of his friends - and the entire galaxy - just because one of his students suddenly changes to the dark side and from now on wears a superfluous face mask and adores the half melted helmet of Darth Vader... The whole film is based on this silly thesis, and it goes down from there on.

What do you get in the movie? You get an Empire Mk2 being this time a kind of 3rd Reich in space, not an overwhelming military power, building planet-size Super-Death Star Mk3. You get dumb Stormtroopers who still are not able to hit a barn door with their guns at sight. You get some complete unbelievable "heroes" including wonder woman just for plot reasons. Etc. Everything has been pointed out here on IMDb so many times.

Did the film makers really think "yeah, let's put in the Falcon, Droids, Leia, Han, evil Empire, Death Star, black coated main villain with laser sword, desert planet, X-Wings and a trench run and these dumbs will buy it as Star Wars"? It is to be feared to have been like that.

I have to fight back my tears considering Timothy Zahn's "Heir to the Empire" being adapted for the screen. They could have done any story. Any story would have been better than TFA! I personally don't consider this one to be Star Wars. And I will not watch episodes VIII & IX on big screen. No Sir, you killed Star Wars for me!

title: A Disappointment on Every Level
review:
This film was a huge disappointment to me. Here's why:

1) CHARACTERS

Rey - An obvious Mary Sue. Mary Sue characters are BORING. There's a reason they are so passionately argued against by lovers of great storytelling.

Finn - Paper thin. He has zero depth. Maybe one of the most boring Star Wars main characters of all time.

Kylo Ren - A sissy. He was not a compelling villain in any sense of the term. I liked Darth Maul better and he had barely more than 10 mins of screen time in The Phantom Menace.

2) STORY

Completely Unoriginal - I felt like they cut and pasted the story elements from the first three films to make this script.

3) PLOT

What's the Plot? - They're trying to find Luke. Honestly, I can't even remember why now. Then they have to destroy another death star. :YAWN:

It makes me sad that this film is doing so well at the box office. I hate to see mediocrity so well rewarded.

Terrible considering the money spent.

Harrison Ford, congratulations on the paycheck, you did a great job. Sorry, they did in your character.

title: Biggest cosplay ever
review:
This film is meant as an earnest homage, much like the Star Trek films from the same director. Just don't expect anything too creative or risky.

There is a lot of action, but character motivation is established too much by exposition and dialogue, instead of actual drama. The drama that gets shown is probably meant as dramatic fuel for the plots of the inevitable sequels. This is not a standalone product.

As cosplay, this product is bar none. The new stormtrooper armor is slicker, reflecting light like a newer model of a car (there is even a silver captain's version). The sets and props are all well recognizable from episodes 4-6, but made to look more detailed.

The music is also very recognizable from the original trilogy, but without the Empire/Anakin's theme. Instead, there is a shiveringly clear five note theme every time the new bad guy appears. Maybe this theme will develop fully in the following films?

Thankfully, there is not as much lens flare as in the Star Trek reboot, but there seems to be problems with the extremely short focus area of the lenses used. It is very visible when an actor's face fills the screen that he is one inch too close to the camera.

title: Not much to do with SW
review:
*** MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS ***

This is quite an enjoyable adventure-like movie. A lot of action, special effects, hilarious moments and fancy weapons. And Harrison Ford, of course.

But that's it. Nothing else to do with SW (if you exclude the complete copy and paste of the script).

And moreover...I really don't get it. How is it even possible to rate Episode VII almost 9 when Episode III is rated 7.5? This is a great marketing job, no doubt. If only they had dedicated the same amount of money and time trying to put a good story together, this would have been a sequel worthy of its name. But that's not the case.

title: I finally figured out what went wrong
review:
J.J. Abrams was confused about which space movie he was creating. Star Wars is about the inner conflict of the characters. These inner conflicts interact to either bring out the best in each other or the worse. The is always the struggle against darkness. This struggle for the light is the most challenging. Each saga doesn't require a happy ending, but an honest ending reflecting this conflict. In Star Trek the conflict is with society and communal responsibility to the whole.
The only movie that captured the heart of Star Wars is recent years under a Disney is 'Rogue One'. The recent Star Wars are not even loyal to the Disney classics which deal with loss pain and redemption. J.J. Should have watched movies from the Disney Vault Such as 'Bambi' and 'Lion King' which dealt with themes found in classic Star Wars.

title: False promises of the galactic kind
review:

JJ always wants to go bigger, do things greater, ALWAYS money behind his projects, which is a good thing don't get me wrong, but YOU have to want to put out the best possible product. Instead of Vadar, we have KYLO-REN (Han/Leia)son where as it was Luke/Vadar (Anakin/Padme)son.

This would be a good film for a rainy Sunday morning with nothing to do but fill time.

title: Star Wars did not need a reboot
review: The Force Awakens was a fun if uninspired movie, that fuses a cast of new quirky characters almost seamlessly with a number of old time favorites. And the onscreen chemistry is great. The adventure is exciting if already done and the pacing is very Star Wars. While Kylo Ren was a week and unconventional villain, that give him the potential the be a more interesting villain(Ante herow?) than usual. And the ominous supreme leader Snoke fills the niche of evil mastermind well enough. None of this however saved the movie form a number of unfortunate truths. The most obvious of which is that the movie is actually A New Hope but different and in a decisively worse way. Almost trope for trope the force awakens was a copy of A New Hope. Not to say there weren't some very different elements but the skeleton was still there. Orphan hero growing up on a desert planet, secret data carried by a droid that speaks in beeps, new heroes' meat old heroes, old hero sacrifices himself in front of new hero. And before it is all over a bar fight at a really sketchy bar. Retooling the old movies however was not as bad as what they had to do to the Star Wars Universe to do it. Taking the rebellion back to square one betrayed the entire first trilogy as a whole. Sending Han and Chewy back into the smuggling business undoes all the character evolution he underwent in the first 3 movies, and requires that we imagine Laya would just let him go. And there is a huge plot whole established with the introduction of Supreme Leader Snoke. All of the Sith were destroyed. Twice in fact, the first time before A Phantom Menace, the second time at the end of Return of the Jedi. So where did this new guy come from especially since he seems so old. I must say that although it was an enjoyable movie it's popcorn value dos not make up for the fact that they had to reboot the universe to retell us a story we liked but in a worse way. Say what you want about the screen writing of the prequels, but you must admit the story was fantastic. The Plot of The Force Awakens leaves much to be desired and that is as thoroughly un Star Wars as a movie can be.

title: meh
review:
Kind of a rehash of the original star wars movie.

fairly bad acting and characterization throughout. its not like it was even the younger cast members, who were all pretty wooden. harrison ford though was terrible, he phoned it in like he was bored and didnt want to be there. it reminds me of the lastest installment of die hard when bruce willis just wasn't into it. terrible. carrie fisher was just as bad, rip and all but she clearly needed help, she reminded me of the weird aunt that isnt ready for a nursing home but is starting to lose it. beyond the bad acting, what motivated these characters? nobody knows its a mystery!

tldr, not terrible but not good either, would probably be fine for someone who wasn't into the series but a real letdown for fans.

title: The weakest villain in the history of cinema
review:
Attention, spoilers!

Kylo Ren was the weakest, most pathetic villain in the history of the movie industry. JJ Abrams made him as a mockery of the sith lords. Every Star Wars fan knows that a trooper can't stand in a fight against the weakest sith accolite or jedi padawan, not to mantion against a trained one. And he was too easily defeated by a newly discovered force sensitive that had no training whatsoever. Come on! Also, every SW fan knows that those who are not trained in the force cannot wield a lightsaber. I love the SW series, but I felt insulted in my intelligence by this one. Kylo Ren should die in the start of the second movie chocked with an olive, because he has no more credibility as a villain. If a before-to-be padawan defeated him, imagine what a 1-day trained one can do to him. Or a Jawa. A tusken raider would be too vicious for him, unfortunately.

Kylo's mask had no point, other than that it is a copy of Revan's mask.

title: Painfully dumb!
review:
This is not about making movies anymore, and certainly not about good story telling, or good acting, or anything good. This is all about HYPE, like the latest Bond movies, Star Trek, and whatever Hollywood is dishing out these days. Disney is nothing more than an attraction Park for kiddies and their parents who have to go along for the necessary photo albums. I won't repeat what has already been said, but yes the movie is awesome as a bottom feeder in cinema history. The one star I'm giving it is in compassion for the actors who tried their best to do something with the absence of a script. Sometimes, you can say ''it could have been better''... but not with this one. There is nothing in there for Rey to salvage. All junk not even worthy enough to feed yourself. I'm old enough to remember seeing the original Star Wars in a cinema, the joy and excitement I felt, nearly all of us science fiction fans felt at the time. Waiting in line to enter the cinema, it dawned on me that almost none of the people waiting were born in 1977. Such a pity there was nothing exciting to see or feel for them like we did then. Some have talked about nostalgia. But this thing is not about nostalgia, it's about harvesting the most money possible with hype and trailers and nothing else.

Edit:

Reading comments from others that did like the film so much that they feel compelled to defend it from us 'trolls', let me simply say that I can make my own mind on a movie, that I don't need someone to chew it up for me before I go see it or don't. I went in for SW7 with an open mind and a new hope for a really new dazzling SW. Instead, I saw a rehash of old SW movies, no originality whatsoever and really nothing worth sh*t. Some people characterized it as a reboot, or even a Tribute. Tributes are something we see on TV along with 65 car commercials we're usually not interested in. And after six SW movies and more than 30 years waiting, I was hoping for a trilogy that would out stellar the first one. If a number of people are willing to settle for that, for a vapid plot with a Sith Lord that can't control himself and Luke Skywalker stuck up a mountain because he decided he failed as a teacher of the Force, it's perfectly fine with me. Imagine if people on our own planet reacted the same after a failure in their life, there would not be a single mountain top left without a hermit. I didn't want a reboot or a tribute when I walked in the cinema, a wanted a new, I mean new SW, and that's not what I got, hence my acute disappointment and that of many, many others. One last thing, I liked Daisy Ridley as Rey and certainly hope to see her in other movies. I've got some good feelings about her.

title: A Disappointed Dieheart Star Wars Fan
review: I have been a Star Wars fan all of my life. While I was not born before the original trilogy was released I have watched them countless times and have been around for the release of every prequel trilogy movie. I've connected with each character and the stories that are told are timeless. With hearing the release of the new Episode VII and with J.J. Abrams directing it, I was definitely skeptical about it from the start. However being the dedicated fan I have been I gave the movie a chance and went to see it opening night. Unfortunately my skepticism would be right and I would be left disappointed. The plot of this movie is nothing new. A basic remake of A New Hope with some character changes is all I felt throughout the entire movie. Nothing stood out and nothing was new. The characters as a whole had no depth to them and I could not connect with characters such as Rey so easily as I did with Luke and Anakin in the past. The movie as a whole felt too forced upon the audience (no pun intended). The filmmakers obviously tried too hard to bring back the grandeur and depth of the original trilogy and in my opinion failed miserably. Another point that also annoyed me was the fact of the many plot holes in the movie. How does Rey coincidentally find Luke's original lightsaber in the box even though it fell off of Cloud City in Episode V with Luke's hand? And the fact to not even explain how it ended up with Maz. It just seemed like an easy way out on the filmmakers part to introduce Luke's original (Anakin's old) lightsaber once again. Plus the fact that Rey can use the force so well by the end of the movie to even get the lightsaber out of Kylo Ren's grasp when Luke could not even do that until the end of Episode V when he was already an almost fully trained jedi. Rey just realized she can use the force and already is able to do this? Doesn't make any sense. For a long movie, plots such as these felt way too rushed. I wish more character development had been taken place as from this movie Kylo just seems like a whining "wanna-be" Darth Vader and Fin seems like just a clueless Han Solo. Speaking of character development, I wish Captain Phasma was elaborated on instead of being shown for only five minutes and half of it being easily taken down by Chewbacca. The antagonists do not seem as threatening as they did in previous movies. Scenes like this and making Kylo already struggling with Rey already make them seem weak. The only thing I will give credit to this movie are the dogfights in space and on Jakku. These were both visually appealing and the only scenes that brought me back to the original movies I know and love. I'm all for more sequels to Star Wars, but do it right at least. Making a movie such as Star Wars is a powerful thing. No matter if its good or bad people from all over the world are going to watch because of the sole fact its Star Wars. But for a dedicated fan like me who has seen the other 6 movies countless of times, make it worth while. Stop milking a successful and timeless story and instead make original yet nostalgic editions to it. I'm only hoping Episode VIII and IX are able to do this. Until then I'm stuck with this unoriginal sequel.

title: Terrible: trying to be a reboot and sequel at the same time simply can't work
review:
If this was the first ever Star Wars movie I might have given it a pretty good score as a bit of fun, but the original movies do exist, this movie is a bizarrely rehashed sequel of those, and my life would have been better if it had never been made.

Let's play a game. For each of the points below am I describing A New Hope or The Force Awakens?

1. The main hero is living unhappily on a desert planet.

2. The main hero is an orphan.

3. The main baddie is a black-masked villain.

4. A droid that bleeps has key information wanted by the baddies.

5. The droid that bleeps hides on the main hero's desert planet and meets the hero by chance.

6. The baddies search for the bleeping droid and destroy the main hero's neighbourhood.

7. There's a cantina scene with a band playing music.

8. The main hero meets a father figure who helps them against the baddies.

9. The baddies have a planet weapon that can destroy other planets.

10. On the planet weapon the main bad guy kills the father figure with a light saber.

11. The planet weapon has a major weakness that requires a pinpoint accurate shot to exploit it.

12. The goodies fly x-wings to the planet weapon and destroy it against all odds.

Let's play another game. For each of the points below am I describing The Empire Strikes Back or The Force Awakens?

1. There is a revelation about a father-son relationship.

2. The main hero goes in search of a famed, reclusive Jedi Master to receive training.

Well, for each of the 14 points above you have a 50/50 chance of being right, because The Force Awakens is primarily a rehash of A New Hope with bits of Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi thrown in. I could have added even more examples of plagiarism if I'd had enough of a word limit.

If you enjoyed this movie then I'm genuinely pleased for you; taste in movies is subjective and each to their own.

However, I don't get what they're trying to achieve and it doesn't work at all. If they had said "we're doing a reboot of A New Hope to bring youngsters / newbies into the fold" and not included any old characters then I would have been disappointed but could at least understand the rationale. But it can't be a reboot because they have old characters in it and refer to their history from the earlier films, so it fails utterly as a reboot and therefore must be considered as a sequel.

As a sequel, despite some good scenes and characters, in my opinion they rip off far too many key plot elements from the original trilogy (see above) and it is a deeply unimaginative rehash as an overall plot. Of all the options they could have chosen, this was the worst.

If you are in denial that this film massively copies A New Hope then I question your ability to reason. Fine, feel free to overlook that and like or even love this movie, but denying irrefutable facts (not opinions) of major plagiarism is not a path to credibility.

title: A shameless remake of Star Wars (1977)
review:
I came into this movie with a lot of excitement and hype December of 2015. Once the movie concluded, it all came to a crash. All the scenes in this movie play on your nostalgia. It never tried to be it's own thing. Nothing new or refreshing was added. They simply copy the Star Wars (1977) blueprint.

We are introduced to the first order, which are essentially the first galactic empire from Star Wars (1977). It is lead by Kylo Ren who answers to Supreme Leader Snoke. A Lord Vader and Emporer Palpatine relationship. We are introduced to the resistance. They are essentially the rebellion from Star Wars (1977), except their name is copied from Terminator. The protagonist, Rey, comes from the planet Jakku. A desert planet like Luke's homeworld of Tattooine. The first order have built starkiller base. It's basically a bigger death star. If you haven't guessed already, it blows up in the end. Once again, important information a galactic empire is after is stored in a droid. JJ Abrams blatantly plagiarized the original Star Wars plot and passed it off as his own work.

Kylo Ren is a much less imposing villain compared to Darth Vader. He often whines and throws temper tantrums. The writers seem to think that's intimidating, but it's really a sign of weakness. Darth Vader and Grand Moff Tarkin never had to yell to have an intimidating presence. They sometimes raised their voice, but never show such emotional outbursts in front of their commanding officers. Such outbursts would show them they have no control, authority or confidence to solve a problem at hand. That's not how an organized and powerful galactic empire conducts leadership.

Rey is an extremely boring protagonist. She is simply perfect at everything. She knows how to use the force without training. She can do jedi mind tricks without training. She can fly the millennium falcon better than Han Solo himself. At the end of the film, she beats the main villain of the film with no training. Note that Kylo Ren was trained by Luke Skywalker. She is truly the epitome of a Mary Sue and that's why this movie has no stakes whatsoever.

Luke Skywalker was a character that had a lot to learn and room to grow. He needed to earn his way to become a jedi. In Star Wars (1977), Luke was being mentored by Obi Wan Kenobi. In The Force Awakens, Rey didn't even know the force existed and yet has all these abilities without anyone to teach her. Luke's development was much more interesting because Rey's was virtually nonexistent.

Rey beating Kylo is like having Luke beat Vader in the very first movie. Would Darth Vader be the iconic villain that we know today if he was bested by a farm boy from Tattooine without training? A reoccuring villain is much less of a threat if the protagonist easily defeats them the first time they meet. That is how you lower the stakes. When Luke Skywalker first faced Darth Vader, he was toyed with and got his hand cut off. You had a feeling of hopelessness when Luke was dueling with Vader. That's how you portray a serious threat to the heroes.

If you want to have a good star wars experience, just rewatch Star Wars (1977). It's pretty much the same movie, but better.

title: "The Most Overrated Movie I Have Ever Seen"
review:
The fact that this movie has even broken into the top 250 astounds me, but its current comfortable placement at no. 138 (and an 82 rating) stupefies me.

The movie's biggest criticism is its plot as it is almost entirely unoriginal and is largely derivative of "A New Hope". I remember turning to my friend 5 minutes into the movie in utter disbelief as it followed "A New Hope's" opening LITERALLY note by note. The movie tries to be a sequel and a reboot at the same time- which makes little sense at all. It takes me out of the film when the same events transpire and the original trilogy characters don't just stop in their tracks and say "we've done this before". Its a real shame because it was the rare pieces of original content in the film that I really liked which could have made for a really good movie. Hopefully these aspects will be fleshed out more for the sequel.

Aside from the plot the characters were quite one dimensional. Rey essentially shares the same backstory as Luke and is the dictionary definition of a Mary Sue. Whatever the plot required of her and any skill which ought to be outwith her abilities (at this point in time) she achieved with relative ease and little struggle. Finn's character was more layered but was largely a comedic presence in the film and I felt that he was there largely to accentuate the strengths of Rey's character. Poe was a fighter pilot- and that was the sum of his character. Carrie Fisher also gave a pretty uninspiring performance as Princess Leia.

With all this negativity its good to highlight the movie's strengths. The effects, cinematography and direction of the film are all top notch. The acting of the leads are also able to transcend the limitations of their roles and is the only reason the characters can be deemed likable. Harrison Ford returns successfully as Han Solo (picking himself back up from his poor return as Indiana Jones). Kylo Ren is an interesting character and, although I feel the character dipped a bit halfway through is probably a highlight of the film.

The film is certainly not below average as there is still a lot to enjoy and appreciate in this film to earn its 6/10 rating from myself. This film needs to be put into perspective by disappointed fans and overly optimistic fans alike. That being said I was extremely disappointed with the final product as a major Star Wars fan and expected far better things. It was well polished for what it was and I'll give it credit for that, but they did play things very safe. I believe it has its inflated rating purely due to the fact it wasn't abysmal like the prequels (even then I'd say Revenge of the Sith is superior to this film). It does ignite some excitement, but for me it was just allowing me to reminisce about the original trilogy.

For me the Force was not Awakened. This film showed me that Star Wars has a past, but not a future.
