title: is it plagiarism if you steal from your own stuff?
review: Never a great fan, but always liked the visuals. But this this..... simply boring, could barely keep my eyes open, another death star, but a really big one, is blown up, another weird alien infested bar is seen, long and boring shots of old actors reprising 40 year old rolls. The one good thing is that the big visual scenes were beautiful, the wrecked desert bound space ship, the interior scenes where Solo is gutted by his son. The actor who plays the son is actually a really really good actor, kind of out of place for star wars, but something to comment on positively. I was glad to see that Carrie Fisher's diet and plastic surgery weren't too silly drastic. Can't for the life of me see why this movie is so freaking successful

title: A New Hope recycled
review:
Just to warn you, this whole review is one big long spoiler. So SPOILER ALERT!

Everyone can save their time watching TFA  just watch A New Hope again. It's THE SAME MOVIE. Lucas recycled everything from the characters to the plot only we get lamer next generations of the original characters. Poe is the new Han, Rey is the new Luke, Kylo is the new Vader, Supreme being is the new Emperor, Luke is the new Obi-Wan, and BB-8 is the new R2. Even the groups are the same: the New Order is the new Evil Empire, the Resistance are the new Rebels complete with base on forested planet.

Opening: Poe gets a disc with important information intended for the Resistance which he hides in a droid. The enemy unexpectedly show up so he sends the droid away. Poe then gets captured and tortured for information until he gets rescued. The droid after wandering the desert dune planet for a while gets picked up by a local girl, who doesn't know it, but she's actually the new hero. She figures out the droid is important and meant for the Rebels  I mean sorry the "Resistance", so together they hightail it off her desert planet home. Sounding familiar yet?

Meanwhile the bad guys have built the Starkiller base, (basically Death Star the next generation) and they use it to destroy a planet very original.

So then the rag-tag group get to the resistance base, they download the droid, they find that the death star thing has a weakness that is in this one exposed spot, they launch an attack, the father figure gets killed by Vader 2, and they blow the new Death Star thing up.

Tell me that's not the entire plot of A New Hope.

It's really inexcusable to me that with as much money as Lucas makes on these films he can't get any decent writers to create an original script.

Fans of the movies will likely always be fans and will like this movie anyway because they'll get all nostalgic about seeing their old characters brought back. But the film is just lazy in its execution. There's nothing new here.

title: The Force put me asleep.
review: I've never done this before but I can't stand it anymore so I had to write something about SWVII. So for those who care to read it this is my take on the last Star Wars. Warning spoilers are included for those who haven't seen it yet. The only good thing about this film to me is the female lead. She's good and she has the right tough temper. Overall I'm very disappointed because of the lack of imagination. This film is mostly a copy/paste of the 1977 episode IV. Remember the droid sent with something hidden in it and found by Luke ? It's really disappointing that with a universe like that writers in Hollywood can't come up with something new, original and creative. But anyway that's what Disney does all the time (copy/paste good film recipes), so that's what they wanted and that's what they did. We even have to stand the same old « I disable the shields so that you can destroy the death star » which we've seen three times now ! It's so boring. The only surprise is that the death star is bigger ! Wow shocking ! The other weaknesses in the film are : - The Bad guy looks strong at the beginning which is promising but then gets his ass easily kicked by a girl who's not even a Jedi yet ! - The phony and unoriginal « last Jedi location map » and one piece of the puzzle map missing. - The Han Solo'son and reverse father/son relationship is predictable cheap and doesn't work for me. - It's nice to put Harrison Ford back in but he's there too much sorry. And now to compensate that he can't have the same action scenes as before they have added humour. Some are good but it's way too much. Sometimes it made me feel like I was watching a Star Wars parody. Also because Han Solo is an important character it creates an unbalance in the story since the true heroes are Finn and Rey. The light saber is a holly thing to me and that's what they want to show when Rey touches it for the first time and the all idea of going to this island to bring it back to Luke. But then why does the old woman proposes Rey to take it since she doesn't even know her much or it appears so ? Why also is it so simply passing to the hands of Finn so he can have fun with it a little ? It's nice coming up with the idea that Finn is a storm trooper who wants to break free but how do you make us buy that ? Why does he so easily escapes ? Why all the others don't do like he does ? Why is he the only one that thinks « oh my god I'm killing innocent people I have to stop » ? The beginning of the film up to the moment when Han Solo is coming back was promising then the Force put me asleep If you want to see good truly imaginative, and gripping Star Wars films watch episodes IV, V, VI.

title: Plot holes galore lack of originality and anemic character building
review:
The Bad

I left feeling empty. The lack of real character attachment and re-hashed plot lines just felt like this was a script that needed to be worked on some more. It really felt like a slightly modified version of Episode IV and lacked almost any originality.

The sheer amount of plot holes is what kept me thinking about the movie afterward. The movie felt as though the full scope of the story was laying on the cutting room floor waiting to be discovered. The scenes did not flow, they just were choppy and left me wondering what was happening to certain characters as the focused switched. Then miraculously, they appeared down the road.

I actually left the theater not knowing most of the characters names. Poe's character had no real importance to the movie and could have been any pilot. Captain Phasma character was also propped up as major part in the film, but was really just filler that was so unimportant to the plot in any way no one would care if the part was written.

The good

Special effects were great! The tie fighters and Millennium Falcon scenes were awesome. Daisy Riddley as Ren was also great. The only character you could really follow and care about. Han and Chewie were good to see again and helped prop the movie up.

Overall it felt like the movie could not decide if it was going to be dark and depressing (it should have been) or be a marketing platform for the brand. I am still really torn on how I feel except it was by far better than the last 3 prequels.

I was entertained but left hoping the next movie VIII would be original and new for a change.

title: Unnecessary, boring and juvenile
review:
Did the world really need ANOTHER Star Wars movie? It depends on who you ask. Star Wars junkies don't count as they're a notoriously biased and juvenile bunch and obviously they can't get enough of all things star wars, no matter how bad or unnecessary they may be. To everybody else, like me, the answer is NO.

This movie is totally unnecessary and adds absolutely nothing to the Star Wars saga. To make matters worse, it's boring, predictable and simply juvenile. There's nothing original, good or memorable about it, other than the star wars label that attracts so much media attention and, therefore, sells so well. Harrison Ford looked jaded, bored and generally unconvincing. Everybody else was mediocre at best. The special effects are good, but if all a movie has going for it are special effects and no substance, then, no matter how "prestigious" the title and its history, one can't help but go away empty-handed and express a negative opinion.

I've never been a star wars fan but I still went to see the movie with an open mind expecting to see, at least, a decent movie. As the clock ticked, though, I just got more and more bored, frustrated and disappointed. When I left the theater, I felt screwed by the Hollywood propaganda machine and by all the fake positive reviews I've read over the past few days pretty much everywhere. Rest assured this will be the first and last Star Wars movie I've ever paid to see.

Do yourself a favor: if you want to see a truly memorable, meaningful movie, check out "Bridge of Spies" by Steven Spielberg.

title: My thoughts about The Force Awakens
review:
+++This review contains spoilers!+++

First of all I would like to make it clear, I'm not a professional in movie reviews, I don't really know much about the camera angles, the special effects etc. I'm just a simple Star Wars fan, like all of us here and I would like to share my feelings and experience. This is not really a review, please treat this wall of text as my own opinion.

When Disney announced they will make a sequel of Star Wars I was so excited. I tried to avoid all spoilers, and of course I jumped on the hype train. Everything they showed us in the trailers was so exciting and raised my hopes of getting a good Star Wars movie. (I have to state that I love all movies, yes, even the prequels too. Despite all the hate they received they always felt Star Wars to me, and that's the most important thing for me.)

So when we got to the cinema and took our seats I felt like this 5 year old boy again, who just watched The New Hope and started living his life with a beautiful fairytale we call Star Wars.

Then the room went dark and the familiar crawling text appeared in space. I don't know if I was prepared for what has been coming after this.

The opening scene at Jakku felt "new". I don't have a better word for it. It had some connections with the old feelings but yet it felt like I wasn't watching star wars. (this feeling remained until the very end of the movie)

The introduction of the characters went well, but I still feel them distant. This is not the actors' fault, I know I'm getting used to new things slowly.

For me the funny parts were funny enough, didn't always felt like they are out of place, but I have to mention I think by far this one movie has the most of the comic relief moments and I'm not sure this is a good thing.

I was literally shocked, when they revealed that Kylo is Han's and Leia's son. Don't get me wrong, the shocking part about this was the audience in the cinema sitting through this scene in complete silence. This should've been one of the most surprising moments in the movie, yet they couldn't get any reaction out from the viewers. It is very disappointing for me.

Another sad moment for me when Han and Leia were reunited. I get it that they were separated for years and carry the burden of their son's dealings, but this shouldn't end up in a forced conversation. Because that's how it felt for me: forced.

And now we get to the most disappointing scene in the movie. Well at least it is for me. Han's death. This just wasn't the Han I remembered. The badass scoundrel, who roams the galaxy, kicks anyone in the butt, saves the day, gets the girl, etc. The true "space pirate" we all loved, and part of us wanted to be. I haven't read any of the books, so I have no clue how Han handled the father role in them, but this scene... From my heart, it is the most disrespectful, unworthy death they could come up with for Han. He deserved better.

Well that's about it, when the movie ended I stood up and almost couldn't believe this is it. This is what I was waiting for for so long. I was worrying maybe I had too high expectations or I'm just being too critical. I'm pretty sure I wasn't the only one, not a single applause or cheer could be heard in the cinema.

I could mention a lot of thing which i din't understand or disliked in the movie. But please let me highlight just two: - The music. I absolutely respect John Williams and love his work, but the previous six movies had so much better music. I really missed that extra "life" that music gives to certain moments in movies. For example please remember the Binary Sunset scene. No words were spoken, yet everyone knew what Luke thought standing in the desert watching the two suns. - New faces. I mean the aliens. I really love the idea to introduce new races to the SW universe, but i missed the old ones really bad. 2 or 3 alien were familiar, but most of the time I was staring at completely strange beings. Again no SW feeling at all.

To sum it up, I don't know how I feel. I will give it another chance, I could forget the plot holes, the reused ideas, even the cliffhanger at the end (Only the Empire Strikes Back could do it well and it never felt so out of place like this one) everything, just let it feel like Star Wars. I don't know if time will change my opinion, maybe this will be better when episode 8 and 9 will be available. Until the time is right, disappear we will.

One last thing for all of us, I saw different reactions in reviews. Some people like the movie, others are not. Please RESPECT each other, be happy for those who liked it and had a good time, and hope the later episodes will meet more people's expectations.

title: "Remember your failure at the cave..." #Fail #Fail #FAIL
review:
"Remember your failure at the cave..."

This is what viewers will need to be saying to JJ Abrams after this travesty of a "new" episode. We got duped by all the pre-release hype and this thing fails miserably.

*** VERY LIGHT SPOILERS ***

Here's a litmus test for ANY movie that you watch, especially one hyped as much as this one was: If at any point in the movie, you are so disinterested, you would get up and walk out and not feel you were missing anything... the movie's a failure. If it's hyped as much as this one was, it's an EPIC failure. #Fail #Fail #FAIL

No spoilers needed. How many ways did this movie fail?

Bad acting: Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher looked reluctant and like they mailed it in. No screen presence whatsoever. The girl is adequate and I guess Finn as well. The rest of this is nothing but a way to wedge in a reunion of all the previous characters in less than impressive ways (including the previous droids). Kylo Horrible. The spoiled brat thing was both puzzling and wasn't sold. Did you ever figure out what a massive effect James Earl Jones' voice as Darth Vader had on the previous originals? JJ doesn't get what it takes to create a real nefarious PRESENCE as Lucas clearly understood. Kylo is way less than intimidating. I could go on and on here.

Bad casting: Really bad casting. I have nothing against Oscar Isaac, but he's not the right guy for the role he's in. Neither is the actor for the antagonist, Kylo (as detailed above).

A Reboot: Name almost any scene in Episodes IV, V and VI and they can be found in this film in different configurations.

Uncreative: Because of the reboot aspect, there's absolutely nothing creative about this movie. JJ Abrams sat down with a clean slate and THIS is what they came up with?! Even the reboot sequences are hurried and without much background. Example: Rebels huddle in a room for 15 seconds and figure out how to blow up a new Death Star that supposedly is 100x bigger and more impenetrable. There are loads of other scenes delivered with almost no background and with a hand wave.

Comic Scenes: JJ couldn't decide if he wanted this to be funny, serious, dramatic or what. Some reviews say the comic lines don't work -- a lot of them were funny in the moment, but when woven into the overall fabric of the movie, you realize something's missing.

I wasn't going to leave a review but SMS comments by my son, who did NOT grow up with Star Wars back in the 1970's and 1980's put it so perfectly, I had to include it:

"The few people who wrote 'good' reviews (here on IMDb) on it were like 'I'm just happy it was Star Wars. I love Star Wars. It was Star Wars. It was amazing. Go see it. Don't listen to the naysayers. Title says Star Wars...' Blah, blah, blah..."

Exactly.

For the sequel to this rubbish, JJ, you're going to have to earn it next time. No more pre-release movie hype that plays off the pent up anticipation of a past generation of viewers. "Remember your failure at the cave..." The cave of a movie house I walked out of last night knowing I and everyone else had been snookered.

Won't watch again and won't buy when it comes out on BluRay. Litmus paper says "acid."

A very generous 2/10.

title: The Force just died...and so did my childhood
review: Where can I begin? I am a huge Star Wars fan, and perhaps I was a little too hopeful that once again we might catch a glimpse of something from our childhood. How wrong I was! It's a remake of EP IV, and a bad attempt at that. Instead of a nefarious Sith Lord, we get Kylo Ren. Grandson of Vader. Whiny kid who throws tantrums and YES, HACKS APART HIS OWN SHIP WITH A LIGHTSABER when things don't go his way. We have no complex bad guys, and that's a shame. A real shame. Tarkin, Motti, Veers, Piett, Needa, Ozzel, Vader, Palpatine...all characters with purpose. There are no memorable villains in VII. Also, we have these crazy abilities...the Falcon can now jump to hyperspace without even taking off. Anyone can use a lightsaber. And while many dispute an untrained adept's ability to best a Force user in a duel? I actually bought it. Kylo Ren whines. He doesn't train. Han Solo is the highlight of the movie, and what they do to him and how they choose to do it is unforgivable. Obviously, if you're a fan, you have to see it. I did. I didn't walk out either. But I went out and bought Phantom Menace just to prove to myself that the prequels were actually better. To my horror, I was right. They are. May the Force be with you as you watch this film, because YOU ARE GONNA NEED IT. Pros: The sets evoke the feeling that you're in the Original Trilogy. The harsh reality is that you're not.

title: Awful - Just Plain Awful ( Contains Spoilers )
review:
I agree with the many posters here who gave this a low rating! As one who saw the original Star Wars in 1977, I am truly disappointed with this remake. And lets be honest it is a remake any way you look at it. Nothing original in this movie - same plot as episode IV. Couldn't they have come up with something better? The bad guy is another Darth Vader look alike with an evil looking mask who happens to be Luke's nephew (spoiler alert). But does he really need that mask? Why does he wear a mask anyways because in part of the movie he takes it off and breathes just fine without it?

Amazingly the heroine in the movie is able to fight just as good as a Jedi Master with a light sabre without any sort of previous Jedi training. Wtf? I thought they had to go to Jedi school and spend years to master the force before they are able to hold their own against a trained Seth Master?? Then there is the planet destroyer that oddly enough looks very familiar to the original Death Star in ep IV. Couldn't they have come up with something more different?

The storyline and plot just seems to me to be put together without too much thought. Nor does it adhere to any of the rules and guidelines of the original "Star Wars" universe. JJ Abrams has truly butchered this franchise with this awful remake. Save your money and wait till it comes on Netflix. And judging by the reviews here it shouldn't take too long.

title: Don't follow the blind nostalgia
review:
Let me just say that this is not a good movie. At all. This was more of a really bad remake with washed up characters that should have had cameos instead of pivotal roles. It is a fan service that relied too heavily on the familiar and brought basically nothing new to the franchise. People tell us not to compare to the OT, but that's exactly what they did with the PT and that's exactly what I'm going to do here. Why should the TFA come under less scrutiny just because George Lucas is not at the helm?

To start: the sheer amount of coincidence felt extremely forced and did not flow like the previous 6 movies did (Rey, a force user, just happens to be on a planet where the Falcon is stored, runs into a droid who coincidentally has the whereabouts on the last Jedi known, and miraculously finds the most significant lightsaber in history in a basement).

The dialogue: People harp on the prequels all the time due to the sub-par dialogue but I argue the conversations between Leia and Han were worse than Padme and Anakin ever were. By this virtue alone, the prequels are better due to the sci-fi factor that it brings vs. the non existent innovation from The Force Awakens.

The plot was basically the same: vital information stored in a droid / go to a cantina / kills a main character with lightsaber to enhance connection to the dark side / fly through a trench in order to destroy weapon capable of destroying planets. Homage is one thing, blatant rehash is another, and this movie does the latter in spades.

In summary: why do you come to watch STAR wars? 1) Characters: Check. 2) Space battles: no, not really, even death star 3 was a planet converted into a weapon, AKA not in space. This movie literally had no wars in space. It was Planet Wars. 3) Cool spaceships that stir the imagination: not at all, we get rehashes of the TIE fighter, X Wing and the Falcon. Say what you will about the Prequels but at least they delivered something new every. single. movie (ARC-170 star fighter, Republic Gunship, Jedi Starfighter) 4) Character development: that's a stretch. How did Rey magically learn all these force tricks and become adept at the same level of saber dueling as Kylo who's basically trained his whole life? 5) Storyline: So. Many. Plot holes. But the biggest, most burning one: What is the Republic? What were the effects when the planets were destroyed? It seemed like a side piece with no repercussions. Prequels and OT alike had their story lines influenced by government (prequels arguably a bit too much) - this was just there as a placeholder for SFX.

When we look back at this in 10 years and the fanfare has died down, we will see rate this at the same level as the prequels, if not lower; and the critics who reviewed this as baby boomers blinded by nostalgia. The biggest faults that the prequels had was the forced, unnatural dialogue, but at least it had amazing, grand scale sequences to balance out the bad. This is just an overall bad remake with the exception of excellent chemistry between Rey and Finn.

For all it's flaws I will say this: TFA is an excellent set-up movie and raises more questions than it does answers. I just hope Episode 8 will actually bring something new to the table and not recycled characters/starship designs/plot.

(Full Disclosure: I made an IMDb account just to write this review - this is how much TFA disappointed me)

title: How to Sell a Film with its Name
review:
Bare in mind this is coming from someone who was really never much of a Star Wars fan and has found at least 2/3 of films in the series extremely "meh", but I thought 90% of this film was a completely unnecessary and uninspired retread of previous Star Wars material.

The plot is an extremely eye-rolling carbon copy of the original 1977 film whilst 90% of the characters are completely cardboard and uninteresting. There was potential mind you, but Rey is the epitome of a Mary Sue and Poe, Finn, and whatever other characters there were, were completely forgettable. The one exception to this is Kylo Ren, who is an admittedly interesting character but he isn't given enough to do. There are only maybe two scenes in the entire film that I found remotely entertaining, and those are the last scene involving Han along with maybe the lightsaber duel near the end. But beyond that, it is a horribly bland film. It's still well-made and well-shot, but at its core, it's mostly hollow. The only reason it got positive reception and made the amount of money it did was because of the Star Wars name and nothing more. If this film had a different title, its Rotten Tomatoes score would be in the 30's.

Normally I'd rate this more like a 3/10, but given that the general IMDb consensus is surprisingly an 8/10. all it's getting for now is a 1/10.

review:
I went to see this with a friend of mine who really loves SW. He seemed to really enjoy it but I didn't.

I want to say this much. I never was a big SW fan. I remember sleeping on Star Wars sheets as a youngster but not being overly wrought with joy from looking at them. I have yet to see A New Hope and Return of the Jedi. Yes, pathetic I know. And I think I am one of the rare ones out there who loved The Phantom Menace which I saw before any of the others.

In a nutshell, I hated Attack Of The Clones other than Yoda's awesome light saber duel. Revenge of the Sith was way too violent and this one is more like The Force Died.

This one was a slap in the face. Why does Disney have to take over every franchise known to man? I'm sure Walt is spinning in his grave over this. title: I am utterly disappointed!
review: For me personally, the main and the biggest flaw is the way Han dies. I was disappointed that he died at all, but if Harrison Ford didn't want to pay the saga any more its fine for me. Still, the way Han dies is just... It's just (hard even to say) - pointless, meaningless, useless. It changes nothing. It is not like death of Vader, as he saves his son or even death of Ben Kenobi. Of course, you may say: "it's just like happens in life", but what I expected from the movie was a "fairy tail" happening "long, long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away". If any producers will ever read my or others review: please, just consider in a future if not asking some fans for their expectations. Other flows: another Death Star like super-weapon destruction with a tiny ships - with another trench run - nothing new (maybe Empire will learn eventually, that their battle-stations are vulnerable to small crafts ;) ). Mark Hamill listed at the top of characters appearing?!?! He shows up at two scenes for about a minute in total! Frankly speaking, I would like Han to resurrect somehow ;) I don't care if anyone think it's stupid, these are just my fillings :) or at least to "appear" to his son like dead Jedi like to do ;) I will see, maybe bad fillings about the movie will pass away with time, but for me Episodes IV-VI will remain the best saga (of my childhood and beyond).

title: I'm very saddened to see this.
review:
I'll give J.J. Abrams props that he has co-written and directed a decent movie. The acting was alright, though a bit wooden. The action scenes were OK, for what they were. Daisy Ridley actually seemed to be the only one in the entire cast who, at some point in her life may have actually SEEN a light-saber duel and attempted to make her performance fit that image.

Now, to get to the meat of this comment: J.J. Abrams should be charged with attempted murder of a Space Opera icon. This is an example of a decent Hollywood movie. It is a less than desirable example of a Star Wars movie.

It seems quite obvious to me that J.J. Abrams is a much bigger fan of Star Trek than he EVER was of Star Wars. Considering that his take on Star Trek actually made me like the new Star Trek, and I don't know if I will ever watch another Star Wars movie, especially if he is the director.

Now, I know a lot of you are thinking, this guy just wants to rant, and that may be partially true, but now comes the reasons why I say this isn't a Star Wars movie.

SPOILER ALERT.

I'm sorry, I don't care how angry you are at Harrison Ford, you don't have a Legend like Han Solo get killed by some whiny little brat who is SO intent on emulating his grandfather that he literally cries about it. If you absolutely MUST kill Han Solo, you bring back Boba Fett, or some other character that is just as Legendary.

And I'm sorry, Darth Vader would have KILLED his "grandson" for being such a weak, whiny, pathetic creature. In fact, he's so weak and pathetic, I can't even remember his name to put it in this comment. The Sith lords of old must be rolling in their graves.

Another thing. The storm trooper turned "good guy". I guess it's plausible, but these guys are raised from childhood knowing only "follow orders and die". From everything we've seen throughout the Star Wars Universe, these guys are as close to robots as humans can get, yet this one guy, on some distant backwater desert planet suddenly relearns his entire belief system and way of living, just because one of his fellow cannon fodder gets killed and puts three bloody streaks on his helmet? There are so many other user comments that say what I'm trying to so much better, I'll stop here by saying one last thing. If this is what Star Wars is going to be from now on, I will keep my Episodes 4, 5, and 6 and dream of the good ol' days when Star Wars was a great movie franchise that I could sit down with my entire family and we could all enjoy a great movie with a great story.

title: Entertaining, but disappointing
review:
After knowing that J.J. Abrams and Lawrence KAsdan were going to be on board the new project, I was expecting the movie anxiously. The Star Trek reboot done in 2009 was, in my opinion, an excellent movie. However, after getting out of the cinema, the magic (or "the force" in this case) were not with me.

The movie is undoubtedly entertaining and it is good fun. Daisy Ridley is filling the screen, and I believe if she manage well the fame brought by this movie, she can make a great career. BB-8 is charming and funny, special effects at its best.

However, the movie is just a compilation of Star Wars things already seen (particularly in Episode IV and in a minor extent Episode VI), but with different characters. Not going to say what to avoid further spoiling. The anticipated return of some of the old characters looks quite forced into the story... and with all respects, every time John Boyega appears in the screen feels to me like one of those teenage TV movies. Maybe he will improve... and Daisy Ridley, despite her charisma, does not have a character allowing her to show her true potential.

In the end, despite the blockbuster-type of fun, I am disappointed. I will return to the old trilogy (ep. IV, V and VI) as a reference for everything related to Star Wars.

title: Re-Hash of the Jedi
review:
I guess I'm in the minority here and yes I enjoyed it for the most part (though probably mainly for nostalgic reasons) but it was tough to really lose myself in the film as I felt I'd been there before.

The hardcore fans are celebrating the fact that J.J. ticked all the boxes but for me that was part of the problem, too many boxes were ticked making it little more than a remake with old actors thrown in.

On top of that there were some serious plot holes and inconsistencies as well, things I didn't expect J.J. to let slip though. I can't go into them without giving away spoilers but if you've seen the film you should know what I mean.

I guess it was always going to be a tough ask to continue the saga and do it justice (though it seems most people think that's what has been done) but I feel that the problem is that the Star Wars story really ended with EP6:ROTJ, sure there's always the chance that the Empire rebuilds and a new Sith Lord shows up but so what? That's a remake or reboot right? Anything after that is hitting the reset button (which ironically is what J.J. did with Star Trek allowing him to essentially remake Wrath of Khan but do it fresh). That'll work great for the new fans but for those of us that were there at the start it feels like just another reboot of something we loved as a kid.

EP7:TFA has a lot of good stuff in there as well, it's not a 'bad' movie and it's certainly far better than EP1:TPM (what isn't) but over all I felt EP 7 really didn't continue the story it was just J.J. remaking his childhood memories which to me was disappointing. To be honest I'd love to know what George Lucas had in mind for episodes 7 - 9.

I'll give it 6/10 but mostly for nostalgia.

title: An exercise in nostalgia and CGI
review:
After watching this film (and being relatively unimpressed by it), I went to Superstore to pick up a few groceries. Unexpectedly, the film's value hit me there, rather than when I was in the theater watching the film, as it was in the store that I became aware of modern film's propensity to market rather than to innovate. Pictures of Stormtroopers, Rey, Finn, and Kylo Ren crowded the shelves, plastered onto Shreddies' boxes, Jam jars, Eggs, TV screens, clothing, toothpaste, organic chips, and even diapers. I realized that a two and a quarter hour exercise in bland escapism had managed to transcend the silver screen, embedding itself firmly in our everyday lives, from our diapers to our cereal. While I do find this rather abhorrent, I can't deny that it is definitely remarkable.

Art and novelty have been pushed to the side in favour of economic triumph. The Force Awakens, buoyed onwards by skillful marketing and rabid nostalgia, will end up as one of the highest-grossing films of all time. Collectibles, diapers, cereal, etc. branded with characters and logos will bring in even more billions of dollars. And, as we glance at the lineup of big-budget blockbusters coming to theatres (Batman vs Superman, TMNT 2, Allegiant (split into two parts), remakes, reboots, and a slew of Marvel and DC extravaganzas) it seems as if Hollywood has figured out that this is the way to go. It has finally donned the costume of a clown that knows only one trick, but can do it better (and bigger) each time.

I'm not down on Hollywood. I'm down on (most) modern action films for their money-grubbing emptiness, and the new addition to the Star Wars franchise exemplifies my sentiment.

Star Wars: The Force Awakens is highly reminiscent of the original trilogy, borrowing plot points, scenes, and characters directly from the most memorable and enjoyable bits in Lucas's classic galactic romp. Although this is at first quite fun, one eventually realizes that this film brings nothing new to the table, except for a plethora of CGI and a surprising new character. The film's fear to be its own film is its undoing. It panders to expectations, forcing the audience to be unable to watch the film without comparing it to what came before.

My excitement at being returned to the Star Wars universe ended after the opening crawl.

The Force Awakens begins in about the same way as A New Hope. A base of some sort is attacked, a droid (who communicates in beeps) is given a valuable piece of information by some guy, who is taken prisoner by the First Order (led by a creepy guy in a mask with a low voice named Kylo Ren). Damn, what movie did I just describe? The plot eventually takes a better hold, with a Stormtrooper named going rogue, teaming up with some girl named Rey (who has found the droid), and them leaving the planet, chased by Stormtroopers, in...the Millennium Falcon. And or course, since they brought the Millennium Falcon back, they have to bring Han Solo back, so they do, and he's, well, old. Chewbacca hasn't aged a day, though.

And while all this is happening, the new Death Star (Basically the original Death Star except a planet) blows up a bunch of planets, while Kylo Ren feels the "pull of the light". I wanted to punch the screenwriter in the face at this point. One does not simply have the bad guy kill billions of people, and then have the audience sympathize with him. Sure, Darth Vader did the same thing, but in A New Hope, he was the essence of evil. Ren is weak, boring, and takes off his mask way too early in the film.

Oh, and the Emperor is there too. But he's got a different name. Coke or Snoke, or something like that.

The screenplay is rather poor. The characters and their interactions are forced and implausible. No secrets are kept from the audience. Many of the pivotal plot elements occur by chance. I felt as if the screenwriter lacked sensitivity to the things that he wrote as the film did not deliver story and innovation. Instead, it served to recreate the plot all of us Star Wars fans know, and amp it up with visuals, while not realizing that simply by copying the success of the original trilogy (and not even copying it well), it is a useless cinematic experience.

Although I did not like the film, I would still like to applaud the visual effects team. Some shots and sequences were simply divine. The recreation of the bridge scene from Empire Strikes Back is gorgeous (albeit ridiculously scripted), and the final battle scene is rousing enough to be commendable. If the screenwriter and crew were passionate about making something original and sensible rather than appealing to nostalgia, I think that The Force Awakens would have actually been worthy of its critical acclaim. But as it stands, The Force Awakens is insipid, lethargic nostalgia that attempts to reignite the franchise's former prestige without feeling a need to create its own.

title: Poor Sequel - Great Money Maker
review: I was so looking forward to this Sequel The story was weak and no real depth mostly relying on the originals to take the film forward. Rey's character was way to much she seemed to jump straight to master jedi with no training. title: I see why they kept this movie a secret now.
review:
I'll keep it short and sweet without repeating what some reviewers have said because if I did that well my review would be like the movie. Should I leave it at that? If they were going to reboot a movie Disney should have practiced its dark art of the force on remaking the prequels. This movie was not as good as I had hoped. It's episode IV in a 21st century shell. I saw it 12/18 in an IMAX theater so bare with me as I try to remember it all.

Deserted planet with data evil guys are looking for... Stored in a droid who travels far until data is in right hands... Masked villain comes looking for it with an army... title: Makes a mockery out of the 'old' cast.
review:
A story about an untrained girl, who 'beats' a Dark Jedi (Sith, whatever...) who was trained by Luke Skywalker, and a Sith Lord. He also killed a bunch of other students (some who were very good), that were all trained by Luke Skywalker.

No back story as to why she's basically the best Jedi ever, (able to use advanced force moves) with zero training. She seems to know more about the Millennium Falcon than Han Solo (and Solo's not even a smart ass about it). Han Solo from '77, would have put her in her place! It's who he is! Look at how he talked to royalty....

Basically, she makes the 'original' heroes look like a bunch of droopy eyed armless children. Her prowess of the Force seems even more innate than Anakin, who was CONCEIVED by the force and had the highest Midi-chlorian count ever seen, by a large margin.

It just wasn't believable.

Why Disney ...just why?

title: The wait is over, and Star Wars Episode Four marks its debut on the big screen...again!
review:
So, after years of waiting, many people have been eagerly anticipating some sort of fix to the Star Wars universe. Sure, the prequels weren't the best, so whatever is to come should be better. The prequels didn't feel like Star Wars to some, or there was too much CGI, or too much politics, or Yoda was butchered or something along those lines...

After years of complaining fans who desperately want something that feels like Star Wars, we get this:

Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope: Remix: The Force Awakens

That's right. The Force Awakens, is unfortunately THE EXACT SAME MOVIE as Star Wars Episode IV. Okay, I'm being a little dramatic, but it is almost plot-point per plot-point the same movie as Star Wars Episode IV with a little touch of Episode V thrown in there. I just don't get it. I was never a HUGE Star Wars fan, so I didn't go into the movie expecting good or bad. I intentionally did not read any review of this movie and I avoided watching trailers. I wanted to objectively watch this movie, without getting distracted by other people's opinions... and yeah, this is Star Wars Episode IV.

What is the plot? Get this, rebels have secret plans that can't fall into the Empir *whoops* I mean the First Order's hands. So, the First Order sends troops into a rebel outpost which is lead by a dark hooded sith that wears a mask. The plans are then put onto R2D2 (whoops, BB-8) where the droid is supposed to run-away and find someone to receive the message.

I kid you not, this is the beginning of the movie. And it gets worse.

Our main girl is a character who lives on a desert planet (Not Tatooine), and finds scraps and sells them to dealers for money. We are later introduced to Han Solo who is (yet again) being chased by people he owes money (not unlike A New Hope) and he has to escape on the Millennium Falcon. And they have to go to a cantina, and there are rebels, and then the bad guys are lead by a giant dark figure in a big chair, and the bad guys decide to use their ultra death star to destroy several planets, but then the rebels (are they really rebels at this point if the First Order isn't an empire?), so the main characters have to infiltrate the Ultra Death Star to find its weak-point and blow it up by flying through trenches, and... and...

Yeah. This is THE SAME PLOT AS A NEW HOPE!!!!

Granted, the tasks and characters are rearranged. Instead of Yoda, we have Luke, instead of Luke, we have Rey, instead of Han Solo we have Han Solo, instead of Obi-Wan, we have have... Han Solo, in place of Vader we have Kylo Ren, instead of the emperor we have Snoke, instead of R2 we have BB-8... heck even Commander Akbar and Porkins are in this movie!

I just don't get why people are liking this. The problem with this movie is that it is essentially taking the easiest route possible. It would be HARD to make an original story, it would be HARD to think up of new concepts, but unfortunately, it gives us the same movie we already liked... That isn't just a little lazy, that is incredibly lazy.

And it is sad, because a lot of time went into producing this moving, shooting it with film, and making sure it feels like a Star Wars film. And it does feel like a Star Wars film, but just not a good one.

The only real redeeming factor this movie has is the chemistry between Sol and his son. That was a unique and interesting aspect (unfortunately, nothing like the Expanded Universe but I don't really care about that at this point haha).

Now, I've ranted about how this movie is similar, but the movie is full of a lot of problems as well: Why is Kylo Ren influenced by Vader even though Vader turned good? Why is the First Order more powerful than the Empire if they are merely the remnants of it. Why in the world did the Republic not destroy or do anything about the First Order who has obviously had a planet destroying planet on their hands for a long time? Did they really blow-up the entire planet by hitting one of its stabilizers? I thought that would merely paralyze it, not blow-up to kingdom come. WHY DO THE BAD GUYS HAVE PLANET SIZED STATIONS THAT DIE FROM ONE HIT IN ONE LOCATION!!!!

And the list doesn't end there, there are so many strange plot issues with the movie and strange conversations. There is this orange lady alien whose voice just sounds... odd. It sounds clean, but she is supposed to be incredibly old. A lot of characters also speak in exposition. Heck, the first character interaction we see in the movie is really forced exposition.

Granted, there is some other good in this movie. For instance, I like how Finn and Rey are both innocent and child-like. The effects are pretty nice as well. Kylo Ren is also kind of neat because he is both weak and boring looking, immature, but also dangerous.

Hopefully, all of the original concepts in this film will be expanded upon in the next entries. As it stands, this movie is far from perfect.

title: First trilogy remade...
review:
Disappointing really. First trilogy remake efforts, in an awful way...

This movie cannot/must not get a rating of 8, no way, this is marketing act only. We should not promote lame film making...

title: Clear your mind must be, if you are to find the villains behind this plot
review: My disappointment is real and valid. This was not a good movie. I was not expecting it to be better than the original but i was hoping it was at least a good story. Unfortunately it was the same story and not retold very well. As a longtime fan of the original trilogy i was always hoping someone would delve deeper into the star wars universe, expand on what little we know of the force - the light and the dark, show real commitment to the actual power of the story itself and respect its origin and artistic authenticity and not it's potential for profit and merchandising. The original trilogy was not a new story either, not really, good v. evil stories have been told and retold forever, but this one was told in a very new and innovative way and with a commitment to the viewer that most movies never achieve. Force Awakens fails to engage. I walked away feeling cheated and disgusted.

title: How is this rated 8.8/10?
review: There is no way this film should be rated so highly. You're telling me it's as good as Lord of The rings, the original Star wars films, The Dark Knight, Fight Club etc....? No way... the plot was an exact rehash of Episode IV. Unoriginal, uninspiring, and lackluster all round. The only good thing about it was performances and the nostalgic music, sounds etc. As a stand alone film i'd give it like a 6/10, but since it's being rated so highly I'm going to give it a 1/10. An 8.8/10 film should be original, not a film that is an exact copy and paste of another movie from 30 years ago. I will say, it was better than the prequels in terms of acting, production etc. But even the prequels had better ideas, and MUCH better music. The music wasn't special at all in this - no Dual of The Fates etc etc. Overall im disappointed. Over-hyped to the max.

title: The force has indeed awakened for Star Wars, and the haters continue to embarrass themselves. XD
review:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens is a fabulous film and is a good dose of escapism from mundane everyday life, just like The Original Trilogy was. We can forget all our problems when seeing this movie. The Force Awakens sparks a joy for the child in all of us which many of us have been waiting for since The Empire strikes Back or Return of the Jedi. There couldn't have been a story more worthy of the subtitle 'Episode VII'.

After the whole Trade Negotiations rubbish that plagued the Star Wars Prequel Trilogy. J.J. Abrams reinvigorates the assaulted franchise and gives us some of the most powerful moments ever seen in the saga.

Don't give in to the trolling of the prequel or original trilogy fanboys. They're just upset that somebody did a much stronger job than Lucas could have managed on his own. They couldn't tell a good movie apart from Transformers 3 & 4, or any Michael Bay movie for that matter. We are entitled to our own opinion and mustn't succumb to these 'emotion vampires' that do their best and ultimately fail to make a difference in the end.

The Force Awakens is a refreshingly fun film that as a form of escape in this day and age plagued by terrorism, cyber-terrorism, LGBT discrimination and racism. Star Wars is a welcoming series that isn't conformed by anything in our world ; it's a self-realising ecstasy that will always be there for us like an old friend.

10 stars

title: "You want fries with that?"
review: Imagine Luke Skywalker receiving his Fathers lightsaber from Ben Kenobi and then immediately rushing to a pawnshop to sell it, while screaming" so long Sucker!" at Ben. That's how disrespectful the makers of this for profit only toy commercial are. title: Worst Starwars Film
review:
We have all been deceived by the Sith Lords that are JJ Abrahams and Disney that have lead us to believe we are getting something fresh in a legendary franchise...

In a nutshell it's a episode IV remake:

1 droid is stranded on a desert planet with plans that the bad guys and good guys need desperately.(Episode IV)

2 storm troopers slaughter group of innocent people.(Jawas and Luke's aunt and uncle Episode IV)

3 a nobody on the desert planet meets up with the droid and is hunted by stormtroopers. (EpisodeIV)

4 the nobody escapes the bad guys on the same ship used to escape in episode IV

5 bad guys have created a planet killer (Death Star on steroids). (Episode IV)

6 bad guys blow up a planet of innocent people.(Episode IV)

7 good guys need to hit the Steroid Death Star in a specific place to destroy it. (Episode IV)

8 father and son confrontation on a bridge. (episode V)

9 x wing fighters have minuets to destroy Steroid Death Star before resistance base planet is destroyed by it. (Episode IV)

10 x wing fighters attack Steroid Death Star by going down a narrow trench laced with laser cannons. (Episode IV)

Let's not forget the endless catch phrases and throwbacks form the original trilogy. Scene with the chessboard on the falcon, C3PO "thank the maker!", "throw her into the garbage dispenser?!" Just to point out a few.

Really?!! How can people buy into this Hollywood money spinner and say it's the best Star Wars yet.There is nothing new here at all. Fair enough the prequel trilogy didn't match up to the originals but at least they did have a totally different story. You cannot criticize the prequel trilogy and seriously tell me this film is better. At least they hand new ideas and didn't blatantly rip off the original story and rehash it as a brand new film! Best to put this film into the deepest darkest corner of the force (where it belongs) and forget about it.

title: Can't figure out how come this movie is close to 9 stars on IMDb
review: Honestly it is beyond me why this movie scores close to 9 stars on IMDb. Plot and story is close to non existent in this movie and 5 stars review comes mostly from being action packed. Main characters were rather bland comparing to the bunch in the original trilogy. I dig more BB-8 than any new character in the movie. And main reason for that is when JJ have money he will blow most of it on CGI and VFX instead of the story. Story is re-booted from Episode IV (droid that holds some important data, sand planet with some peasant doing hard labor instead of being a Jedi, ultra-mega-huge death star masked inside the planet, tho I am not quite sure that it would be possible to build that thing in ~30 years since I doubt that after destruction of second one and death of Emperor, next day Empire recuperated and started building new and improved one). Yeah action sequences are decent, tho I really have issues with Finn and Ray fighting Sith without any training (I though wielding light saber is not, or hard at least, for non Force users) is rather pathetic. 30 years passed, we have Luke Skywalker went AOL, one fallen Jedi that he trained him, and yet we don't get slight flashback how, why or when it happened. Overall 5 stars is VERY generous for this movie, and honestly I would be perfectly OK if no other Star Wars movie is ever created. But since re-boots and milking is the thing Disney do, we are looking at at least 2 more with possibility of making them as long as they feel fit.

title: Little substance
review:
Felt rushed, little plot, too many things crammed in. The villains felt extremely weak and underdeveloped/not inspired.

It gets one star for Han and Chewy's adventures the 4 seconds of Luke Skywalker we get, and that is about it.

The New Order just plain sucks. Supreme Leader Snoke and Kylo Ren?! Complete freakin' jokes compared to Darth Vader and Darth Sidious. The Emperor needs to come back, that is the only thing that can save this mess of a beginning to the sequel trilogy. The expanded universe was much better that this crap and ultimately ripped off some of its ideas anyway.

title: Sigh, I've seen this movie before, 38 years ago.
review: Well JJ has yet again made of mockery of a great franchise. It's like they've spliced pieces of the OT and chucked it in a food processor. Kylo Ren is the most pathetic Sith Lord ever (and you thought dooku was bad) he comes across as a petulant child with a big stick and kills his dad (Harrison ford finally getting his wish to kill off Han since he first played him) the main cast were good (besides Mark Hamill's 2 min non speaking role right at the end in which he looked like the beegees) biggest beef was with the secondary cast, they all looked mid 30s and hardly stood up to the older more experienced looking commanders admirals etc in the OT. Most the action sequences were good because we all knew that's what jar jar Abrams was gonna do, some of the CGI characters looked woeful especially gollum the supreme leader (Andy Serkis) or Snoke the stupidest name since Sheev Palpatine. My other gripe was the pathetically obvious use of Nazi-ish visuals that are so over the top they might as well gave them all Hitler moustaches. So if you thought jar jar Abrams would be the saviour of Star Wars and return it to its former glory you're sorely mistaken. I never thought anyone could out "Michael bay" Michael bay then JJ is surely a contender.

title: Boring
review: The film is more or less a remake of part IV. The villain is pale in comparison to the other villains we saw before. Why he is wearing a mask is not obvious and is totally useless. The crowd in the cinema laughed at the final reveal of the face, an emotion the director of the film hasn't planned for that scene. The whole overall story is so useless and boring I can't believe that has passed the quality control. The film was watchable up to a certain point on a bridge in the converter building. After that it was over for me. I won't go into details but how in the hell could they do that? Is this the Star Wars for the New Age? Forget that for me then. All in all uninspiring and boring with great but no many overblown special effects. More a mishmash of Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings and old Star Wars....Last but not least: who came up with the names? What was that villains name? Snoke? Snake? Snape? Doesn't care a lot for it.....

title: A Total Let Down
review:
This is not my original post but it says just about everything I felt about this movie:

Besides the fact that there are so many glaring plot holes in this new Star Wars episode: the Millennium Falcon being able to escape the mighty First Order starship, but getting caught by Han Solo's tractor beam, ships going around in space without even a radar to learn of approaching ships (I thought this was a 70s sci-fi thing only), planets populated by only a handful characters (the prequels at least stayed away from that, with the Republic shown as a giant metropolis and Naboo heavily populated. how exactly do they search for people on a planet the size of Earth?), characters just sitting around in medieval pubs gambling and drinking without any sort of new technology or at least portable computers, blown away planets being spotted by main characters from another planet who immediately realize what has happened (that line really hurt! why don't they bloody have a TV news channel in the gazillion century to learn that the Republic's Senate in the Hosnian star system has been attacked?) and so many more.

But what truly hurts this movie is that it's not a movie at all. I could get over all the plot holes if they had just given me something,something, but it was all just a bunch of repeated scenes from the previous movies: A greedy dealer buying spare parts on a desert planet check Desert planet from where main hero starts off check A trio of heroes check A member of the Skywalker/Solo family turned to the dark side check An evil leader staying in the shadows check A message hidden with a droid (sent on the desert planet) check Escape from an evil starship by team of heroes check Infiltration of evil base by team of heroes check Council of the Resistance check Another Death Star.

I mean, this was literally Star Wars from the 70s and 80s all over again. No change, except that the main character is now a baby girl instead of a man. Yeah, fem****t movies strike again. I can understand her using the Force, but pushing Kylo Ren with her shoulder!

And Kylo Ren, you all complained and complained about Hayden Christensen being vulnerable and his relationship with Natalie Portman's character being cheesy in the prequels, but Adam Driver is the definition of cheesiness. No matter what he does, no matter how he speaks I can't stop laughing every time I see his bubbly face. It's not his fault, it's just his face! He was born to play cheesy roles. Maybe this is what the producers went for, but he's not scary at all, I just want to squeeze his cheeks! He is 100% an actor destined for comedy roles. And that scene with Han Solo so obvious. I could see it a mile away. So overdone in films. So cheesy! And the dialogue was so cringe worthy Harisson Ford almost deserved what happened to him. That's no way to talk to your troubled kid, it was like he was trying to make Ben angry, to show him who's the boss! No "I forgive", no "Please", no "I'm sorry, it's my fault hat I've hurt you". Just: "Take off that mask, you don't need it. Come home!" that's about

I had such high expectations. I just wanted to see something, anything new. Something that would blow my mind. I can't believe this took so many years to be made. It's just sad really, I wasted 2 hours on... nothing. No feeling

title: someone just had to make another movie about the same thing but hype would do over substance
review:
If there is a movie to miss at all costs then this is got to be one of them. It disappoints on so many levels and the evil of the enemy is not even close to being the slightest intimidating.

If there is a true fan of Sci-Fi out there that are not so freaky as to live their lives through a single franchise then this movie is not for you. It was hyped beyond even the spiteful lengths which in my view could have been used to help ignite a thousand better projects. This movie was neither great or worth the wait.

It lacked thought and script integrity throughout. The special effects may have been loud and totally captivating but the visual substance of the plot lacked severely. The acting was so lopsided that it was difficult to bare who were supposed to be veterans and who rode the high horse of a big pay day. I did not see where the budget of $200, 000, 000 had gone but it sure did evaporate into nonsense and monotonous dribble. No new ideas or story could have been a theme of this horrible excuse of a movie. Being sci-fi was about all it had going for it but it was difficult to sit through knowing that nothing I was watching was even remotely exciting.

There wasn't a single surprise or plot twist other than its total waste of time and space, totally predictable to even children in the audience. The bad guy, whatever he was supposed to be wasn't in the least bit intimidating. His helmet should have been left on through the entire movie as once he was exposed, his drippy looks just made watching him with his helmet back on all the more uncomfortable knowing that he was just some kid with a altered voice under a Halloween mask. I implore anyone eager to watch this to wait and see it in a couple of weeks after the true ratings have been adjusted and read or listened from the non-fans of this now detrimental franchise.

If I really wanted to watch another movie with a Death Star, I would have watched the original. This Death Star may have been bigger to the point of being totally ridiculous and comparatively easier to destroy, they could have looked beyond dropping a guy off and for him to switch off its shields by asking a crew member comparatively politely for heaven's sake. Furthermore, Carrie fisher/Princess Leia, should have been left to retire gracefully in the depths of obscurity for all she brought to the movie. A total misfire for all movie goers unless you can look past this for what it is, a total failure in entertainment, unless you are totally into yourself and are a freaky fan of no matter this franchise brings.

title: After so many lessons throughout so many years, how could they do it wrong?
review:
After watching TFA 3 times and letting it settle down (a bit) on me, I feel ready to share my opinion. I know there are hundreds (and soon thousands) of funny liners making jokes with the "force" here so I'll spare it and go straight to the point.

They missed a HUGE opportunity to make things right again after the prequels. By "they" I mean Disney, JJ, Lucas, even Kasdan, Williams, Ford - the entire Hollywood. I'll give it a 4 star because it bears the name Star Wars and has some (few) moments to it that mechanically and automatically trigger my infancy memories and feelings, and I'm a helpless fan ruined by the original trilogy myself.

How could they get it so wrong is my wonder. What is so hard to get about SW to make it so wrong after all??? There are so many holes that I could go on and on, many have nailed it here already quite good so I'll just say it to the records what really bothered me most in this "sequel":

To me, the way BB-8 ends up being in his position vs. the way C3PO and R2 end up in the hands of Luke is representative of the main difference between the two. It is a million times less elegant and clever, and this can be said of most other situations too. BB-8 is cute and likable, but R2 is cute, likable and has a personality of his own and doesn't act like a puppy or The Cat in Boots.

If they have gotten that one idea right maybe TFA could be slightly better. The original trilogy - ANH in particular, being the first episode - took its time to develop the situations and characters at the same time the action is developing, and everyone and everything was in the context, and we are taken by the hand to the journey as it unfolds. And that is the most important in any film. It's something very few flicks can pull right, an JJ failed here more than he did with Star Trek IMO. We're not taken to much in TFA, and I feel really really sad to say that.

The magic of the original trilogy is that it makes us feel part of the adventure. JJ treats us like spectators, and the scenes don't disappoint in that sense. He's a good scene maker. It's easy to "like" BB-8, or cheer for the rogue Stormtrooper, or pity for the Victoria's Secret model starving scavenger with fancy brit accent. But not in the deep ways we cheered for Luke, Han and Leia, and even the villains are dubious, shallow, vague because they have no real sense of purpose, no big aspirations. Even the horrible bad guys from the stupid prequel have more depth, and that is unfortunate to say. I'm really sad to say that but it's true, I wish it wasn't. The 80's won't come back, I know. But it was special.

Take Ren for instance: if Darth Vader himself turned "good" again, what in the galaxy could lead his grandson - being the son of major Resistance characters - to become a bad guy and believe he can "finish what he has started"? Vader hasn't started anything in the first place, or killing Luke is still the major objective of the villains after so many years??? Pathetic. And he's a wimp too, making him weak both with the Force and mentally and psychologically didn't add anything to the character, sorry. I won't even mention the master villain, what the hell was that???

Also, where did the first of Luke's lightsaber come from, if he lost it in a bottomless pit of Cloud City in Empire Strikes Back when Vader chopped his hand off (and he built himself a new one for RoJ)??? Or am I missing something here?? They had to put on a Grafflex one in there too didn't they, oh my...

As I said I could go on, there are way too many flaws. And no, Ford does't look like he's having fun. He's old and grumpy and tired and that's how he plays Solo. And Leia... Why would a Rebellion general use so much Botox and care about high heels??? She's a sad shadow of Leia of the past, both physically (that'd be OK time passes for us all) and mentally (that's not OK we get wiser and sager with time). She looks like she can't lead his grandson and some friends on a trip to Disneyland, much less a rebel army against anyone. She wasn't even able to educate her son for god-sakes. The "new old guys" almost ruined the "old old guys", that frightens me because we're about to get more of them in the next films and could potentially kill SW.

That brings me to Luke, I thought he was a wimp too by leaving it all but once again he saved the story: in those short 2 scenes he's in irradiates with charisma and shows he still has the force, even when we only see his mech hand on R2. That alone totally blows it, they should have gone that way that is so powerful, so powerful. He is the saving mystery of TFA to me. When I saw him at the end of the movie, I knew exactly why he got away from all that pathetic friends and stupid galaxy that Disney built around him. I'd do the same if I could run away from the overwhelming hype and oppressing marketing of Disney's Star Wars.

Maybe I'll take a DVD and TV set with my 3 copies of pre-editing trilogy to that island too. Hopes dies last so I'll wait for the next episodes on this. Fortunately no one can undo the original trilogy, it is what it is.

title: I can't call this a Star Wars movie
review:
I just watched it and the first thing that's coming to my mind is : what the heck is this?This movie has too many plot holes, too many idiotic characters, too many stupid jokes, too many downhills...

So basically if you've seen the first trilogy that came out, the one we hold dear in our hearts (Star Wars, The Empire Strikes Back and The Return of the Jedi), you've seen everything in this "The Force Awakens". I mean you take the whole trilogy (and I mean TRILOGY not plot) and you put it in a 2h30 SINGLE movie! It has no personality, no originality, they just took the same script and give it to different actors (well not even all different because you have to include some fan service so everybody and every press will give it a good rate). People complained that the 2nd trilogy was bad but at least it tried something, it had an identity, it had a plot, this one has none!

Now that we covered pretty much the whole plot I will say how this Star Wars is just full of plot holes, a huge disappointment and just raises too much unanswered questions... because yes it's not bad enough that they had the most uninspired story, they had to destroy also the rest of what makes a movie : The actors. No depth, no identity and no charisma. No character development whatsoever, I felt nothing for any of them really, you had nobody to get attached to and please the acting is just plain awful. Rey, she has no family anymore and apparently they won't come back for her said the orange frog in the ridiculous rip off of the cantina so : no background. Finn has no family because abducted as a baby : no background. Solo Junior is just a crybaby who swings his lightsaber everywhere when he gets angry and has family issues because God knows why and frankly I couldn't care less because he just looks like a teenager who has lost his pony so he turned into a "Sith" (I refuse to grant him the title of a Sith Lord). Poe is Jesus, coming back from the dead other than that he's just useless. Leia is back but doesn't really do anything. So we're left with Solo and Chewie who happened to come by in the movie but if they weren't we wouldn't have much left in it because they are the only entertainment we got.

Now I am sorry but you don't come up with a movie that has such a rich universe and say : that's all folks! Seriously, the title appears and the plot lines you read contains already astonishingly gaps that the movie never fills. Okay so the First Order (kind of the Empire, nothing much of a difference so I'll call it Empire) is at war against the Republic and the Rebels because... they seek Luke Skywalker?! I know this sounds silly but they have no other relevant explanations! But how did they come back in force? What the Republic was doing in 30 years? Who's in power? There's a bigger Death Star now ready to blow not 1, not 2 but 5 planets with a single shot (I am not kidding, why being imaginative when you can take a new Death Star?) and nobody cared? Luke had a student turning to the Dark side and he just rage quit, leaving no trace of him?

And this is just the beginning because a gap of 30 years is not enough, there had to be others within the movie like the Force, is that not enough that they had to kill the myth in the Phantom Menace that they had to rape it and give it to the banthas too? Now we're back to the Force is magic but hey who gives a sh*t about the Force, now you can be a coward and annoying as hell with stupid jokes but use a lightsaber just because you can (imagine Jar Jar with a lightsaber, nobody in his right mind would want that). The Force can even control your body now! A novice with no knowledge of the Force whatsoever, who said 1 hour ago that she thought it didn't exist can now use Jedi Mind Tricks, shield her mind against a so called trained Sith and use the lightsaber for the first time against the same so called trained Sith and prevail.

How did the Yoda like creature got the lightsaber? Oh "a good question but for another time" she says...?! Now the movie is making fun of me?

How did Poe survived?

And the map? Good lord what about locating the stars, the planets around the map and setting a perimeter for searching parties? Remember Obi Wan when he tries to locate Kamino? A Padawan came up with the solution. Are the Empire and the Rebels THAT stupid? Then what became of R2? Has he become senile or something? He waits for planets to be blown off, the Empire to come back and the whole galaxy to go ape sh*t before giving the map? Not that it was already obvious since he shut down when Luke left.

All of these things have no sense at all and I could go on about these useless characters such as the commander of the fleet or the commander of the stormtroopers but it's just killing me because I realize that I wanted to like this movie...

This movie treats you like a moron and almost everybody bought it, is this the future of movies? Then we're in for some troubled times... Give me Maul, Tyranicus and Vader back please! All in all it's bad and as long as these movies get high ratings we'll have to endure such garbage in the next decade... 1 star for Chewie and Harrison Ford, 1 for Star Wars effects : How shameful.

title: We've been snookered
review:
Imagine if the following plot was released/leaked before the movie came out and how people would react:

1. Droid with important info lands on desert planet; 2. Droid meets up with orphaned, scrappy youth who becomes main hero; 3. Hero escapes from the bad guys looking for droid (in the Millennium Falcon no less); 4. Hero leaves home world because there is nothing left there for him/her; 5. Hero meets up with old guy who becomes father figure; 6. Old guy tells hero about the Force; 7. Bad guys have giant weapon in shape of planet; 8. Bad guys blow up home world(s) of good guys; 9. Good guys decide they have to destroy giant weapon planet; 10. Hero and old guy/father figure end up together on weapon planet and successfully sabotage it; 11. Old guy/father figure gets killed by the main bad guy (with a light saber no less) right in front of the hero; 12. Good guys destroy weapon planet by targeting the only weak point; 13. Hero leaves alone to find teacher to learn more about the Force.

I tell how people would respond - they would be bull****, which is exactly how I felt after leaving the theater. After all this time they couldn't be a little more original with the story? The production, special effects and battle sequences were OK, but I can't believe this movie is getting so many positive reviews by people who I'm sure are aware of the previous SW movies. If people knew beforehand that the plot was just a retread of the original, JJ and Disney would have never been able to make this movie. As a SW fan (who doesn't consider himself a fan boy), I was really disappointed that this what they came up with after all this time. - fin

title: Episode VIII had better be fantastic.
review:
A fairly long time ago, in a county not so far away (Elstree Studios are an hour's drive away from yours truly), a great adventure took place. Now, J.J. Abrams, in league with the 'House of Mouse', has returned to make a seventh chapter in the franchise, and it's almost identical in plot to the first film, but with only a fraction of the magic and charm.

Daisy Ridley plays Luke sorry, I mean Rey a scavenger on the desert planet of Tatooinesorry, I mean Jakku who becomes involved in the rebellion against The Empire sorry I mean The First Order after she bumps into R2D2 sorry, I mean BB-8, a droid carrying plans to the death star sorry, I mean to the whereabouts of Luke Skywalker. Meanwhile, the First Order are preparing their new weapon, the Death Star sorry, I mean Starkiller Base for use against the rebellion, who are forced to launch a risky counter-attack that sees Rey coming face-to-face with masked villain Darth Vadersorry, I mean Kylo Ren (Adam Driver).

I've learnt to keep my expectations low for Star Wars films since The Phantom Menace, so I can't say The Force Awakens was a massive disappointment; it is what I feared it would be—a rather safe reboot, lacking in fresh ideas, which aims to please younger viewers with flashy visuals, whilst pandering to the older generation by including sly nods to the original trilogy. Personally, I would much rather they had taken a bolder approach: let's be honest they couldn't have got it any more wrong than the prequels.

There's a spark of originality in the form of Finn (John Boyega), a stormtrooper who has a change of heart and joins the rebellion, the production design and effects are incredible, and I admit that the return of Han Solo and Chewbacca warmed even my cynical heart, but on the whole I was left wanting by this latest instalment, particularly the final assault on the Starkiller Base, which was completely bereft of tension. In fact, my favourite moment of the whole film is when Carrie Fisher tries to convey anguish, but her plastic surgery doesn't let her.

title: Disappointing movie
review:
Saw the new one last night. It was decent. I enjoyed watching it. Might even see it again. For a Star Wars fan after so many years this was like a cold glass of water after being stranded in the desert for an extended period. But would probably rank it last among the 7 Star Wars movies so far.

Fin with no training takes on Ren who had extensive training, apparently under Luke as a kid and then for years under this "Supreme Leader". That saber battle should have lasted all of 2 seconds.

Speaking of "Supreme Leader" that title feels like something from a cartoon.

Rey who we are led to believe had been abandoned as a child and has lived as a scavenger with no family or anyone to look after her. She is easily captured by Ren but fortunately she is strong with the force and thus able to resist Ren's mind probing. Then with no prior Jedi training apparently remembers the myths about Jedi powers and remembers she can tell the guard what to do. She too like Fin is able to take on the Ren guy in a saber battle. But she not only lasts longer she had him beat and could have finished him if the planet had not started ripping apart separating them.

I can buy that Fin and Rey are strong with the force. But their skills are too advanced for people with no apparent training.

And yet another death star? What pray tell will the story line be? Solo sums it up with just a few sentences. There is always a single weakness to attack, always a shield someone needs to bring down first.

Then there was Leia. She was supposed to be the next big hope if Luke failed. Decades have passed and she shows no indication she has any more force skills than I do. There is the brief look of agony as Solo gets killed. Part of the problem here I suppose is in the decades since episode VI I have come to expect more from female heroines. Movie would have been much more believable if Leia and Rey had met and there as a scene or two showing Leia providing some training. Our imagination could have filled in that much more took place off camera just as we did with Yoda training Luke.

Inconsistencies: The new order has control of the storm troopers, but not the galactic republic and the restored galactic senate. Leia and her buddies have control of that. Yet with the support of an entire galactic republic behind them Leia's group is still described as rebels.

This movie provides little information on what happened between Vader redeeming himself by killing the emperor and now. Luke tried rebuilding the Jedi order but was betrayed by one person who was apparently Kylo Ren. And that brief explanation is all we get.

The plot and writing had the feel of a fan film. The special effects were much better than any fan film which one would expect with the much larger budget. But there have probably been several fan films that had better Saber fights than the brief ones we get here.

Kylo Ben. No wait, Kylo Ren. Several times in the movie it sounded like they were pronouncing his name like it started with "B". Several times it sounded like "R". These are professional actors. Can someone not have told them what his name was and how to properly pronounce it? In summary, I enjoyed it. I am a Star Wars fan. But reminded me of the original Star Trek movie that seemed to be making a movie for the sake of making a movie and giving fans something to spend money on.
