I saw the movie and it was OK, but definitely not what I was expecting after all of the rave reviews. I think these reviews came from people who never saw the previous movies? I was very disappointed with how the movie flowed.

It appears that the characters were all acting separately. Instead of the interactions shown in all of the previous movies this one was just not flowing like it should have. I expected the same camaraderie and pacing from the other movies. It just seemed choppy.

I was floored when our evil character turned around and lifted his mask to reveal his face so that the audience could see it. It would have been so much more exciting to have him lift the mask slowly, for Han only. Plus, this character is a far cry from the type we had in Darth Vader or even Darth Maul.

I did not like him at all. He was just too flaky - whiny, weird, whatever. He did not strike fear in anyone. We needed a real evil character - not one constantly throwing temper tantrums. He really should have been a cyborg or something - anything but what he turned out to be.

Even the relationships between Kylo Ren, Han Solo, and General Leia were convoluted. I did not feel they were presented in a way that made me feel any connection - even to Han and Leia.

I just hope the next installment makes up for these strange changes and gets back on track to better follow George Lucas' original films.

title: Anne of Green Gables in Space
review:
Does it feel like Star Wars? No. Wonder what Star Wars would look like fast paced & gritty with hard colour grading, editing, & angle shots? You know, like Star Wars fan films? It's filmed in JJ style. Lucas used mostly flat & face shots. Yes it's static way of filming, but it is also a very classic way. It lets you focus on the richness of the scene. Everything was so streamlined in Force Awakens that it felt like a cheap 3D amusement park ride.

But how were the characters? Rey? Daisy Ridley is wonderful, but sadly she's written as a Mary Sue. Literally every action she does is: showing up the boys. & I mean every. single. action. There are at least 28 moments..... in the film where they directly show this to you, then do a camera wink nod - she can take care of herself. But I love her charisma and my "only hope" is to see her in other things besides Disney Star Wars.

Ohh Finn. The new Jar Jar Binks. Ohh wait, Jar Jar actually had a strong character arch & came from a creative well designed species with incredible alien technology. What was Finn? -He gets TRAUMATIZED when his storm trooper friend dies -He frees the man who killed his friend -He murders his fellow troopers on watch patrol....all while LAUGHING........to go AWOL What?????? What's more? They remove Boyega's beautiful SouthLondon accent & make him talk like....a "typical" American. Yes they go out. Even giving him cringe lines like "H3LL NO" and "DROID PLZ" (seriously. they actually put an n-word joke in STAR WARS). Just every typical Hollywood Trope you can imagine. He was a clown buffoon saved by Rey every scene they are together. What's more, his fake US accent is horrible and sounds HOARSE while yelling (which he does a lot). If you thought Anakin and Padme were awkward in the prequels, baby you ain't seen nothing yet. Wow. Do Boyega and Daisy have good chemistry irl? Absolutely! But it's lost when you change accents. Typical Hollywood fare, changing accent for zero reason. It's not convincing to native speakers of the accent. Stop.

Onto design The new Storm troopers look horrendous, okay. We have to see so much of them, and it's these goofy gigantic duckfaces. They also seem to be composed of pure eggshell white nonreflective bristol board.

Lucas exercised a level of Quality Control over Lucasfilm that is now gone. JJ was given Kasdan, Williams, & Struzan. Keys to the kingdom. But what does he do? Sat like a giddy fan-boy, letting them "do their magic". Lucas certainly didn't. He micro managed. The results are obvious.

TFA John Williams score: mediocre

TFA Drew Struzan poster: mediocre

TFA Lawrence Kasdan script: rehash

Experiment made! And the results are...guess what! It really was Lucas' genius that pulled together his 6 films. Lucas even added all of the good elements to Empire Strikes Back. Yes, George Lucas.

another thing, Lucas' Star Wars were loaded with just BIZARRE quirkiness. so much The closest this movie got was BB-8 is traveling at night and the Alien pops up before the screen wipe. Had Lucas made this film, it would have followed BB-8 through the desert and focused on his strange Alien encounters. Like most Hollywood movies, the Aliens are mere cameo props shown for a "weird" gag, not major forces in the narrative

In Conclusion...Star Wars Episode 7 The Force Awakens is THE worst SW film and below every prequel. Lucas said it is "not his story", meaning Not Canon. The closest thing we can get to his treatments are the EU material that yes, still did go across his desk

So please. Don't insult me this fan service JJ fest. Blips. Tiny references. Blowing up Coruscant. Death Star 3 (destroyed in the most passionless way imaginable) With Lucas there was exploration, richness. Now we know why he left the project. Those people didn't understand. It's about Imagination. Wonder. Pushing Boundaries.

Never again will we have wild NEW RISKS like a muppet kungfu master...giant gangster worm who chains up women in bikinis..forest kingdom of man eating bears...outer-worldly pod-racing...arena monsters/catacombs...kamino facilities...downtown courosaunt Any of that. It's just ripoff the originals time. Even Geonosis, also a desert planet, was completely fresh under Lucas's supervision, unlike Jakuu *cough* Tatooine 2.0

Tarkin > Hux

Emperor > Snoke

Boba Fett > Phasma

Darth Vader > Kylo Ren

Darth Maul,General Grevious,Count Dooku too all of these villains remained completely original unlike the bit variations in TFA.

Sadly with Kathleen Kennedy ... quality control lack extends to everything. SW Battlefront, Novels, Comics, everything. She's not an artist & doesn't have Lucas' mind for approving design. and remember, this is Disney, so NO SPACE BATTLES.

speaking of that tensionless lazy Starfighter battle.. Just wow. Even the original A New Hope had Y-Wings to the mix. Each installment added different ship designs. In the sequels had the Mon Calimari Ships, Super Star Destroyers, Frigates. ROTJ introduced A-Wings and Tie-Interceptors. But here we have Only X-Wings and Tie-Fighters....lame. Oh they put a red stripe on them and the lead X-Wing is black. Congratulations. Want WONDER? here's a paint job and a Shiny storm trooper. Enjoy! Give. Me. A Break!

*sigh* it looks like Star Wars is over. I did not enjoy this film one bit. I was bored by the nothing because there was nothing. I followed this film for an entire year. What we're given is an MCU level film. A film that is not re-watchable or even cohesive. I have no desire to watch it again. Why would I? For what? It's a forgettable movie with nothing creative to feed the imagination. It's Hollywood.

You made me appreciate George Lucas that much more.

title: Are critics and consumers that dumb ?
review:

title: Soulless Counterfeit
review:
This was nothing but a high-budget fan fiction.

I had a completely open mind, and during the first half-hour I actually really enjoyed it. And then in true J.J. Abrams fashion, it became apparent that there really was no point, and that it was being made up as they went. The prequels had a long list of flaws, but they at least had heart, whereas this one is a soulless counterfeit.

The viewers who are rating this 10/10 will say that critical reviewers are just looking for something to be upset about. Not true. It's completely reasonable to be disappointed by such a slap-dash, string of stitched-together nonsense presented as a coherent story.

I guess for some fans, no dramatic tension or pacing is needed – just neat ships and fun action – like when playing action figures or video games. And all this talk of "nostalgia" The original Star Wars wasn't good because of "nostalgia." So while some viewers enjoyed the jokes and the self-parodying, force-fed references to other Star Wars movies, what makes a movie work is and always will be competent storytelling.

title: Disappointing rehash (spoiler review)
review:
******MAJOR PLOT SPOILERS BELOW*******

I'm posting this mainly to see if there is anyone else out there who feels the way I do about TFA, I haven't read/watched any reviews yet but the 95% on RT kind of surprised me. I'm not trying to rain on the parade at all here -- I really wanted to like this movie -- but to me it was disappointing. I'm actually kind of jealous of those who really loved it.

Cons: I did not buy any of the major relationships at all, to me this was by far the biggest failing of the movie. Finn/Rey, Finn/Poe, shockingly even Leia/Han. They all felt extremely forced and came across as trying REALLY hard to recapture the chemistry of the Big 3 in the OT. When Poe and Finn rush to embrace after Finn sees him for the first time alive, I was kind of taken aback because to me they just hadn't "gotten there" yet, so it just came off as weird. I don't know what the problem was, the acting, the script, or some elusive, hard-to-quantify, movie magic thing.

The whole movie felt like a point-for-point rehash of A New Hope -- a few nods here and there are cool and would be expected, but TFA went way beyond that. I'm honestly pretty surprised that this script was OK-ed because it is so blatant in parts. Just a few examples:

-The fact that once again a critical bit of info is given to a droid who is left to his (its?) own devices -- said droid is then taken hostage by desert scavengers before being "rescued" by the protagonist.

-All of the ball turret scenes on the Falcon.

-A "scoundrel" type character that makes snarky remarks and likes to use his ship's undercarriage gun to blast baddies while trying to escape.

-Death Star 3 (I'm REALLY surprised they went with this as I thought it was a common problem that people have with ROTJ)

-Cantina scene

Due to the above (and more) I frequently had the feeling that I was watching a straight up second rate remake. Last major problem I had with the movie was that it was just not subtle AT ALL. The worst example being the scenes setting up Finn to leave the First Order. I could practically hear JJ yelling into my ear "HE'S CONFLICTED ABOUT WHAT IS GOING ON RIGHT NOW! LOOK AT HIS FACIAL EXPRESSIONS! -- CAN YOU TELL HE IS CONFLICTED? IN CASE YOU COULDN'T -- LET ME SPELL IT OUT FOR YOU -- THIS CHARACTER IS VERY CONFLICTED!!!"

There were also a few really bad exposition scenes where it felt like characters were just vomiting up important plot points because the script couldn't think of a more clever way to explain the story.

OK so enough of the bad, there were some parts of this movie that I did really dig:

Every scene with Snoke was great. What an awesome character design. When he first came up on screen I was just blown away -- the holograph-making-him-seem-huge trick was a stroke of genius, though part of me wishes he really was that big.

-Lightsaber duels following more after the style that Luke and Vader have at the end of ROTJ (i.e. passionate hacking that looks like they are really trying to kill each other). The only problem was I couldn't get emotionally wrapped up in them in the same way because again, I just did not buy the character relationships.

-Some very cool landscapes: my three favorites being the backdrop as Rey "sandboards" down a dune, the Snoke "throne room", and the bridge where Han bites it.

-The vision sequences when Rey picks up Luke's lightsaber were pure awesome.

So to conclude, for me this movie failed, though in a different way from the prequels. Say what you want about the prequels (and I am not at all a fan -- not trying to stir the pot here -- just want to give some context to my views), but George did not "play it safe" and rehash the OT at all. This movie takes zero risks. And as much as the prequels suffer from general "woodenness", I found TFA's character relationships even less convincing (excluding Anakin/Padme).

title: Episode 8
review:
I can complain about everything that's wrong with Episode 7, but it won't do any good -- what's done is done. Here's what needs to be done in the next episode to get Star Wars back on track:

+ Kylo Ren needs to grow a pair. He started off as a true bad ass, but by the end of the movie he's completely harmless, even laughable. I mean is anyone really scared of Kylo Ren anymore? He lost a light saber duel to a girl who never held (let alone used) a light saber in her life. Heck, he had a hard time taking on Finn who also has virtually no experience using a light saber and isn't even force sensitive. What happened to Darth Maul, Vader, Dooku, Palpatine? -- you know the bad guys who were so skilled with a light saber it took multiple JEDIs to even stand a chance in a saber battle. Snoke mentions at the end that Kylo Ren needs to return to 'complete his training' - - hopefully this entails learning how to use a light saber. Kylo Ren coming back in Episode 8 as anything short of the most evil villain in movie history will ruin this trilogy.

+ Finn needs to go away. Sorry, but it's the truth. He was in a coma at the end of episode 7 and let's hope he remains that way for episodes 8 and 9. Within the first 30 minutes, we learn he's a traitor, coward, and liar. Why would anyone like this character? The fact that he used Luke's light saber in a battle and is not a Jedi is sacrilege to all of the people who grow up with the original trilogy. It's clear as a day Finn's just in the movie for PC reasons which is nonsense. I couldn't care less when he got injured at the end of the movie because he's not likable.

+ Rey needs to train with Luke to become a Jedi in the most epic Jedi training scene in Star Wars history. The fact that she somehow already knows how to use the force, mind-tricks, light saber, etc is going to make this difficult, but it needs to be done. Of course, we don't know why she was able to learn this stuff almost instantaneously while it took Anakin, Luke, Obi-Wan, etc years of training. The movie needs to climax with Luke/Rey battling a MUCH, MUCH more powerful Kylo Ren in an EPIC light saber battle -- a battle that ends in Rey losing an hand, arm, leg, etc.

+ We need a back story. What the heck is going on? Why did Kylo Ren switch to the dark side? Why did Luke give up after Ren turned to dark side (he should be used to it by now)? What were Han and Chewbacca doing for the last 30 years besides looking for the Falcon? What has Luke been doing on his island? Who is Rey and why was she abandoned? Why is Finn against the First Order? Why did Han and Leia separate? What happened to the Empire after the second Death Star was destroyed? How did the First Order rise? Why does Kylo Ren have Darth Vader's mask? Why did that yellow creature have Luke Skywalker's light saber in an unprotected box in her basement? Why does 3PO have a red arm? I was looking forward to hear what happened in the last 30 years since I saw 'Return of the Jedi' and we learn nothing.

+ Stop with the CGI -- This movie definitely cut back on the CGI compared to the prequels, but still used too much. Why was the 'new Yoda' CGI? Why couldn't they use a puppet? The 'new Yoda' was some pretty lousy CGI too -- she looks so fake and we're supposed to find deep meaning in what she's saying? When she first turned around and screamed 'HAN SOLOOOOOO' with that horrible fake CGI face, I felt embarrassed to be a Star Wars fan. And, then there's Snoke -- another CGI character that looks straight out of a 10 year old video game. The original Emperor was much scarier because he was a REAL person.

Some other thoughts:

+ Luke Skywalker being in the movie for 30 seconds and not saying a single word is a really crappy move on Disney's part. I know I'm not the only person who's been waiting 30 years to see Luke on the big screen again and then to pull this crap and make us wait another 3 years is a cheap move -- especially when they made such a big deal about Mark Hamill being in the movie and giving him top billing. Heck, I would have been happy if just said one or two lines but, no, we get him turning around and looking like a crazy homeless drunk.

+ The trailer is misleading -- two of the coolest scenes were 1) Luke touching R2D2 with his robotic hand and 2) Kylo Ren lighting up his light saber in the rain with his knights around him. It turns out neither of these scenes are actually 'real' scenes -- they're just part of some vision Rey has when she touches Luke Skywalker's light saber for some reason.

+ I'm OK with Han dying and it helped to make Kylo Ren look evil by killing his father (which was later ruined in the subsequent saber battle). But I'm not OK with the way it happened. Han should have died in a blaze of glory. This is the guy who, being told he'd freeze to death if he went outside to find Luke on Hoth, responded 'then I'll see you in hell'. And he gets killed by a cheap 'saber though the chest' move. Wrong.

review:
Many months ago now, I decided that I would watch this film as soon as it became available, which meant going to the midnight showing of the film on the day of its release (17th December 2015). I was excited, optimistic, even beatific that not only was my beloved Star Wars returning for its seventh installment, but it was also doing so in the hands of a relatively competent director who seemed to understand just what made the prequels so unspeakably nauseating. From this I could enjoy reassurance that this franchise would be continuing in the same vein as the witty, exciting and genuinely clever original trilogy.

But I was misguided. Oh, how cruel can life be, that one film can generate so much hope, followed all too swiftly by the crushing agony of despair that will be familiar to those who have watched The Phantom Menace. The trailer for this film was exceptional: Ray appeared to be a solitary, intriguing character; Finn's conversion from stormtrooper to Rebellion fighter promised a fascinating ark; Kylo Ren seemed capable of perpetuating the evil of Vader and the Emperor into this new trilogy.

But I can never trust a trailer again. Ray's character shows promise, but is thus far under-developed and quite uninteresting. Finn is a clown, parachuted into the movie for (weak) comic relief more than anything else. And Kylo Ren... Well, without wanting to give anything away for those of you who are fortunate to have not watched this 'movie', you will understand just how pathetic a villain he is when you see him take off his (totally unnecessary) mask. Nothing can prepare you for the superlative lameness of this moment, I assure you.

People speak sometimes about the "bestial" cruelty of man, but that is terribly unjust and offensive to beasts, no animal could ever be so cruel as a man, so artfully, so artistically cruel. JJ Abrams made us trust him. He assured us that this film would mark a departure from the horrible and pointless CGI of the Prequels. So why, oh dear god why, does he feel the need to animate in some pointless octopus monsters which serve no purpose in the plot as a whole, and look neither cool nor impressive? WHY? Why does there have to be another Death Star (just this time slightly bigger and powered by the sun) with exactly the same faults as the previous TWO models? Yes, we wanted this film to return to the themes and quality of the Original Trilogy. That does not mean that we want a feeble copy of Episode IV. Unfortunately, this is exactly what JJ has given us.

This film is full of plot holes and lazy assumptions. Is it better than the Prequels? Just about, and only by dint of the lack of Jar Jar. Having said this, Kylo Ren is weaker even than the wholly undeveloped Darth Maul, Count Dooku and even General Grievous.

As I write this, I am curled up in my bed. I haven't left my room since returning from the film. I'm not sure whether I can ever face the world, and such crushing disappointment, again.

You have been warned.

title: A Star Wars void of character and depth is merely a giant ad for toys.
review:
This movie has about as many (or more) plot holes and inconsistencies as some of the worst B-movies of the Eighties. Nothing makes sense, nothing feels designed to have some meaning or to build drama, instead everything that happens is like a loose succession of trivialities:

Protagonists stumble upon each other as if the whole galaxy was small like a village.

Protagonists don't seem to be able to express any real human emotions, apart from violent outbursts like 8 year olds, or shallow friendships. Nothing feels real. Protagonists turn into friends or enemies without real character development. It's like when you watch 8 year olds narrate stories while they play with their SW toys. Movie plot has the exact same emotional depth as 8 year olds playing with toys, I am not kidding.

Don't expect to hear a new compelling music score, you won't find any. Also don't expect to see new creatures or planets that stimulate your imagination, creature design is just a rehash of what we are used to, NOTHING new is explored, no new planets or sceneries. (you just get the obligatory desert and ice planet, etc... I thought we had a whole galaxy to explore???

Can you believe how shallow the character design is? Apparently there exists an Asian looking gang in this universe whose name is KanjiKlub-Gang. You can't make this stuff up. It's EXACTLY what an 8 year old would choose as name.

Also there is a childish understanding of astronomy, like in one scene having multiple planets just a few thousand miles apart from each other. (the old trilogy had much more scientific accuracy, at least they didn't make such glaring mistakes)

This movie feels like a giant jedi mind trick. It's a TRAP!

title: It ain't broke, so JJ didn't fix it
review:
I have heard quite a bit of hatred about this movie being too much like episode IV: A New Hope, but the one question I have is what would YOU do differently?

Need I remind everybody that when George Lucas tried to do something completely different than the original trilogy for the prequel trilogy, it blew up in his face. What direction can a villain faction such as the first order head into rather than another menacing death star that happens to be not only a death star? In my opinion it was a good decision.

I have also heard hatred that the dialogue was meant for kids and it was. But why is this a bad thing? This was done in the original trilogy and nobody cared because of the breakthrough.

Without giving too much away other than the new death star, I will say that many were a bit tough on this movie because of the high expectations. Is it the best of the series? No way, but it is way better than the prequels including Revenge of the Sith. All the humorous cracks fit in perfectly to give us a reasonable mix of old and new. Yes, there is new as well. What also stood out for me was JJ's ability to strive for an independence of green screen photography and using more real environments as backgrounds for scenes. This gives a more realistic feel that the other movies lacked most of the time.

If it ain't broke, don't fix it. Thank you JJ for making us feel like kids again at the movies.

A note to IMDb: Please look at what percentage of voters have rated this movie 8 stars or higher. Why do you place the 1-star reviews under the best category just because many people have responded to them? It has a 92% rating on rotten tomatoes and an accurate 8.1 on IMDb. You are inadvertently spreading hatred for a kids movie that most people really enjoyed. Rethink please.

title: Worst Star Wars Movie Ever
review:
Where is George Lucas when we need him?

Episode 1 was not very good, episode 2 was decent / good and IMO 3 was really good, but all were original and moved the story along. This movie however, is nothing but a redo of episode 4 with elements from 5 and 6. George Lucas is an amazing Writer / Director. George Lucas's main flaw has always been trying to make an adult dark story but keeping it palatable for kids (by including JarJar, Ewoks). Without these cheesy elements the series would have been much better.

Episode 7 is filled with plot manipulation, all of it aimed at recreating episode 4 with a new cast of characters. Remember when Obi Wan dies in 4? With the new would be heroes looking on? Han Solo dies in the identical way but instead of Darth its Kylo. The end sequence is identical to both 4 and 6. To recreate this the Rebel fleet is destroyed in 2 seconds by the star killer. Apparently everything that happens in this story is to recreate episode 4 nostalgia in audience members.

Another example of plot manipulation / plot holes is that Luke is so intimidated by Kylo Ren he has been in hiding for 10 years. Kylo can barely beat Finn when he picks up a lighsabre (despite Finn just being a Storm Troopet) and is defeated by Rey when she picks up the same lighsabre for the first time. And this guy is the leader of the Knights of Ren? Run Luke Run! So much of how the characters and story are unbelievable like this.

I like Finn and Rey. Both were well introduced, and for the first half of the movie I was excited and hopeful. The villain Kylo Ren is terribly cast. He just look like a nerd. He is not a believable offspring of Solo and Leia. He is not intimidating. He is just bad.

I am so disappointed by this movie. Maybe if someone had not seen any other Star Wars movie this could get a good rating. Otherwise it's hard to understand how it could.

title: A Jar Jar Abrams Sci-Fi Space Opera Spectacle
review:
If you thought Jar Jar Binks was bad, then just wait until you see what Jar Jar Abrams has in store for you.

First off, the writing is very poor and comes over like poorly written fan fiction. This movie lacks a real plot, character development, character chemistry and any logical connection between most scenes. The main villain isn't even menacing, he just feels like a hot-tempered cry baby who throws temper tantrums like a little brat. He even has problems fighting the weakest non-force sensitive characters in close combat because he suddenly forgets how to use his force powers thanks to the awful writing. All of the supporting characters, even returning ones, are extremely shallow. Only the main character and one very beloved returning character have anything redeemable about them, and the latter is only on screen for about 30 seconds.

The directing is also abysmal. There are just so many unflattering camera angles, poorly choreographed as well crudely visualized scenes and the pacing is simply awkward. Jar Jar Abrams never went to film school, and oh boy, his abysmal directing skills really show in this movie. The only thing that Jar Jar Abrams seems to have gotten right was copying the aesthetics of the Original Trilogy, although he completely fails at implementing it in a creative and artistic way to please the audience.

Only the final scene can bring any redemption to this train-wreck, but it is not enough to save it from being a bad film. If you only care about flashy lights shown in an awkward manner, then this is the film for you. Otherwise stay away. 3/10

title: Disappointing
review:
Star Wars The Force Awakens 3/10 I was, unfortunately, very disappointed with the new JJ Abrams directed Star Wars.

As a 2015 Disney kids movie it was OK, as a movie in general it was so-so, as a Star Wars movie, it was bad.

Story is basically retelling of A New Hope, but with a female lead and very weak antagonist. And trust me, weak Kylo Ren as a character is. Childish, prone to tantrums and unsure of himself. Everything the Sith were not. He gets into a single sabre duel and manages to lose, to someone with zero training. He is also "drawn to the Light." WHAT?! No one is drawn to the light, Light requires disicpline and dedication, you are drawn to the Darkside. Drivers acting was good, the character is just fundamentally flawed.

New lead couple aren't great, but they aren't bad either. Lead character Rey is by far the most capable being in the universe ever. Not only can she fly Millennium Falcon just by looking at it, only Han was supposed to know how to do that, she flies it better than him and also knows how to fix it better than Chewie. Just because she can. She is also able, with no instruction or training, to use Jedi mind tricks and not only overpower but also defeat in sabre duel the Master of Knights of Ren, movies main foe, Kylo Ren. One tough lady.

Force Awakens suffers from incoherence, possibly due to numerous rewrites.

Chewbacca is by far the best part of Force Awakens and Ford does well as Han Solo.

Last note; I really hate it when they have stuff in the trailers which is NOT in the movie. False marketing by definition.

Leader of the bad guys is Supreme Leader Snoke. He looks like a badly done Gollum from LOTR.

Force Awakens has a bad plot full of holes, and practically no character development.

title: Not perfect but an excellent starter for a future wider scope of the Star Wars Universe
review:
Well first thing is its a whole lot of fun !!

I can see what JJ has done here which is to introduce new characters as well as reviving the older ones. This creates a huge nostalgia trip and gives you a very familiar setting.

The story is nothing new granted and I can understand avid Star Wars fans who are well versed in the expanded Star Wars universe that may be a bit disappointed. Having said that as a stand alone film it is far from disappointing and for the younger audience this is a new story.

The new characters are great, Fin an ex Stormtrooper plays a rather naive young man who is clearly trying to impress the girl Rey. Rey takes the lead however yet Fin is not just a tag along buddy. Rey certainly seems like the most interesting character with the most depth, a scavenger from a desert planet who doesn't know her parents ( sound familiar )

Ren as the bad guy seems more like a petulant child early on who hes a lit of anger issues. Cant say too much more without spoilers although I wish he had kept his helmet on.

Poe is the dashing Xwing Pilot as part of the resistance and he is quickly separated from his sidekick BB8. BB8 is a very likable character and is an R2 replacement but slightly cuter.

You then have other characters such as supreme leader Snoke, Captain Phasma ( who looks awesome ) and the quite scary General Hux.

On top of that Han, Leigha, Luke, Chewie, C3P0 and R2 all return in varying degrees.

What we end up with in story terms is a bit of a reboot of a New Hope with slightly different elements. This is not a terrible thing as for older fans its a great nostalgia trip and for newer fans its a great introduction to the Star Wars universe.

You will however leave the cinema knowing the previous 6 films wanting more answers as to why things have turned sour again. As a standalone film it works on all levels but is slightly vapid in depth and at times could have done with a slow down in pace.

It seems JJ tried to cram as much as possible into one film to move the sage forward, JJ is of course not directing the next instalment so I can see there being a lot more depth in the next 2 films ( plus 2 or 3 more expanded universe films )

I just hope that the following films can find some emotion and spirit that is somewhat lacking in the Force Awakens.

I will look forward to a second viewing but one thing Force Awakens does do is puts you back in the Star Wars universe with a great big bang !!

May the Force be with you !

title: The Force Awakens into a bunch of nonsensical fan film
review:
Ever since George Lucas sold STAR WARS to Disney company, I feared about the future of these movies. I knew it would never be the same, I knew it would never have the same amount of depth, substance, soul, imagination and creativity. I knew that at the helm of J.J. Abrams & Disney company it will degenerate into generic fast paced action film and will lose its essence, magic and mythology. That is exactly what happened to The Force Awakens. Like Mace Windu said: "Our worst fears have been realized." For a STAR WARS fanatic and a huge fan of George Lucas such as myself who loves so dearly all six previous films and who truly understand the mythology and core of the saga, it was very bitter watching episode VII.

The film is a nonstop fast paced action and a showcase of well-known relics from Original Trilogy. The new characters lack development, therefore you can't invest in them emotionally. You have no idea what motivated Kylo Ren to join the dark side in the first place or what made him do all the things in the movie. What hurts me the most is how greatly they misunderstood STAR WARS, The Force and Jedi philosophy. The concept of The Force, a mystical energy field created by all living things (basis for spirituality) was completely mocked and ridiculed in Force Awakens. It became a simple nerdy tool for "probing" mind, throwing people around and freezing shots in the air. First time Rey heard about The Force, she was instantly able to perform a mind trick and do all the silly things with it. In STAR WARS, the lessons the hero must learn are those of the Jedi Master. They combine morality, spiritual faith and strict physical discipline. The Jedi use The Force for knowledge and defense and their greatness lies in handling The Force with wisdom and not with comedy and nonsense. Jedi possess almost magical powers that reflect a lifetime of study, discipline and acquired wisdom. Episode VII destroys this mythical aspect. I missed those perfect memorable conversations given by Lucas - for example Yoda in the prequels was like Dalai Lama in space - Lucas's films had heart, soul, depth and substance. Abrams especially misunderstood the core of the saga - he thinks it's just about action, spaceships and lightsabers. But the STAR WARS saga is a theatrical soap opera in space. It is about family, family problems, about fathers and sons, friendship, love, rise, fall, redemption, mythology and spirituality. That's why it resonated with millions of people around the world. I can't help myself but I think The Force Awakens was a huge disappointment for the hardcore fans of previous six films.

The Force Awakens lacks dialogue and conversations and is just an action fan film with comedy elements that steals ideas and scenes from the Original Trilogy. The originals and the prequels were a monument of human imagination and had great space opera like theatrical conversations, beautiful visuals and amazing music. For example one of the themes of The Phantom Menace was about letting go, about having organisms realize that they must live together and they must live together for mutual advantage. Not just humans but all living things and everything in the galaxy is part of a greater whole. That's basically the idea of midichlorians and the Force, and the realization that Gungans and people of Naboo must live together, in this case the most unlikely character Jar Jar becomes a central figure that brings two nations together. I loved how it taught you lessons like:"Fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. Hate leads to suffering." or the scenes with Anakin and PadmÃ© in AOTC were touching: "Attatchment is forbidden. Possession is forbidden. Compassion, which I would define as unconditional love is essential to a Jedi's life. So you might say, that, we are encouraged to love." We didn't get any of the classic dialogue and themes that would have meaning in The Force Awakens.

To sum it up, The Force Awakens is a shallow reboot of A New Hope but without any mythology, soul and depth. It bets on nostalgia and gives you nothing new, nothing that would touch you and is a huge letdown for the hardcore fans.

title: A beautiful empty shell
review:
I am a big Star Wars fan. I'm however not a Star Wars nerd, I couldn't tell you what race Yoda belongs to or what Boba Fett's spaceship name is but I know enough about the Star Wars universe to understand it. To me it is an exceptional coherent and amazing setting for space adventures, and up to today always had been.

Remember how you felt in Episode I when you learned that the Force could be measured in one's blood sample? Well take this feeling and multiply it by at least 3 and this is how you will most probably feel after Episode VII.

First the good. The visuals and special effects are sumptuous. The return to the practical effects delivers the original Star Wars touch and this in undeniable. Most actors do a very good job. OK that's it.

Spoilers ahead.

Now to the bad. Where is the story? Everything seems a rehash from episodes IV and VI. Not only is the story paper thin and filled with gaps and deus ex machinas, a lot sacred star wars "facts" just get destroyed in this movie.

  • Han Solo and Chewie popping out of nowhere and literally "bumping" into main characters in the middle of space, cause you know, the universe is a village now. - R2D2 hibernating for decades but then waking up to a convenient time without ANY reason. - Non-jedi able to fight with a saber laser on par with a (semi?) trained Sith. - Sith able to sense the presence of Han Solo (who can't use the Force) over a great distance but not when he's standing 10 meters behind him. - Force sensitive character (Rey) able to pull of Jedi Mind tricks without ANY kind of training. Also mentally resisting a trained Sith. - Zero background on the Solo-Organa family drama, which in my opinion is the core of Episode's VII story as far as I can tell. Son got trained by Luke himself and then turned to the Dark Side. That's it. - Zero talk about the force, the balance of good and evil, cheap philosophy, in short all the things we loved about Star Wars and what embodied the first 6 episodes. - Generic dialog and lack of depth for ALL characters. - Except for the opening theme, I could hardly recognize John William's work here. Even the soundtrack felt generic.


This is what annoyed me the most, and I'm not even talking about the new deathstar-planet thingy, every second review complains about that already.

I'm not disappointed, I am angry. Visually the movie feels like an authentic Star Wars and I would give it 10/10 hands down. But why was everything that made the Star Wars universe unique and adored left behind to create a soulless space action flick.

title: Wall-E meets Voldemort
review:
A big disappointment.

There is no story, the acting is weak and the movie is too violent. The only good elements are the characters from Star Wars 4 to 6, the original series. Most of the time it feels like they've been brought back for no real reason.

The good thing are the space scenes which were quite impressive in Imax 3D.

I will not go to see Star Wars 8.

The chicks are Mary Sue are lame and feel inauthentic. The way we're introduced to each of the old classics was exemplary. This reboot is not. I hate it.

I was thrilled by the graphics of the movie, which was great even to this day, as it was a immeasurable experiential leap for me from watching the movie Weera Saradiel. As in most popular Hollywood movies, the kind-hearted, strong n' protective, supportive, Black guy dies before the movie ends, leaving the "stronger" protagonist white guy (gal in this movie) taking the fight over. The black guy is usually an honest subservient, less intelligent, humble, army-worker serving the best interest of the white guy/gal. There is no cool science, no technological advancement, no romance, no kisses. But politically correct to have had a dominant female protagonist, not playing a role merely as a sex object, which men often fall in love with. title: Nostagia fueled mess
review:
The Force Awakens has a huge score on IMDb, yet it also has some of the worst reviews. While I certainly don't think the film deserves a rating above a 5, I also am confused at people giving anything below.

TFA was an enjoyable adventure with fantastic SFX, wonderful puppetry and some well timed humorous moments. Unfortunately it suffered from some terrible acting from its lead actress. It also took far too much story line from ANH. It contained some of the worst plot holes that I've ever seen in a film and some of the editing made for some very confusing scenes. It was brilliant at tapping into the feel of the original trilogy but forgot to take any risks. This is a film that is terrified of letting down its fans.

I have no doubt that this film will have its loyal followers. If you want a brainless, episodic kids sci fi, then this is the film for you.

title: The praise is truly unfounded.
review:
**** SPOILERS AHEAD ****

With all the praise following the release of The Force Awakens, I was kind of expecting more, despite my initial expectations being rather modest. In all honesty, I am confused with the positive feedback, because the film provides very little to justify it. Is it just a reaction to the lingering memory of the ineptly written and directed prequel trilogy or simply fandom enthusiasm spilling over to the general movie audience, I don't know. It is definitely a very competently made film from the technical standpoint, which is to be expected having in mind the people involved (director, cinematographer, writer, score composer, ...). But where the artistry and original/clever ideas are to be expected they are not to be found. While I am not a huge fan of the original trilogy or the prequels, both of these trilogies offer a lot more than this installment. From the originality, sense of wonder and technical achievements in the original trilogy, to the world-building and unchecked imagination in the prequels (putting on the side Lucas being totally not in his element both in the directing and writing department). Despite how much the prequels were weak, I was way more intrigued by them than with The Force Awakens. The amount of details in which The Force Awakens copies New Hope and somewhat less the sequels I found embarrassing to witness. You have your orphaned child left on sand planet, now grown up, discovering its hidden potential and saving the day, your standard cutesy emotional droid, a family member of the heroes falling to the dark side but struggling with the light, and a planet destroying weapon with a weak spot. And it's all done rather superficially, in all honesty. As I mentioned earlier, everything from the technical standpoint is very good, but once you scratch the surface, you realize it's all a shiny facade, including the zany/funny exchanges between the characters. The first alarm I got was right off the bat in the way Finn was written. His mannerism and behavior is so out of place for a person kidnapped as a boy and raised to be a soldier in a military dictatorship. For points to proper characterization of such individuals think of Solider with Kurt Russell. Then there is Rey with her magically appearing skills that help propel the plot whenever it's needed. Someone called it video game characterization, where characters happen to be able to perform unexpected feats exactly when and where required. The constant convenient setups just become too predictable too soon, from the way Rey and Finn find the Millennium Falcon, unguarded, unsecured and power it up without any trouble, to the light sabre being stashed with Maz, where Han Solo just happens to take Rey and Finn. The way the shield of the starkiller base is lowered is a colossal joke. It's all very calculated, terribly unimaginative and predictable, and I'm not letting myself being bedazzled with a clever scene or two (Rey's vision is a conceptually very well realized segment) and funny exchanges. It's mildly fun, but above all weak and derivative, definitely not a classic which will history, as always, show.

title: Not worth the hype
review:
I am not a film critic, just a film lover so I will just share my thoughts. No matter how many "Star Wars" movies are made, none will ever fare well next to the original trilogy. Back then the technical advances were astounding. I did not see this in 3D and since the original wasn't in 3D, I am comparing apples to apples. I am not an expert in film technology and I doubt that most people watching films are. However, after 40 years of advances, I was surprised that I didn't see any significant differences. In fact, I felt that the original was much more memorable. I will never forget the feeling I had when it started with the space ship going over our heads. Now that was noticeable advancement with the wow factor. This one fell flat in comparison.

I was most excited to see Hans Solo and Princess Leah's returns. Needless to say how disappointed I was in Ford's and Fisher's stiff performances. I realize they are both seniors and aged but their characters should have been written to portray that rather than as action hero's. While Hans Solo's death was shocking and extremely sad, at least he won't be back as the hero again. I would have preferred that the character would not have been in the film so that my memory of him would have been that of the rugged pirate he was in his youth.

The story was a repeat of the original, the Resistance defeating another bad intent galaxy. Nothing new there.

The only redeeming part of the movie was the cast of the new young adventurers. I truly hope that the next part of this trilogy will bring fresh new stories for these fresh new stars.

title: Its a disappointing remake :(
review:
I was really disappointed with the story. There is not a single piece of the story, which was not somehow "stolen" from the old films.

This film is a boring remake without any new ideas (although there are amazing actions and visual effects).

A droid has some useful information on a desert planet?! The X-Wings destroy a new "death-star" by flying through a narrow entrance? There is an energy-shield, which protects this "death star" and it can be de-activated from the planet? The new "Darth Vader" interrogates a little girl?!

I really liked the visual effects and the new characters (Finn and Rey). The new droid is also cool. But this film has the first place on my own "Worst of Star Wars"-list.

title: Trite and redundant
review: Well I really didn't expect much when I saw that they were going to try and make another Star Wars and I didn't get much. This movie is trite and redundant. You know there is definitely room in movies made from previous films for references to its predecessor but this film just has the same thing happen that happened in the previous films (just bigger)and thinks you won't notice. Finn is a terrible character. You don't know why he does what he does and he really has no reason at all to be in the movie except to be annoying. Ray would have been an interesting character if you knew more about her from the beginning. And who is God's name came up with the villains in this movie. At first when I saw the big bad I thought I was in a Marvel film and not Star Wars, come on people. And the Darth Vader substitute is just some whiny boy in black clothes. This movie has the worse dialog that I have ever heard. Listening to Harrison Ford speak became almost painful and Carrie Fisher was worse. When the movie was over my daughter asked me where the real Star Wars characters were? I was asking the same question.

title: Very Disappointing Episode
review:
One of the success factors of Star Wars was the simple story, somewhat naive, and each episode in this amazing story is dealing with another subject / issue / idea

In this new movie, the writers tried to get everything from all the old episodes in one movie. Disney also tried to add some success characters and scenes from other successful movies that has nothing to do with Star Wars.

So basically, if you are going to watch the movie just to see all the hero's from the past episodes and great scene that look exactly like in the older episodes (only this time in HD) - have fun.

===> BUT, if you are looking for a good story: forget it. it's not there. get ready to be disappointed.

title: Absolutely Gutted
review:
Slight Spoilers ahead.

I was so excited to see this film, booked my tickets ages ago and went saw it on the opening night.

I knew it had to be good to live up to everyone's exceptions, but watching JJ Abrams make a really good effort on Star Trek, I was excited.

I am so disappointed with what I saw. It was a rushed ditch effort at a plot, with no character development, poorly timed jokes that fell flat, and a villain that was not a villain.

I walked in to the cinema expecting and hoping for a gritty serious extension to the Star Wars universe, and left feeling like I watched a Disney family adventure.

More importantly, how does a Storm Trooper from the sanitation department know how to take down a death star? Absolute sh*te.

Damn you Jar Jar Abrams.

title: Disney Star Wars.
review:
Well..

I didn't have any New Hope for this new installment, and it just as worse as I could imagine. I don't consider myself as a deep SW fan, but I respect the material and appreciate what Lucas created. I like to imagine, when I watch the first episodes (4-5-6) what could have been a very nice experience at the theatre at that time, considering how impressive was the technology compared with what came before it, without any cartoon CGI, with a fresh John William score.

What can I expect. First, Disney buying the Rights, second Mr.Jar Jar Abram directing. Third and final, removing all the rich Expanded universe, declaring it as non-canon. HAHAHA

How can it go wrong? You know quickly something is gone, as the camera work and fast-paced scenes, the JJ Abram-touch : it is simply not a Star Wars movie. Character buildup never reach anything, shock value and cheap trills, never ending Deus Ex machina situations typical of the director. Something is gone.

Horrible script, with a committee approved check cases. Over-Inflated hype (which nowadays is standard, as the modern movies budget goes for a marketing more than twice the cost of the movies themselves (yes, an army of sold-reviewers can cost a lot). It is not a movie, it is a meticulously calculated Product. It look and feel like a contract were the stressed director had 2 years to quickly come up to whatever-something to please the Disney committee approval. End up as a rushed product.

The movie do not respect what has been done before, there show zero understanding of material and even destroying what the first protagonists fought for. I came to understand that Star Wars is a series of 6 movies, a complete saga with the rise and fall of Darth Vader. Thanks George.

And as far as the 3 prequels had quite cringe-worthy dialogues and unbelievable action scenes, the main story was finally more than respectable, with new twists and a Star Wars feel to it. At least some kind of a conclusion (for me).

I do not accept, nor I will, how they wrote Han Solo, Leia and Luke. Kill Solo, Leia in a Resistance, Luke rejected. Don't expect any explanations of what happened, or try to understand how it ended up like that. Disney nor J.J. knows. BS. The director, as always, used again a representative group of emo teenagers, unbelievable and unreliable. Watch (Star Trek, Super 8, Cloverfield or Lost). That doesn't feel in any ways in a galaxy far away but just your average American culture right next door with typical nuclear family problems and frustrations. Oh. and Hitler WW2 logic. Great stuff.

Talking about teenagers, just explain me how a Darth Vader-wannabee kid without a real cause, manipulated by a not so mysterious Golum-type, can have a sufficient amount followers to create a Death Star 3.0 simply 10X larger that the last one... As easy to destroy as the last one in the same way. They don't have an empire nor the resources! Answers : Simply because the movie say so. Accept it or leave it.

I prefer not talk about Mary Sue the heroine. She is the sole representation why this movies does not belongs in this series. As far as I am concerned, I consider this EP7 and what come after has "non-canon."

I came to understand as we all grow up, that modern soul-less movies sequels, especially made from different directors are just to ignore. The Force Awaken... What awoke exactly? Still trying to find out.

The force may keep sleeping...

title: Time has not healed this wound
review:

title: 10 out of 10 my ***!!!
review: Whoah!!! Where to begin? Well I am not a fanboy crazy of the Star Wars universe but I was 9 years old in 1977 and saw the first (Episode IV) movie in a 70s fleapit cinema in the north of England and loved it, bought the excellent Marvel comic adaptation comics, bought the action figures and toys (Boy! were they a rip off) etc.... Didn't hate the prequels but was appropriately unimpressed with them. And now at the end of 2015 I get to watch "the movie highlight of the year", "the film fans have been waiting for", "the resurrection of the Star Wars legacy" and well..... 1: The Story. It's basically a remake of Episode IV. A droid has important data to help the rebel's cause and is discovered by a young romantic protagonist in a back end of nowhere part of the universe. The empire has a planet weapon of mass destruction and wants the data. and... if you've seen the first movie you'll know how the rest pans out. 2: The Acting: Harrison Ford may sadly be too old for this kind of role and he had a nasty accident during the filming and this I conclude is the reason for what can be euphemistically called a lacklustre effort by him in the role that gave him his career. John Boyega is way out of his depth in a role that requires him to show a guilt ridden stormtrooper who moves towards the lighter side of the force (To UK readers who are Ah emm of a certain age) he reminded me of a talented young actor plucked from the set of Grange Hill and dumped on the set of Hollywood's biggest movie in production and told to do your best unfortunately it isn't good enough. Daisy Ridley was fine and was for me one of the few highlights in this movie, she shows range, enthusiasm and brings a likability to her character Ren. I actually wish Oscar Isaac wasn't in this movie as he is one of the half a dozen or so actors in the last few years who are really worth keeping your eye on (checkout "A Most Violent Year") and I spent most of time when he wasn't on screen (which is a chunk of this film) waiting for him to show up. Adam Driver plays Kylo Ren (the new Darth Vader) and I'm sorry folks but it does not look good when even a trainee Lord of the Dark Side shows a bad case of Beverly Hills teenage angst. Mark Hamill and Carrie Fisher are only in this movie for seconds (literally in Mark's case). 3: Direction and Story: Weak and derivative on both accounts especially the story which is IMHO the most egregious offence inflicted on Star Wars fans in this movie. I bet Kasdan is laughing his *** off all the way to the bank. To sum up: It's the equivalent of The Artic Monkeys rerecording The Who's Quadrophenia with Pete Townshend brought in to supply a few vocals and guitar licks and the rest is just respectful if plodding cover versions and 21st century digital remastering. A very weak 5 out of 10.

title: JJ, put down the Planet Killing Planet...
review:
JJ, Put down the Planet Killing Planet and step away from the tired, old, over used, broken plot line!

Its a shame that this film had to go back to something so boring as much of it was a pleasant watch.

My 6 year old wouldn't do something which had failed twice for a third time, so why is the dark side so obsessed with super weapons when they ALWAYS get blown up? Talk about having all your Force Eggs in one basket!

I'd guessed that Han Solo was a goner in this film after seeing that Harrison has wanted him killed off at the end of Empire Strikes Back a number of years ago. I think perhaps he only accepted the role on the proviso that he was capped.

Disappointed with the choice of Adam Driver as Kylo Ren - Really weak actor I thought and why mask the voice like Vader without having an injury reason? They had that with the collapse of the 'Luke School of Jedi' plot line but missed it.

If this storyline had been written by someone else, then Disney would have sued for Plagiarism as its 'A New Hope' all over again.

Really poor effort. I've scored it 5 because it has places it can go but lets be clear...you pull out another planet killing planet and I'm out of the theatre and wanting my money back.

title: Top Two In Star Wars Movies
review:
I have no idea why there is so much hate on this movie. This is one of my favorite movies ever! This passed the original by a complete landslide. There are three very critical reasons why it is better than the original.

A+

title: Star Wars Episode VII: A Painful Generational Gap
review: I'm nineteen years old and a movie like this is one of the reasons everyone hates on my generation. This is mainly because the role of the mentor, so cherished in the Star Wars universe, was made to look entirely unnecessary. I mean, it took Luke failure after failure before he could deflect those training lasers with his father's lightsaber; a new weapon clumsy in his hands. And if it wasn't for old Ben Kenobi in his head would he have switched off his targeting computer and known that the force would be with him, always? Or what about those painful days training on Dagobah, which wouldn't inaugurate Luke as a Jedi until frustration and failure at a critical moment? Luke Skywalker's quest to become a Jedi was one ridden with struggle and redemption. Not so, it seems, for our new protagonist, Rey. It appears as though she doesn't need a mentor when she can apparently call upon the force at random to mind-trick storm troopers and win a lightsaber duel. She defeats an antagonist whom from what I can tell has trained with the force for years, even though just a few days ago she was scrounging Star Destroyer debris. In the words of Han Solo: "That's not how the force works." The movie seems to forget who Luke's character was when modeling Rey after him. Sitting in the theater I felt myself sarcastically thinking that Luke wasn't so great after all while watching Rey slash through Kylo's armor and Poe Dameron miraculously blow up a space station a hundred times the size of the death star. I guess we're just trying to show all you old farts out there that we the millenials don't need a teacher or a wise one in our lives to be the best. Anybody can pick up Anakin's lightsaber and be a winner. At least, that's what it felt like watching this movie.

title: Can we stop with the remakes...please
review: Can anyone tell me why these ships miss each other with lasers? These space ships and inter-galactic stuff is super high tech. Why aren't their guns / lasers computerized? why wouldn't computers auto target ships? why is it, that with this super high technology that you couldn't target enemies that are like 1-5 AU away with near light-speed lasers? Just shoot, wait 8-40 minutes and boom, opponent is dead, it's over. God star wars is stupid. it always was...even the first one. their stupid lasers on their high tech yet somehow primitive space ships miss only to heighten the moment and make you think the heroes are cool cause they can dodge lasers. even today with our garbage human technology on earth we have computerized targeting systems...star wars doesn't make sense. let it go. drop it. star wars sucks and you all know it.

title: Warning: has spoiler. Delete the movie, all of it and try it once again. Please!
review: This was a remake of Star Wars 4. Another Death Star, another person from a deserted planet, becoming a Jedi. Plot: Droid has a secret map. It escapes to a desert-planet where the hero finds it by chance. Another Death Star. The villain wants to look like and speak like Darth Vader. But he has no physical problem!
