title: amazing return to the star wars universe
review:
We've waited.... and waited..... and here it is! The Force Awakens is everything we've come to love about Star Wars. It's big, it's epic, it's spectacular. And underneath, there's actually a big heart to it all. You get a sense from watching it, that it was made by true fans of the series. I won't give away any real spoilers- but rest assured Jar Jar Binks does not put in an appearance, so remain calm.

The good guys are very likable, I thought the relationship between Ray and Finn worked out very well. It gave the film it's emotional anchor.

The villains are pretty much what you would expect, but the filmmakers threw in a few twists about them that were interesting.

Add some terrific battle sequences, and you get a very welcome return to the greatness of Star Wars. Go and see it (but you already know you will). Take a friend or a family member. You'll have a great time. Because that's what these films are about when it comes down to it.

Overall, Force Awakens shows off some snazzy visual effects combined with a compelling story and great characters. It won't disappoint.

title: The true attack of the clones.
review:
FA is rather a nostalgic clone than a continuation of the Saga. It brings back some of the old characters/actors, although mostly with the over-the-top feeling of a Comic Con convention, "omg, is it him? is it her?". It also brings back the cheesy atmosphere of 4-6, in opposition to the darker and more dramatic tone of 1-3 (which I had liked, because it gave more credibility to the dark side, making it scarier, and positively accentuating the contrast between good and evil). And it copy-pastes a LOT from the old trilogies. There is not much interesting here and definitely nothing innovative. Just a comfortably numb variation on the theme, which feels pleasantly familiar to some, but so familiar to be unexciting for those who were hoping in something new.

Lucas may have made mistakes, but he always experimented and innovated, and I respect him for this. Disney and JarJar "I-want-to-be- Spielberg" Abrams cowardly decide to entertain with the known. Like they've explicitly said, their aim was just to "make a film which could please the fans". And apparently they only considered those fans who've hated 1-3.

It's not all bad though. The CGI are more realistic and feel less invasive than in 1-3. Most actors are good, and a female lead is a nice choice. The film itself would be quite good, if it was a reboot. But it is a continuation, and I give three stars because I am disgusted by how they have literally copy-pasted the old trilogies, in the most shallow and commercial way. They've cloned everything, the story, the dynamics, and some aspects of the new characters. Even the new bad guy, Kylo Ren, is a laughable copy of Darth Vader, continuing the tradition of "Luke I am your father" with a spectacular lack of imagination. But at least Darth Vader was imposing, while Kylo would not scare a cat. He remembered me a bit of Draco Malfoy from Harry Potter, weak and insecure behind a mask of aggression, behaving like a spoiled child, and acting evil to please his model (for Draco his father, for Kylo is Vader) while living on his shadow.

Talking of Harry Potter, I am noticing more similarities: Rey is somehow like Hermione (strong, intelligent, beautiful, brave) and Finn is somehow like Ron (jumpy, rather sweet than beautiful, a bit clown and not so strong), and we even have an almost identical Voldermort in that giant dark smoky thing with no real face. It is clear who is Dumbledore, so now we just miss Harry Potter, and then they can all start fighting with light wands.

Did they do this intentionally? Putting hidden elements of Harry Potter to take advantage of its working formula, just like they've copied the story of the previous SW instalments? I do not know, and I do not care. I have seen enough and I am not interested in their offer. It is all a bit of a cheap soap opera with poor artistic and storytelling value and full of plot holes and contradictions. Like (LITTLE SPOILER) Kylo, the son of Solo and Leila, trained by Luke, turns evil like the father of Luke did, and takes Vader as model of evilness even worshipping the rests of his burned mask, although he had turned good again before dying. Seriously, who wrote the script, Barbie and Ken? What should we expect from episode 8, the return of the Pokemons?

Forget it. Star Wars is dead. Congratulations Disney.

title: The worst Star Wars so far, story wise
review:
The Force Awakens is a lazy mess. It's a rehash of mostly the first film and parts of the next two. Absolutely riddled with plot holes.

Kylo Ren - this is one seriously weak and confusing character. I get they are trying to show shades of Anakin's petulance in him. That he idolises Vader. But let's think for a moment. Vader was long dead before Kylo was born. Vader gave up his life to stop the Empire and redeemed himself. Anakin became a force ghost. Anakin wanted to control the galaxy to enforce peace, he really wasn't interested in the Death Star or annihilating planets. He honestly thought he was the good guy. For some unknown reason, Kylo idolises a Vader that never existed and was never redeemed. Finish what you started? What does he mean by this? Why would Kylo idolise a grandfather he never knew over a mother, father and uncle he did? Why doesn't force ghost Anakin appear to him at some point and tell him he's on the wrong path? This character is so weak that they have him kill his father in a cheap, predictable turn just to try to give him some depth. Shameless. Kylo also talks about being pulled to the light - this is something new in Star Wars canon. The light side has no pull - it requires discipline and sacrifice. The dark side has a pull because it is seductive. Just bad writing. And why is he named Ben? Han and Leia have no emotional connection with Kenobi.

Finn - maybe it will be explained in the sequels, but this is another character who makes no sense. Either the Empire/First Order utilise some strong behaviour/mind control on their troops and officers, or these are all just really evil people who have no problem massacring villages and blowing up planets. The fact that Finn appears to exercise free will suggests that it has to be the latter, which opens up all sorts of problems and questions. Stormtroopers by the way have learned how to shoot finally. And the Star Wars blasters all now pack a punch and throw people back on impact - odd considering they are meant to be piercing lasers. I am also uncomfortable with the deliberate pushing of the mixed race couple we will no doubt see in the next two films. Considering the background of the director, it gives fodder, perhaps justifiably so, for so called "racists" to complain (ie. people of European origin free of self loathing who object to being told their race and culture needs to be bred out). It wasn't necessary for the story for these two to become a couple, or for Finn to be black. But you can't even please the left, who have called Finn's antics "racist" or conforming to black stereotypes, like the "sass" and over the top enthusiasm/aggression. My chief problem is where did he learn this behaviour from? He was taken from birth and raised as a Stormtrooper - was his Stormtrooper commander Will Smith? I don't blame the actor for any of this. He's just doing what JJ told him to do.

Rey - probably the worst offender of all, character wise. The embodiment of the currently very popular "girls can do everything boys can do, only better, and without any training, practice or experience!" trope. Rey appears directly out of Twitter/Tumblr/SJW fantasy. Despite being all of 100lbs, she fights off multiple thugs and Stormtroopers with ease. She knows Han's ship and technology better than he does, despite never having been on it. And despite having never used one before, she outdoes the main villain in a lightsaber duel and physically overpowers him - not a huge man by any means but certainly above average in size who'd probably have approximately double her strength. Yet he's unable to overpower her from a position of advantage because Hollywood girl physics. Can you imagine Luke in ANH showing up midway through the film and destroying Vader in a lightsaber battle? This is way stupider, but we accept it because girlpower I guess.

Poe - probably the only of the new characters with not many flaws - except his claim about being thrown clear of the explosion. It's not like there wasn't a tonne of visibility in the desert there, and his exposed body baking until sundown? Sounds ridiculous. If he said he jettisoned as the crashed ship was coming down that would be more believable.

Leia and Luke - Leia for some reason has none of the force power Luke said she'd learn to use in time. Luke stays on his serene temple planet watching the ocean while his sister and the entire rebellion/resistance is in mortal danger and Han is being killed. Okay? And what happened to the flesh on Luke's mechanical hand?

Worse than the the characters though is the plot. This is JJ "teleport to Klingon" Abrahms we're talking about here.

So the new death star is a planet that somehow moves from solar system to solar system (I guess?) and charges itself by sucking the sun dry, somehow storing that energy on a planet billions of times smaller, and then firing it out through space where it fragments off magically taking out multiple planets at once. Whose idea was this? This is a thousand times more stupid and offensive to the laws of physics than anything in previous films. Oh yeah, apparently you can hyperspace into a planet's atmosphere and not burn up too.

I think I'm just about done for now. There will be many plot hole lists to come.

Was it entertaining? About as entertaining as the prequels, but the story arc is kind of important and if this was the best they could come up with Lucas should come out of retirement and do the next two. If they'd just gone with the EU material it would have been a massive improvement.

title: The franchise is rescued.
review:
Episode 7 has redeemed a franchise that for many hardcore traditional fans had become a niggling source of disappointment.

This is everything that 1, 2 & 3 weren't. The acting is solid - something we've never really associated with the franchise. The music is not clichéd - there are some new themes which will most likely catch on. The storyline is coherent and promises longevity and the action is gripping.

title: A New Hope Awakens...with the same plot lines (spoilers abound)
review:
The good: Fun, re-watchable, roller coaster type movie with very fast pacing. John Boyega was a standout & Harrison was as snappy as ever. Great action overall, fun choreography of lightsaber fights,etc

-------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------- -

The bad: The same story, EXACT story, as the original Star Wars. The big threat? A bigger Death star. The 3rd one. With the same easily destructible "tunnel" area. They even copied the exact same ideas for a "cantina" and a "team meeting around a holo table" to map out the rebel attack. Come on. I paid for a new movie, not a rerun of the original. Very uninspired.

Rey is Luke v2.o, almost to a tee, until the bad writing takes place and she goes from stick fighting 2 no name alien thugs on Jakku in the intro of her character, to becoming a Master Jedi within 20 minutes of her getting screen time.

Touching up on that note, Luke's character took 3 movies, 1 lost arm (to Vader), and almost dying a couple of times, until he BARELY defeated Vader (whose power diminished drastically after Obi kicked his butt and chopped him up). Not to mention, Luke was NOT able to kill the Emperor. Vader had to save him.

Rey takes on a trained(since birth, by Luke) Sith Commander, with little problem. They stop fighting in the middle of the fight for her to "look within" for 5 seconds (it was quiet for dramatic effect but failed quite miserably as the timing was "off" for that to even happen in such a dynamic duel), and then literally she becomes a Jedi Master with a lightsaber, proceeding to defeat him.

Another ridiculous Rey moment starts from the very start of her intro to the audience. She, out of nowhere, pilots the Millennium Falcon, as well as Han & Chewie in their twilight, with NO EXPERIENCE, while being chased by Tie fighters through the innards of a downed Star Destroyer. WHAT? HOW?

Horribly lazy & bad writing.

The pacing of the movie allowed for no character development, unless it was instant. She INSTANTLY knew what to do, without any knowledge of the situation or the ship, etc. He INSTANTLY thought of something that totally worked without any prior knowledge or education about the subject matter. Everything had to be instant, because there simply was no time.

The script is what irks me the most.

CG in some parts, was sub par. A lot of times used needlessly (unlike the originals). Characters which could've been cast as actors, and used prosthetics, were pushed to CG for no reason at all. Snoke & Maz specifically.

Cinematography was made for a Disney ride & feels video game-y. Lots of upside down, and side to side flipping camera angles that trail the action, all mixed in with GoPro's on XWings. For non action scenes, it was anywhere between mediocre to great, but very all over the place as a package.

The dialogue wasn't much better, but still a step above what Lucas was writing in the prequels.

-------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------- -

Final thought, a fan boy (JJ) and a big corp (Disney) teamed up to make a safe (unoriginal), toy commercial with park ride implications.

Lucas at least had the balls to explore new terrain, while making some screw ups in the process. ALL prequels were new, ACTUALLY new, movies. This is a remake with a new cast and more CG than needed.

Your kids will love it, and you will find it very re-watchable because it literally has no depth. I liked it in theaters as a joy- ride (much like i experience Fast & Furious movies), but i'm disappointed as a Star Wars fan.

6/10 due to lack of originality & badly written shallow characters

title: Disney not off to a great start
review:
My intention was to go see this film with no expectations. I was doing okay until that text started rolling across the screen and the theme song kicked in, I started hoping.

An hour and a half into the film I was just hoping for it to end so I could go do something else. To me this sums up the Force Awakens - it's not terrible, but there's absolutely nothing there to keep you in your seat, unless you want to watch some beautiful scenery.

(Spoilers incoming) There's no point going into any in-depth analysis of the story, or the plot, cause it is bare bones. I'm surprised they decided to go with a plot that is almost identical to IV: A New Hope (another death star, really???) - they could have made it all much more interesting with some proper back story, but instead everything leading up to the current circumstance is told to us in the opening text and rushed bits of dialogue - I found this particularly annoying when it came to the new fallen jedi, his story is basically explained in a short and stiff dialogue between Leia and Han Solo, they could have done so much more there.

Granted, IV: A New Hope was much the same - the audience was thrown into the midst of a galactic civil war without much explanation. But in new hope the circumstances of the war and the factions unfold at a good pace as we follow Luke Skywalker's budding steps into becoming a jedi and a hero of the resistance: In The Force Awakens they've decided to throw two hours of roller-coaster action into our faces instead of giving us a proper story or a proper character - They provide us with the superficial trappings of a coming of age story but rush through it in order to get more screen time for showcasing visuals and action - unfortunately this is common practice these days and it simply does not make good film.

A lot of people have heaped praise over Harrison Ford in this film. Ford is not bad, but his one-liners start feeling increasingly forced the further the film goes on. Fischer on the other hand is wooden throughout the film and the heartfelt moments between Han Solo and Leia are so stiff they are almost embarrassing to watch.

On a positive note - I think the two new leads do a decent job. The Force Awakens is also visually stunning - they definitely did a better balancing act in that respect than the three previous Star Wars films.

Let's see what the next films bring - The Force Awakens is by no means a disaster and I'm enthusiastic about the new generation Star Wars saga, I really hope we get some old republic films at some point.

title: The Force Awakens is really just another New Hope
review:
The first (or fourth) Star Wars worked so well because it was something new. The older mentor Jedi walks the hero through a desert planet opening,finds Han Solo and Chewbacca, gets cut down by the Sith while X-Wings fight Tie Fighters, a giant planet destroyer is itself destroyed and the forces of good are saved.

If you're thinking of A New Hope, The Force Awakens (or minus the the specifics of Han Solo, X-Wings and the planet destroying weapon replaced by another weapon) you would be right, but what I find most disappointing is that J.J Abrams, who is not known for avoiding innovation, basically remade the old Star Wars formula. I see no Star Wars revolution replacing the known and loved young protagonists of A New Hope with new characters while the roles of the older mentors are now the cast of the 1977 title.

I will give the film credit for a few fan pleasing moments. I found Rey a very fun character and felt she acted well. Seeing Han Solo being himself for a few minutes was great, as was watching the Millennium Falcon fly again. I was positively surprised when Keylo Ren actually took off his mask and seeing the downed Star Destroyer in the sand was visually impressive. However, these few tidbits were too few and far between in a story that was as lacking in uniqueness as most of the new characters in it.

It is our collective loss that an innovator like J.J. Abrams basically redid A New Hope to a T, from the familiar opening of a droid wandering the desert and anti climactic ending with an X-Wing Tie Fighter battle less exciting than the original. I understand that there is a fear to try something new when there is a formula that is proved to work but the Star Wars galaxy far far away is a huge place, and I personally would rather a director take a risk and show us the characters we love doing new things. Watching this movie I felt that I'd seen it all before and if I knew that I'd be watching A New Hope again I would not have hurried to watch it opening night knowing that I'd already seen it 38 years ago.

title: I can feel the hate swelling in you now! A review for the fans.
review:
The film is a masterpiece of escapism entertainment and so what if the template was borrowed in part from previous Star Wars movies (especially the original trilogy) – those movies worked!

I'm not surprised at all with some of the hate filled reviews on here, I guess you can't please all of the people all of the time – only the vast majority of the developed world who can afford a ticket. Admittedly nostalgia levels were very high, but I felt as though they were warranted when I watched the finish article, as all boxes were ticked.

*Potential very small spoiler* I particularly enjoyed the quite literal 'Force Awakening' scenes with the main force sensitive characters (not yet Jedi or Sith), who in some cases were literally fighting for their lives with zero training and a yet unknown midichlorian count.

I'm looking forward to being able to share the experience with my 6 year old son one day soon, I'm sure he won't be dissecting the plot, drawing parallels with the originals and complaining about a "lack of vision".

The torch has finally been passed to a new generation, well done JJ and company!

title: Unexpected Disappointment!
review:
I just watched The Force Awakens! (Not to spoil anything), generally I loved the film very much, but what I sensed at the end was that I do miss George Lucas's story telling! I think JJ tried to stay far too faithful to Episode IV. I was a bit surprised about this at the end.

People were always complaining about Episodes1-3 and criticized George for the dialogues, etc., but the stories of those episodes were very powerful. George (as Steven Spielberg once said), is a magnificent storyteller. Even when you watch the animated series "The Clone Wars", you can still feel the impact of George as the master mind of story. That series had lots of new innovative stories. The Force Awakens, on the other hand, did not have much of that kind, I have to say. The music of John Williams is just magnificent! Seeing the end credits and those epic themes were extraordinary. Now I understand George's interview with Charlie Rose (from a few weeks ago) in which he said he decided to go on his own way and let them go on their own! Finally! The Force Awakens is of course still a must-see and will satisfy Star Wars fan, but we will miss George's empty chair!

title: The Force Has Indeed Awoken
review:
We waited for years, and it's finally here. At 3 o'clock this morning I entered the cinema wide-eyed, full of hope. As was with many people's childhoods, Star Wars was a staple of mine, and to this day the original trilogy still stand as some of my favourite films. J.J. Abrams famously managed to reignite the Star Trek franchise with two fantastic films, so when tasked with doing similar to Star Wars, some people were sceptical, but nonetheless excited. The main questions is: did he deliver? Yes he damn well did!

You know that tight throat feeling you get when you have a sudden urge of adrenaline, for the last hour of the film, I had that feeling, sitting there on the edge of my seat, heart pounding fast. What I was watching was exhilarating to say the least.

Let's look more at the film (don't worry, there will be no spoilers featured). First off, the opening - the classic text followed by the panning shot to a planet (or death star) with a Star Destroyer emerging into the frame, it all features, as does the use of practical effects and puppets / robots over the extensive use of CGI that was utilised in the prequel trilogy, thus giving fans the old school style of Star Wars they wanted oh so much. The film is fast-paced, with stunning action scenes and spectacles, but not rushed, the shots linger and the camera moves gracefully, giving us a spectacular view of the situation at hand.

The prequel trilogy shunted the franchise on a downward spiral, the overuse of CGI and the introduction of some of the most annoying characters in film (a-hem Jar Jar Binks), but Abrams, the finest choice of a director to reignite the franchise, did nothing more than show pure love for the films and has created a sequel that definitely exceeded my expectations. A film that features endless nostalgia with appearances from Ford (who is beyond fantastic), Fisher, Hamill even Peter Mayhew as Chewbacca and constant references to the original trilogy.

The only partial negative aspect is its somewhat lack of originality, it acts more as an homage to 'A New Hope' than an original tale. But if you overthink points like this when viewing it, you won't enjoy it, so just empty your head of that and watch the film for what it is: a space opera that acts as nothing more than a sheer piece of movie magic!

title: This is as bad as it gets
review:
I was a big Star Wars fan some 30 years ago, in fact, for a long time, because of the original trilogy. Those parts were truly new and breathtakingly original and visually mind-blowing. The prequel trilogy's main problem was that it entirely depended on CGI which made it unbelievable, but in many respect was way more better than this new instalment. At least there was a new story. The Force Awakens succeeded where the prequel failed (CGI), I have to admit that, but the story is so bad, so-so bad, that it spoils every effort the filmmakers put in visually. The whole story is full of clichés from the original trilogy, in fact, feels like a badly cut version of that. The poor scavenger emerging as hero from the desert (not a farmer, but nonetheless a hardworking survivor with no parents on the horizon) the father's son turning bad guy (the reverse story of Darth Vader and Luke), a "new emperor" dark leader, a "new Death Star" etc, etc... The visuals, the scenes are not only similar but sometimes seem identical to the original trilogy's. Way too bad. Desert, desert town, town bar, the flagship, all the fighter ships, etc. All the way during the movie you have the feeling that "yeah, yeah, I've seen it already".

To be blunt, it was hard not to quit watching the movie and not only once but many times.

I feel really sorry for all of it. Rebuilt old scenes, cliché after cliché both visually and story-wise. I just feel sorry for the actors and the filmmakers. I think the producers but most of all, sorry to say, J.J. Abrams screwed this up entirely.

A badly made "remake" that's what this is. As bad as it gets.

title: Relax, weirdos. It's just a space fantasy movie.
review:
10/10, if only to irk all the whining fanboys on here.

I cannot believe the outright rage and anger over this movie. Grown men getting all bent out of shape and throwing tantrums because the latest installment of a movie series that features a guy in a shag rug outfit, garbage cans on wheels and a ninja gremlin that can lift spaceships with his mind didn't meet their expectations. Relax. I mean seriously. Its just a space fantasy movie. Its not supposed to clean up at the Oscars or have a story like a Pulitzer winning novel. Its a big, fun, goofy ride with explosions and lasers in space and that's all.

Look what introducing too many new characters, spaceships and concepts did for Lucas in the prequels. They apparently according to the fans all stunk so why cry now when they stick to the original winning formula. You willingly bought your ticket so don't cry and demand your money back because it didn't meet many peoples quite frankly outrageous expectations. Be thankful you even have a new Star Wars movie. Most people couldn't even draw the Millennium Falcon let alone bring it to life on the big screen.

Another thing I would like to bring to the foaming at the mouth fan boys attention is that the prequels were largely downright awful and they were made by its creator, who sold out and walked away by the way because he knew the story was pretty much tapped out and you know it, and if this new movie sucks and the prequels suck and the only decent films were the first three (many thought those sucked too by the way) then maybe that means Star Wars just simply sucks and it was over in the 80's and that the fan boys should simply move along and find something else to fill the voids in their lives. Part of the problem is that Lucas much like his fans started to take this franchise way too seriously and it wouldn't appear that there is just no pleasing any Star Wars fan.

Is the action and story line supposed to be realistic and believable? Heck no! Was it fun and loud and did it bring you back to the wacky Star Wars world for a couple hours? Yes. Thats all its supposed to be is a big, fun, goofy space fantasy to lose yourself in for a couple hours and nothing more so stop taking it so seriously, get over it and stop whining.

And some of the plot hole arguments on here are ridiculous. Hundreds of comments about how does Rey know so much about the Millennium Falcon? Well because as very clearly stated in the film it sat in pretty much her backyard, owned by her employer for much of her life so you think she might have been on it more than a few times. I mean seriously are Star Wars fans really that thick? Even a 12 year old would have a hard time missing that glaring plot point.

Personally I liked the movie and thought it was fun. It brought me back to my childhood but I certainly did not hang my happiness or mental health on whether or not it would be good or totally change the format and introduce all new concepts. I saw Han and Chewy and Leia and Luke and a bunch of new characters and I ate my popcorn, drank my drink, watched the explosions and went home satisfied.

Star Wars was never intended to be the pinnacle of human story telling with an Oscar winning script, nor was it intended to change the world or be a crutch for people to rely on to bring meaning to their lives.

Just enjoy two hours of incredible escapism and get a life already.

title: A New Hope, But Not
review:
This movie was painstakingly average. There are many reviewers on this board who compare this movie with the prequel trilogy and base their review on that. However the success or failure of other films should have no merit in this movie. The use of practical effects also has no merit.

The Force Awakens can best be described as taking A New Hope and baking a cake around it. All of the key elements from A New Hope have been copied over to this film. Only you have to dig through a bunch of surgery junk to get to it. Just some of these key points are as follows:

1) Mysterious masked sith who speaks with a robotic voice, and who is related in some way to a main character. 2) A droid given valuable information required for the plot to progress, who stumbles across our main protagonist. 3) Deathstar, only bigger. Even Han Solo mentions that it is just a giant Deathstar. 4) Trench battle at end to destroy the "not Deathstar". 5) Old mentor who becomes a father figure, who is killed by the masked sith. 6) Seeking a jedi master at the end for further training.

Episode 7 lacks very little originality and feels more like a fan film riddled with references to the other movies. We get to see Luke's blast helmet and probe that he was training with, the chess game Chewbacka and C3P0 played, etc etc.

While certainly making me laugh throughout, the newer characters that will be taking over this series felt more like cartoons of themselves than actual people. Finn reminds us throughout that he was raised to do nothing but be a soldier, yet he is consistently shown to be useless. Rey is a junk scavenger, yet can fight of countless soldiers (better than Finn).

There are many key points in the film that are left unexplained. The argument that a movie should not need to explain everything is true, so long as there appears to be some sort of unspoken explanation.

A character, Maz Kanata, has Luke's first lightsaber in her basement. When Asked how she got it, she responds with "That's a long story". R2D2 is in sleep mode for some extended period of time, only to wake up for no reason when it became convenient for the plot.

In all this Star Wars installment is nothing more than a popcorn movie. It adds nothing to the series, and was done too safely to take anything away. My recommendation would be to just watch A New Hope again.

title: Interesting but disappointing
review: Interesting but not exciting. New characters, sure. Older actors seen in their roles again, OK. Everything happens within a plot that seems derivative of every other Star Wars movie - so nothing really new there. One might ask -- so what can you expect, given the preceding movies? One thing would be a finale that is not just a rehash of the "destruction of the death star by rebels in x-wing fighters flying down a tunnel" scene from the first movie, right down to the "final countdown"that results in destruction of the enemy world seconds before the evil weapon of mass destruction is operational. Send those screenwriters back to writers boot camp and come up with a better ending! The movie was mildly entertaining, but I expected more. The popcorn was fine,though.

title: Deja vu
review:
As I was born in mid-90s, the first movie from Star Wars franchise I've seen was "Phantom Menace". Alright, it wasn't the best film, but still I quite enjoyed it: space, cool cg, amazing lightsaber fight, Liam Neeson and Ewan McGregor. Then I watched 2 and 3 movies and my reactions was: "Um... what?". Seriously, nobody can say that prequels were great.

Then I decided to see the the original trilogy and it was amazing! Absolutely fascinating, interesting and enjoyable. So, of course, even thought I am not a big fan, I was waiting for the 7th episode of this saga. And, man, I waited for something else.

First of all, just to be clear: movie isn't bad. Particularly i mean It was worth watching and was quite entertaining, funny and beautiful. But that's it.

And here goes the sense:

1) "Empire died, but now the is First Order". Alright. So nothing changed, right?

2) "There is new villain sith with black mask". Wait a second, I think I've seen it before...

3) "They built the weapon that can destroy planets". Hmm. So basically, it's new Death Star, but bigger?

4) "To destroy this weapon pilots of the Resistance should fly on the X-wings towards it and destroy the compressor (or whatever)". Yo, guys, I wanted to watch 7th episode, not 4th.

5) SPOILERS!!! ATTENTION!!! "Han Solo's son (Kylo Ren) kills his father on the bridge, because.... " Daf&c?! What with this guy? Why did he do that? And what the heck is with this bridge? Is it nostalgic sign for "Empire strikes back"??

And tooooooonns of things like this.

Seriously, if you watched original trilogy and can do primary school maths, after 40 minutes of movie you will know EXACTLY how it will end. (Especially, Han's death. I would be more surprised, if Ren decided to come back and live with his family happy ever after).

Thus, I was very disappointed. It's like Abrahms thought: "Well, nobody likes prequels, which were different from original trilogy. So I will make a movie exactly as the old one".

As a result: old plot, old characters, old problems, old places, old ABSENCE OF COOL LIGHTSABER FIGHTS... God... Now I have really bad feeling about next one.

title: A New Hope 2
review:
I came in with high expectations, some good reviews. But three quarters of the way through the movie, it was the exact same story as 'A New Hope', with a few juxtaposed characters and a slightly different ending.

I'm surprised this was directed by JJ Abrams, it felt more like I was watching a Chris Columbus or Steven Spielberg dumbed-down 'blockbuster'. Like he was under too much pressure to pander to the lowest common denominator, we wouldn't want to confuse children or the shallow noob Chinese movie consumer now would we? And produce something that was deeper and more meaningful but could be watched on several levels, no, be conservative and just plough the new 'New Hope' furrow. Except that this had packed in scenes that were not properly played out, motivations and emotions seemed to be ignored to skip through the narrative, so the furrow was not ploughed very straight.

Harrison Ford, Sigorney Weaver and even the one second he was on the screen Mark Hamill looked like they REALLY didn't want to be there at all, and that they had been basically bribed and bullied by a corporation to be on screen.

The visual effects are stunning, and if you are with some kids aged 5-12, they probably enjoy it, so it's not a complete waste of time and money, but really it could have been so much more.

title: Meh.
review:
A fun time at the theatre but not much else. I liked the additions, and how the Force worked, but it was kind of a mess. Weird pacing, hyperactive editing, and plot points straight out copied from A New Hope. Rey was okay, she was overacting at times and her performance felt a bit too artificial, in fact the whole movie felt artificial. The directing was just, too much! Too much intensity, overly polished and produced, out of place crooked camera angles and slow zooms to make everything intense when it's completely unnecessary. Good performances overall, fun action, I was eating my popcorn pretty fast. Well timed fan services and winks to the original trilogy, but when I left the theatre I told myself:"Meh, it was fine." Better than the prequels obviously, but that is not saying much. They crammed so much in one movie, that the movie itself felt claustrophobic. Kids will LOVE it. I, personally, liked it for what it was, but I was disappointed considering the hype and fantastic reviews. NOT A BAD MOVIE, at all, it's a fairly competent big budget space movie, but not as good as I thought it would be. Haters giving this 1 star are just lying. It is far from a bad movie, there was a lot of love and craftsmanship behind this film and it would never deserve a one star.

6.5/10 :-)

title: The Emperor has New Clothes....(or 'May The Forbes Be With You').
review:
I wanted to keep this short as very few people will read it. However to understand my POV you need some background to give it context;

Imagine being 8 years old, wearing flares without any regret or taste, nagging dad to take you to see Star Wars until he gives in and does. After coming out of the flicks in '77 we were both hyper and couldn't stop talking about it - everything was 'Amazingggggg!!!!!'. We were pretty poor, but I still got the huge cardboard Death Star and a dozen figures for Crimbo, Dad 'got it' so got them, good man.

Then 'Empire', even better, and an AT-AT for Crimbo, he was earning more. Jedi was okay, certainly not bad, but the Death Star MkII was grabbing at straws. No memorable xmas pressies this time.

Then adult hood smacks me in the face, many substitute Carrie Fisher girlfriends, many Star Wars gen' friends, many fancy dress parties dressed as a Wookie. Then the news 'there's going to be prequels'. Much excitement replaced by utter disappointment and hate for Mr. Lucas when I and others realised this was just an adverts for plastic toys and lunch box makers. But still we went to all 3, more in loyal hope and desperation than anything else.

So imagine how we received the news that we were going back to basics with Disney and a master of action, JJ Abrams? After a million emails, texts and toasts in many bars we were all set - December 2015. Only 2 years to wait whilst devouring every morsel of news and gossip, no matter how minor. We felt vindicated, that the original fans had been heard, that although the franchise had lost its way, someone had found the original map.

Closer to the imminent release date and a work colleague buys me a ticket to a 3D screening with a sofa seat in one of the few UK cinemas with a bar (Dukes @ Komedia, Brighton). 'Happy Christmas Lew!'. 'Ah, man! I only got you a book on 'Medieval Iconic Art' (he's cultured and stuff, always going to museums and art galleries); 'this film is way better, thanks Ludvig!' (that really is his name, he's Dutch).

I have the date all set, December 27th is on my ticket, a Sunday. I make sure I have a nap in the afternoon so I'll be super fresh at the flicks. I shower and change so I'm all set and ready (I'm normally a bit of a scruff), I even trim my beard. This is more to pass the time than because I care about how I look; my nervous excited energy means I can't sit still for a second. My inner child is screaming 'Are we there yet.....?!' It's good that I'm going alone, no distractions are allowed because this is just way too important. On the bus there I listen to J M Jarre's 'Oxygen' specially dl'd for the journey just to get me into that '70's ultra sci fi vibe. I always put that album and SW together in my mind, probably because they were both iconic and of their time?

I get there, my sofa awaits (normally a 2 seater, but it's all mine tonight). The place is packed, the punters, old and young, are excited, you can feel it,touch it, taste it, slice it with a light sabre.

A thousand ad's later and the main title comes on screen - much applause and whooping (not normal for a UK audience) YES!!!YES!!!YES!!!

Within minutes the sense of de ja vieu is setting in, old plot lines are being resurrected and cannibalised. Yet I refuse to acknowledge this at first; 'give it time, Lewi, give it time'. I wish I hadn't, I wish I'd never gone, I wish that the Star Wars team were on the destroyed Death Star MkIII. The over riding emotion I had was boredom tinged with regret at being a sucker for the hype. How bored was I? At one point I got a tap on my shoulder because I was snoring.

There was a smattering of applause at the end, no where near as energetic as at the start, so I wasn't the only one feeling let down. Yet the chat in the bar after was muted appreciation, like no one wanted to be the first to say 'I thought it was the Star Wars story all over again, but not as good'. But you knew they were thinking it.

So why does the Emperor have new clothes? Because no one can admit he's naked in case they look stupid, which makes everyone stupid as a collective. To be fair, there are a few on here that think the same as me, but a lot more that don't. And like everyone else, I'll go to see the rest of the sequels, but with expectations way lower than before. We all should have known better.

Rule #1 - The Greater The Hype, The Bigger The Disappointment. This is an unbreakable rule of the universe and relates to all things. Like many true fans to the originals, I fell for the hype '...going back to the 'real' Star Wars, blah blah blah....' Why do we always forget the 1st rule?

Mr Abrams, your directing and manipulation of 3D were excellent, bet you wish you'd had a decent story and dialogue to go with it? And Mr. Lucas, can I just say 'May The Forbes Be With You'? You will certainly be in their 'Top 100 Richest' this year. You still own a lot of the merchandising and royalty rights after your sale to Disney for $3 Billion don't you? I bet you see a naked Emperor too, but at least you can wrap him up with $1000 bills as you blame Disney. You owe Ludvig £11.40.

title: Character line/history was not followed. (Possibly has a spoiler. But I tried to keep it as vague as I could).

title: STAR WARS: The Plot Holes Strike Back
review:
The only reason I gave this movie 4 stars is because, after enduring the prequels, it was nice to see Han, Luke, Leia and Chewbacca again. Beyond that, I have some very big issues with this movie. First of all, if Luke (the superhuman Jedi Master) has gone into hiding and doesn't want to be found, then why is there a map that says "HEY EVERYONE.... Luke IS HIDING OVER HERE" and why does everyone seem to know about this map??? Second major problem, at the beginning of the movie, Rey had only heard rumors that the FORCE existed, had only just found out that she had Force ability and has had no training whatsoever, but somehow she's able to lay a beat-down on a trained Sith ???? And why does this same Sith Lord seem barely able to handle a light saber fight with Finn, a non-force using human ??? Third of all, in the first STAR WARS, why did the rebellion need detailed plans for the Death Star, a full invasion force and Luke's supernatural Force skills to destroy the Death Star, but in the Force Awakens, all that was needed was a sanitation worker with no skills, a few low level explosives and a couple of easy X-Wing blaster strikes to blow up the much bigger Starkiller base??? And why would Han Solo "lose track" of his most prized possession for so long, and then happen to conveniently look out the window and happen to miraculously find it flying by ???

Anyway, I could go on because there are many plot holes. In the end, I wanted to love or even like this movie, and in part I kind of did, but it was SO riddled with ridiculous plot holes that I just can't get past it. When I watch a movie and the plot holes are SO glaring and in your face,it's hard to like it.

title: Trying too hard and wants too much
review:
I was really looking forward to the new Star Wars - not only do I love the universe it describes, it is directed by JJ Abrams, can you ask for more ?

The movie starts out as expected, the familiar "in a galaxy far far away" runs across the screen, and all is as it should be... And from there it just goes the wrong way. So many things are wrong in the lore and the movie just takes up too many clichés.

If the old empire has collapsed, the senate or the old rebel-army should have taken over, but it is still just rebels.

The rebels know of The First Order, but knows nothing of the new death-ray-thingie, thou it would take enormous amounts of resources to build - now without an imperial government and a galaxy to support it ?

For the smaller and even more annoying things, why does a man like JJ make the usual movie mistake, where a professional army cant hit anything and the rebels can hit all ? It feels as if Disney just stuck their nose too far out.

Why add a new character in a cool silver uniform (cant remember the name), and then just kill her off ? Bearing on mind that see at the same time did nothing to prevent the "heroes" destroying the oscillator (?)

And what is the purpose of destroying five plants with an over-sized death star, other than trying to outdo the original empire ?

And honestly, did he (JJ) really have to make that non-hidden reference to the nazi's ? Its so cheap and doesn't help anything.

I could go on and on, with elements that are just bad or out of place. The sum of it, is that Disney wanted way too much in a way too short movie, using old tricks that I would have thought most viewers would have seen through.

No, we still have to go back to to the first two movies (IV and V, should you be in any doubt) to find the best ever... Sad, I really thought JJ and Disney could pull it off.

title: No Novelty Film
review:
The original Star Wars IV released in 1977 and it was the most avant-garde Science-Fiction(Sci Fi) feature film that audiences have had an innovative experience of the universal scale of mythology, intricate cinematography and also conceptual props design at the time. Star Wars VII The Force Awakens is the story about 30 years after Star Wars VI.

Pros. The original casting in Star Wars IV, V, VI are appears in Star Wars VII. The film completed with the same look and feel of the original Star Wars such as special effect and therefore time line looks like real. If you have seen the original Star Wars film in theatre you might feels back in the time.

Cons. No story during three decades, insufficient character development and no backstory about main acts such as Rey, Finn and Kylo Ren. Poorly scripted dialogue and inadequate plots that leads main acts doesn't look a right in time and location. They are not charismatic either. The biggest disappointment on Star Wars VII is no novelty existed. The film has almost the same props, cinematography, design concept, and winning strategy that noting has been improved from the 30 years behind the original Star Wars time line.

Overall If you are expecting an imaginative mythology that equivalent to the original Star Was film, Star Wars VI is not the right film. However it is good to see the original casting again.

title: Terrible Reboot Puts the Final Nail in the Star Wars Coffin
review:
What a wasted opportunity.

After the god-awful prequels I thought the only direction left to go was up. But unfortunately Jar-Jar Abrams takes it down another half-notch with the most uninspiring Star Wars film in the canon. At least the prequels, as awful as they were, made a feeble attempt to show us some new planetscapes and interesting design motifs. The Farce Awakens is content to merely retread everything that has come before. Sand planet. Ice planet. Forest planet. Villain with breathing mask. Cantina scene. X- Wings. Tie Fighters. Death Star...you know the drill.

But the cardinal sin of this movie is its lack of credible heroic characters. We have an annoying ex-stormtrooper guy, who doesn't do much but run, trip and look constipated. Then we have a teenage girl who can of course easily kick the crap out of sand people twice her size, repair any spaceship in the universe, learn to fly the Millennium Falcon in less than 30 seconds, oh and fight and kill a Sith Lord with NO TRAINING WHATSOEVER.

Even Luke Skywalker had to be trained by Yoda on Dagobah for weeks - and he still lost and got his hand chopped off when he faced Vader. But a 100- pound teenage girl? No problem! Instant Jedi! I know the movie is fantasy but come on. At the very least a fantasy universe should stay consistent with its internal rules. And that means an apprentice requires intense training and effort to become a Jedi, even for one gifted with the force (Luke, Anakin). If a lithe teenager could just wake up one morning and be able to kill a Sith Lord later that afternoon, with no training and no prior experience - then that just makes a Farce out of the Force.

Main villain was weak and lacked motivation.

Leia - Han relationship was flat and wooden.

Han's big dramatic moment was predictable and anti-climactic.

Final x-wing battle was boring and uninvolving because - who cares?

Every scene of this movie was simply rebooted from the original trilogy but without any spark of emotional truth or creativity. Pure fan-service pandering and nothing more.

And I actually liked Jar-Jar Abrams' Star Trek reboot in 2009. Sure, it wasn't really Trek but it was at least a rollicking and entertaining space adventure. The Farce Awakens, on the other hand, is just a pure misfire on every level (except visual effects). Never thought it would get this bad - where the prequels, or at least Revenge of the Sith, was a better movie. And I *hated* revenge of the Sith!

Sad to say but, after almost 40 years, I'm done with this movie franchise.

title: Second worst Star Wars film
review:
This was easily the worst Star Wars movie ever made, apart from the Star Wars Holiday Special. This film is an insult to Star Wars and that's mainly because, although I wouldn't have minded just a few nods to the other Star Wars films such as Darth Vader's helmet, the storyline is a rip-off of the Original Trilogy.

I like the Prequels. Yes, they have flaws but they have a huge advantage over The Force Awakens because they tried something fresh and original. It didn't pay off as well as George Lucas hoped but at least he wasn't just ripping off one of the other Star Wars movies. Harrison Ford and Max Von-Sydow were good, BB8 was cute and Mark Hamill said everything that needed to be said with a single look, but everything else about the film was crap. I didn't realize how bad it really is when I was watching it but it's clear that Abrams didn't give a damn about making a genuinely good movie, only pandering to the masses. Either that or he's deluded enough to think that this is a good movie and can't see that he's a terrible director.

I never liked the idea that Luke Skywalker could defeat Darth Vader with so little training but at least he actually HAD training. Rey had literally NO training whatsoever, at least not as far as we or even she knows, yet she beat the hell out of Kylo Ren. To be fair, Kylo Ren was injured at the time but he's still a trained warrior so the only way I can forgive Abrams for putting Rey's seemingly impossible victory in the film is if the following movies reveal that she actually did receive training but somehow forgot.

Kylo Ren started off okay and managed to look pretty bad-ass at the beginning of the film, especially when he held off that blaster bolt for an extended period of time, before allowing it to blow something up before he left. However he was clearly a weaker man than Anakin Skywalker and his relationship with Han was just Luke and Vader with the roles reversed. To Adam Driver's credit, he was okay in his scene with Harrison Ford but that was the only scene where he showed that he has any talent. Overall he wasn't much compared to Darth Vader and I'm not even a fan of Vader. Also Ben's light saber was ridiculous but at least he made use of its unique design when fighting Finn.

Rey is the only fictional character I can think of who deserves the title of Mary Sue. I feel like that term is used too freely but Rey wasn't a complicated character and anything interesting about her was because of her mysterious past rather than the character herself. Throughout this entire movie, she could deal with any situation without help or any real difficulty. The very few scenes that give her some depth, such as when she was scared by the Skywalker lightsaber and denied that her family weren't coming back, can be easily forgotten. She had no problems resisting the lure of the Dark side, she could fix anything, fly anything, shoot more accurately than trained soldiers, beat up anyone who messed with her including a trained Dark Jedi and wield both the Force and a lightsaber with an impossible level of skill for someone who, as far as both the audience and character knows, has never been trained.

Normally, I love strong female characters but in order to make a character realistic and interesting, you have to make them flawed. Daisy Ridley clearly had no idea of how to play Rey and not all of that can be blamed on JJ Abrams' bad directing since Abrams himself told Ridley that her acting was wooden. There are vastly more talented actresses out there who could have brought more to the role. To be fair, Rey was a badly written character but if speaking like a noblewoman whilst playing a character who lived in the gutter is the best she can do, it's pretty obvious that Ridley sucks at her job.

John Boyega was an over-the-top, idiotic mouth-breather in this movie. That's all I have to say about him. Domnhall Gleeson was also over-the-top and Oscar Isaac had so little to work with that he was forgettable. One of the saving graces for me was BB8; he was cute and I liked his design.

If TFA was a comedy, it would have been fine but it wasn't intended to be a comedy, hence making it a "so bad it's good" movie. Aside from Harrison Ford, Max Von-Sydow, Mark Hamill and BB8, everything in this film was so bad that people can laugh at how badly Abrams screwed up. I prefer not to think of it as part of Star Wars canon. ROTJ symbolized a new beginning but the people behind this project spat on that and showed us that defeating the Empire was completely pointless. The Empire destroyed millions of lives and obliterated entire planets and a mere 30 years later, The First Order is doing the exact same thing.

The people in charge clearly cared more about money than making a good sequel and used peoples nostalgia to manipulate them into watching this crap. Even before I actually saw the film, I wasn't very enthusiastic about it. The next film MIGHT be able to redeem this movie but I doubt it. If I watch the sequels at all, I won't do so in the cinema. The Prequels are not perfect but they deserve their place in the Star Wars time-line. This film does not.

title: The Kool-Aid Returns
review:
The drinking of the Kool-Aid continues. I mean sure, the Force Awakens wasn't terrible and quite fun at times but it at best can be described as mediocre. As of now it has 95% on Rotten Tomatoes while films 1 and 2 only have 94%. Would the critics seriously have me believe that this film is better than Empire Strikes Back?

Sure, there were funny and engaging parts and I certainly didn't feel bored. But there was nothing great, nothing that would let you forget the flawed parts and say that at least we had X, Y or Z. The biggest flaw is that it's not really a sequel, more like a reboot. A seboot? The film's makers are just comfortably treading familiar ground instead of bringing anything new to the table.

The second big flaw is that Rey is a textbook Mary Sue character and she's supposed to be our main character. As I look back Finn stands out so much more in my memory and that's because of his flaws and failings. He seems real and I would much rather watch him grow through the movies than just Rey being instantly perfect at everything she does.

Overall, The Force Awakens can be enjoyed but this is not the big step forward for Star Wars and personally I don't get what everyone's raving about.

title: A howling disappointment
review:
Repetitive, dull, and overly reliant on special effects, this film is an unashamed rehash of the previous movies. It did not even have the respect for its audience to take itself seriously, epitomized by the fact that Jaja Binx is back, only this time he's black. Possibly the most self-indulgent movie ever made, it is only partly redeemed by the wonderful performances given by Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher. Sadly these acting gems were scattered so sparsely they were hardly worth waiting for.

The had sorely hoped this film would continue the epic saga, explaining the complex fallout from Episode 6 and telling the stories of the main characters. Instead, the film dedicates itself to a cast of unknowns in a vain attempt to recreate the magic of the originals and fails. Unless you are a die-hard Star Wars fan, this is best watched for free on terrestrial television at some point. I would rank it on a par with Episode I.

title: completely average movie: Remake of NEW HOPE.
review:
Abrahams should have just told us we were getting a remake of A NEW HOPE. I don't hate the movie. The action scenes feel like Star War, much more so than the prequels. The bad thing about the movie is EVERYTHING about the movie feels like A NEW HOPE. Who didn't know HAN was going to die when he confronts Kylo Ren? It was a complete redo of the Darth Vader/Obie One scene at the end of A NEW HOPE. They really needed to add a wrench into the story line that wasn't expected. Making Luke the bad guy would have been a good start. Instead, Luke shows up at end playing the the role of Yoda the trainer.

The Kylo Ren back story certainly could have been developed more. Why would he worship Darth Vader when Anakin Skywalker turns at the end of Return of the Jedi. He certainly must know that story right??

title: Turn to the Disney side is complete...
review:
This was not the movie I was hoping for... its slick and pretty, but is missing all the elements that made the original trilogy tick. There is no back story, no character development, weak plot points... and too much forced humour. Some of it works but most of it fails. This plays like a action movie... it should have made me interested in the characters - but it didn't.

Chewie and Han were great. Hans death could have meant so much more if we knew early on the back story of Kylo and his struggles with the dark side. Leah was underused and we really have no idea how the resistance works...

I know many people will like the full on action approach. It really was incredible... like watching a video game... but I really wanted to connect the characters and their story's... but Im repeating myself..

I really hope Rey has already had Jedi training and the memory was erased... if that plot point is not resolved then Im sad to say JJ missed the boat.

Many too convenient plot devices took out he believability of the movie. How do one just stumble onto the stolen Millennium Falcon, take it and then have Han and Chewie show up - boom. Yes they are plot devices but way too easy...

The Force awakens is equivalent to watching a zoolander style beautiful supermodel - all looks and no real substance...

title: Lived up to the hype
review:
This is the first movie i have ever gone to see back to back and I must say it lived up to the hype.

Like most people when i first saw that Disney where going to be making new star wars movies I was a little disappointed because i thought that they would be more like the prequels than the originals. But JJ did a fantastic job of making the film fresh and at the same time you knew it was a star wars film.

I loved Rey and think that she is better than Anakin in the prequels, and I might even say she is on par if not better than Luke. i hope that the 2 other main movies and the spin off movies are just as good if not better than episode 7.

title: Get over it already, fanboys. The movie was massively entertaining and better than the originals.
review:
I've watched the original Star Wars many times growing up, and I know the story inside out like anyone else. Classic films that many people like my self have been wanting back. I saw the movie today and walked away satisfied and eager for the next one. I read some of these highest rated reviews and it's literally awful how full of yourself and pessimistic some of you are. You're giving the movie a 1 star, for what? Most of you have a delusion of 30 years of fanboy pathetic bias that nothing released will live up to your laughable, impossible to please standards.

First of all, this is a movie, it's pure entertainment. It isn't a real galaxy, it isn't real people, it's just a movie guys. Because it doesn't add up to every painful fan boy theory you wrote in a thesis somewhere, doesn't mean the movie didn't deliver. You cannot take it this seriously. Yes, the movie followed the same guidelines to the plot as #4 that made the original successful, but there is plenty of juicy story to build on that is completely original. It pays tribute to the old, and you care about the new offspring of the main characters going forward. The story does develop perfectly from #6, 30 years later with the offspring and new heroes to root for. It gives us the best x- wing, tie fighter, millennium falcon, storm trooper, battle scene fights in any of the movies. It's modern movie making and CGI at it's best, but still giving us the unique Star Wars elements we want to see. The John Williams score is epic and masterful with the movie. The story ends for old characters in awe, and it starts new interesting story lines for other old characters continuing the story, like Chewy and Luke.

This movie had to get people excited about Star Wars again. The 2000 movies weren't very good, so it had to go back to the guidelines of the original story. I suspect this movie will reflect closet to the originals story guidelines, because it had to deliver what we wanted, and the next two will develop entirely new unique adventures and story for the new heroes that will, through the characters family lineage, constantly pay tribute to the old.

After reading some of these, it seems people put the originals on a pedestal. They were very good movies, but not everything was explainable or made to prove science and follow every law of nature. It's a movie. It is made to be fun, and you can't take movies that seriously. Most movies going back, including the originals, are all like this, it doesn't always have to follow physics like it seems hardcore Star Wars fans think. I don't think the movie was perfect,I would have liked to see Fin and Rey's relationship go deeper so I cared about it more. But it was very close, and the main pieces we've been waiting for have come back and are as good as before. Nothing will replace a classic, but we don't have to because this story is excellent on it's own.

Just appreciate what it is, it's definitely the best Star Wars film made. It was exciting, extremely fun and satisfying, and I loved every second of it. Rey, Poe, and Fin are going to be fun to watch, and I can't wait to see Luke's role in the next one training Rey and seeing how she can harness the force against Han and Leia's kid. I took my girlfriend to see this movie, she had only seen part of the originals but somewhat knows the back story, and she knew exactly what was going on and absolutely loved it. They made it very watchable and entertaining for any level of fan. Very good movie.

title: Yep. Disregard the laughably biased, contrarian "reviews". The Force is strong with this awesome movie!
review:
This is a great movie. It's also an extremely popular and mainstream movie, and therefore is going to bring out people that will needlessly nitpick it to death in an attempt to look smart or edgy. Star Wars fans will find a lot to love hear. Great set pieces/locations, excellent costume design, flawed and relatable characters, hilarious banter/quips, dramatic and complex relationships, and a ton of space adventure fun. It's the best Star Wars film since Empire, hands down.

title: Star wars gone bad
review:
Start wars The Force Awakens

I have grown up with this world, mythos and characters. Episodes 4-6 were something that shaped me and my preferences in life, art, science fiction and values.

Then there came episodes 1-3. They weren't terrible, especially 2 and 3, but nowhere close to the actual originals. And now this abomination which I can only compare to Indiana Jones 4.

I wonder why are the movie makers in Hollywood making this filth in the last decade. Are they that desperate for money that they are making generic template based movies that are sure to be lucrative ignoring the fact that, on the long run, they are embarrassing themselves and destroying the mythos we grow up on because they are afraid in indulging in any creativity which might not bring back the cash in amount they want. Well it's not true, people would see this movie anyway and there is no justification for the terrible scenario (or no scenario). I am not an American and I do not consider it a minus concerning criticism towards American art. Intelligent is intelligent, beautiful is beautiful no matter where you are in the world. There may be some subtle differences among cultures but we all have standards as human beings towards quality.

Let's start by giving some positive feedback. Costumes are great, effects are OK. And that is it.

Movie start with generic intro without any deeper explanations about the lore. What happened to the Republic and Empire after episode 6, why is there still rebellion if they won? The empire is now called "The first order!". Who came up with this name which suits some Harry Potter world or some other fairytale.

Empire (I am gonna call them like that from now on) is just evil without any explanation, inner struggles or the reasons why are they doing the stuff that is being done. They are portrayed like stereotypical Nazi culture. The evil antagonist is totally generic, Dart Wader wannabe, and just bad without any reason (everything is black and white without gray undertones that makes us human). Even Hitler, had reasons for his action in his head. This depth is missing completely in character development thought the movie.

The plot is copy paste from the first movies. Some droid has important info (episode 4), he is running from the empire (e-4), there is a desert planet (e-4 & e-6), main female and male character instantly bond, there is a death star on steroids (e-4 & e- 6), empire has no sane engineers that learn from their mistakes (blowing up the death star with the same strategy as before). Rebels are just a chaotic bunch who plan complicated missions in minutes. R2D2 is chilling for a long time, inactive, without any reason and then he wakes up at the end and has magically the missing info which he combines with info from the new droid.

Jokes are terrible and, although they are self explanatory, the director had to explain them again and ruining them. For example there are monsters released in the spaceship and one of the characters asks how do they look and then they appear. There it should have ended with the joke, but the other character had to say that they looked like that emphasizing the obvious. All the jokes are made with this mold which ruins them and are aimed towards children which I assume was the intent so that they would cover the biggest possible span of audience.

The antagonists are generic, Disney like villeins without any scary elements. Even the Wader copy was more interesting until he took the mask off. When I saw him, I started laughing and he looks like some dude from Monty Python with terrible acting. Who cast him for this?. His boss (the emperor analogy) is like a giant Golum from The Lord of The Rings.

The plot holes are many and I will just mention that there are no explanations why Luke left, how the map is found, why R2D2 has the missing part of the map and many more.

I do not understand the point of making this kind of garbage except for the financial gain. Are there any decent writers in Hollywood capable in making intelligent scenarios? For a this kind of budget, lack of script has no justifications. I would make better scenario as would any intelligent star wars enthusiast who grew up on this world and lore.

I am giving it 2 because of the old school SF effects but they were not many and also the camera was chaotic which took our chance to enjoy the design and world of Start Wars.

title: The force is still asleep
review: I'll try to be honest and plain. I really like how this movie is directed,visuals are stunning,music score is joy for ears,the cast is fantastic. Two new characters are very charismatic young people who blended perfectly into SW saga and generally the whole movie has that SW atmosphere. This is where I stop praising the movie and look upon where it fails. In few occasions I almost went out of the movie theater. The movie is set 30 years after the events in episode VI. We all wanted to know what happened next and this is why I hated the scenario. We find out that from the remnants of the empire a new force has risen and its called "First Order".We also find out that there is a New Republic and also a gang of freedom fighters - The Resistance. The Rebels in episode IV were fighting against the Empire so that a New Republic could be founded and democracy restored. Why does the Resistance exists if there is already a New Republic? And why New Republic is not helping the Resistance? Not a single ship or a soldier is sent to help in their fight against New Order. By the way,the Resistance is trying to destroy New Order's new weapon:you can surely guess that it is a new Death Star,only this time it is three times larger and it sucks energy from a star and later fires that energy into guided projectiles which can destroy entire planets?!? And what is also familiar? The Resistance must first destroy its shields and then attack with a dozen of X- wings,fly through a narrow space,and then destroy it?!? Also nothing is said about who has the upper hand in this war? Who is holding Corrusant? What area of galaxy is under control of New Republic and what area is controlled by New Order? What happened to the Jedi? Is Luke still the only surviving Jedi? I imagined that this movie would be about a Luke's efforts to restore Jedi order. Instead,Luke is gone to some place which he chose to be his exile. On the other side of the force we have Supreme Leader Snoke in a role similar to Emperor Palpatine and Kylo Ren,a Han and Leia's son who turned to the dark side. Are they following the teachings of the Sith or are they simply dark side users? Nothing is explained in the movie. In fact,the whole movie is deprived of terms such as Jedi,Sith,Force etc.My biggest disappointment is that at the end of the movie,Fynn(former storm trooper)who takes a light saber for the first time in his life fights a fully trained and very powerful Kylo Ren like Obi Wan or Mace Windu would do.Still,Kylo somehow defeats Fynn,but is then confronted with Rey,who just found out about a existence of the Force and had no training,in a light saber duel in which she has the upper hand and also manages to out power Kylo in the force?!? I cannot describe how disappointed I was because of the things like this. I hope that the Force will eventually awake,but we will have to wait for the next episode for that. Please,for everybody's sake,you have two more shots to make things right. Use them wisely.

title: Ignore the negatives, this movie is AMAZING
review:
Only people that "think" they are fans are giving this movie negative reviews. This movie is absolutely incredible and I don't think anyone could have done any better with it. If your nit picking little things you should really re-think your entire view. This was probably one of the hardest movies ever to remake and JJ Abrams did an awesome job. He had a lot to live up to, and a lot to follow up.....and he did it!!

For those of you bashing any of the story lines.. if you had the slightest idea of what you were talking about you would know George Lucas already had Most of this story written, and J.J. followed most of it. So complaining about the story is silly. You should sit back and enjoy the movie and appreciate you were given the opportunity in time to view it.

So stop picking things apart and enjoy this movie, I saw it last night and cannot wait to see it again in a few hours!

title: Star Wars The Force Awakens is the best star wars movie.
review:
The Force Awakens is the best of all the star wars movies by far . All the new actors in this movie made it even more enjoyable, especially Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver. They were the breakout stars of the movie. Adam driver was a complex villain and thankfully will be in future episodes. Daisy Ridley did a brilliant job as the main hero of this movie and her performance was amazing.

The overall story and action was spectacular. The new cast and story is what makes this a great space epic . Oscar Isaac was also a welcomed new addition to the cast, he did a fantastic job as the best pilot of the resistance. All the original cast of the first trilogy did a good job, even if their part was brief. I also loved new droid BB 8, he was funny and a hilarious side character. John Boyega was awesome as the ex storm trooper.

All in all, this was an excellent movie.

title: Terrible cliché storyline, some nice special effects
review:
Waste of time and money. The story is really cliché, unoriginal and predictable.

You won't miss anything worth caring about and that isn't completely predictable for any halfway intelligent person watching the movie, but

Han Solo dies in a really dumb, predictable and meaningless way.

They made a new Death Star that is simply 100x larger than the old Death Star and shoots a ridiculous beam that splits into multiple beams halfway and then destroys multiple planets instead of one. Really, couldn't you think of anything else as the antagonist's weapon?

title: The force has awakened!
review:
Loved the original 'Star Wars' films as a kid, still do. Especially 'Empire Strikes Back' while considering 'A New Hope' a genre landmark. Didn't think the prequel films were that bad personally, but they had a lot wrong with them and were a long way from great, especially 'Attack of the Clones'.

Despite seeing 'Star Wars: Episode VII- The Force Awakens' around the time it first came out (maybe a little after), there was a long time of being put off by the vitriolic hate it's gotten here and the practical war zone there is in order to review it (even when it was critically acclaimed). Finally mustering the courage, count me in as somebody who loved 'Star Wars: Episode VII- The Force Awakens'. A masterpiece? No. Better than the prequels? Absolutely, and although some may disagree this is saying a lot. The best 'Star Wars' film since 'The Return of the Jedi?' Yes.

'Star Wars: Episode VII- The Force Awakens' is not the most original plot-wise. It has been criticised for being a re-hash of 'A New Hope', understandably. However, instead of being done in a cheap and slap-in-the-face way, it felt like an affectionate and nostalgic homage. Exemplified by bringing back major characters from the original trilogy in supporting roles. JJ Abrams, and this may be considered blasphemy, does a much better job here than he did with his 'Star Trek' reboot films, here he keeps the original spirit of the original trilogy intact while giving the film its own identity at the same time.

While it certainly dazzles in spectacle and action, 'Star Wars: Episode VII- The Force Awakens' doesn't feel too big, too noisy or too chaotic at the expense of creating memorable characters, a fun story and brains and heart. The characters are memorable with easily identifiable leads, the original trilogy characters bringing a lot of affectionate nostalgia and a well executed if not iconic (not by Darth Vader standards anyhow) villain in Kylo Ren (unpredictable and dangerous but feeling he is morally justified).

The story lacks originality but more than makes up for it in energy, non-stop heart-thumping thrills and excitement, generosity, a cheerfulness that is positively space operatic, vibrant charm and a few fresh twists along the way. In many ways it is a celebration of the universe while also an expansion of it. It is sometimes sentimental but never overly so, one crucial death scene is just heart-wrenching (particularly Chewbacca's reaction) and doesn't feel like a slap in the face to the character in question.

Could the villains have been better written? Ren is fine but Snoke only just about works as a character thanks to the visual effects and especially the powerfully enigmatic with a touch of vulnerability performance of Andy Serkis, other than that the character is underwritten. Also felt that Gwendoline Christie's character was unnecessary, so limited was her screen time.

Visually, 'Star Wars: Episode VII- The Force Awakens' is a triumph. It is gorgeously shot and designed with Abrams' visual storytelling shining far more here than it has in other films he's done. The special effects are a dazzling marvel. John Williams delivers yet another rousing score that has its own character but cleverly includes the well-known iconic themes from the previous films. Thank goodness that the dialogue contains little to none of the cheesiness heard in the prequels, and it even has more layers than that of the original trilogy.

Acting also shines, with winning charismatic performances from John Boyega and particularly Daisy Ridley. Mark Hamill, Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher still have it, while Max Von Sydow shows himself to be a master of gestures and eye contact speaking louder than words. Adam Driver is a suitably menacing Ren and Serkis makes much of his somewhat underwritten character. Oscar Isaac gives a typically strong performance.

In conclusion, a great film, the best 'Star Wars' film since 'The Return of the Jedi' and one of the best of the saga too. 9/10 Bethany Cox
