title: A paint by numbers continuation of the Star Wars universe
review:
Not a huge fan of star wars but I have seen the original series many times as a kid and saw all the prequels in the cinemas upon release. My personal opinion on this movie is that it did not meet the hype that it generated - not even close and that to me is quite a disappointment.

The story is a bit too similar to what was going on in the original series - which is such a shame as the Star Wars universe is developed and mature and yet they went with a story that lacked imagination and creativity. The acting was decent enough but also quite poor in the serious dramatic moments. In the end the story was just a derivative of the original. The pacing of the movie also felt wrong - it was hard to connect to some of the characters and the drama involved because the story moved way to fast.

  • Death Star 3.0 .... I don't understand the point of this and to me this was the worst part of the movie. The revealing of this was also lackluster. They could have done with not having the death star at all in this movie - everything about this plot device was just wrong.


The rebels could care less about it - in under 5 minutes they already worked out how to destroy it - and who could blame them - does not matter how powerful this weapon is it has the exact same flaws as the previous two designs! The battle to destroy it was also so generic - I'd expect the first order to put up a better fight - this is after all their secret weapon it should have been an epic battle to destroy it - yet all it took was a small group of X-wing fighters to fly in rather casually like they are on a holiday cruise and blow it up without any real dramas.

  • Kylo Ren. Was menacing and imposing at the beginning and around the middle of the film. His powers were quite impressive but once he took his helmet off - for a quick second I thought I was watching spaceballs 2 - did not look at all menacing and I hate to say it but it looked like a confused teenager going through puberty who was pretending to play what is supposedly one of the biggest badass in the star wars universe.


Barely a resemblance to his father/mother. He is still kind of conflicted and not a total convert to the dark side yet which I understand but they should have shown his backstory a bit more so we actually cared for him when he unmasked himself. As mentioned earlier the plot just moved too fast for this happen and its unfortunate because I bet they could have made quite an interesting and compelling backstory for him instead of just casually mentioning who his father was as if it was done by two guys making casual chit-chat at a bar.

  • Hans Solo's death and how it was handled was almost done in montage style - so quickly did the plot move on from this it was not really treated with any respect to the character. Its as if no one actually cared - not even Leia. Han dies (in quite a disposable way) and all we get is a shot of Leia looking like she is trying to remember where she left her car keys and the new main characters screaming like they have just been grounded by their parents. In short for such a dramatic event it was quite melodramatic.


  • Rey's knowledge of the force. Rey is pretty much the only character with some character developing scene in the movie (though still minimal) yet she develops her powers at such speed and with pretty much no one to guide her.


I find this quite hard to believe considering all the previous jedi-wannabe's had to go through years of training with a mentor guiding them - they had to constantly be reminded of what the force is and how to use it and yet we have Rey who needs barely any help doing what she does in the movie.

Overall this was an 'OK' movie on its own merits as the special effects were decent but the story telling was quite poor and sadly way to similar to parts of the original trilogy.

However this is a star wars movie and considering how much wealth of information they could have used from the star wars universe they played it way too safe.

title: Good but disappointing
review:
As a long-term fan of the series back when it first hit the screens in the late 70's, I wasn't too sure what to expect when I sat down to watch this but as The Force Awakens unfolded I couldn't help feeling that I was just watching an amalgam of episodes 4, 5 & 6.

The action starts on planet Jakku, which is basically Tattoine minus the Jawas and Sand People, however the surface is littered with downed star destroyers and old tie fighters. 30 years after The Empire was eradicated, a new military complex called First Order has manifested itself as the new antagonists. Stormtroopers are no longer clones, but captured children, raised and conditioned to take orders without question.

The action then heads to a forest planet Takodana, (which for all intents and purposes looks like Endor minus the Ewoks), and it's here that a newly reunited Han Solo, Chewbacca and Millennium Falcon seek answers from a knowledgeable alien called Maz,(queue Yoda right about now) inside a seedy bar full of weirdos playing equally weird music, (so the cantina from Mos Eisley has now relocated to Endor).

A new emperor like character called Supreme Leader Snoke, is the one behind the First Order and it's new planet sized ultimate weapon called the Star Killer, or some such, and it's powered by having to fully drain the power from nearby suns in order to fire it's weapon across the galaxy and take out an entire star system, not just one planet. The Surface of the Star Killer is snow and ice, so what we have is another Hoth like world.

Han Solo and now "General" Leia have a son, Kylo Ren, who wears a mask (which is just for show) and talks not unlike Darth Vader, whom he admires and also has Vaders burnt mask as a keepsake. How the hell he got hold of that is anyones guess. Kylo was force trained by a now missing- in-action Luke Skywalker before he turned to the dark side. And it's another Obi-Wan versus Anikin back story.

The action, special effects and the reunification of the old stars aside, it's the glaring lack of originality and obvious plot holes throughout that prevented me from loving this. A stormtrooper feels that indiscriminate killing is wrong so he goes against his conditioning and decides to rebel and helps a captured resistance fighter, Poe, to escape. With a new name of Finn, instead of his designation number, he crash lands back on Jakku and teams up with a force sensitive girl called Rey, and a BB8 droid. The droid is holding onto plans that show a portion of a space chart showing the location to Luke Skywalker. That bit looks all too familiar as well.

Rey has never had any formal Jedi training, has only recently discovered that she's force sensitive but somehow still manages to mind manipulate guards into letting her go and also wield a lightsaber well enough to beat Kylo Ren in a fight. Did I suddenly fall asleep during all the training she's supposed to have to learn how it all works? Obi-Wan had training, so did Anikin and Luke, but not this new comer, she can manage it all by sheer will alone. Not only that but she can suddenly fly the Millennium Falcon with her only having piloted basic land speeders before, and manages to out manoeuvre seasoned tie fighter pilots. Impossible? Maybe. Implausible? Definitely.

Leia only turns up in the last half hour of the movie as does C3-P0, (with a new red arm), R2-D2 is only in this for the last 10 minutes and Luke only for the last 2 minutes and he never utters a word. Everyone made such a big deal of Lupita Nyong'o being in this but she's a voice actor only for the new Yoda-esque character of Maz, so really that could have been done by just about anybody. The end of the film is the same as episode 4 - A New Hope; a bunch of X-wings fly in to try and take out the Death Star/Star Killer before it uses it's weapon on the planet where the resistance is based and they manage it with seconds to spare.

So overall while the Force Awakens is good, it's not great and is rather a let down. Considering that this is supposed to be 30 years later and the galaxy was at peace after the empire, there's no real explanation as to how all this started again and no one seems to have ever attempted to prevent it. This started pretty much the same way as episode 4 did, with everything already in place, which would be fine if this were a stand alone movie and we were unaware of what came before. So for me, this is a disappointment.

title: Buried underneath the melodramatic fan reactions, there's a good movie here
review:
My Disney cynicism runs pretty deep - but not unfounded, what with the Mouse's recent announcements of killing Slave Leia merch and banning blasters from their theme parks (hello? It's Star Wars!) - so you can imagine my level of anticipation for "The Force Awakens" wasn't all that great.

Still, certain promises were made in the trailers, and all I really wanted to see was the Millennium Falcon fly again And it does, beautifully. Also, there was a flamethrower Stormtrooper. Talk about hitting the right buttons.

I can't adequately describe my schoolboy glee when Han and Chewie walked in. Harrison Ford is beyond terrific in this movie and he made me want to see the rest of the band back together.

I have a theory that a lot of this movie's appeal (magic, if you will) lies in wanting to see those long-dormant characters. Just their various reveals is enough substance of that. It's very in-the-moment, emotionally rekindling. And who knows how well the this will hold up down the line on rewatch? But as a movie, it's pretty cool. All of the fun aspects of Star Wars are here. Is it fan service? Yeah. A remixing of "Star Wars" (1977)? Absolutely.

But I had a good time.

7/10

Revised 7/1/16:

Sadly, that appeal wears off a bit and the holes tend to be more glaring on the small screen. It's not all that fun as a rehash of "Star Wars", and killing off Han Solo just to give the emo villain some depth is infuriating. Aside from Rey, the new characters are bland, and it functions like most of Abrams' films: frenetic, but empty.

It's not a bad movie, at all, but they were clearly going for fan concession. And that just doesn't hold up after the first buzz. I know it's the first movie in a trilogy, and we have to see where this is going . . . but how many times have we been asked to do that in the past 15 years? This should function on its own.

6/10

title: Well-made, but ultimately shallow
review:
Star wars, the force awakens has all the makings of a great movie, and sometimes nearly reaches them. Its editing, pacing, cinematography, music and visual effects are amazing, and you can tell JJ Abrams put effort and care into making this movie look and feel like a true original star wars movie, and yes I said TRUE. Along with the competent filmmaking on display are some truly incredible performances by the cast. I wont argue that Daisy Ridley's acting is perfect (believe me it isn't), but she defiantly shows more emotion than Hayden Christensen in the prequels. The old cast is great once again, even though some characters don't have, or are given, much screen time to work with what they are given. It is nice to seem them back into character again and you can tell some of them (especially Harrison Ford) really are thrilled to be back into character. Even the new cast really do try, even if they are not amazing.

My problem with this movie is that it plays things very VERY safe. Despite some unexpected turns in the plot, it still feels like your average star wars movie, with Jedi, space-battles, action and the force. Everyone's complaints with this movie seem to stem from the plot feeling like a complete repeat of the previous original trilogy, which i wont argue with. The movie has plot-points that feel WAY to close to that of the originals. Trust me, I'm all for playing on nostalgia, its one way to market a movie and make it work, but it feels too close to the originals. This is something I hope that the sequels will move away from as the trilogy continues and concludes. People do need to calm down. Spamming IMDb with 1/10 ratings implies that it fails on almost every single level of filmmaking including the basics of how a film should be written, shot and directed. This movie like I said is well made but it's too familiar and doesn't break any new grounds in terms of story or progression. If the sequels don't fix this problem, I will start to like these movies less and less.....

title: A fun film, but gets worse the more you think abot it
review:
TFA is an ok film. Personally, I do not hate it, like many do. When I first watched the movie i genuinely loved it. Unfortunately, this is one of those movies that gets worse the more you think about it.

Rey is not an interesting character. Not because she is a mary-sue or because she is a woman or anything like that. It's just that I do not find her character very interesting. She is not in the story because she chose to be in it, but because other characters drag her into it. She does not even have a proper arc. I honestly find the side characters and the villans far more interesting than her. Kylo Ren had a lot of potential and so did Finn.

The plot is not exactly a retread of a new hope, but it does borrow a lot of story elements. There are some ideas that could lead to some good stories, but the main plot is way to similar to A New Hope. Again, this movie is enjoyable if you shut of your brain when watching it, but I wish we had a more unique story that did not rely on the original trilogy.

title: Overplays the nostalgia card
review:
So, the behemoth franchise Star Wars have produced another sparkly 2 hour long advert for their never ending range of merchandise, media and memorabilia..

I don't really need to set this one up, do I? Star Wars is something that transcends cinema, it's a global cultural landmark, it's already cinematic royalty, in a league above 'classic film'; everyone's seen Star Wars.

However, this isn't an institution that's too big to fail, the memory of jar jar binks is still fresh in collective memory, so despite an estimated 200$ million budget, a hard hitting credentialed director, and promising cast, producing a good film is definitely not a guarantee. There's still a heavy anchor of expectation.

Perhaps this fear of failure alongside such a beloved classic is what led to this film, in my eyes, playing it safe, and not attempting to do anything story-wise that may have rocked the boat for the die hard fanboys. Sadly, 'The Force Awakens' feels like a overdrawn reunion show for the original 70s cast, a 'where are they now?' film that never has the confidence to fully hand over the reigns to the new generation, it lacks any original spark, or definitive bite, it's got some undeniably fun blockbuster entertainment, but there's a load of rehashing, reusing and regurgitating of old ideas.

*SPOILER ALERT*

You could almost call it Star Wars bingo, what did past audiences love about the old films? A soaring John Williamson score? Check. Blowing up a Death Star? Check. Droids with a special message that has to be delivered to the rebels? Check. An emotional father/son scene above a illogically perilous bridge? Check. Bad guys with strange voices, the millennium falcon, chewy, and Han Solo? Full house.

A film being aware of being a sequel is fine, but this seemed like a nostalgia omnibus, riddled with cameos, and although the film is fundamentally technically brilliant, it's unoriginal. It's enjoyable, but forgettable. I liked it, but I wouldn't watch it again. It doesn't break the mould. And it doesn't try and stand on its own two feet.

Although I'm unimpressed with it, I can't rally alongside some commentators that have been quite vicious with their reviews. There's enough action, tension and entertainment to keep you on board for what is a reasonably long film. And if SW is about anything at all it's about the special effects (industrial light and magic etc) and the film certainly delivers on that front. The scene with Ray finding the light sabre stands out for me.

Star Wars never really dropped out of the public consciousness, and they really missed an opportunity in trying something new and different. Isn't sci fi the genre we turn to for interesting and fresh ideas?

title: Go and have a nice time with your children/friends/others...nothing more
review:
The movie is good enough to enjoy it without even knowing the prequels, and if you are around your 40's it is likely that you will feel a tender nostalgia from the first minute.

Some quick points: 1)Technically is well made, nothing original; 2)Action scenes oscillate from OK to very good; 3)Actors harmonize in general,but you can feel the age of Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher; 4)The history makes no much sense and has a lot of coincidences, but if you want logic don't look fantasy pictures then! (yes, Star Wars is fantasy, not science fiction).

Well, that's it. I tried to be as objective as possible, hope it helps someone.

title: Apart from the beautiful visuals, an average on-time watch
review:
First of all, I do not consider myself a hardcore Star Wars fan. Episodes IV, V and VI were part of my childhood, but compared with the Alien or Terminator movies, they played only a minor role. Nevertheless, I enjoyed them, and a few days ago I watched them again, together with The Revenge of the Sith.

More than two weeks after its premiere, out of sheer curiosity, I watched The Force Awakens. I didn't put much effort into avoiding spoilers, so I knew what to expect: great visual effects, and from that point of view Episode VII is phenomenal.

But there should be more than just beautiful scenery, fantastic battle scenes and great costumes, and I am not thinking about scientific accuracy. I accept that in Star Wars laser beams barely reach the speed of a normal bullet, and lightsabers cut through solid metal, yet, in interactions with each other, they behave like ordinary sticks. So I clench my teeth, put aside facts about the size and mass of stars, and accept also that the newest Death Star gets energy from a star by sucking it in altogether, even if nowadays this grandiose nonsense is on the intellectual level of a three-years-old.

Measured strictly by Star Wars standards, Episode VII lacks real heroes. Luke had the Force within him as an inborn talent, but he started small, and for his talent to manifest he needed heavy physical and mental training. He reached greatness not overnight, but through a long process full of success and failure. This is one of the very few messages of the old Star Wars movies, which can be found in the prequels too, that applies to real life.

Compared with the above, Episode VII protagonist Rey picks up a lightsaber for the second time in her life, and defeats the villain Ren. A villain, who has the Force at least as strong in him as she has (after all, he stops laser beams), not to mention his considerable routine with the lightsaber in combat. If that is not silly enough, Finn, without the slightest Force in him, uses a lightsaber relatively successfully in the fight. All these make the portrayal of the Force somewhat comical.

Speaking about Ren, to achieve a great goal, good or evil, one needs to be disciplined and organized, otherwise nobody follows him. Ren is more like a parody of Vader: he is infantile and hysteric, and in his fit of rage destroys his own valuable equipment. The funniest moment in the film is when, after Rey escapes, two storm troopers catch Ren in an angry mood, and wait by the corner for him to stop punishing the hardware. Silly.

Countless plot elements are taken from episodes IV, V and VI, and I find that unimaginative. The family tree thing is also rather forced and dull. I wasn't moved by the presence of the old characters, except maybe by Luke's. Daisy Ridley's portrayal of Rey is sympathetic, but the rest are average. Finn doesn't convince me a bit that he was a storm trooper, who got an austere training from his very youth.

In conclusion, I enjoyed Episode VII for its magnificent visual effects and scenery; in 3D it was breathtaking, although the pointless haste of a superficial storytelling didn't allow me to fully appreciate it.

title: Why It Didn't Quite Work For Me
review:
-THIS WAS HARRISON FORD'S MOVIE AND NO ONE ELSE'S

The movie started and I began to get into it, but I found something in it wasn't quite taking off. Three protagonists are introduced: Finn, Rey, and Poe Dameron. Poe is right away the most colorful and amusing, yet the movie disposes of him for most of its screen time. So we follow Finn and Rey as they eventually meet each other, get caught up in an adventure bigger than them, and run away from the First Order, and I just found myself drifting. These two characters felt stiff; their dialog was perfunctory and they were just there to move the story forward. I kept thinking "Wait, tell me more about this First Order and Kylo Ren. Finn was conditioned since birth to be a Stormtrooper? That's interesting. Tell me more about how that works. Can others break away too?" Instead the characters kept running and shooting with no backstory. I figured that the quest to find Luke Skywalker would lead to explanations, but instead of being on a linear journey, the characters keep getting sidetracked. Throughout this entire first act, I found myself oddly detached from what I was watching: something wasn't clicking together.

Then, Han Solo shows up, and from that point on, he dominates the movie. If you were to cut all of Han's scenes and edit them together, you'd have a complete film with a clear protagonist and arc. Ford is so warm and colorful, full of human moments, that you're reminded why he became the breakout star of the original film. His scenes with Leia are fantastic and have strong human emotion. In the second half of the film, Rey and Finn felt delegated to secondary status and their arcs seemed half-hearted as we follow Han to confront Ren. Furthermore, the objective of our main characters changes. They suddenly stop caring about the map and their new goal becomes to take out the Death Star Thing That Isn't the Death Star. Only after it's taken down does R2-D2 magically come alive and go "Oh, now I can return to your original objective and tell you where Luke is, because the plot needs me to."

-TOO MANY TWISTS TO COMPENSATE FOR LITTLE PLOT

I feel like another movie needed to take place between the end of RETURN OF THE JEDI and the beginning of this film, and that would probably have been a more interesting film than this one. THE FORCE AWAKENS keeps hitting you with twists and reveals while leaving other things unexplained. Every time something was revealed I would think: "Tell me more about that. I'm curious about the backstory." But the plot they chose to use as a vessel for these reveals just isn't very strong. It's full of homages/rehashes of elements from the 1977 film. There's a MacGuffin hidden in a droid, the villain wears a mask that isn't quite the Darth Vader mask but basically is, there's a Supreme Leader Snoke who isn't quite Palpatine but fills the same role, they have to destroy something that isn't the Death Star but basically is, etc.

-THE VILLAINS ARE TERRIBLE

Snoke and Gen. Hux are all generic villains with generic villain plans. They just say villainy things and want to take over and conquer and be evil. Kylo Ren is a little more interesting once we learn his true identity, but what we got was too little. Instead of making this guy look like Vader and do Vader-y things, I wanted to see him go in his own direction. What is his reputation like? Do others fear him? I was never intimidated nor felt threatened by him.

-YOU KNOW WHAT THIS MOVIE DESPERATELY NEEDED?

A scene where our hero characters all sit around and just talk a little, showing their human side, specifically saying things like:

Finn: "You know that guy Kylo Ren? Let me tell you about about the legend surrounding him and what a horrible mystique he has and all the bad things he's done and why we're all scared of him. And let me also tell you a bit about the First Order and what makes them bad guys."

Rey: "That's interesting but let me now tell you about something called the Force and the weird quasi-religious thing I feel sometimes. I don't know what it is or what it means, but I want to learn more about it. My life feels empty; like I'm destined for something but don't know what."

Finn: "Wow, I just realized for the first time what it feels like to have an identity and think as myself and not part of a collective. That's so interesting. I want to explore this more."

Han: "Aww, kids, let me talk to you a little bit now about the magic and sense of wonder of the universe so we can bond as characters and my death will have a more profound affect on you later on."

"ALL THESE THINGS YOU'RE CRITICIZING ARE GOING TO BE EITHER EXPLAINED OR FLESHED OUT BETTER IN THE SUBSEQUENT FILMS!"

Well, yes, I should hope they will be. And maybe I'll like THE FORCE AWAKENS better on repeat viewings after learning whatever it is the sequels will reveal. But for right now, all I can do is judge it as a standalone film, and all I see are shortcomings.

"HEY, AT LEAST IT WAS BETTER THAN THE PREQUELS!"

Yes, it was. It definitely was the first STAR WARS film since 1983 to have a sense of grit and feel grounded in reality, with real locations and an epic sense of scope. They succeeded with flying colors in that department. But I just don't feel a baton was properly passed on as well to this new cast of characters, as they were aiming for.

title: A very well crafted action film, but horrible as Star Wars
review:
JJ Abrams somehow managed to do exactly what he did with Star Trek-make a flashy, technically well made film that's fun on a certain level, but fails utterly as Star Trek, or in this case Star Wars. It's like he's watched some of the franchise, but doesn't really 'get' what it's about.

If someone hasn't, I HIGHLY recommend watching all 6 vastly superior SW films by George Lucas, as well as the 2008 The Force Unleashed game (which functions as an amazing film in between episodes 3 and 4), before bothering with this. From what I've seen of The Clone Wars show, that's much better too (though I've yet to watch more than part of the first season...I hope to get to it!). For that matter, the books are overall much better too...one particular series of books, and The Force Unleashed do an infinitely better job with a character who switches sides...antagonist in this doesn't actually seem to have any motivation at all for what he's doing. He also gets the most inept lightsaber fight in all of Star Wars...despite what must be years or decades of training, anyone with a stick can apparently run up and whack the guy. It's actually hilarious, even more so when compared with all 6 films and The Force Unleashed.

Like in Star Trek, things just randomly happen because the plot says they should, and like ST it's basically soulless. Like ST the actors do a great job. Daisy Ridley is top notch, and I'd be thrilled to see her in a real Star Wars film. It's great to see Carrie Fisher-I hope she's got a bigger part next time, but it's wonderful to see her and she's great. And Harrison Ford is just a god-he owns the place the second he steps on screen, even if Han Solo still doesn't make much sense as a focus.

I wish Lucas could do episode 8 *sigh*

title: Your Ratings Aren't Doing Anything
review:
I just want to say to all you people voting out there that IMDb has a "weighted" way of rating their movies based on votes. That means it's not just the average of all the votes put together. I'm assuming this means that all you folks rating this a 1 or a 10 are probably greatly diminishing the weight of your vote as outliers. This is a shame because most of the reviews i've read are 1's, meaning people hated the movie, and yet the rating, as of now, remains at 8.7.

So if you hated the movie, try to make a proper, unbiased rating. It's not a 1, because it's not the worst movie ever made. Obviously, it's a huge disappointment for a Star Wars fan who desired an actual continuation of the story-line. I think mid-range votes will probably have more sway over the final rating because they seem more objective.

I thought it was a 6. If i hadn't grow up watching the rest, i would think this movie was enjoyable enough on it's own. I actually enjoyed a few performances, it stayed light and fun, and fast-paced, like the original trilogy. Unfortunately, the story-line was exactly the original trilogy. Hopefully the series will move forward from here.

title: Flawed but Entertaining
review:
I've given TFA 6 out of 10 because for 60 percent of my time watching it I was entertained, the other 40 percent I was a little disappointed.

I can see why people are loving this film and also hating it. First the love.

I think on the hole Abrams got the look and pace of the film spot on (a little two spot on for some people) I liked the new lead Characters especially Rey. I thought the character interaction was good and the most enjoyable moments were when Finn, Rey and Han were interacting. I liked the humour and I enjoyed the nods to the original trilogy.

For about 90 minutes everything was going well, there were a few annoying similarities between the OT and TFA but I could let those slide but the last 45 minutes were a real let down for me.

The Hate... As I said above I enjoyed the knowing nods to the OT but when you start tearing huge chunks of ANH & TESB and shoe-horning it into a new "original" film then that's really lazy.

A droid with crucial information....A planet sized space station with a weapon that can destroy planets....A vulnerability to the death star....sorry, Starkiller that can only be exploited using X-Wings making a bombing run down a trench....

I would have liked to have seen a little more originality for the start to a new trilogy.

Secondly Kylo Ren. At first I thought this guy was going to be a bad-ass, he stops a frickin laser blast in mid air!!! but he turns out to be a whiny man-child. I understand he's conflicted and he isn't fully trained but he's just not a convincing character. Hopefully episodes VIII & IX can flesh his character out a bit so we have a better understanding of why he acts this way.

Lastly, ignoring truths that are already established in the OT. Kylo Ren isn't fully trained but we know he has some training and is skilled in the ways of the force (Stops a laser blast!!) Rey has no Jedi training whatsoever so how can she defeat a trained Jedi in a lightsaber fight? OK he's been injured but she just seems to summon up this knowledge of the force, it was just not realistic (Yes I know I'm watching a Sci-Fi film) She manages to grab the lightsaber before he does, Errr hello? he stopped a laser blast!!!

A few additional niggles, Carrie Fisher is as wooden as an Ewok tree house. The last shot with Luke and Rey seemed to last ages, if I were Rey I'd have thrown the lightsaber at him. Poe's miraculous escape (Finn "I thought you were dead!?!" Poe "Nope.....")

I am aware I'm watching a $200 million dollar blockbuster film, I know Disney have to hedge their bets and cater to the masses, I wasn't expecting Schindler's List (That would be awful, gassing Ewoks...) but I do expect some new ideas.

I think the dire Prequals and the longing of SW fans for a good film has blinded them to the flaws in TFA and when all the dust has settled they'll see this for what it is. A solid but flawed start to a new Trilogy. I'm hoping for better from Episode VIII but lets keep the fun.

title: I cant help feeling dissatisfied
review:
I am a massive massive Star Wars fan, particularly of the original trilogy, like most people. When I heard that Disney were doing a Star Wars sequel trilogy I thought to myself "oh here we go again, just another Hollywood studio cashing in on an already exhausted franchise". When I saw the trailers for "The Force Awakens" I got my hopes up more than I ever imagined I would. I started to believe. And when the critics came out overwhelmingly in favour of the movie after the premiere my expectations went through the roof. Sadly, I think they got it wrong. The Force Awakens is a decent movie, but it is extremely flawed. This is where I think J.J. Abrams got it wrong:

1) You cant kill off Han Solo, he is an icon. Whoever decided to do this should be hung, drawn and quartered. 2) We've had two Death Stars already, having a bigger and more powerful one was just lazy writing. 3) This giant Death Star was far too easily destroyed - it was just a re-hashing of the plan carried out in A New Hope and Return of the Jedi - disable the shield, find a superficial reactor, fly in there in a X-wing and BOOM. Only it was done so simplistically in The Force Awakens that it made the writers look cheap, unoriginal and boring. 4) Anakin was supposed to be the chosen one and to bring balance to the force.....this movie totally ignores that prophecy. 5) How did Han Solo happen to come upon the Millennium Falcon above Jakku?? No plot thought here at all. 6) Kylo Ren couldn't look any less intimidating without his mask. 7) The whole movie was about finding Luke Skywalker, we get 2 min images of him standing looking at Rey holding out a lightsaber from numerous different angles. He never speaks once...the end. 8) Han and Luke never get a reunion which is something most fans wanted I'm sure. 9) Why bother having a Storm Strooper turn out to be one of the main characters??? Storm Troopers never had a conscience before...why now!? Seems a bit lame to me, even if Jon Boyega did a fine performance. His part just seems a little irrelevant. 10) I could go on and on and on.

The major positive for me was Daisy Ridley as Rey. She is mesmerizing on screen, beautiful and harks back to great on-screen performances from the original Trilogy. It was also Harrison Fords best performance in years until they killed off Han Solo.

I really wish I liked this movie more, but there are too many plot-holes to make this possible.

title: Wasn't terrible
review: Despite what some think. I thought it had a good story, until the end. I mean did anyone really buy that Rey just all of a sudden was a Jedi Master, with absolutely no training? Even an injured Kyle should have easily defeated a female scrapper, who had only heard about the force, but had no idea she even had it until days earlier. title: Fun, but nothing I haven't seen before
review:
Let me just start by saying that I never intended to see this movie in theaters. I was going to just watch it when it came out on DVD, but I decided to see it yesterday. My co-workers were excited about it, and I thought, "What the heck."

Now, to address the reviews. Many seemed to either love this movie or hate it. While it didn't seem as bad as some say it is, The Force Awakens wasn't as great either. It lies in the middle.

I went into the movie expecting something along the lines of the prequels, which I liked, although they weren't better than the originals. I was even prepared for something worse. I was pleasantly surprised. I enjoyed the characters and was excited to see that Harrison Ford wasn't in the movie for a mere 5 minutes that would serve as a cash grab.

However, this whole movie felt like a remake of A New Hope. There were plenty of examples, but I'll just name a few: droid being hunted because it has valuable information, planets that were reminded me of Tatooine and Endor (I genuinely thought that they were using the same planets until they said the names), and blowing up another Death Star in almost the exact same way (X-wings, internal sabotage, etc.). Blowing up the Death Star once was enough for me. The second time was excessive. A third is just annoying, even if this Death Star is bigger and badder.

Another odd thing. I recall thinking during Finn's fight scenes with a light saber that no one should be that good already. I mean, Luke sucked! But not Finn, who I don't think is even a Jedi. And then, he fights Kylo Ren. Either Finn was too good or Ren was awful because there's no way Finn should have almost beat a trained Sith lord in a fight.

This is still a cool movie to watch. But I'm a bit regretful that I paid to see a movie that I've pretty much seen before.

title: The Awakening Of A Strange Force
review:
**Warning Contains Spoilers**

First of all let me tell you all where I come from, within the Star Wars universe. Not only have I seen all the movies, but I practically read all the books of the expanded universe. This being said my vote is made quite clear. But still let me elaborate.

J.J. Abrams did a fantastic job with what he had. Visually the movie is beautiful. Most of the scenes in the movie had a reason to be. Also the interaction between the original and new generation of actors and actresses was done very well. For at least 2/3 of the movie I was hooked. And I actually hoped that this new timeline would somehow let me bypass the fact that now, most of the EU is non- canon. The character Rey also fueled that hope, because there was so much there. Her personality, her posture, her very presence and state of mind, could never go unnoticed. Finn on the other hand, I didn't liked so much. Throughout almost the entirety of the movie it felt like he was being thrown from one direction to another, with little control. Kylo Ren was so unstable that he looked more like a spoiled brat playing with powers that not only he didn't understand, but at the same time he carried little to no authority when compared to Sidious or Vader.

The story itself goes by very quickly, unfortunately at the cost of key information. When we left Luke he was the last Jedi, and now so many years after, he's still the last Jedi. We learn that he left the republic after Ben aka Kylo Ren, basically was the main responsible for the destruction of the new Jedi Order. This and some of his opening feats lead me to believe that Ren powers were quite strong. Which is why I found it hard, if not almost impossible to believe that someone like Finn that had no Force powers of his own, was even able to hold his ground for more than a second against Kylo. And Rey, that had only awakened to the Force, not only was she able to resist Kylo mind prove, but was then able to mind trick a Stormtrooper, and lastly fight and defeat Kylo in a light saber match. This to me was simply too hard to believe. I mean even Luke had guidance and training from both Obi-Wan and Yoda. Rey had nothing. She had heard stories, nothing more, and in less than two days she was already at Jedi Knight level... No way any real hardcore SW fan can swallow this.

It also made it hard if not impossible, to believe someone like Kylo Ren could've destroyed the new Jedi Order. It was the little things that started to pile up and pile up until there was no more room for me to accept what I was seeing.

And while all this was happening, where was Luke Skywalker, you may ask!? He was somewhere in the outer rim, chilling to the ocean view of the planet he had exiled himself to.

I had high hopes for Luke, when it was confirmed that the original cast was coming back. And the story, the movie itself could've been awesome. It could've initiated an all new timeline that those that had followed the EU could follow. Me especially. I hoped and I hoped until all hope was lost. When I saw that scene where Kylo kills his father, Han Solo, it was then that I hoped that Luke would show up, and used his Force powers to not only save Han but close the cycle like Vader and Obi-Wan. Because Luke had been Ben master it would've been awesome to have seen a showdown between the two. Only unlike Vader and Obi-Wan, Ren would fall. Luke would've fought Kylo Ren, left him for dead and then he would've joined the others. Then at the end of the movie Luke could've taken Rey to train - not sure about Finn because we never actually see him use any Force abilities - but lets assume both had Force connections to the Force. Luke would've said goodbye to Leia and Han. Took R2-D2 with him, and as a final high note surprise, upon arriving at the planet where Luke had spent all those years, we should've seen that he had built a new Jedi Order, one not bound to the Republic. We should've seen Luke being greeted by other Jedi Knights and Masters, but above all, other padawans. While Rey and Finn looked in awe to all that they were seeing. And the movie, and this part of the story would've ended there.

But none of this happened. Han Solo died at the hands of his own son, for no reason at all. And when it was all said and done, and Rey goes to search for Luke. What does she find... but an old man. Still obviously hurt by what had transpired. No Jedi Order, no academy, no nothing.

To me this marks the end of an era. At least movie wise, I see no reason to continue down this road anymore. It was painful to see 1/3 of the movie basically destroy all the build up and hopes the 2/3 of it had created. It is said that all good things most come to a end. And to me, personally... They have. I'll always cherish the six episodes and all they've given me. But this one... I'm not seeing myself ever accepting this new timeline. This to me was the last movie.

title: No enrichment to the saga
review:
I am a huge Star Wars fan and I love the original trilogy and after some analysis I liked the idea of the prequels. If this was my first Star Wars movie I ever watched, than I would have really enjoyed it, but I'm no Star Wars virgin.

First of all it is from the technical aspect the best film of the whole saga. The atmosphere and the effects are great and there are only CGI-Effects if there hasn't been another good looking possibility.

But the most important thing of a movie is it's story and on this The Force Awakens disappointed. What did the writers think? "We know that many people don't like the prequels, so we take the story of the original and change the characters." Han takes the mentor role of Obi-Wan, Poe is a cool pilot like Han Solo, Rey is just like the young Luke Skywalker. I admit that there are some interesting characters like Kylo Ren who is some kind of schizophrenic because he wants to be on the dark side but he is a good guy on the inside. And then there is Finn, who doesn't know what he is doing. Also the the relationship between the characters is not credible. For example are Poe and Finn best buddies after five minutes.

But even though there are new characters, the story is the same as in Episode IV...there are plans given to a droid...the droid has to be returned to his master...the droid should be brought to a resistance group...the bad guys have a giant killing machine...it only has one simple weakness... and so on. Sounds familiar right?

It is almost exactly the same as the original trilogy! Maybe they did not dare to do something new because the prequels did, which problems actually were poor CGI, bad acted characters, strange written dialogs and Jar Jar Binks.

I hoped The Force Awakens would bring me a new original Star Wars story with new ideas and more enrichment to the universe but it got me the same story as in the original trilogy, with some new characters.

All in all can be said that the directing of J.J. Abrams is great (except the lightsaber battle, after Episode 3 I have a high standard) but the writing of the story could have done much better.

Was it a mistake to reject George Lucas' ideas?

title: Could have and should have been better...
review: The ending to this messy, nostalgic nonsense brought home the fact that J.J. Abrams really does know better. So why doesn't he ever DO better in his movies? One of the things that made the first trilogy immortal was Lucas's epic focus on simplicity, gathering us around relatively uncomplicated characters and scenes stretched out into longer scenes and eventually, before you know it, the whole movie was over and imprinted on our souls forever. And this movie also proves that the golden age of casting is in the past for Hollywood. The lead chick in this future Oscar winner for Best Visual Effects does little more than cutesy her way through, uninterestingly, from beginning to end. Albeit she was definitely part of the glue that held this thing together, the other part being HARRISON FORD. Of the old actors that make their appearance, he is the one who still has the old magic on screen, proving that George Lucas and Steven Spielberg once knew exactly what they were doing. What story there is here just falls flat until the very, very end, when we are briefly, and impressively, reminded of why we still care about Star Wars in the first place.

title: Retread from the original 1977 Film
review:
I should probably say this now, I've never been a Star Wars fan. I like certain aspects of the movies but as a whole, they are way overrated in my eyes. So it should come to no surprise I found the new movie rather tepid. Again, the movie had it's moments of great action, lightsaber battles, and uses of the force, but outside of those moments, the magic wasn't there.

Nothing felt new in the sense that this was supposed to be the movie to reinvigorate the franchise. It felt like a total retread of the first movie from 1977. Yes, it had new characters and a slightly new mythos, but everything else was more of the same. The Force Awakens was trying to be nothing more than nostalgia, which is bittersweet. It succeeded as such which will please fans of the original three but at the same time, nothing new was offered, nothing except future promises. It was nice to see old characters and their introductions, but it was borderline too much. Had the movie introduced them then put them on the back burners, we could be talking about something different, but that wasn't the case. It is hard not to talk about specific beats without spoiling the movie. Even the mighty soundtrack by John Williams was borderline the exact same thing as the original, yes it is nice to see it appear once again, but this is a new generation, something new must be offered.

That's not to say everything was about the movie, the young new characters seem like a great new addition. Only time will tell how well they develop and fit in within the Star Wars universe. Not to mention they are a driving force behind the great comedic moments in the movie. This was something that was unexpected yet very welcome. The movie has made promises (Mockingjay Part 1 anyone?) so only time will tell where we head from here. But as of now, all these new characters are just treading water waiting for their time to truly take over the franchise.

Yes, the movie will break box office records and fans will rejoice the franchise is back. But with the promises of an unknown amount of sequels the franchise will have a difficult time maintaining the stakes at hand. So at the end of the day, it really comes down to the following, is this something I want to rewatch? Something that demands to be seen multiple times because of its greatness? The answer, sadly, is no.

title: Very Underwhelming.. *Spoiler Free*
review:
I was very excited to see this film and purposely stayed off social media for the past couple days to avoid any spoilers or reviews. While it is not a bad film by any stretch of the imagination and is entertaining to watch. I was overall very underwhelmed.

The Good. Daisy Ridley is great. She really has a presence and carries the film well. So does Adam Driver and Oscar Issacs. The Special effects are well done but not next level. The action set pieces are good but not great.

The Bad Don't see in 3D... john boyega is awful, every time he opens his mouth I think why the f did they hire this dude. title: Great movie
review: I watched every Star Wars movie in a row and I think Star Wars The Force Awakens is a great continuation of the sequel. There's new characters which makes The Force Awakens a little more interesting. Plus there are some original characters in the movie which of course is very awesome. review: The ending of Return of the Jedi might as well never have happened. We're back to where we started. These wars never end. review:
at one point they actually say 'remember in the last movie you watched that was exactly like this, well the death star was this big, but this movie, with it's massive Disney budget, the death star is THIS BIG!' and point to a projection of the difference in size of death stars, to firmly prove the point that this movie is indeed bigger that the original.

title: In many respects recalls the original Star Wars film.....
review:
The latest addition to the Star Wars stable of films, The Force Awakens, recalls the first film made way back in 1977.

There's a hero who is unaware of her Jedi powers, a new, bigger Death Star and and a villain who shares the same lineage as Darth Vader and wants to be like him.

This film is not really doing anything, in other words, that has not already been done. Moreover, the original achieved what it did with more class and flair. The villain in this film lacks the presence and menace, of Darth Vader. The hero comes across as a rather desperate re-run of Luke Skywalker, whilst, "super sizing" a Death Star doesn't change the fact its still, well, a Death Star.

Reintroducing some classic Star Wars actors and characters, aside from the obvious nostalgia factor, does little to lift this film either.

The result is a rather ordinary flick, that is not bad, as such, but for those of us old enough to remember the original film, its not doing anything new either. Instead, The Force Awakens, looks more like a retread of a much better, earlier, envisioning from the Star Wars universe. Six out of ten from me.

title: Well done JJ Abrams
review:
What an undeniably difficult task to direct this film. You need to appease a loyal and vocal fan base, appeal to a new audience and stamp your own mark on the biggest franchise in cinema history. I think overall JJ Abrams was successful to a large extent but also failed to take the risks that made the original trilogy so special.

It is truly a wonderful experience to see this film, however, it is awfully familiar. It is no doubt the product of a think tank exercise, taking the most successful elements from the previous films and rehashing them in a new package. Not that this is a bad thing... Those elements work and work well. Further, other elements seemed to have been pulled from films like Harry Potter, Tomb Raider and Hunger Games to name just a few with similar effect. It is a collage of epic cinema and is very successful to that end.

The screenplay is watertight in structure given the huge amount of information they needed to portray, the dialogue reasonable (bar a few cringe worthy lines), the scenes memorable and it's remarkable how much they were able to fit into a 135 minute film. The action is strong, but at times a bit overdone and long and for true Star Wars fans the deep philosophy lacking for the most part. The performances again are strong across the board after a somewhat shaky first act, though this may have been me trying to adjust to the new faces in the Star Wars universe. On the universe itself, Abrams did a wonderful job making it feel how it should.

Technically it's very well made. It brings a modern take to the series without compromising its integrity. For example swipe cuts are prominent, yet many scenes begin with extreme close ups to close up to mid shot to long shot as opposed to the reverse in the original trilogy. Little things like that make it more familiar to a modern audience but don't bastardize it for everyone else.

Without giving anything away, I really did enjoy this film, but more over I think the cast and crew did an admirable job in a very difficult situation. Definitely worthwhile, 6 out of 10 is extremely fair for its lack of originality. Well done JJ Abrams, hopefully episode VIII brings many more new concepts to the table, I truly can't wait.

title: When disappointment awakens
review:
The force awakens is definitely not the best Star Wars movie you could watch but it's not the worst either (the clones attack is in my opinion).

* Spoiler Alerts *

First I would like to say that J.J. Abrams really tried is best to refresh the characters: Ray and Finn are excellent and I like the idea of introducing new young faces. However, and I must admit it is one of the greatest disappointment in the movie, the evil character alias kylo ren is a pale copy of Vader and lost all credibility after removing is mask. Seriously how can he act so bad? I also believe that it was totally unnecessary to make him part of the Han Solo family but whatever...

About the plot: the idea in the beginning is a catch but in the end it is only a remake of the death star story from the previous movies. Hopefully the characters are moving and funny which makes the conversations very pleasing. Getting back some characters of the original SW was a nostalgic touch but it was clearly approaching fan service at some point... I find it also hard to believe it is so easy to master the art of the Jedi in a few days time. The final battle scene is in this regards a good sum-up: Ray is able to confront kylo ren without any light saber knowledge! Congrats!

In the end I granted the movie a 7 which is more a 6.5 because I believe episode VII was designed to build the intrigue for the next episodes and I hope J.J. Abrams will correct the mistakes he made in this one. Besides the movie is keeping you alert so it deserves some credit.

Mickael

title: Entertaining Movie but that's It
review:
Although Epidode VII is a very good standalone Star Wars movie, once again they do a terrible job of trying to make it fit with the previous movies. Return of the Jedi left me very happy with the way things ended, the Sith and the empire were vanquished, Leia and Han lived happily ever after, Luke was a consummate Jedi and he turned Vader back to the light side of the force before dying.

This new chapter pretty much destroys all of that in trying to continue the story. Episode VII begins with chapter IV all over again, copying many aspects of the original story. It's the rebels against a new empire again now called The First Order (with a silly emperor called Supreme Leader Snoke), a new pet droid where they once again hide the maps of something valuable to the rebellion, another masked villain with an intimidating voice, another death star, X Wings again flying inside a ditch requiring precise shots to destroy it, etc, nothing new.

The production again fail to see what made the original trilogy so great was that it touched the hearts of all of us who grew up watching the movies, it had great characters and a beautiful story that teached many wonderful human values. Maybe Lucas believes that what makes the movies great are the special effects, monsters, cool lightsabres, ships, robots, etc.

So overall, It was an entertaining movie that made a terrible job of continuing with the Star Wars legacy.

title: Nothing like a Spielberg
review: Just watched star wars the force awakens. Incredible graphics, but in terms of story flow and character development, there's nothing like a Spielberg/Lucas film. Too much talking scenes. Unclear goals. Too many parts are taken from episode 4. Again, characters are not well defined . in terms of comedy, there were some good moments with Harrison ford, but not quite like his younger self. Leiahs character wasn't defined as well, just felt like fan service. The force felt like a super power instead of something you learn and tend to. The new Droid didn't do much. Not like r2 where u can see it knows it's stuff. They should get Spielberg on the next one 6.5/10

title: They owe us episode 6.5
review: I had the misfortune of watching all 6 previous episodes before viewing this movie. Both trilogies before this had very clear targets. Episodes 4, 5, 6 had the death of the Emperor as main purpose. And it was beautifully scripted and played. Episodes 1, 2, 3 had the creation of Vader as main purpose. Even if I did not appreciate these movies the first time I saw them, viewing them again, with full knowledge of the story, was a surprise really. They had a quite good overarching story, and the evil genius of the emperor was really well portrayed. Creating a conflict in which he was on both sides, it was a good script, and in the midst of action, alongside Anakin, Qui Gon, Yoda, Windu, Obi Wan, you tend to do the same as the Jedi: focus on the task at hand, and wait for the well planned and well played hand of the emperor to develop. Episode 3, and the last scenes were again, quite good. And then comes episode 7. What was decisive for episode 7, was the version of the universe it was set up in. I expected to see a universe more similar to episode 1. Full of life, and freed from the evil empire. I think this was my biggest disappointment. The fact that they made all the fight of such great characters (Luke, Leia, Han Solo, Chewbacca) to be for nothing really. It is disappointing to see a character appeared from nowhere (Snoke) could in 3 decades make all good characters to appear as if they never won. How about a version of the universe in which they had 30 years of peace, and these old characters need no back story because it was peace-time? It makes much more sense than all that non-sense presented as explanations in 2-3 phrases over the duration of the film. Really, what do they plan to do, a 6.5 episode??? There lays the key to the disappointment of most Star Wars fans. And while there is hope for the trilogy, they really need to stop it with blasting Death Stars, especially with 0 planning. It was like a brain-storming over coffee is sufficient to destroy a heavily militarized huge planet. Come. On. I really dislike that they made the movie for kids, and marketed it as a sequel for fans. Think of it. There was no mention of a Death Star in the trailers, nor of this joke character Snoke. If I saw that CGI created pseudo-Sith lord, I probably would have passed on the whole movie. The lack of character development was obvious. I would have preferred a slower story, with no Death Star destroyed in the first episode, but with good characters. Even if we don't know much about her, Rey is the only good thing in the whole story. Kylo Ren for me just did not deliver. Even if he killed Han Solo, he just did not seem credible, even after that. Maybe if he had the mask on all the time. The same can be said about most characters. Harrison Ford was good, but my guess is that he did not want to be involved in the next movies, so they had to take him out of the story. It felt a rushed move. The whole movie is in a hurry actually. Hurry up, quick, there needs to be time to blow up a super weapon after we briefly introduce the characters. To conclude, I think this franchise was conceived with episode 6 as the last episode. The death of Yoda is a symbol to that. I am still hopeful for the future, as probably they have scripted a good finale for the trilogy. But taking episode 7 by itself, it is probably the worst so far. And that should be of concern to Abrams. He may choose to just sell us toys, but it will come at the cost of his name in the business. If he wrecks this up, many people will avoid his movies in the future.

title: Better than TPM and AOTC, worse than ROTS
review:
Not as bad as I expected. From the reviews I was expecting cameos from the classic characters and the most minimal service possible of Star wars themes. (Star Trek Into Darkness was frankly a dreadful movie, so I had very low expectations going into this. )

The storyline is typical 'blockbuster'. You have a stereotypical bad guy. The good guys overcome obstacles and finally prevail in the end. The new characters aren't terrible. The classic characters seem very out of place here. Harrison Ford is an old man. He looks like a retiree. Carrie Fisher's role is completely unnecessary.

I suppose it's pointless to ask questions of the plot. But a couple of the ones I had: How is the Empire still around -and apparently more powerful than ever- after being defeated in ROTJ? And related: why do we still have a "resistance"? I thought the Republic won the war in ROTJ.

All in all, I'm glad I watched. There is one good scene where they jump into lightspeed with a huge bug on the windshield. That was very clever. For one brief moment, it felt like Star Wars was back.

title: Predictable? In french we say "phone called"
review:
My, my my Here we are. Star Wars episode VII, the force asleep!

I took defense of this movie since day one. "Relax people, it's J.J. Abrams. I was the Jedi against the bad Sith whom said "no F way, it will be awful".

He'll do good, I was telling myself, he has to. I was confident and maybe too much. I'm a fan of the Star Wars myth, but not hardcore. I found that it was the best option to wipe out all of (uh :p) the extend universe to start a new fresh day. But nothing was new, nothing was fresh (despite BB8).

Alone this movies is good. The first minutes, as a fan, you like the many similarities with Ep IV, but then by the time you learn who is Kylo Ren's father, the movie falls in a disaster of of "predictableness". New Emperor? I have promised my stepdaughter go go see the movie with her too because I thought it was worth seen twice. Now I will still fulfill my promise, and I hope that knowing everything will make me see the movie with a new eye, and maybe see and understand what it seems I have missed.

Or is it?

title: Felt a little disappointed
review:
This review will eventually contain spoilers but I will give fair warning before they begin.

I will admit that I was cautious entering this movie. I personally am a huge fan of the Expanded Universe but I am in no way one of those nuts that keeps harping about how "the book was better." Nevertheless, I was immediately disheartened way back when Disney announced that they were going to write off the EU as no longer canon. Still, I am willing to give anything a try and always go to movies and keep an open mind. Here is my review of Star Wars Episode VII: The Force Awakens.

As a simple, sci-fi action flick, it's not bad. There are plenty action sequences, strange creatures, interesting worlds, etc. If you want to see a movie that uses Star Wars names and technology and has explosions and light saber fights, you will enjoy this movie. But if you are looking for the hyped-up sequel to one of the greatest sagas in movie history, you may find yourself disappointed as I have. To me, this movie did not feel like it was a complete thought. Maybe when Episodes VIII and IX come out, they will all tie together nicely and feel complete, but as a standalone movie, VII felt lacking. When the end credits ran, I felt only like the first act of a play had finished. Maybe stylistically that's what J.J. Abrams was going for, but I feel like VII only exists to set up VIII and IX. In many other trilogies, each movie usually can stand on its own as a movie with a simple plot arc while also have the larger plot arc in the background. In the original trilogy, Episode IV had its own story that was about a simple farm boy breaking out on his own and becoming a hero. In VII, while there are several new characters who all have their own (very minor) arcs, I feel as though not much was done or not much focus was put on them. Not to mention the clunky timing of some things/scenes/events/etc.

****The next section may contain MINOR spoilers:****

The two new main protagonists (Rey and Finn) feel very hollow. The movie starts essentially in the midst of Finn's inciting event. There is no lead-up and we have no feelings towards his character and we're already witnessing his life going through a major change. This makes him hard to relate to or connect to when we don't know anything about his origin besides what little we're told throughout the movie in expositional dialogue. Next, we have Rey who is presented as a strong, independent female character who has compassion. The lead-up to her inciting event is a little more drawn out and has nicer pacing. After that moment, though, everything about her character is just very sloppily thrown at the audience or revealed when it's convenient to the story. Throughout the film, she feels less like a character and more like a walking ex- machina plot point. She has a plethora of skills that while could plausibly come from her life experiences, seem a little too good/convenient to be true. And that's not to mention the big reveal about her character.

Another protagonist is BB-8, the rolling ball droid. I will admit that BB-8 is adorable and a little funny, but the comedy seems awkward in the Star Wars Universe. In the original trilogy, the only real humor came from R2-D2 and C-3PO but that was not as prominent as it was in other Star Wars films. Yes, George Lucas went full slapstick with the prequels and that was one thing that people did not like about them. In Episode VII we get the slight droid humor that you came to expect from R2 in BB- 8 but you also get a lot more of the sarcastic one-liners that used to only belong to Han Solo from the other human characters. But I guess that's a problem in the modern cinema world where writers believe characters can only be liked if they are all as witty as a Joss Whedon character.

The antagonists also fell flat. The chrome, female storm trooper did not have enough screen time to really establish herself as a threat and Kylo Ren only left me wanting to rather see his journey to the dark side than what he did once he got there. The reveal of his character's backstory (what little we got) was a bit clunky and honestly predictable. And we got NOTHING on the Captain Phasma (the chrome trooper).

****MAJOR Spoiler****

The story arc was aggravating due to it returning to the "successful" story arc that existed in episodes IV and VI; big start base, rescue mission, all blows up.

***FINAL WORD***

I was disappointed and can probably write a thesis on the problems I had with this movie from character development to how they used the force in the movie, but I'll just sum it all up saying hardcore Star Wars fans (EU fans) will be disappointed but those who have only seen the movies may enjoy this. Younger crowds will like the fast-paced story and action and I would recommend it to anyone who just wants to watch an entertaining movie for a couple hours.

Me: 6/10

title: Abrams brings the wonder of The Force to a new generation.
review:
If you don't include the dreadful prequel trilogy from George Lucas, many Star Wars fans have spent over thirty years waiting for the next great addition to the sci-fi saga worshipped the world over.

With The Force Awakens, J.J. Abrams has delivered a thrilling, energetic, though not altogether mind- blowing film that has deftly added to the rich tapestry that is Star Wars, putting the saga in good stead for years to come.

We first meet the villainous First Order and Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) through the eyes of heroic Resistance fighter pilot Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac). Hidden inside Dameron's droid, BB-8, is a map to the mythic Jedi Master Luke Skywalker, who has disappeared off the face of the galaxy since overthrowing the Empire many moons ago.

When Dameron is captured, disillusioned stormtrooper Finn (John Boyega) helps him escape, and the two team up with backwater scavenger Rey (Daisy Ridley) – and some familiar faces – to find Luke before the enemy can.

The film ticks all the boxes demanded of the tent pole of a new trilogy. Our new heroes are introduced organically and the effortless chemistry between them is immediately apparent.

More importantly, each character just feels likable; a far cry from the cardboard caricatures and stiffly spoken occupants of Lucas' prior trilogy. Boyega, the most lighthearted of the three, is particularly great at mixing comic relief and deathly seriousness to form a well-rounded, magnetic character. No Jar Jar Binks is he.

The trio is still made up of the handsome, rougish pilot, the unwitting and sometimes unwilling youngster, and the anti-damsel-in-distress whose mysterious origins confound her comrades, but each character has enough individualism for this to not be a huge problem.

Somewhat more concerning is the film's over-reliance on fan service and obvious hark backs to the original trilogy, and Episode IV especially. More than once, Abrams' safe decisions cross the line from merely winking at the audience to recycling giant chunks of a plot we've already seen before.

The main setting is a bigger, badder Death Star. The main battle is waged both on the ground between mentor and fallen apprentice, and in the sky between fighter squadrons. The main revelation is again familial in nature. The film spends so much time making these comparisons glaringly obvious that it detracts from the other major arcs a couple of new characters go through. As a result, their journeys feel rushed and perhaps more suited to span across two or three movies, not one.

Regardless, The Force Awakens does everything a Star Wars film should. It is blistering, absorbing, and ends on a heaving, operatic note sure to leave fans theorising until Episode VIII.
