title: Star Wars Episode VII: A New Hope(ish)
review:
The Force Awakens, contrary to popular belief this is the movie fans have been looking forward to. After the dreadful taste left in many fans mouths because of the Prequel Trilogy, this is the film that acts as the mouthwash. After many groans and murmurings when Disney bought the Franchise, I can safely say that you shouldn't worry, at least not yet.

The Force Awakens brings back many classic characters, some a bit unexpected I may say. It also brings in with it a host of new characters, locations and fresh air. Even the music in which John Williams could've just replayed a CD containing his old soundtracks and gotten away with it, but instead has them hinting at the surface while bringing a fresh face to this universe.

When the film starts, we're instantly shoved straight into nostalgia, from the opening crawl to the cheesy 70's scene transitions. But that doesn't slow the pace down at all, the film chops between paying homage to the original (A New Hope) and bringing in a fresh exciting new tone to the movie.

This movie I could safely say is very good, it's exciting getting to see a fan in the reins of another one of the biggest franchises . Not only does Abrams managed to pull off the fine line between homaging and making new. He also makes sure that it isn't rushed or off-kilter.

This film could've been what many films are doing now and simply be full of action, near-constant CGI but it isn't. In fact, it seems that CGI is expressively been reserved for things not physically possible. The plot is well done and everything new brought in blends seamlessly with the old.

I have to praise both Daisy Ridley and John Boyega. Their characters are sympathetic and I could say that this film will launch their careers from their performances. Adam Driver's Kylo Ren seems to be a more well-thought out character and doesn't come across as a one- dimensional villain I felt that Darth Vader was in A New Hope. He is conflicted and unstable and delivers a powerful performance, especially in the last half-hour.

After saying all that though, it doesn't all come to a fantastic movie. Some characters that aren't especially well done include Emperor Snoke, who doesn't really seem to compare that well to his counterpart Emperor Palpatine. Oscar Issacs Poe Dameron seems extremely underused considering that he was advertised as one of the three heroes of the new trilogy.

My other concern is that the nostalgia is going to overcrowd it. The homaging that frequents the movie at times borders into outright recreation, which makes it feel as though the only reason that the film is liked is because it is the movie they love remade. There's enough new content for it to be its own entity and I just hope that in the next two instalments they can shake off the reins and become its own.

I have high hopes for the next instalments after this, especially with JJ Abrams who helped Rian Johnson work out some of the kinks in the upcoming Episode VIII and Colin Trevorrow who helped revive the Jurassic Park franchise after a lot of dead-end sequels will be directing Episode VX.

In short, fans of Star Wars will love the new film, it shocks, amazes and rings true to what came before. It will capture the interest of new watchers and possibly bring more into the fan-base. To casual viewers, it'll be fun to watch but nothing spectacular. And that is kind of what this film is, it's better than you would of thought but still nothing compared to the originals.

title: Everyone Has Already Seen The Film Anyway...
review:
I don't think there are any real spoilers in this review, but I checked the box just in case.

No one will be influenced to see or not see this film based on these reviews because everyone that reads these reviews have already seen the film and are just deciding whose opinion agrees with their own. With that in mind, this review will be down-voted by all of my fellow Star Wars fans, but I have to be honest about it anyway.

If you enjoyed the first film of the franchise ("Episode IV"), which I loved since I saw it as a 10-year-old in the Cine Capri Theater in Phoenix in its second week of release in 1977 and the dozen or so times I've watched it since, then you'll enjoy this one, because it's basically the same movie with more advanced special effects. When I saw it on opening day, I would have rated it six or seven stars. After seeing it again a few days later, I feel it's worthy of eight stars. The humor could have been better with the caliber of writers in the business these days, and it would have been cool if there had been some surprises or plot twists, but there just weren't any.

A protagonist whose aspirations are linked to the stars is living on a desert planet, is found by a droid carrying important information that has to be delivered to the secret rebel base, and gets caught up in a galactic struggle via the Millennium Falcon and its big-hearted smuggler owner, Han Solo. Sound familiar? Except this one has a masked villain in black who takes the film's heroine prisoner on his planet-destroying space station to extract information about the resistance... Oh, wait.

Okay, well this bad guy used to be a good guy but was seduced by the dark side and is now the protegé of a holographic evil leader... Dang! That sounds like Episode IV also.

Well in this one, the villain uses his his light saber to kill... Ah, never mind.

The most "tragic" part of the film could be seen coming a mile away, but a lot of people act like they were surprised by it. The good news is there are no Ewoks, Gungans, or other goofy species in large numbers, so it doesn't have the silliness of some of the other episodes.

From the perspective of this being the introduction to another potentially good Robin Hood saga about the benevolent rebels fighting the evil empire, this is a very enjoyable film. I'm very interested to see where the story goes, and how it develops before Rey kills Kylo Ren and the Resistance destroys the First Order.

I'm looking forward to the next episode to see if there's an explanation as to why the heroine of the film is already practically a Jedi master without even being trained in the ways of the Force. I'd also like to know more about that light saber/tonfa combo weapon with which that stormtrooper was kicking Finn's butt! Where did that come from!? LOL

title: Great Movie, Recycled Story
review:
It's true. The movie is good. It's also true that all of the complaining people on here upset about the recycled copy of a storyline as it applies to the other Star Wars movies have a point. Let me first of all touch on a fact that everyone knows by now: it's a good movie.

The pacing in this movie is basically spot on. When I say spot on, I mean that from the minute we finish the vanishing text wall at the start of the movie, SW starts you on the edge of your seat. At the end of the movie one quickly realizes that the edge of your seat is where most viewers potentially spend the majority of the film. There are few lulls or downtime in the film. As far as pacing goes I am going to say 9.5/10 well done.

The acting is decent. Not great, but definitely decent. Harrison Ford convincingly and expertly pulls off his character as Han Solo. From the minute he enters the story until the bitter end Ford uplifts the quality of the movie. In fact I think that if Ford were not in this movie, the overall score for this movie would suffer. Daisy as Ren does a good job and is interesting. Fin played by Boyega was decent. As the series continues he could excel or fail depending on how his character develops. Kylo Ren by Adam Driver has the opportunity to become a legendary actor if he can pull it off in the sequels, but I felt he just didn't get enough face time (no mask) to provide a solid review on Driver. Leia, General Hux and the other supporting characters did their job of supporting. That said there was something about Hux that fell a bit short in my books. Leading the entire army he should have a more commanding stage presence than he carried. Lupita playing Maz Kanata was top notch for a CG character, and I felt that Supreme Leader Snoke was poorly done played by Anthony Serkis. I believe Serkis was a victim of poor CG combined with poor on-screen acting presence the result of his character being a 40 foot tall hologram. So acting overall for this movie 7.5/10

The story was most notably copied from their earlier SW episodes, as if JJ just took the parts that seems to work from the other six films and copied them into Episode 7. While this seems to have infinitely angered many a fan boy, the fact of the matter is, is that it was still well done. I am going to give the story a 6.5/10 because of the recycled story.

Special effects, creatures, equipment, scenery, and backdrops were top notch. SWVII managed to capture all aspects of the dirty, greasy, used equipment look that the original films did so well. 9/10 on CG, cinematography, practical effects.

Canon, lore, plot holes and impossible moments: The mistakes like how could Kylo sense a non-force users presence like Han Solo's? How was Ren able to learn to use the Force abilities at such high levels with ZERO training? I was particularly excited to see Snoke on screen, but quickly let down as he neither radiated wisdom, nor the type of sinister dark side presence compared to Darth Sideous, Darth Maul or even Vadder. For the guy that is likely to turn out to be the ultimate mastermind of the dark side being that he is probably Darth Plaguis "The Wise" what a let down...thus far. 7/10 on Canon, plot holes and things that just don't make sense.

Flow, overall impact, impression 9/10 Grand Total for SWVII is 8/10 Not perfect by far, but it's still a great movie

title: Entertaining, not fantastic.
review:
C'mon, we all knew that this film couldn't live up to the high standards the original Star Wars films set. We also all knew that the "magic" of the originals wouldn't be largely intact in this new film.

For that reason, I was pleasantly surprised with JJ Abrams' newest installment. Sure, it was full of hackneyed clichés and admittedly relied on recycled material from the original trilogy. However, the plot was solid, the new main roles were great, and it's a heck of a lot better than the prequels.

I won't belabor the point, so here's a tldr. It's entertaining, albeit flawed. You'll laugh every now and then, you might feel suspense, and it won't make you too disappointed. So you might as well watch it.

title: same story and yet unexpected
review:
Expectations where high on this blockbuster, but though I was in fear of being disappointed, that was not the case. The movie keeps your attention and packs everything a movie needs. The makers knew it packed everything it needs, because it is a shameless remake of A New Hope and that was about the only really annoying thing about it. They should have made it "more different".

The main characters are quickly introduced in the movie and their journey throughout the story makes sense, but even in the characters the remake is way too obvious. Kylo Ren is, just like his example Darth Vader (Anakin Skywalker), a winy little snot on a power trip and this is where I did expect something more. The older Leia and Han and Chewie are a nice touch, BB-8 holds is own and though I would have preferred R2-D2 it will be nice to see those two side by side in the next installments.

Visually the movie grasps your attention and at times the 3D is astonishing (and I'm not a 3D fan). At no point was the movie doing "too much" visuals or 3D.

The first links to the older movies have been laid, but it will be nice to see how things start tying up further down the road.

Job well done and I can't wait to see the next one.

title: The Star Wars movie we deserved, but not the one we needed!
review:
If you are a Star Wars fan, give this movie a second viewing before you make a decision on it. Judge it like you would if 'Star Wars' wasn't in the title.

Overall The Force Awakens is an entertaining, but not groundbreaking movie. The new characters are great in it. Daisy Ridley is amazing as Rey, and definitely deserves more screen time to make it more about her. All the actors did fantastic jobs, and I was especially glad to see Chewbacca actually get a decent role. The fight scenes are well done and look amazing. The humor is well placed throughout the movie to keep it light-hearted.

Despite these things, I do not think this movie will be remembered or that in ten years anyone will care about it. There are a few major problems with this movie:

1) Movie is less about the story and more about the action. Episode VII sets us up for a new trilogy, and in my opinion it should have spent almost all its time on making us understand and care about the characters and what they are doing. There is plenty of time in the next two for explosions and lightsabers. The beginning of the film does a great job introducing Rey, but this is quickly swept under the rug to make room for more action scenes.

2) Answers too few questions/Tries too hard to not be the prequels. They avoided this at all costs, and went a little overboard on it. Sometimes things need an explanation for us to actually care about it. Who was that guy that just got killed? What was that planet they just blew up? Why are the Republic and the Resistance not the same thing? How did the First Order come around? Who is the stormtrooper with shiny armor? Who is hologram guy and why is he supposed to be scary? Why is Rey scaling that wall and going in that hole?

3) Story has too many conveniences. It is important to me that my space opera with laser swords and tentacle aliens be semi-believable. Obi-wan Kenobi said there was no such thing as luck, but that must have been a different galaxy because there is a lot going on in this movie!

4) Plot is basically a re-packaged New Hope. I keep debating with myself if this was done intentionally or if they thought no one would notice, but it still bothers me that they basically took A New Hope's script and changed the names of characters and places.

5) Natural talent with lightsabers/force?? The fact that Rey and Finn didn't immediately lose appendages after turning on a lightsaber without any kind of instruction blows my mind. I guess you can explain that Rey has her staff so is used to melee combat, and Finn may have been semi-trained as a stormtrooper. But a lightsaber, and a lightsaber duel is completely different and they should have been clueless. This may only bother me. Rey's ability to just start using the force is the most annoying part though. Luke had to be trained by Yoda (a revered Jedi Master) on Dagobah to learn simple things, yet Rey jumps into expert mode in a moment's notice.

Despite my long list of negatives, I did enjoy the movie and wish I could spend more time talking about what I did like without spoiling anything. I rate this as worth watching but nothing to get particularly excited about.

title: Disappointing
review:
I was expecting so much more from this film. Instead what we seem to have is a remake of the first film but with updates. At the end I was left flat. While the new actors showed some enthusiasm the others seemed to sleep walk through their roles.

Carrie Fisher should have stayed in bed. While some attempt is made to cover the missing 30 years this is disjointed and hardly believable.

I thought Daisy Ridley did a good job with her role while Harrison Ford made the best of his role.

The Supreme Leader was a real disappointment.

Far too many ideas taken from previous episodes.

title: Strong the force with the new cast is
review:
Daisy earns 10/10 for her intense play. The scenes on her home planet are the best and on par with the ones in 'Hope' as well as Williams' absolutely beautiful 'Scavenger' theme. Finn is a great character and Boyega the perfect actor for it. I like also Drivers subtle performance, he's great as (already very dangerous but still unsure) Vader wannabe. Poe is also a great character and the actor plays the pilot the way I know this optimistic tough guys in reality. the bad guy general as usual in SW has not enough room in the movie to be exposed in depth but is also great play. Snoke was somewhat disappointing but OK.

I was a 15 years old when watching the original movie in '78. It changed my live and influenced my choice of profession. But at this time the movie was a revolution. TFA is solid and very entertaining. I can't simply understand why some people are that frustrated. I felt great most of the time even I've missed the simple, dreamy story development of 'Hope'. But this times will never come back. Today everything is fast paced. And considering the way movies are made today, under pressure of a big company, this is perhaps the best we can get.

I'm looking forward to see great scenes and moments when Rey will be teached by Luke in EP VIII. This two exceptional actors together will be able to create a remarkable moment in movie history. I hope the director and the script are able too.

And Disney: go for risks! Send your marketing guys on vacations for the next release! We don't need a death star like thing twenty time bigger in there! Let the force flow through you...

review:

title: Good Story, Bad Scenario, Missing Opportunity
review:
"This review contains spoilers" First of all, it's a nice thing to we have a new Star Wars Movie.

If I didn't watch Original Trilogy, I would like this one more. But it really feels as remake of the A New Hope when we watch it.

I really liked the good characters. But what I didn't like is the Dark Side characters & empire's new name: "The First Order".

What we learn from this movie is after some years of the Return Of The Jedi, Luke starts to teach young people the Force. One of his students is his nephew, the grandson of the Darth Vader. He choose the Dark Side & this collapse our original trilogy heroes. Han leaves with Chew to get himself together, Leia stays & become a general at Rebellion. Luke is also leave & search for the first Jedi Temple. The movie itself is searching for the last Jedi, Luke Skywalker.

What I didn't like it about this movie is weak Dark Side characters like Kylo Ren. He is weak in mind & soul. Also his master Leader Snoke has nothing special. What was really special about Star Wars is how strong & charismatic of their evil characters & unexpected surprisings(love interest Luke & Leia are brother & sister, main villain is their father, Obi-Wan lies to Luke etc).

It was a good idea that Han's son & Luke's nephew turn to dark side. But what it isn't good is we know this from almost the very start. They should reveal it at the end of the movie.

I liked the new lightsaber & duels of the movie.

But Kylo Ren is way too skinny, mentally weak & unstable crybaby Darth Vader complex boy. Darth Vader has a lot right about to turn to dark side & stayed in it but it seems this boy doesn't. He also "SPOILER ALERT" killed his father for nothing, there is no good on him anymore. Han's death was way too easy.

The end of the movie, who really are Rey's parents & who the hell is Sith Master Leader Snoke is still interesting & these are can save the next movie. But I hope they won't start to build another Death Star like structure, its really annoying.

If you like the original trilogy, you may like it, but don't get too high expectations.

title: Most boring Star Wars movie
review: 1. It's a "New Hope" Remake 2. The Enemies are bad. Snoke is 1:1 like Sidious, Kylo Ren is a crybaby and i can't take him serious and the rest of the first order are space Nazis. 3. Rey is overpowered 4. It was obvious that Han Solo will die 5. Boring 6. Many things don't make any sense (like a third Death Star after the first and second one got destroyed) 7. THIS MOVIE IS WORTHLESS! Why should I watch it again? It's the same Story like in "New Hope", the character aren't interesting and it's adds nothing new to the Star Wars franchise!

title: Oh Lord help us...
review:
Again, I was so excited when the these sequels were announced....WAS.

The only redeeming quality in this particular movie, was Harrison Ford coming back. Nothing else. As much as I disliked the prequels, these new sequels make the prequels almost watchable. These new movies, especially this one, misses the spirit of Lucas's original vision. Its noticably more violent for some reason, and that was a turn off. Star Wars doesnt have to be violent...Sure, the original movies had some dead guys, but nothing like how this movie started, with execution. Its overall distasteful and has no place in the Star Wars universe. its supposed to be a fun place to visit....what I saw here, wasn't fun at all. The forced comedy, the overall rehashed plot, a Ginger bad guy who cant seem to use his inside voice, a chrome stormtrooper that literally serves NO good purpose.

Im spent...signing off....

title: World war two in space
review:
It is great to see older characters still playing key parts. It should be fun to see star ships and alien pubs. However, it is the same movie over and over.

The movie is better than the three predecessors cinematically but the stories are like groundhog day. In a never ending loop of baddies surfacing, goodies triumphing, people being saved to be killed off in next iterations. The outfits resemble earlier world wars and there is a very strong Nazi vs allied theme in wardrobe, script and settings.

Personally I am tired of reliving the past and reliving old relics. Some originality would be nice. They had to find creative inspiration from a bygone era, but instead of making it into something new and fresh, it was a poor carbon copy.

The costumes and characters have changed but the story is no different. We all continue to watch the same thing over and over again as the magic of the alien worlds and the Force keeps us believing that the next great film is possibly hidden in there somewhere.

Please be creative. Please make cinema fun again.

And can the baddie perhaps be completely unrelated to one of the main characters and just a random crazy?

title: It didn't work for me really
review:
I guess I'm not an Abrams fan. There, I said it. I think he's almost ruined the Star Trek franchise. Sure, he's producing the action-filled and CGI-based sci-fi that young men 16 to 21 years of age want to see, but his work seems to lack originality, thoughtfulness, cleverness. I just don't find it that entertaining. He's good at fast-paced adventure, but that's not really what I want out of a movie.

What can I say about the rest of it? It was all competently done, but it just didn't seem new, original or exciting. It dragged on.

The return of the old cast was an interesting twist, but to me it just highlighted how the later movies have failed to develop a cast of equal impact.

The high score has been bestowed on Abrams by his teenage male fans. The rest of us just didn't like it that much, I suppose.

My heart sank when I saw that Oscar Isaac was in this movie because I think it's beneath his talents. But I appreciated his part in the movie. I like everything he does, really.

So I want to give this movie about 7.5. I'm going to round it down to 7 because I spent most of the movie on my smart phone.

title: Review: Star Wars â€“ The Force Awakens (2015)
review:
WARNING: POST CONTAINS SPOILERS

After nearly a decade, the Star Wars franchise blasts back on to the big screen in J.J. Abrams' long-awaited episode seven.

The film is set some thirty years after the death of the Emperor and follows the search for Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) who has gone into self-imposed exile after the failure of his attempt to resurrect the Jedi Order at the hands of his apprentice, now named Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), who was seduced to the Dark Side of the Force by Snoke (Andy Serkis), the Supreme Leader of the First Order that arose in the aftermath of the galactic civil war and is attempting to restore the Galactic Empire. With the Senate of the New Republic refusing to acknowledge the threat of the First Order, Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher) has gone back underground and is the General in command of the resistance within the First Order's territory and is supported in a deniable fashion by some elements of the New Republic. To some viewers dismay, the original trilogy cast are secondary to the plot and this is very much a 'passing of the torch' film, with the new characters taking centre stage as it focuses on Rey (Daisy Ridley), a scavenger on the planet Jakku, and Finn (John Boyega), a defecting Stormtrooper, who meet on Jakku after Finn helps resistance fighter pilot Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac) escape from the Star Destroyer he was being held prisoner on, and how they all are swept up in the search for the last Jedi.

As with all Star Wars films, the effects are stunning and the action fast passed and thrilling, but my prejudices against Abrams' story telling abilities remain very much intact as the plot is a rehash of episode four with Lawrence Kasdan's writing efforts seemingly limited to ensuring the original trilogy characters remain true to form. Of the original trilogy characters, it is Han Solo (Harrison Ford) who drives a lot of the action forward as we learn that Kylo Ren is, in fact, his and Leia's estranged son, Ben Solo. Because the plot is a reworking of episode four, we could see very early on that Solo was the Obi-Wan figure and that he would meet his end at the hands of Kylo Ren in the same way that Obi-Wan died at the hands of Darth Vader. Even so, his death is a genuinely shocking moment as, even though we all saw it coming, it was still a surprise to see that the writers and studio had the nerve to kill off such a popular character.

There are a lot of plot holes and gaps in the storyline such as how Han lost the Millennium Falcon, how the First Order came about and why they're not using clone Stormtroopers who are programmed for obedience, and who Snoke is and how he came to lead the First Order. I know that there is a trilogy of novels being written by Chuck Wendig to bridge the gap between episodes six and seven, but there's no guarantee that all of the fans will read them which means the pressure is now on episode eight to deliver a lot of this back story. Having said all of that, the writing is very well done with well-rounded and likable characters, good action set pieces and an excellent lead in to episode eight in 2017.

One of my biggest gripes with the writing is that it was stressed that this would be a new storyline for the Star Wars universe and that it would not have anything to do with the story lines in the extended universe novels, and yet it certainly borrows from both the Heir to the Empire and Fate of the Jedi series so much so that I have to wonder why they didn't just film those books. Even with all of the above mentioned flaws I'd still recommend going to see it, but, for me, this was a six out of ten movie that just about escapes being a 'meh' moment.

title: Not as bad as Some Say, Not as Good as it Could Have Been
review:
I just got done reading a bunch of reviews and wow, close but a bit harsh. Here's a quick honest review that isn't based on immediate hatred.

The movie is good. As everyone has commented on, it closely follows the first movie (IV) in plot, however it is not exact and by the end it starts to walk its own path. After walking out of the Theater, my first reaction was: I wish I could see VIII and see where they take it. It's faster paced than previous movies and the dialog is a little stupid at times. Its big budget, so there's lots of explosions, CGI, characters, etc. I did appreciate the softer touch on the CGI than episode 1-3 had. After reflecting, the movie seemed to want to re-introduce the SW world to a new generation, and then set up a long string of additional movies. I felt that this was the way the movie had to go: meaning: they had to set up the old world SW with similar characters and ideas, but now want to move the franchise into a more modern feel/theme. Its a movie that had to be made to move the series forward and no matter what was made, it would get hated on. It's honestly not that bad.

For the bad: it's a little bland for characters. Lucas really took the time to set up his characters and this movie fell just a little short. Its easy to say as we can look back and see all 3 movies (4-6) as whole though. Because it was really close to IV, there wasn't to much that will be surprising, as left me feeling a bit tired at times. The force or lack of. This movie really had the worst inclusion of the force in all 6 previous ones. As a viewer, we're already very versed in the use of the force and this was a complete slap in the face in this regards. The force is set up like IV when we knew nothing, so it's a bit lame (best word I could think of). The second is the final battle. As everyone has pointed out, having Fin and Rey fight a Sith with relative ease is absolutely ridiculous. My only saving grace is that it's explained in VIII (this alone was 3 less stars), so...

If 8 goes in a newer direction, then this will turn out to be a really good movie. If 8 stays as close to the previous movies as this one did, and without giving us a really good reason on the 2 main characters apparently have super powers, the series will all but be over.

Final note on all the 1 stars: I think Star Wars must be like Heroin: The first ride is so good, then the rest can never live up to it, but you grudgingly keep going back for more.

title: Graphics were awesome but the story was not.
review:
The graphics was amazing. Everything looked like real. If I would rate this film by only the graphics I would give it a 10/10. And I must admit that even if I hate 3d, the 3d in this film was very well.

So the story.... It's just a modified copy of Episode IV. A copy of Death Star, a copy of Darth Vader -but less powerful and a teenager- (Kylo Ren) , a copy of Luke Skywalker(Rey), a copy of destroying Death Star, a copy of defeating a sith lord without any training(Episode VI Final Battle). Yes Luke was trained but it was not enough to defeat someone like Darth Vader.

I'm not saying that the film was bad, but it's not worth 8,9,10/10. If I had a chance to rate it in decimal It would've been 7.6/10.

title: Star Wars - Recycled Plot Awakens
review:
A droid containing vital information is being pursued by the bad guys on a desert planet. The droid's orphan companion meets up with a new friend, a smuggler and a wookie. Meanwhile, the bad guys have built a massive weapon capable of destroying planets. Luckily the good guys figure out they need to take out the shield then fly fighters at its core to blow it up. Also, there is an old Jedi who has exiled himself to a remote location and the main bad guy wears all black and a mask which makes his voice sound scary. There is the surprise death of a main character and "surprise" revelation about family members.

Does any of the above sound familiar? It should because it's almost a direct copy of Episode IV's plot with elements of the other movies of the original trilogy thrown in.

Let's start with the bad so we can finish on a positive note.

1) Don't they have email or something similar in this universe? Why are they still relying effectively on carrier pigeon (droid) to relay vital information. It's ridiculous.

2) The Villain: sorry, but this has to be the wimpiest Star Wars villain ever. I thought the prequel Anakin was the whiniest little sook in the galaxy until I saw Kylo Ren. Yes he's obviously powerful, but when it comes to lightsaber duels he struggles to beat a garbage man (Finn literally worked in the sanitation area of the super weapon) and a girl who found out five minutes earlier that she had special powers. What the...?

He could easily force choke or force push both of them so why didn't he? Doesn't make sense.

3) What the hell happened in the previous 30 years? Really, there's no discussion about what has happened, how First Order and the supreme leader came about, how Kylo Ren turned to the dark side etc etc. I know you need to be mindful of info dump conversations and flashbacks but I think we needed something to fill in those years.

I shouldn't have been surprised at the laziness of the writers but I was. There's so many ways they could've gone with this and they took the easiest way. Recycle recycle recycle.

The good:

1) I loved the way this movie looked. Had that gritty look that the original movie had. The thing I hated about the prequel trilogy was how intrusive the CGI was. Everything was a little too glossy for my liking. As always the creatures, aliens, ships etc looked great.

2) Humour. I know some people didn't like the humour in this movie, but humour, like beauty, is in the eye of the beholder.

3) The old: was great to see the old characters again.

So why 7 out of 10 rating then? Because it's Star Wars: fun, action filled, not something to be taken too seriously. Switch your brain off for a couple of hours and just enjoy it for what it is. Just don't expect anything new or even creative.

title: A Mimic of Star Wars
review:
J.J. Abrams is an exceptional mimic and director.

In this extension of the Star Wars series, he faithfully captures the visual tone of the original trilogy, specifically episode IV. It was an enjoyable movie. That being said, though the tone and quality direction of Star Wars The Force Awakens was clearly evident, the actual genius and depth found in the other Star Wars movies was nowhere in this film. Even the much maligned prequels had way more depth, plot points, thematic quality, and character development than the Force Awakens. If not for the appearance of the original cast from this movie there would have been no emotional drive or connection in this movie.

It was an action movie with a borrowed heart.

This may well be that a generation raised on Star Wars primarily from a gaming console has now lost the expectation of anything more from the series than well directed action. I am not saying I didn't enjoy the space romp, I did. I enjoyed both the main characters which were well acted, though screaming for enough back story for me to actually care for them. If not for the presence of the original cast there would have been no emotional pull at all.

The beautiful message, memorable characters, and depth of storytelling that was in Lucas's movies I hope they get back to. For the first foray into this universe by someone other than Lucas, it was promising. As a full fledge Star Wars movie, it was lacking. I am still holding out hope for the future of the now Disney franchise.

title: welcome to 1977 - without the surprise

in the meantime, we've got freakish aliens in a cantina and people playing board games with little monsters.
