title: Not original but good if you loved the classic
review:
So I have been saving the latest Sar Wars movie since there isn't anything worth watching in the cinemas at the moment, and I finally watched it in the New Year's day. The verdict: I enjoyed it, but don't think I would bother watching it again. I don't think I would call myself a Star Wars fan, but I love the characters and the concept. I have the entire DVD collection, classic and modern, but I don't buy memorabilia and I don't remember many details about the movies like a lot of fans do.

If you have watched all the star wars movies and have talked to others who have done the same, you should know that they can be divided into two groups: those that prefer the classic movies (Episodes IV to VI , made in the 70s) and the ones that like the modern ones better (episodes I to III). Personally, I prefer the modern trilogy. I enjoyed the classic movies, but I can't get in the mood to watch it again.

I like the modern ones better because even though it's filled with cheesy dialogues, the characters feel more modern, the action and fight scenes overall are much better, there is plenty of "Jedi wisdom" and you can feel the intensity of the characters and the drama of the stories, specially with episode III. And because of that, I have watched them more than once.

This latest film feels very much like the classic ones, the action is mediocre, and the special effects have nothing new to offer. The plot, while enjoyable, is far from amazing, and for anyone who has watched the previous films, there is a constant feeling of Deja-Vu, as they have reused many elements of previous stories, even though this is clearly a continuation, as it supposedly carries on where the previous episode left off! I also didn't find myself "falling in love" with any particular character, I just wanted the good guys to win as always and I liked some more than others.

So don't expect to be amazed by the action, the drama or the (lack of) originality. You will however, get pretty much every element of a Star Wars movie, so if you are a fan, you should enjoy watching a fresh episode, even if it seems somewhat regurgitated from previous ones. When you are done watching, you will realize that they are in essence setting the stage for the other episodes to come, which I am hoping, will be more exciting than this one.

title: Bright & exciting but ultimately too safe to be Gold-- just Gilded Metal.
review:
*** S P O I L E R - F R E E - R E V I E W ***

Star Wars: The Force Awakens follows the adventure of a conflicted former Storm Trooper Finn (John Boyega) and the tough-as-she-looks desert scavenger Rey (Daisy Ridley), when their lives take an interesting turn following an energetic droid, BB-8, with important information that can change the fate of the galaxy. BB-8 is in a tug-of-war between The First Order, an army risen from the ashes of the Empire and led by the Emotional, yet powerful Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), and the Resistance, doing the same job as the Rebels in the previous movies, and led by their Ace Pilot Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac).

Those four names are very important, because besides the simply awe- inspiring feeling of seeing Star Wars in a bottom-less pit of Disney money to offer incredible production value, the characters is what this movie is truly about. I believe that is what director JJ Abrams set out to achieve with rebooting the Star Wars franchise. Because, to put it frankly, the overall story and pacing of the movie is quite lacking. With all the throw-backs to the original trilogy and twice as many main characters, the movie feels like it moves very fast.

It would make sense then, to put the characters into a safe setting that you don't have to worry about, so you can focus on their development. That's exactly what Abrams did; the plot is egregiously sampled from Lucas' original Episode IV. I figured the addition of Lawrence Kasdan (screenwriter for Episode V/VI) and reuniting the old cast of Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher, and Mark Hamill was enough to ensure fans the movie was in good hands. Unfortunately, that wasn't enough of a safe guard for Abrams, and he decided to play in the kiddie pool, and not jump into the vast sea of possibilities that is the Star Wars universe and allowed this movie to feel more like a "reboot" or "greatest hits" rather than a true sequel.

For now I will present to you my scorecard for the movie:

MOVIE SCORE 7 / 10

  • STORY: ( Plot / Pacing) 1


  • CHARACTERS: ( Acting / Character Development ) 2


  • VISUALS: ( Sets & Camera Work / Effects ) 1


  • SOUND: ( Music / Effects ) 1


  • ORIGINALITY: ( Creativity / Overall Significance) 2


The story ends up collapsing on itself as the film goes on, but the acting and character development was quite good on it's own before that. The sets were beautiful and were shot in the style of Lucas' original trilogy to give the movies the same feel. However, some camera shots were a bit uncomfortable.

The music, possibly because I've heard it for nearly 20 years of my life now, just didn't seem to interest me in this film. I believe the music tried to be conservative as well. Like I said, seeing all the space ships in 2015 is just breath taking and super fun to watch. The sounds were great as well, and there is one scene with the Millennium Falcon that I can't talk about but the sound just rings in my head and is the main reason why I want to see this movie again.

That same scene with the Millennium Falcon is why I scored the movie so highly with originality, it's something I've never seen in Star Wars before. As for the movies overall significance, there was a lot of potential if it didn't copy IV so much, but the new characters are great, and unfortunately I have to admit that the diversity offered in the casting was quite refreshing as well, sorry!

End of the day though, Star Wars: The Force Awakens played it too safe to truly be great, but still offers unforgettable moments that make it worth watching. It's impossible to rate this movie more poorly than I have, but the fan outrage on the Episode IV rip off is completely justified.

title: Good flick!
review:
Star Wars was, and always will be, space cowboys. If you accept this then you will enjoy this movie. It was a delightful bit of entertainment and a treat to see some of the old characters and how they grew over time.

Granted, there was some blatant re-hashing of past scenes but what do you expect when J.J. Abrams is at the helm; we all know how he butchered Star Trek. I groaned at one or two, and sat aghast at the audacity of a few others. I also found myself questioning some of the action scenes as implausible within the context like "why didn't he just use the force on Fin instead of his light saber?" Some of the story was predictable as a result. I found myself wondering if I should boycott J.J. Abrams entirely since he obviously thinks all movie- goers are brain-dead idiots...or at least Star Wars and Star Trek fans are now that I have seen what he has done with both franchises. (I have already decided I won't see another Star Trek movie unless they start making new stories and developing new characters and not try to spoon-feed me another version of Kirk and Spock.) Is it that J.J. Abrams has become a harbinger of the end of something, even though it makes a boat-load of money, or is he right in thinking the average movie-goer is an idiot?

If you are looking for great dialogue then you will have to look somewhere else. If you are looking for great character development, again, you will have to look somewhere else. If you are looking for real ingenuity in the script then you will have to look somewhere else. If you are looking for another Star Wars shoot 'em up and chase 'em up movie then you will have spent your money well as is always the case with this franchise. The pacing of the action scenes was good enough to over-shadow any faults with the script.

I would not go see it again but I came away thoroughly happy with the few hours I spent watching this movie.

title: Episode IV: The Force Awakens
review:
I, and as I see many others have already stated, have seen this movie before in the form of "A New Hope". And just like them as well, I was gravely disappointed...at first. I had to watch this movie twice, and even plan on going back to watch it a third time, to fully understand what is going on.

The Force Awakens is more than just a rehash of "A New Hope", it is an entry for the next generation to appreciate Star Wars as we all did before the Prequels were made and...well you know. Fans may be disappointed (what else is new), but they have to understand that this movie is NOT for them, at least exclusively. Some may argue that its strictly fan service, but I argue that the main villain Kylo Ren denounces that. POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD.

I was expecting a dark, brooding villain similar to that of Darth Vader going into this movie. Needless to say I was very disappointed with what I ended up getting. Kylo Ren was much too emotional for an established villain, I felt. And that's where I discovered my first mistake. Darth Vader was an established villain from the moment he was introduced in the first movie. He has had years of fighting for the Empire under his belt that it made him the cold, fearsome Sith Lord we all have come to love.

Kylo Ren, on the other hand, is NOT an established villain, he's a new one. We don't get much about his back story other than he's Han Solo's son who trained with Luke Skywalker before being turned to the dark side by the even more mysterious Snoke. Throughout the movie, we see him struggle with not only good and evil, but personal issues of whether he'll ever be as strong as his grandfather, Darth Vader. If I recall, Vader never once doubted himself in the original trilogy.

The point I'm trying to make is that Kylo Ren was more human that I was hoping for, which I didn't like initially. But I'm sure they did it this way to change the story up a little and make you relate to Ren, like most modern films try to do with their villains these days. Because I understand this, and understand that Kylo Ren is not established, I was able to then see the film for a second time in a new light. And guess what? I found it enjoyable :)

The main issue people have with this movie is that it is too similar to the first one. That may be the case, but should it matter? Especially if we all loved the first one? Take what I took into account, and I'm sure you'll appreciate the movie, and look forward to where this new trilogy is heading.

title: Brilliantly directed and well done though very safe.....
review:
I do not usually write reviews I usually just leave a rating and then leave the page but as I am a fan of the Star Wars series I suppose I should give my opinion and battle against all the idiots saying they would prefer to watch The Phantom Menace all over again.

What really stood out to me in this film was the character development. Every character I knew who they were and what they were like and in some sense felt relatable even Kylo Ren had good development which is a great change from Darth Maul especially.

Another reason I liked the film so much was the animation. The film could of been good without such great animation but it really helped enhance the viewing pleasure and the CGI was some of the best I have ever seen in my short life.

The young actors chosen to carry the torch from the older actors were great John Boyega and Daisy Ridley were both amazing leads and were a great pairing for the film as they bought action, emotion and some very funny bits of humour (Finn and BBY's thumbs up). Harrison Ford also did a great job though some are angry to see him go, I believe he has reached the end of his story and usefulness in Star Wars and Kylo killing him really developed Kylo's character but I am still sad to see him go.

The questions. It's been 24 hours since I watched The Force Awakens and yet my mind is still trying to piece together and figure out certain points of the story. Some examples are 'Is Rey Luke's daughter? If not how is she so in touch with the force?' also 'Who is Supreme Leader Snoke? Is he really Darth Plagiuse?' and the final and most important question 'Why is C-3PO's arm red?'. This is what I truly love about how it was written and directed it has answered enough questions to be satisfied and create a basic understanding of the new trilogy but at the same time he is giving the new directors a chance to adapt the story to what they want and gives them the chance to have some fun with the story and has made me, one want to re-watch and two I am so hyped for number eight already!

I also like the modern day adaption of the older stories and I feel Abrams has done a great job of attracting new Star Wars fans as well as keeping the interest of the older generation as it is not so mature only adults like it but at the same time still makes sure the movie appeals to them. A very fine balance for new and old fans with me being a younger fan.

The bad....I wish there was no bad but unfortunately there is as after I got out the cinema from watching the film I didn't feel overjoyed and ecstatic, I felt satisfied which left me disappointed and now I know why. JJ played it all to safe.

Before everyone starts imploding from the fact I just said that here is the reason why. One word being thrown around a lot is nostalgia and I felt it to. The story was so similar to the other films and had different segments from each one but most notably a droid who holds important information for the resistance and is stranded on a desert planet and then he is taken to the resistance and then they kill the First Order/ Empire's new super weapon which destroys planets. I mean come one maybe a bit of originality....

Also following my last point why the Star Killer. WhY!??!? I mean they have seen two previous ones fail but they believe another, bigger one will do it? That was bugging me all movie and bugs me now. It felt more of a remake then a sequel from this film which is the main reason I don't like it as much.

There were so many plot jumps and coincidences which annoyed me but may of been due to the fact they had top delete scenes, didn't have enough money or just hoped people wouldn't mention it. What I mean is the fact Finn and Rey accidentally stumbled upon Han and Chewie after Finn coincidently ran into the droid who he was looking for after a strange girl saved the droid just in time to stop him becoming scrap. It doesn't even end there with the last scene being Rey defeating Kylo in a lightsaber duel which though awesome left me questioning how a Sith Lord and the head of the Knights of Ren got defeated by someone who had just picked up a lightsaber. It should of been no problem for Kylo to slay her where she stood considering he had already burnt down and killed the new Jedi order.

I can look through these negative points for the sake of the story and lore though it lowered the score I gave it because of it. To sum up I loved the film, I want to watch it all over again and I really want to see how the story continues in number eight but the story is predictable and the plot twists were not really out of this world mind blowing like other films all due to the similarities to the ones in the past...

title: If you just want to be entertained, go see it!
review:
This is my first review on IMDb, and I hope someone gets some use out of it. Just got out of the theater, and I must say that I enjoyed Star Wars: The Force Awakens. I saw episode IV when it was released in 1977, and I've watched them all through the the years. I've glanced at some of the reviews here (seems likes hundreds), and most everyone seems to have jumped on the 1/10 stars bandwagon.

When I sit down to watch a movie, I want to be entertained, to escape from the cares and woes of our world. I want a little fantasy, action, humor and positive human relations. I know that perfection can never be attained, and for me, I don't need it.

Mr. Lucas has given the world something wonderful that generations have enjoyed, with still more to come. He has left this story in the hands of others to finish telling on film, and as for me, I'm so thankful that he did. I myself wondered if I would be able to know the full story that he created, and am very happy that I will. I look forward to the next installments.

I'll get off my soapbox now! If you want some action, adventure, laughs and a little love, I highly recommend this movie to you. Enjoy!

title: A love letter to the franchise! Superb!
review:
I had a chance to see "The Force Awakens" in 3D, which made my experience even better, despite my viewing starting 15 minutes late due to a problem with my theater's projector. In any case, this film was extremely well done and felt very similar to the classic installments. Keeping in line with the traditional beginning and ending credit sequences was a nice touch, too.

Not only are Ford, Fisher, Hamill and the rest of the gang back (although Luke Skywalker was only primarily seen at the end), there are also some newer characters added into the mix as well, which is fine. If anything, I thought that the newer characters actually added to the story. Resurrecting the Millennium Falcon was awesome, too! My only chief complaint, however, is that the original characters seemed to have far less screen time than the newer characters. Not too big of a deal, I guess, but I was hoping to see more of them throughout the film considering the fact that they haven't played these characters for decades. I was glad to see, however, that Ford and Fisher were used pretty well throughout the remaining half of the film.

Whether you or a "Star Wars" fan or not, "The Force Awakens" is THE film of the year to see. Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

title: Too Similar To A New Hope??? - The Ultimate Movie Review! - http://tss5078.blogspot.com - @tss5078
review:
***THIS IS A NON-SPOILER REVIEW***

For the first time in thirty-two years, the cast of the original Star Wars has reunited, to tell billions of fans around the world, just what happens next. With the largest weekend opening in the history of film, and the merchandising off the charts, Does the Force Awakens live up to the hype? Yes and no.

The story starts with Leia (Carrie Fisher) still in charge of the resistance, looking for a missing Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamil). The only clue to his location is inside a droid, that is discovered by a planetary scavenger and a former storm trooper, who together embark on a journey to return said droid to the resistance.

As far as special effects, make-up, sound effects, costumes, and 3D goes, this is easily the best Star Wars ever. Even if you're a person who has never seen a Star Wars film, you can't help but be impressed by the visual impact of the film. It's was also amazing to see the old cast back together again for another adventure, but even that somewhat failed to meet my expectation.

Maybe my hopes for this film were too high, but as I watched it, I couldn't help but think that I was just watching A New Hope again! The characters may be different, but throughout the film, certain situations are almost exactly the same. I am sensitive to spoilers, but I will give a small example, using just the description of the story.

A New Hope, Princess Leia sends a droid down to a desert planet with a hidden message, where it is discovered by a young worker, who takes it to Obi Wan and then on to the resistance. The Force Awakens, a droid is send down to a desert planet with a hidden message, where is is discovered by a young scavenger, who takes it to Han Solo and then on to the resistance.

Unfortunately the parallels don't end there, as they continue throughout the entire film. In reading other reviews, some people say it was intentional, to honor the original film, but with one of the largest budgets and audiences ever seen in the industry, why not instead go for originality? That's not the only thing that bothered me, as this film takes place thirty years after the original, the empire has fallen and a new villain has arrived, yet everyone still uses the same ships, blasters, and technology? Has this civilization not progressed at all in three decades? Aside from the similarity to A New Hope, I did enjoy seeing the cast again, and every actor involved in the new story was outstanding in their own right. Star Wars continues to be the pinnacle of success at the box office that all films are measured by, but I wouldn't be doing my job if I didn't tell you, the similarities to the first film are more than just perceived, and in my opinion, they take away a lot from the franchises third trilogy, right from it's very beginning.

title: There has been an awakening... and it's wonderful!!!
review: Finally Star Wars is back in full force. Beautiful acting, stunning practical effects and a great story. Although there are many recognizable plot devices it doesn't really hurt the film, since there is so much new stuff going on. Now that the theme has been set, there are a lot of paths down which the next installments could go. My only complaint is that 2 hours and 15 minutes really isn't enough to explain the major political conflicts and certain scenes therefore seem a little rushed, in order to progress the story. But I guess you can only cram so much into one film. Hopefully that will be explained a little better in episode 8. All in all this makes for a great Star Wars.

title: The movie gets better the more you think about it
review:
When the ending credits rolled across the screen, I was shaking my head with disappointment. Too many plot holes, too many similarities to the original trilogy and rushed scenes make the movie a bit lackluster due to all the good reviews.

However, after letting The Force Awakens percolate in my head overnight, I am still going to recommend people to watch it in theatres AND give it a 9 rating. Why?

a. The graphics are amazing. Fork out some extra money to watch it in 3D and only then you'll see the masterpiece that modern technology has made combined with JJ Abram's vision.

b. The Force Awakens is intended as a homage or a mirror image to A New Hope, so there are bound to be similarities. Abrams did a great job bringing modernity to a plot which has been reused countless times since 1977.

c. Addressing my concerns above, some plot holes can be filled in by reading the novelization and the rushed scenes may be done because everything was happening so quickly that the protagonists did not have time to what was going on around them.

Star Wars The Force Awakens is a masterpiece. You just have to look at it with an open mind.

title: This is Star Wars
review:
The Star Wars original trilogy films have been my favourite movies for a very long time. Episode VII, The Force Awakens, is absolutely a perfect fit in to the Star Wars universe.

This film pays homage to the original trilogy and original characters while introducing the new. It's a generational changeover. I half expected not to but I immediately warmed to the new characters. All of them. They're strong and feel like Star Wars style heroes. They're they're own unique character but have elements of ones we love which helps them take their place as the new leads. I thought I might keep wanting to see original cast members the most and focus on them but I didn't feel that way as I liked these new ones straight away. I was happy to see them all on screen.

There are elements to the film I've read people labelling rehashed or recycled from previous films because they are familiar but what they neglect to note is the previous films, even within the original trilogy, used to recycle these same lines, parallels and story patterns. Pick one of those mentioned as being recycled and you can pretty much find it repeated in the old movies already. To do it actually makes this film part of the universe. The Force Awakens isn't using these ideas to rehash and be cheap or because they don't have any new ideas, they've selected just enough old concepts to make it a very Star Wars thing to do. I do not believe they took it too far or crossed a line with it. They have blended in some entirely new ideas but balanced them perfectly with familiar ones so that ultimately it's not a new trilogy that feels disconnected and dissimilar from the others. They've done it so that this IS Star Wars. The familiarities were ones that made me smile. I feel they "got" the universe and respected it too. I encourage you to enjoy these things and go "This is Star Wars and what I love" because I believe that is the spirit of it. I felt that and was loving it. Try not to pick apart everything that follows the first movies as a sport because I think you'll love this film.

Abrams and Kasdan can be proud of the balance in the script of the old and the new, bringing two generations together, making it feel like Star Wars and rejuvenating the saga. Perhaps this a reflection of Abrams and Kasdan as a team, the original generation and the next. There is great character depth, excellent acting and fantastic action that makes you feel caught up in it especially for how close it occurs to the characters. I love how they've done that. If only they could have done I, II and III! I'm so sad they aren't continuing with VIII. It worries me if we will be down again from this high.

This movie and everything in it feels real. There is no plastic CGI, it's real and gritty.

I did not see any lens flare either. Good work on recovery JJ. You are a talented guy with directing, writing and a score too. You can play in the Star Wars universe anytime.

I have been left hungry for the next film. I rated it down one only because I'm not sure how comfortable I am with one thing in the script but won't say what that is or why.

This movie is up there with the original trilogy and is exceptionally well done. It is flat out awesome.

title: The return of the original cast
review: 10 years after the revenge of the sith and 32 years after the return of the Jedi, the original trio of Han, Leia, and Luke are finally back, this time around the story focuses on a younger trio, Rey, Finn, and Poe who are in their own way the younger version of the original trio, the film also faces a new villain named Kylo ren who wants to be in a sense the next darth Vader. There is a also a super weapon called in the shape of a planet called star base killer which is even more powerful than the Death Star, what made the film rather special was how it had lots of references to the original film which was great for Star Wars fans, Harrison ford sure seems to be enjoying playing the Han Solo again and has the most on screen Time of the trio, Carrie fisher plays leia as more battle worn now that she is general of the resistance which was once the rebel alliance. Mark ha ill shows up at the end which sets up the next installment.

title: What movie did all the naysayers actually see? Don't listen, it is great!
review:
So, my daughter and I just came out of Star Wars. My short summary is it is a perfect mix of old and new, and an excellent movie, probably one of the top 10 movies I've seen in 5 years or more.

I'm not sure what those who gave this 1 to 7 stars are thinking, it is FAR better than your average movie. Of course it was going to have throwbacks to the others, heck, it has several of the same characters in starring roles. I also thought the new characters were outstanding, especially Daisy Ridley as Rey.

I don't want to give a play-by-play analysis of the movie, just that JJ Abrams is truly a great director, the movie is beautiful, the story is engrossing, sets are amazing, and the overall pace and feel of the movie is top notch! Does the movie feel familiar....well yes of course it does, because IT IS a Star Wars movie, and yes, it has some similar scenes to the other movies. That is a GOOD thing, and they are very well done, and the humor is very well done, but not overly done or corny.

Again, the movie is a wonderful blend of everything good about Star Wars. I've noticed over the last 20-30 years, especially in the last 10, there is a percentage of the USA population that is so cynical and negative about EVERYTHING! Those people will never be happy, I see it all the time in movie reviews that are so ridiculously over hyper-critical, I see it life everyday. My advice to those people is to chill, relax, sit back, and smell the roses....try to enjoy life! Star Wars: The Force Awakens IS the real deal.

title: Don't give in to the hate
review:
First review on this site kinda as a response to all the negativity.

Major spoilers ahead so beware.

From beginning to end I had a great time with this movie. The action, music, sound design, camera-work and overall style of this movie was breathtaking and true to the original trilogy while being a 2015 movie.The pace was intense not much room to breath.

Since everything positive has been said let me address some of the criticism.

As stated everywhere the story does feel like a remake or re imagining of Episode IV. Same overall story everything feels familiar. The question is: Is this a good thing? I do think so yes. I'd really like them to tell original stories but this movie was so good in so many other aspects that it didn't hurt my enjoyment. The new characters are all great and its fun to go on this journey with them. I feel like this is a bridge building movie from old to new and it did it's job very well.

Kylo Ren ... probably the best villain in the entire series. Yes I just said that. He has motivation, he is cruel and conflicted. People may cry foul with Darth Vader but please. Vader is so overrated in Episode IV. Only from Empire onwards did he get something like a character. He was not Spacejesus (RLM shout out). Kylo was menacing and brutal but has his weak moments. Those moments without the mask and him addressing Snoke helped make his complete turn to the Dark Side later even more powerful.

On to Snoke. Yes I wasn't impressed either. But keep in mind that this was obviously just a setup for future movies and like Palpatine in Episode V he is kept in the shadows for later. So fine by me.

"How can Rey beat Kylo in the final duel?!?!" I liked that scene a lot. It was just awesome. First of all neither of them has completed their training. Secondly the force is threaded more like a mystery not the prequel like level 7 Sith status etc. Secondly Kylo was wounded and they made sure to show it explicitly. I think he was blasted twice and Finn hit him with the Saber once. So no miracle win here. Another thing. To control a light saber you don't have to be a Jedi or force user, duh! As established in the first act Rey can handle herself with the staff.

But I did have some problems. The third act is a blatant ripoff. Everything goes too smooth and that the resistance can only muster 20 X-Wings was disappointing. Han's death wasn't executed well but at least I think it will work out great for the future movies.

Despite all the nitpicking in the end if you cannot enjoy a movie like this on the silver screen you might wanna go see your doctor.

Overall I had a blaster and am excited for Episode VIII already.

title: An incredible return to the Skywalker saga
review: J.J Abrams's return to a galaxy far far away is a pleasant one with 'Star Wars: The Force Awakens'. Returning the beloved characters of the Skywalker saga and showing what happened to them.The visuals are beautiful as is John Williams score, the brilliant performances also help with Harrison Ford fully channeling Han Solo, and not a grizzled Harrison Ford. The newcomers are very good as well with John Boyega and Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver. The largest complaint I could even have with this film is the fact that despite the over 30 year wait for an Episode VII we get something very familiar, which is obviously intentional to bring back the feeling of Star Wars to fans, however the film becomes predictable once you see the formula, the film is still fun, and does have new ideas but overall you see the similarities. Despite being a very familiar film, it is heavily filled with fun nostalgia and a Star Wars movie that will leave you feeling like you're a kid again.

title: Stop wining about this movie!
review:
I watched this film earlier today, and I came out of the theater with a quite good feeling. It was perfectly fine. More or less what one could expect from a SW movie.

When I came home and read the reviews on this site, I was amazed at all the negative opinions. OK, the movie is not perfect. But no movie is. Some of the critique, I can agree with. Some of it, I can understand. And some of it is just plain stupid.

I agree with... The storyline is not very original. Old wine in new bottles, for the most part. But if you think it is bad, then the original stories are also bad. So what's your point?

I can understand... The main villain is not a very strong character. OK. I get that. I had the same feeling at first. On the surface he seems like just another young Anakin. But considering his Vader-complex, his insecurity and inadequacies make him more interesting. This adds a new dimension to his character that we have not really seen in previous SW movies. The mask? Well, he wants to appear to be a bad ass, and the mask helps. He wants to hide his insecurity and weakness. He cried when he killed his father. He is torn between good and bad, and that makes him (slightly) interesting. Much better than young Anakin.

Rey defeats Kylo Ren. OK. Not quite believable. But then again, he was shot. And she had the element of surprise. I reacted to it too, but I can accept it.

I don't agree... Some reviewers here say that Rey is a bad character. I think she's great! Gender aside, she is strong, brave, skilled, cool... Anything you would expect from a leading character. Much better than Anakin in Ep.1-3 or Luke in Ep.4. On par with Luke in Ep. 5-6. The only flaw is that she has no obvious weakness (impatience, clumsiness or whatever). This would make her a bit more interesting. But if she was a he, the negative voices would silence. And that bothers me. What are you afraid of guys? Why can't young girls have an idol who is more than just a pretty girl?

And the light saber fight IS good. Rey performs extremely well. Her lack of sword skills are clearly intentional and well rehearsed, so don't use this as an argument against her. If you want to see poor swordsmanship, watch the embarrassing performance of Obi-Wan in his fight against Vader in Ep.4. Or any fight in the original movies, for that matter. Ouch!

Some complain about the lack of back stories for the characters. Why did Ben/Kylo go bad? Why did Finn defect? How did the First order emerge? And so on. In my opinion, these "plot holes" are necessary to keep the mystery alive and have something to build on in the upcoming two films. Tying up every loose end is the most effective way to kill a story. The movie keeps us guessing, and I like it.

Too little Luke? What??? I thought it was too much. The final scene is entirely unnecessary. It would be better to cut when the Falcon takes off towards the skies. Or perhaps only give a hint of Luke. Once again, keep the mystery alive. Luke is inferior to the idea of Luke. Kinda like Jaws (the shark). Think about it.

It seems that many people had (extremely) high expectations on this movie, and probably their own ideas about the story line. Of course, this practically guarantees that people will be disappointed. But put all those expectations aside, and you will see that this is a very entertaining and cool movie. Not perfect by a mile, but definitely worth seeing.

Stop wining!

title: Delivered in every way
review:
I wanna start by saying that I'm not the biggest Star Wars fan, even though I do enjoy some of the movies more than others. I believe the original trilogy to be a fine series of films and the prequels to be terrible at times but with some good things accomplished at times. Nonetheless, from everything I had seen from the previews for this film, I was definitely anticipating it a lot and I can definitely say that it was quite a birthday present watching this on opening day. The Force Awakens was entertaining, it set up new characters terrificly and brought back the beloved heroes of the first three movies in a respectable way.

With this new installment, we follow Rey (Ridley) a scavenger that has her life changed when a droid named BB-8 has an important message for a resistance fighting what rose from the fall of the Galactic Empire, the First Order. She must now deliver this message with the help of Finn (Boyega), a storm trooper that has managed to escape the First Order and Han Solo. With the First Order we will get a new villain in Kylo Ren, a Sith in training shrouded with mystery, and could ultimately play a big part in these character's lives.

For me, the franchise is now in great hands as Daisy Ridley and John Boyega were wonderful in their roles and could very well be the big heroes for this new generation that Luke, Han & Leia were for the first viewers of this saga. I thought Abrams held his own in the directing department and delivered a quite competent job. The effects were on point and the movie as a whole was a fantastic piece of entertainment.

As far as I'm concerned, this movie brings back Star Wars in a big way. It's not a perfect movie by any means, but its definitely quite a experience and I can see only very nit picky people not enjoying it. Having said that, I hope you really enjoy the experience like I did, if you do choose to watch it. and may The Force be with you.

Rating: 9/10

title: Star Wars movie but that's it
review:
First of all i like all the star wars movies, the 1st three and the second three... that said.

This movie is beautiful. Fancy graphics, nice acting (in my humble opinion). And so i rate it at least 7 out of 10. But:

This is not a worthy Star Wars movie! Yes it's beautiful, yes the story is nice... but it goes way too quick, way too easy, too smooth... (no spoilers but just saying). The previous six movies were for their age epic, this one too graphic. But when i compare the story... It just doesn't meet the standards of the old movies, yes all six of them.

My advice: Go see this movie, it's worth the money. But don't go compare it with the old ones. It just can't reach their level of quality (graphic + story).

title: Great film, but... (read only when you've seen the movie!)
review:
The greatest thing The Force Awakens did for me was that it made me feel like that little kid again. I was transported back to 1977 when I sat with my older sister in a movie theater in Amsterdam and was watching the first Star Wars film. What an amazing experience!

Overall I think JJ Abrams did a great job with The Force Awakens. Being able to please the old fans as well as the potential new ones must have been a difficult task. He cast great actors, used some excellent SFX and made a great mix of new elements and Star Wars nostalgia. The first part of The Force Awakens is great fun. In a brilliant way we see how the lives of Poe, Finn and Rey get intertwined and how they're forced into a war between the First Order and the Alliance.

Strangely, the pace of the story gets interrupted a little bit when we meet the old cast. Han Solo is the first one. Although his scenes are magical they also divert us a little from the story. Luckily things fall into place very quickly when they join forces and go meet Maz Kanata, a great CGI character played by Lupita Nyong'o. Solo plays a major role in this Star Wars outing. He gets a lot of screen time and when the movie is finished you know why. Carrie Fisher looks great as General Leia.

The bad things then. Daisy Ridley is not always convincing in her role as Rey. But she's charming as hell and at the moments she really must perform she really delivers. Well done! The new bad guy, the Supreme Leader Snoke (Andy Serkis) is a different story. He looks like a low budget Voldemort and therefor isn't quite as menacing as Darth Sidious. Why does he look so fake? Kylo Ren: he is introduced as this ruthless killer who is very skilled in The Force. He can even freeze a blaster fire in the air! Wow, he makes Darth Vader look like a pussy. But later on in the story he must fight Finn who - as a non-Jedi - has a lightsaber in his hand for the very first time. Why doesn't Ren demolish this boy? He doesn't even have The Force!

I was impressed by how Han Solo died. His fall into the fog is both epic and impressive. Although you know it will happen it still comes as a shock. But at that point you know that Kylo Ren can't be turned to the Light side: it's too soon for that. Thanks to Han's death we know that Kylo Rey will go berserk in Episode VIII.

Although the scenes between Kylo Ren and Rey are great to watch, it is strange that the girl knows how to use her Force powers so soon. 24 Hours earlier she didn't even know what The Force was. "Yes, the stories are true. All of them!" That development was not convincing at all.

With the prequels we knew how the story would end: Anakin would become Darth Vader and Luke and Leia would be separated. But now with the new trilogy it's a whole different matter. In the next chapter we'll probably witness Rey being trained by Luke Skywalker and Kylo Ren by the Supreme Leader Snoke. But what else? In this new story anything goes. Luke can be killed. Rey can be seduced by the Dark Side. BB-8 can marry R2D2 if he/she wants. And that makes this new trilogy so exciting.

In the end Star Wars The Force Awakens is the story of an extraordinary family and the one of a great spaceship. Because the way the Millennium Falcon is shown in this movie is pure magic!

Looking forward to seeing the next chapter!

8,5 out of 10

title: Great comeback!
review:
What a hype! And it actually payed off. This movie turned out to be absolutely worth the wait. There are some flaws of course, but not every movie can be like The Empire Strikes Back. I personally got exactly what I was expecting from this movie. Great, but still, not better than the original trilogy.

J.J. Abrams is directing this one and I had a lot of faith in him because I loved his Star Trek and Super 8 was pretty good too. I find it great that they decided to give young talents a chance. Daisy Ridley, John Boyega and J.J. Abrams himself. And they all did a great job! No matter about my first expectations, the closer the release was, the more hyped I was!

Now, more about the movie itself. The effects are great! Star Wars is back and it has never looked so good! The characters are very well fleshed out and you really care about them. The score is beautiful as always. John Williams is a genius! The script is also very good and dialogues aren't cringeworthy like they used to be in the prequels. The combination of the old and the new is perfect and there is just enough nostalgia, but not too much.

Some people say plot is just a rehash of A New Hope, but there is also some of The Empire Strikes Back, and I'm perfectly fine with that. The only problem I have is that I feel like Disney marvelised it a little, and few times I felt like I'm watching Guardians of the Galaxy, but there still was that classic Star Wars feel too and one more thing that was very well done is that one big reveal at the end. So emotional and the beautiful score, oh my god! The only problem is that it ends too soon, but it totally leaves you waiting to see more.

While this wasn't the best Star Wars movie, it's a great new start for the series and I'm looking forward to the sequels and spin-offs!

title: Anything we have not seen before?
review:
THERE ARE SPOILERS IN THIS REVIEW!!!!!

The film as an overall conclusion is not at all a bad movie.

The film is obviously a sequel despite critics and reviews stating that it looks as though the whole plan is a remake. The only remake I see is the love and drama that we got from episode 4, 5 and 6 all them years ago.

Though the movie is a sequel it still remains remarkably similar to the events of episode 4. In E4 the rebellion destroy the death star and in E5 Luke goes off to be trained as a Jedi by Yoda. In E7 (force awakens) the rebellion have to conquer an even bigger death star in which Ray (a possibly new Jedi) assisting the rebellion in defeating the empire and goes off to go and find Luke, and from the ending looks as though she is about to receive some one to one training. So in the grand scheme of things there is a similarity. If we find Ray hanging from a giant sky city in Episode 8 then we know that we might as well not bother watching 9 as the films plot will be pretty obvious.

On Ray. She seems to be a character who was left on a planet when she was young to work in slave like condition, who by the end of the film happens to go and find Luke with only Chewy and R2D2, not even Luke's sister went with her. Why? That is not something that should have happened.

Ray has the force, and if you ask me, as Kylo Ren is Han Solo and Leia's son, it seems obvious that Ray and Kylo Ren are cousins in which Luke is the Father of Ray. Maybe this is a speculation, but there seems to be no other reason to why Ray has the force.It also seems that given that Ray has the force that Luke will train her to become a Jedi. Much like Yoda and Luke in 5 and 6. If this is the case, and certainly seems a valid prediction then i think we are in for a treat in 8 & 9 for sure. It would also explain, from the film makers point of view why not to include Luke's sister in finding him, as the director can focus on Luke and Ray's 1 on 1 training / runion /relationship development.

On Kylo Ren, there are some issues. His mask is in a fact useless. It seems to provide him no real benefit unlike Darth Vader. It seems as though it is just a stunt to cause controversy on the internet and in the cinema on if Luke was Kylo Ren or not. Kylo, though powerful is not very good with a lightsaber as he struggled in a duel with an untrained scavenger (Ray) and an untrained storm trooper (Fin) who both used a lightsaber (at individual times). He also seemed to forget about his abilities to use the force to stun/hold people in position, and throw them left right and centre, when in a battle with Ray and Fin. Though, his master did want to bring him back for training. At this moment, he does not give the same fright as Vader. He cries a lot too.

I would like to know how the Empire became strong again. Though this looks as though this will be answered by Luke, or revealed in some other way in 8 & 9.

Generally speaking, from beginning to end, I was fixed to the screen loving and enjoying quality filming and acting which had a action and humour rush throughout that pleased myself at least. Questions do need to be answered, and hopefully will be in 8 & 9.

title: Relax people. Its just a space fantasy movie.
review:
10 out of 10 only to irk all the whining fan boys on here.

I cannot believe the outright rage and anger over this movie. Grown men getting all bent out of shape and throwing tantrums because the latest installment of a goofy space fantasy film series that features a guy in a shag rug outfit, garbage cans on wheels and a ninja gremlin that can lift spaceships with his mind didn't meet their expectations Relax. I mean seriously. Its just a space fantasy movie. Its not supposed to clean up at the Oscars or have a story like a Pulitzer winning novel. Its a big, fun, goofy ride with explosions and lasers in space and that's all.

Was it a bit of a re-boot of a A New Hope? Sure, but remember that A New Hope came out almost 40 years ago so I can see how they would want to pay homage for first generation fans and re-introduce the story to a new generation and set it up for the future with some new characters. Not everyone watched all the first movies or grew up in the 70's or 80's. And anyone slagging off on Abrams or Disney for ruining Star Wars should keep in mind that no one forced (pun intended) them to watch it or promised they would deliver all new original concepts.

Look what introducing too many new characters, spaceships and concepts did for Lucas in the prequels. They apparently according to the fans all stunk so why cry now when they stick to the original winning formula. You willingly bought your ticket so don't cry and demand your money back because it didn't meet many peoples quite frankly outrageous expectations. Be thankful you even have a new Star Wars movie. Most people couldn't even draw the Millennium Falcon let alone bring it to life on the big screen.

Another thing I would like to bring to the foaming at the mouth fan boys attention is that the prequels were largely downright awful and they were made by its creator, who sold out and walked away by the way because he knew the story was pretty much tapped out and you know it, and if this new movie sucks and the prequels suck and the only decent films were the first three (many thought those sucked too by the way) then maybe that means Star Wars just simply sucks and it was over in the 80's and that the fan boys should simply move along and find something else to fill the voids in their lives. Part of the problem is that Lucas much like his fans started to take this franchise way too seriously and it wouldn't appear that there is just no pleasing any Star Wars fan.

Was it perfect? No. Was it supposed to be perfect? No. Is the action and story line supposed to be realistic and believable? Heck no! Was it fun and loud and did it bring you back to the wacky Star Wars world for a couple hours? Yes. Thats all its supposed to be is a big, fun, goofy space fantasy to lose yourself in for a couple hours and nothing more so stop taking it so seriously, get over it and stop whining.

And some of the plot hole arguments on here are ridiculous. Hundreds of comments about how does Rey know so much about the Millennium Falcon? Well because as very clearly stated in the film it sat in pretty much her backyard, owned by her employer for much of her life so you think she might have been on it more than a few times. I mean seriously are Star Wars fans really that thick? Even a 12 year old would have a hard time missing that glaring plot point.

Personally I liked the movie and thought it was fun. It brought me back to my childhood but I certainly did not hang my happiness or mental health on whether or not it would be good or totally change the format and introduce all new concepts. I saw Han and Chewy and Leia and Luke and a bunch of new characters and I ate my popcorn, drank my drink, watched the explosions and went home satisfied.

Star Wars was never intended to be the pinnacle of human story telling with an Oscar winning script nor was it intended to change the world or be a crutch for people to rely on to bring meaning to their lives.

Relax people. Its just space fantasy movie.

title: Dear One-Star Terrorists
review:
0.1 A film-critic fan boy is an obnoxious adult who spends time nitpicking movies searching for quality. Unfortunately, the FCFB does not realize that most movies are supposed to be enjoyed.

0.2 A one-star terrorist is a reviewer on IMDb who purposely rates a movie lower in order to counteract positive reviews he disagrees with passionately. For example, there are over 6000 one-star terrorists active on the Force Awakens IMDb page.

1. The Ending Is Extremely Frustrating

Yes, the ending is frustrating because it leaves the audience in suspense for a whole year!!! Otherwise, it's a great ending. This cliffhanger of an ending makes me want to watch the next movie! Adding more dialogue here would have killed the suspense. Star Wars is about mystery. Are you for Midichlorians? Hell no!

2. A Ton Of Actors Are Wasted In Nothing Roles

No one cares about the poor little actors. They are merely characters in Star Wars. Star Wars is more important than "movie stars". Boohoohoo, poor little Gwendoline, I cry for you because I'm a film-critic fan boy!

3. John Williams' Score's Just OK

No one wants anything new here. If anything, the OT score wasn't used enough.

4. The Biggest Moment Is Ultimately Glossed Over

Meh, this is clearly wrong. In the scene Han dies, Chewie was the only character who really knew him. His emotional response was perfect.

5. Not Many Aliens

True, new aliens should have been introduced in this film. This is one of its greatest flaws.

6. Original Trilogy Characters Appear Just For The Sake Of It

Leia, Luke, C3PO, and R2D2 are not primary characters. They are supporting characters. In the OT they were primary characters. Therefore, I do not expect to see Leia as a primary character when she is a secondary character.

7. Supreme Leader Snoke's CGI IsNot Great

True.

8. Starkiller Base Is Totally Underwhelming

Yes, I think Abrams downplayed it intentionally. The Death Star is a logical conclusion of interstellar conflict. Whoever has the bigger gun wins. Since the First Order/Empire would never stop building them because the audience wants something original, it follows they are essential to Star Wars. Even the exhaust vent Luke nailed is essential. If you eliminated with some sort of sophisticated heat removal system and closed the gap in the refresh of the planetary shield, what exactly would our Jedi do to stop such a death star?

9. There's Too Much Homage, Not Enough Originality

a. Answer me this: Why would the evil First Order/Empire ever stop building death stars to make the film more original? The Space Ballsesque nature of this question is blindingly ridiculous. The need to build death stars is a logical conclusion of the breadth of this interstellar conflict. However, "Don't be too proud of this technological terror you've constructed. The ability to destroy a planet is insignificant next to the power of the Force." I think Abrams agrees with Vadar. This is why the "Starkiller" is downplayed as secondary plot. It is almost as if the battle to destroy happens in the background.

b. Answer me this: Where else would someone put highly-detailed plans? Would one of the characters memorize 2000 pages of blueprints?

10. Captain Phasma Was Hyped Up For Nothing

As with Dameron, we will see more of Captain Phasma later. This is not a problem. She was introduced in this film as the Finn's cool looking commander, nothing more. She is as important to the film as the storm troopers. Moreover, many secondary characters in the OT were introduced like this as well. They were nonetheless cool.

11. Poe Dameron Feels Like a Third Wheel

Poe Dameron is not a main character. He is a supporting character. He was used in the marketing of the movie simply because he looks cool as an x- wing pilot.

12. The Plot Is Too Reliant On Convenience

a. Rey vaguely humanizes BB-8 as a Reason not to Sell Him.

Maybe morality is part of her character? Ever think of that possibility? Yeah, I forgot, film- critic fan boys don' t think.

b. Han Solo finds Rey and Finn by accident.

Yes, it was coincidence when they met up with Han Solo and Chewbacca. Oh my God!! Coincidences never happen in the real world!

c. Poe Dameron Appears from Nowhere

Poe Dameron returning to the Republic from Jakku is "returning out of nowhere"? Bullshit. He returned to friendly space after purchasing a ship with Republic currency. We did not need to see this obvious sub plot for a supporting character.

d. Finn Versus Kylo

Finn survived as long as he did because Kylo was injured, not a fully- trained Sith , and not thinking straight due to just having killed his father.

e. The Ground Breaks Between Kylo and Rey to End Their Battle

The ground breaking between Kylo and Rey is the same sort of chance which brought R2D2 to Luke. R2D2's ship just happened to be boarded near the same system Luke called his home! In fact, the planet exploding due to the destruction of the Starkiller is far more plausible than R2D2 just happening to hurtle toward Luke with the plans to the Death Star. There would have been fissures all over the surface of the planet as it disintegrated!

13. Feels incredibly rushed.

Are you complaining about action movies in general? Yes, Force Awakens is different than the originals. Instead of a slower pace we have an action version. Moreover, apart from Abrham's style, this action style flows from the characters. There's ZERO Jedi training in this movie. Action's fast; training's slow.

title: The Force is strong with this one.
review:
I thought it would be wise to right a positive review on this movie after seeing all the negative ones all these internet trolls have posted.

After seeing the first teaser for Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens back in November of 2014, my expectations were at an all time high. As the months went on, and the trailers, TV spots, and merchandise came out afterward, my excitement of the 7th installment of my favorite film series of all time went up the same way it did when Episode III was being released.

Finally, opening night came, and I enjoyed the hell out of this movie. The characters, especially the new ones, were great and relatable, the humor was fantastic, the effects were amazing, the music is classic John Williams, and the classic characters returning from the Original Trilogy help make this a Star Wars movie.

It's worth the time, the money, the hype, the acclaim, the 94% on RottenTomatoes, and the by far 8.6 out of 10 on IMDb. And it deserves my rating of 10 out of 10.

title: Not terrible, not great either.
review:
Basically a reboot and utilising bargain basement versions of characters from the classic trilogy.

Not terrible but also not great. Snoke is rubbish as is star killer Base.

Rey starts well and rapidly becomes preposterous. One minute the force and the Jedi are a myth, then she's pulling mind tricks like a pro.

It's fun while it lasts but the story is just stupid.

title: Pfft trolls
review:
Easily one of the best films I've seen in a long time. I couldn't think of a single negative aspect to this film. All i know is i want to watch it again.

I don't want to drop spoilers, but there are so many points of this film that stand out it's insane. The characters are fantastic, the story is spot on and the film was permeated with that Star Wars feel.

Don't listen to the idiots griefing the film to make themselves feel important. Let the trolls be sad and go make up your own minds, thats why you have them.

If your a true Star Wars fan, you'll love this.

title: Amazing! I feel like a kid again!
review:
When I was 15 years old, I read a review in the local paper for Star Wars. Well being a sci-fi reader, and a lover of adventure stories, I was intrigued. When I got to the theater that hot summer day and saw all of these other people in line to see the original Episode 4, I felt this amazing excitement running through the crowd. Like all of the others who were there for that moment in time, I will never forget it. No one had ever seen anything like it. There were no big stars, only the amazing reviews. And were taken to a Galaxy far...far away. A place where planets were like continents. All you needed was my favorite souped up girl, the Millennium Falcon, and my favorite pilot of all time, Han Solo. Rake, scoundrel, sexy, antihero, funny, brave, so lovable, and always up for a good fight. Yeah, I would have had his kid too Leia! Too bad he turned out to be a sociopath. I digress. I was very skeptical of this movie. There was SOOOOO much hype. But after my beloved Star Trek J.J. Abrams reboot, I just had to give this a chance. My son bought tickets for Christmas day. I don't know how we got in. Wow, I haven't seen these kind of crowds since Avatar. It was sharing a moment again with not only my generation, but also a whole new one. My son for one. It was the best Christmas present I've ever gotten. I have the first trilogy on DVD. My son and I are going to have a SW marathon and then go see the movie again. I don't know if he will understand why I left teary eyed. I have read other people saying that this is a remake, but it's not. J.J. gave us all the touchstones of our youth while making the way for the next generation. He re-established the wonderful mixture of comedy, tragedy, and on the edge of your seat action of the original. It's so refreshing to see a real fan make a real fan's movie for real fans. I didn't see it as a remake at all. It was just a new wheel within a wheel. Everything makes a circle. And I loved so much seeing it come around again.

I can't wait for the next one!

title: A true squeal to the Star Wars trilogy
review: I felt like a little kid in the movie theater seeing it opening night. I don't want to spoil anything so this review will be brief. The movie is very familiar to fans of the original trilogy. It captures the magic that was Star Wars in the late 70s early 80s. The new actors mix with the old is great, almost feels like passing the torch. You actually care for the characters and care for what happened to them. It's also the funniest Star Wars movie there's been. Even my wife liked the movie and she doesn't like Star Wars. She thought BB8 was really cute and I'm glad she went with me. I highly recommend everyone give it a shot because it's actually a great movie.

title: best movie ever!!
review: Can i just say that the movie blew me away? cringing, breathless, amazing and possibly the best star wars ever made! so many classic concepts were kept and the storyline blew my mind! one hour passed since i left the cinema and my head still feels like its comprehending and storing information!! the movie is spectacular. best movie ever on my list would be star wars episode 7....bless j.j Abrams. Being myself a star wars maniac and a gigantic fan of the franchise seeing this movie exhilarated me to the fullest degree i would ever thought my mind could possibly handle. I have waited years for the movie days and long months to watch it. Star Wars will forever keep its legacy!!

title: LOVED it
review:
*Possible Spoiler Alert* I was honestly nervous going into this movie...as a die-hard Star Wars fan, I was super anxious about a new director/Disney taking over...but I was NOT disappointed.

One thing I can't understand is why everyone is so worried about Rey's natural way with the force. I am just as much a Star Wars fan as the next SW geek...and I don't see what the frustration or confusion over this is. It seemed to me, that the point was supposed to be that Rey was undoubtedly special in her abilities and that, that was supposed to separate her from the rest of the Jedi characters in previous movies. That's what I got out of it anyway...

I personally can't understand the minds of the rigid critics out there... the point of movie-watching is ENTERTAINMENT. It's an escape. Maybe the reason some aren't enjoying in this film is because they are LOOKING for flaws...

That's my take on it.

This movie was exciting, interesting, and a great set up for the next episodes to come.

title: A Great Addition to the Star Wars Universe
review:
First things first, I love this movie! It delivered everything that I expected it to give me, and did it very well.

Yes, I am a Star Wars fan. But I am not a blind fan and I can recognize some of the issues that the prequel movies had, or even The Return of the Jedi had. This movie gave me the same feeling I had back in 1977 when I was watching the original Star Wars for the first time. It was a lot of fun, had a simple story that made sense, and had characters who are likable and relatable. In addition there were the usual Star Wars aliens, vehicles, and settings in the movie.

I have heard people complain that this movie was too much like the very first movie. In my mind, they were paying homage to the very first movie and using what worked in previous Star Wars ourings to make a new Star Wars. The movie had a few twists and turns as we find out who some of the main characters are and how they're related, it brought back old familiar faces which is always a fun time, and it left us with the mystery about who some of the new players are.

I saw some other guy on here reviewing the movie complaining that there was no character development. First of all, we know who the characters are coming out of the gate. How are you going to develop Han Solo any further? Although I do think the movie managed to add some depth to the relationship between himself and General Leia Organa. It added depth to the main bad guy's character, and gave us a fairly complicated character in the storm trooper.

All in all, I think the people trashing the movie or simply those who want to be hipsters and want to show that their tastes are above the plebian by trashing a popular movie. I don't care, I thought the movie was a blast.

It's not Citizen Kane, but let's face it - unless you're really into making movies yourself Citizen Kane is boring. This movie is not.

As I said, as I sat there and watched it I had the same feelings that I had watching the original Star Wars movie. I highly recommend this movie to anyone who wants to go to the movies and have a good time and see you a worthy addition to the Star Wars pantheon.

title: Made me feel young again! Audience applauded, laughed out loud! A must see.
review:
I remember working at a haunted house setup at Tropical Park in Miami Florida where there was a section setup with characters dressed up as those from the bar scene from the original Star Wars. I was a volunteer to dress up as a character to frighten people walking through the large tent set up with a maze of scenes designed to frighten the visitors. But this was only one of many early memories I began recalling watching Star Wars: The Force Awakens.

I can't even remember if I had a chance to see the original Star Wars in theaters or not. That is how far, far and away the franchise had gotten away from the original look and feel of the original Star Wars after the third installment.

But, after seeing Star Wars The Force Awakens (2015), all that longing is gone.

It was hard to focus on the not so large screen in front of me inside house No. 15 at the Universal Cineplex Theater at City Walk for this early morning 12:15 a.m. showing of Star Wars: The Force Awakens because I sat between a guy behind me and to the right who wanted to put his feet up on the rail off to the side of my peripheral vision left, and the two guys to my immediate right who apparently wanted to be part of the dialogue in the movie by making unnatural gestures and outbursts out loud during the show. However, even with these two distractions, I put mental blinders on and became even more riveted to the screen.

I watched as the characters came alive in the way Hollywood can only do on a screen the size of a wall.

Seeking to see the movie, perhaps for the last time with many of the original Star Wars characters appearing, making their entrance at carefully timed spots during the moving, all made it worth while.

The organic nature and style of this set in the future, but mixed with practical realistic dirt and greasy stains on the space ships is what I think makes this movie all the more captivating.

The sanitary nature of other science fiction space traveling movies brought upon by perfect CGI renditions take away, though visually dramatic, from the grounding nature that Star Wars established in its first edition, and now returns to in its latest edition. This grounding earth tone extends on the planets revealing environment you can relate to by touch and smell by just looking at the animals scattered throughout, may of which needing a bath.

Wanting to see this release in the theaters was also a must.

I knew the fans would add to the ambiance by contributing their reactions through applauds and laughter. Especially when familiar characters made their first appearance as the movie slowly unwound its story line. The audience would not be shy either. Laughing out loud, together, made the movie going experience come alive - again.

Until now, it was hard to justify actually rushing to the theater to watch a release of a movie. Star Wars: The Force Awakens - compels you out of your homes for just this reason.

The audience applause and accolades was most notable at the very beginning of the movie just as the trademark yellow text appeared on the screen, slowly scrolling upward and away and as the Star Wars theme song thundered throughout every corner of the theater.

The film, if you paid attention, paid homage to the original movie with similarly structured scenes such as when a light saber gets lifted from being embedded in a pile of snow by using the "Force". These little jewels undoubtedly and lovingly placed throughout the movie for those trained eyes and emotional hearts to relive and love.

Yes, with the invent of the computer, the Internet, and then the iPhone, this series transcended all these inventions and modern captivations.

I can now say I have truly witnessed history by experiencing in my life time the age of Star Wars.

title: Starwars reborn :)
review:
For me, I believe anyone who enjoyed the original trilogy can't really fault the storyline, yes it is roughly the same as "a new hope" with the best parts from V and VI loosely thrown in, but that's what I found so comforting about the whole movie. I'm not sure what others was really expecting or how to better the entire movie.

There was a few scenes that seemed rushed and a lot of characters that didn't get the chance to develop in to timely favourites as much as they could of such as the original characters who only had minor scenes or minimum screen time such as boba fett,bib fortuna and dengar.

One thing for sure is this film will certainly enlighten the imagination in the younger generation and they get to see how starwars should really be like. My youngest son never really had an interest in starwars until last night but after watching the force awakens as soon as we got home he started to watch and enjoy the entire series, so from this movie a new super fan has been touched by the force.

title: It calls to you
review:
The opening sequence informs us Luke is missing and the "First Order" has replaced "The Empire." It is lead by another helmet covered Dark Lord whose identity is revealed about 50-60 minutes into the film. By this time the other two major characters are developed.

Finn (John Boyega) is a storm trooper who joins the resistance. He becomes a love interest, or so it seems (unless they are somehow brother and sister, they did that twist before) of Rey.

Rey (Daisy Ridley) is a tech savvy fighter who on one occasion takes a Katniss pose. Her parentage is not revealed in this film, but she acts similar to another famous character and my guess she is the granddaughter of...Oh c'mon they make it obvious.

For those who loved the old Star Wars (and I think that is why we are here) there are plenty of identical lines and similar scenes from the original films, including a cantina, search for a droid, and a Death Star type battle...not to mention that scene of which we do not speak.

The role of the Emperor is now the Snoke (Andy Serkis) who looks like a giant Lord Voldemort, perhaps the worse part of the production.

The film hits upon the nostalgia elements using the same sound track to create emotional and heart pumping scenes. And yes, we can guess the sequel will look like "The Empire Strikes Back" because original writing is scarce and that is what sells tickets.

Guide: No F-bombs, sex, or nudity.

title: Good-looking, but unoriginal take on Star Wars
review:
First of all: This is an enjoyable movie. It feels like Star Wars and it is in my opinion the best episode in the saga since Episode VI: Return of the Jedi.

The area where the movie really shines is the visuals. The photography and the special effects are the best we have seen in any Star Wars movie to date. The Star Wars universe has never looked as good as here, and the visuals are by themselves worth the price of admission. Apparently, the filmmakers have given an effort to make this one look more like the original episodes. They did this by using miniatures and puppets rather than excessive CGI effects, and by giving the production a dirtier, grittier look than Ep. I-III. This has really paid off in my opinion. The sound design and music are also excellent. The director is also great at making very fast-paced, engaging action scenes.

As to plot and story-telling: It's not bad, but there are a number of weaknesses. First of all (and this has been pointed out in many other reviews), the main plot line as well as many smaller plot elements are extremely similar, in parts even identical to previous episodes, especially Ep. IV. This was certainly done intentionally by the filmmakers, as a homage and to "quote" the classics, and appears to be something that the director/writer J.J. Abrams specializes in. Yet it feels a bit like a cop-out. It's almost like the makers of Ep. VII didn't dare, or lacked the ideas to do something new. To mention just the major recurring themes (ATT: SPOILERS!): We have a droid which holds crucial information that both sides seek to obtain, the droid is lost (and later rescued) on a desert planet while the storm troopers are looking for it there, we have Han Solo getting in trouble for unpaid debts, we have the heroes hiding inside the millennium falcon, we have the shady space canteen with weird aliens and a funny alien band, we have the bad guys constructing a gigantic space weapon which can destroy planets, we have the plan of the resistance to destroy it by a) sending a commando to disable the shields on the ground, b) sending X-Wings to bomb it from close by, and we have a shocking "family revelation". Many characters are also obvious reincarnations of previous ones: A new R2D2 (BB-8), a new Darth Vader (Kylo Ren), a new emperor (Snoke), a new Watto (junk dealer on a desert planet), and Rey is of course very similar to Luke in the original episodes. The only really new character is probably Finn. Kylo Ren is an interesting character, and I like the choice of a young actor, but his fate is all too similar to Anakin/Darth Vader's.

The character development is also fairly weak. The best new character is BB-8, who is funny and charming, but ultimately fails to make a lasting impression as he is all too similar to R2D2. The two main characters, Finn and Rey, are not badly done, but stay rather bleak. We don't learn much about them except that they are the "good guys" and make the morally right choices. We get only a glimpse of character development from them. Admittedly, this episode was to introduce the new characters, and hopefully there will be more room for character development in the following episodes.

As for plot holes, we shouldn't judge the movie too hard on them. It is after all a space opera and has some elements of a fairy tale, which resist logical analysis (light sabers which are 1m long? explosions in space? Pulsating lasers?). However, even from a fairy tale we can expect that it is in itself consistent, and I feel that in one important point, the plot of this movie is not consistent with previous episodes: How come both Finn and Rey are able to use a light saber and stand their ground against a (still young, but apparently trained) Sith? It makes no sense, especially considering how Luke had to go through a lot of Jedi training in the original episodes to reach that level of skill. It just feels wrong and makes you think that they did it only because they felt that a Star Wars movie "needs" a light saber duel. (Actually, the movie would have worked quite well if the heroes simply left on the falcon with Chewie after blowing up the shields of the oscillator. That would have avoided the problem mentioned above, as well as a couple more stupid "movie coincidences", like Chewie just happening to find and rescue the heroes in the few seconds before the planet blew up.)

We also barely get to explore the galaxy any more than we did previously. The plot takes place on a desert planet, in space, on a densely forested planet, and on an ice/snow planet - all places which we have seen before. Are there really no other interesting planets to explore in this galaxy?

All the problems I have described so far are with the script / plot. Originally, it was planned that Michael Arndt would work on the scripts for the three new episodes. However, after J.J. Abrams was signed as director, he took over as writer as well, together with Lawrence Kasdan. I think the script could have turned out better if Michael Arndt had been allowed to take the time to finish the script.

The acting was overall fairly good. It was nice to see how Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher slipped into their old roles again smoothly. The new, young actors all did well too, although I felt that Daisy Ridley acted a bit wooden at times. But it was definitely right to cast new, unknown actors for these roles, so let's give her and the others some time to grow into their roles.

title: Almost great
review: Overall bit better than Episode I, well executed and updated yet classic CGI Episode VII is great for all viewers. Predictable plot, predictable twists, lackluster re-skinned technology, and underwhelming cast pulls this movie down to a 7. If you are an avid fan of the franchise, this movie will no doubt be slightly disappointing but as a production it attracts new viewers to the franchise without overloading them with information and has levels to the dialogue that is friendly for all ages. It has enough Easter- eggs to reward veteran viewers and builds suspense over the unraveling of the gap well. The movie just answers enough questions to keep us interested.

title: While not perfect it delivers a fun filled Episode VII that lays a solid foundation for the future!
review:
Force Awakens is a solid foundation, and a non-stop action packed nostalgically entertaining opening episode for this new trilogy. However it does have its flaws, which is why I can't say I loved it as much as I wanted to, and which is why I have given it 7/10. Being a massive fan of the OT and a satisfied junkie with the Prequels, I may have made the mistake of over hyping The Force Awakens to a point where nothing could actually meet expectations. I went to see it first in standard 3D and it just didn't feel right. I left the cinema with very mixed feelings; something didn't capture me as it should have done, or perhaps as much as I desperately wanted it to. I knew I had to see it again to decide. So last night I went to see it this time in 2D, in terms of cinematography it translates far better than the 3D version, and more importantly it feels like a Star Wars movie.

What I liked

1) It's beautiful. The landscapes, the battle scenes, everything. Abrams has done a great job in the way he has filmed this movie and his attention to detail in bringing the Star Wars universe to life deserves great credit in itself.

2) New characters. I thought that Rey and Finn were outstanding and despite all the nostalgia they really stood out on their own. I thought they may end up being auxiliary cast, but they are put at the center of the story and I am looking forward to seeing where their characters go in Episode 8.

3) Balanced CGI. This really helps when it comes to the all round feel of the movie, the choice not to go too heavy on CGI really paid off in a way that immerses you in the world.
