4) Nostalgia. Maybe sometimes more than is necessary but I think we all smiled when we saw Han, Leia and Luke again, plus Harrison Ford delivers a great performance.

5) BB-8. I loved him, a great alternative to R2-D2!

6) The beginning. I loved and was totally captured by the first 45 minutes of the film which is mainly set on the desert planet Jakku. It was in many ways the only original part of the movie (despite the sand) and this is because it's the only part that relies on the new cast entirely.

7) The end. After the fairly boring middle section of the movie, things got going again after the Falcon leaves for Starkiller base. This part of the movie really felt like classic Star Wars and brought back the feel of the OT cast running around the Death Star in ANH. It also contains the most drama, not just because of *that death scene*, but also because Rey, Finn and Ren have better developed into their roles. It set the next movie up very well indeed.

What I didn't like

1) It wasn't original enough. I think most of the criticism of the movie is that it just recycled themes and even plot lines from A New Hope. I almost cringed at how many similarities there are including a) Another desert planet b) Rescue a droid that has some important information c) New bigger Death Star now known as Star Killer base d) Resistance base is just like the one in ANH e) Snoke/Ren is a repeat of Palpatine/Vader f) Have the Imperials still not learned the weaknesses with ventilation shafts?

2) The Plot. This follows on from my point above, the plot lacks depth and this is caused in part by the focus on regurgitating themes from previous films. Nothing really came as a massive surprise, it was unfortunately a case of feeling like I had been there, done that and got the t-shirt already.

3) The Middle. This is the main disappointment for me and where I think the movie deflates. We all know that a great film has to have that bit in the middle where the beginning develops into a meaningful ending. When they meet Maz Kanata the opportunity to develop plot and characters was lost. Instead, after taking a brief breather we are plunged into more action as Ren comes down to the planet to wreak yet more destruction. We could have done with a lot more depth here, back story ideally, which would have given us some of the originality the movie is lacking.

4) It was a too crammed. There wasn't chance to sit back and pause for reflection. It was intense while at the same time being somewhat empty, and maybe that is where the movie is flawed, filled with repetitive action scenes at the expense of advancing the story.

5) Kylo Ren unmasked. Our villain started out the first part of the movie as an intimidating and evil presence, but as soon as he throws his first tantrum and takes off his mask things start to fall apart, the teenager is revealed and you sort of lose any sense of fear that had built up.

In conclusion, The Force Awakens was a good foundation. It may not have lived up to my original expectations, but I do believe that in the test of time it will be viewed as a success and in many ways will get better with age and more importantly context. Where it lacked depth, originality and plot it delivers in terms of action, nostalgia and energy. It sets up the scene for the next two movies, pays homage to the past and delivers on the whole a very decent installment.

It leaves many unanswered questions, which combined with the open ending means I am left more excited for Episode 8 than I was for Episode 7. I just hope that the next movie can bring about the same vital effect for this new trilogy that ESB had on the Originals.

title: The best episode since the original trilogy
review:
(This review contains a SPOILER at the end!) I watched it last Saturday at TGV Cinema, Cyberjaya.

To me, being a Star Wars fan since childhood (I was 4 when I watched the original Star Wars in 1978) this episode brought my childhood back during the 2 hour plus duration (unlike the prequel trilogy!).

All the favourites were there: Han Solo, Leia, Chewie, Luke, R2-D2, C3-PO, etc. And the new cast were great as well.

It had it all - exciting battles and lightsaber action, family drama (soap opera in space?), etc.

I must admit - I cried when Han met Leia again and my wife was amazed looking at my reaction! I would give it a 5 out of 5 stars.

Perhaps the only disappointment I had was at the end when Rey met with Luke (is Luke going to reveal that he is her father in the next episode?) and he didn't utter a word! Anyway, great job JJ Abrams and team, and to be honest, I can't wait for the next installment (Episode VIII)!

title: Good but not quite Star Wars
review:
I have been a life time Star Wars fan, I love Star Wars not because of the special effects or story, but the depth of philosophy involved.

I saw the movie on Thursday in 3D, I have to say the movie was good, but not as I expected what a Star Wars movie should be.

The reason is that of all original Star Wars trilogy (Episode 4, 5, 6), there was more philosophy and conversations that is deep enough and could make you think about life. That is why there are so many timeless awesome quotes from the 4, 5, 6 episodes.

Then George Lucas made the prequel of episodes 1, 2, 3, it's more on love, special effects, fights, and spaceship combats, lesser on the philosophy, but it was in acceptable range.

This Episode 7 has absolutely no philosophy involved, I cannot remember a single quote from the movie after I have watched it. But I do remember all the flashy special effects and combats.... So if I were to make a rating on the movie, it's a good special effects movie, the story is okay, but there isn't a depth like the episodes 4, 5, 6.

Another things that is missing is the intimidation of the villain. Episodes 1, 2, 3 didn't have Vader, but they had a complex conspiracy involved and to learn how Anakin becomes Vader , which is fun to watch too. In this episode, Kyo Ren is just a Vader wannabe but is no where near Vader's range in terms of intimidation (probably will never find one that can match), he is more like a bad tempered kid with Force, unlike the cruel, cold, and calm Vader in episodes 4, 5, 6.

So in conclusion, I have to say the movie is good, but not great. But it is a good start for a reboot and the possible episodes coming.

title: Better than prequels; worse than original. Overall good but had its flaws.
review:
Saw the movie last night. I would say that it's an above average film. It wasn't perfect but it was entertaining and left me satisfied. Here are some observations:

Positives:

-Special effects were solid, as expected. Each movie gets better and better with that.

-Humor, when timed right, was great. You can always get a kick out ofChewie and the droids. Han had some funny one-liners.

-Much like the other movies, it was a movie the entire audience could relate and enjoy. I would say this movie is definitely designed more towards the millennials as it should be. The idea of a interracial romance, a female Jedi who fights, etc would not entirely happen in the originals.

-Left you hanging to see what the deal with Luke was and where he goes from there.

-

Negatives:

Kylo-Ren was pretty lame. I just expected more. The Dark Side had years and years go by to develop a well-trained villain. Even Darth Maul was more appealing. He was mixed with emotions the entire movie, he wasn't too intimidating beyond the first scene. There's really no backstory on him with Han at all. And he wasn't even skilled! He literally let Fin pick up a light saber and give him a hard time. What Jedi does this? Not to mention letting Rey read his mind, mess with him and pretty much defeat him in a light saber fight as well. Step your game up Dark Side.

-You couldn't really relate to many characters. For a movie with very similar details to "A New Hope", the difference in clarification on things was insane. You were knew to the whole story in Episode IV, but you still kept up with the mission of characters were and what they wanted to accomplish while explaining back stories at the same time. In this, you had 2 clueless untrained main characters, Han who didn't do much explaining, and others. C3P0 actually was not in it as much as I thought he'd be and he does a great job explaining things.

-Who is Snoke? What's his backstory? How did he take power of more or less the entire galaxy?

Bottom line is at the end of the day, it's a Star Wars movie and you can appreciate it. I would say it's more entertaining then the prequels but not as good as the originals. There are always more things you can nitpick in the negative column because Star Wars is at a high platform to begin with. I liked this movie and would see again. I am looking forward to more to come.

title: Gorgeous immersive visuals, uncharismatic characters, predictable tedious plot
review:
The first thing I was struck by going in was how beautifully shot this movie was. I could tell that everything was crafted with great care and skill, and it felt really immersive.

Unfortunately I was unmoved for three reasons: shallow characterization, little to no tension, weak villain. I only liked 3CPO and Han Solo. Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher were splendid and they had much more on screen charisma than the younger main characters did. I couldn't feel much for Daisy's character at all because she felt so one dimensional and shallow, and so did John. His interpretation of the character never made me believe that he was really a stormtrooper and he was just so predictable and uninteresting. There is some really lost potential there because their characters are actually quite interesting, the actors just never made me believe in them on screen. The characters get out of sticky situations so easily there's barely any feeling of tension or conflict, which got tedious after a while, the battles just felt like something they had to get through and I was just waiting for them to be over. I could remember feeling something in maybe just 2 scenes. Driver felt like an ill fit for Kylo Ren, I could really never take him seriously or believe in him when his mask was off.

The cinematography, vfx, all the art, direction and choreography were superb and there are some truly beautiful shots in there, and it truly was a pleasure to see the Star Wars world come to life here. However visual excitement alone doesn't carry a movie and they really need to stop relying on that. I'm craving for more substance, and I hope the future installments will give us that.

title: Amazing movie, but I ended up crying! Spoilers!
review:
I went in to see the movie with great grin on my face! I felt like I'm 6 years old again, as 34 years ago when I see the new hope first. I really enjoyed the ride, then suddenly I was crying....

Spoilers! Spoilers! Spoilers! You have been warned!

The story is very similar to new hope, which is fine as it introducing the new characters. It is a hero's journey. Kylo Ren is a complex villain with layers and conflicts, what I liked. The acting were great for all the new characters, they have good chemistry. Ray and Fin are great together. The story has dark moments and funny once with a good mixture of both. Harrison Ford made an excellent job, great acting.

What were a bit odd how quickly Han find them in the stolen Millennium Falcon. As it were stolen a long time ago, it were a bit strange he find them right away they took off. Maybe they accidentally turned on some kind of tracking device? It was not explained at all.

Ray had no idea of the force 30 minutes later she were full on using it. However she had mind read Kaylo. Did she learn from him to use the force???? Of course Kylo Ren were not a trained Sith either so they were evenly matched.

Than we came to the point which made me cry.... Han Solo is dead! He were my hero since I'm 6 years old! How could you do that????? When George Lucas were not answering to anyone, he made Jar Jar Binks. No Harrison Ford finally could do what he always wanted... to kill Han. It was not a heroic end like Obi One Kenobi's to save the others, than OK. I could handle a heroic death. But he died completely pointless unheroic way.

I wanted to give 9 stars for this movie, because I loved the rest, but I lowered it by 3 starts because of how Han died.

title: Not a bad film but be warned it is an Episode IV remake
review:
This is Disney's first venture into live action sci-fi since the risible Black Hole of 1979. Having made such a complete cow-pat of that movie, and having paid multi-billions for the Star Wars rights, it is understandable that Disney's execs wanted to play it safe this time, and play it safe they did. They hired a director with form for breathing new life into a tired old franchise and used the most successful and charismatic of the previous six movies as a frame on which to hang the same plot for the latest.

Stop me if you have heard any of this before

A droid containing information vital to the Resistance is hunted by the bad guys. Droid lands on desert planet and befriends a local scratching a living in the dust. Stormtroopers destroy village. Heroic female character is captured by the bad guys and is rescued by the good guys. Bad guys have a massive weapon that can destroy entire planets just like that. Bad guys destroy defenceless planet. Massive weapon has shields that are protected by an off-world shield generator which is destroyed by rebels. Massive weapon is destroyed by small scale fighters navigating down a tight trench under heavy fire.

PS: Storm troopers STILL cannot hit a barn door from five yards.

For crying out loud.

OK – having said all that, there are several good points, the main one being the absence of Jar-Jar Binks or any such irritating CGI character. CGI was used more sparingly than the prequels, and practical effects are well-made and effective. The cinematography was astonishing, there were some quite beautiful scenes. I particularly liked the tie-fighters back-lit by a setting sun, and the shots of Greenham Common, (two miles from my home), with the old Cruise missile bunkers doubling as the Resistance HQ. (I even recognized some of the gorse bushes, lol).

Good to see Mark Hamill again as well, although he looked half-dead. One hopes Episode VIII will have a little more originality than this one.

A good evening's entertainment, but I doubt I'll see it again.

title: Leaves more questions than answers
review: It was kinda what I expected it to be, AMAZING. It actually leaves more questions than it answers, plus that girl Ray is way to overpowered. how can she, with no training, defeat Kylo with years of training. also whats here background, how can the force be so strong with her. How did Poe get back from the dead? It was kinda obvious that Kylo is ether Hans or Lukes son. minus points on Han dieing and R2D2 and Luke only appearing in the last minute. The trailer makes you ask questions and you expect to have them answered in the movie but they are just left in the open.It definitely asks for a Star Wars episode IIV in short, I liked it a lot but it leaves so many questions.

title: Great characters but story too safe
review:
Lets first start of in saying that a lot has been right in this film. They've created relatable characters and managed to make them feel much more human than most characters of the old films. There is no over- use of CGI and everything has the good old Star Wars feel that we all loved from the original trilogy. The 3D is also well done and does not feel strenuous on the eyes during the entire film. The fighting scenes are also well made and the space battles are very pleasing to the eyes. For all this I applaud you JJ Abrahams.

Sadly, while you were busy to bring all these things back to us Star Wars fans you missed out on one thing. The Story. Who thought it was a great idea to bring back a 3rd type of planet destroying laser that has to be destroyed. Why is there yet another droid that has to go to the rebels to deliver secret information, another Jedi in hiding and another desert planet where somebody lives in poverty is accidentally send on an adventure due to a droid that fled when its master was captured by the order. The story is in my opinion very weak. It is simply a repeat of most of the 4th film and a bit from the 5th. I understand the thought progress that rehashing an old story is a safe way to not disappoint the viewers, but sadly it loses all elements of surprise to the film. In all honesty I was disappointed that the writers did not try a different, new and creative story line. Why did they not use the fact that it is a new trilogy to go a different direction?

The acting in the film by the main characters is superb. The scene of Harrison Ford meeting Adam Driver gave me the feels. It is also nice to see that the characters are multi-dimensional this time around and are not afraid to show emotions. I also enjoyed to see a strong female character and equally non-whiney male character. The dialogues were well thought out and it was nice to see some humour back in Star Wars as it was truly lacking in the prequels.

Overall this film is going to appeal to many Star Wars fans, although sadly story wise it is nothing new. It is sad to see such a missed opportunity where they could have made out of a good film something truly great if they would have not played it so safe. The film also contains a lot of fan service such as the game on the millennium falcon or lets just say the entire story line. The film is good but they could have done much more out of it, if they would have just taken some risks.

title: Please wait while the Force awakens...in 2017...maybe...
review:
The expectations too high? Maybe.

A bad movie? By no means! Especially and strangely more to who's new to the series.

Everything is in place - great production value, the galaxy, the Force, the Dark and Light sides, the battles. And one of the biggest fears that Disney will force to make it more, well, disneyish luckily is needless.

Only it does not feel complete. Yes, we know it's more coming, but still, too bland and too little happening.

And strangely, who hasn't seen the previous episodes should be more happy with The Force Awakens. Sure, they won't have the same nostalgic, warm feeling when seeing the Millennium Falcon and Han Solo again after 30 years, but this all will be new to them, to the others - we've seen it all, more than once...

title: Good but not great.
review:
Basically a remake of a New Hope. Some great acting from some quality actors. New light saber seems a bit daft and impractical. Great locations chosen for filming and I liked the original characters and actors being a big part of it.

I think I'm mainly disappointed because it's not really a sequel, there is so much of the film that you have seen before. Same Death Star ( but bigger) same Darth Vader type character, even a Yoda style 1000 year old character. The 3d is good but not as necessary to the film as say Avatar, it doesn't make you feel a part of the film.

I have to say that at least Disney have kept to the Star Wars ethos and have not changed the style that much, which was something I feared.

title: The Force is Calling to you...
review: From the first scene in Space a fan will notice the cinematography difference...The acting is good, the characters are good, the story flows somewhere, but where? I have been a fan of Star Wars since 5 and I wanted to see what happened next... All the basic blocks of Star Wars are present, but some are missing, which are the details... George Lucas is a genius... Even though people might hate "Phantom menace", you couldn't call it unoriginal, there was no fan service either. I will admit, I left the cinema with a lot of exact same questions that I had before the film... What happened to the New Republic? What happened to the Empire? What happened to Luke Skywalker?What happened to Imperial fleet?Who is Snoke? Partially you get the answers to these questions, but those answers are lazy.It also seems like the republic hasn't built a single capital ship in 20 years, nor it bothered to develop the new star fighter types. Don't get me wrong, the film is a hell enjoyable ride for the three quarters of it, but then you just get a rehash of the "New Hope", I've seen this in "Into Darkness" before. It also seems that JJ does not quite understand the concept of the "Jedi" and the "Force". It seems like anyone can use a Lightsaber and fight a trained Sith fighter in "Force Awakens". They tried to make the new villain as similar to Darth Vader as possible, but failed. Vader wasn't a psycho, he was intimidating. There was supposed to be a Jedi fighting Kylo Ren to protect the new characters, unfortunately they can take care of themselves without one. Who needs the Jedi training when you can kick the ass of the main villain 5 min after you took the Lightsaber? The Death of one of the main characters was as much as unnecessary as the 3d Death Star. Overall I am sure this film will find new fans and probably gather a few billions in ticket sales, but the Universe it portrays is not as detailed as the one George Lucas created...

title: The Forced Awakening
review:
Edit-- Went with my original title. Originally put "A New Hope" because felt my title was harsh, but not anymore. Also saved my newbies rant for the end. --

While it's always nice to pay tribute to the originals, the film literally tried to replicate them. It follows the same formula as the original Star Wars (IV), which is to have Indiana Jones type non- stop chase/adventure in Space. It succeeds in keeping you on your toes, cheering on the heroes, but it failed at delivering what really made Star Wars what it is.

First, it doesn't quite capture the grandeur of space and the "feel" of Star Wars' galaxy that was present in the original trilogy, and overly emphasized on in the prequel trilogy. I'm not even sure I caught one of the planets' name. Even John Williams' score felt a little weak compared to the originals, The Phantom Menace's "Duel of Fates" and Revenge of the Sith's "Battle of The Heroes". Worse yet, the new characters. The originals had charismatic characters with just enough depth to have you care about them. The prequel trilogy had far too much depth for most people's liking. In this, the new characters were given a decent introduction, but went no where with it. Nothing but one liners, it felt like. Furthermore, where are the great lightsaber like the one from I and III? I understand wanting to distance this film from the prequel trilogy, but COME ON! The one thing those films nailed were those battles. I also have minor issues that I'd like to list, such as referring to a star in a galaxy far, far away as "The Sun" but I'm going to ignore them in this review. Finally, my biggest complaint has to be the main villain. In the first hour, I honestly thought that he was going to be better than Darth Vader. He was evil, mysterious and had such strong presence. That did not last, as "Vader" rapidly transformed into Anakin from Attack of the Clones. I would like to rant on this a little more, but I'm afraid it may contain spoilers.

Trying to please such a wide audience is not an easy job. JJ did better than I expected, but it could've been a lot better. I only fear he will believe the reviews of vocal, easily impressed fans who want nothing but to belong to a "nerd" group because apparently that's what cool people do nowadays. I have witnessed the slow death of many film and video game franchises because of this phenomenon.

The Force Awakens tried to do far too much in 2 hours, and ended up delivering a somewhat forgettable chase film with Star Wars references and characters. That said, I'm not going to give up on this trilogy just yet.

title: It definitely delivered
review: Star Wars Episode VII: The Force Awakens is directed by J.J. Abrams. This film takes place over 20 years after The Return Of The Jedi. It was long awaited, but it definitely delivered. This film is everything you want a Star Wars film to be. It further deepens and gives purpose to the original characters, as well as introduces very likeable new additions. The action sequences are all incredible. This film really makes the most of modern CGI, but also does many things practically, which is essential for a Star Wars film. It is important that I speak about the new villain, Kylo Ren. This guy is awesome! He's such a deep and complex character. There is so much conflict within him, and when learning more about his back story, it makes you really view him as more than just an evil antagonist. The main criticism of the film surrounds the fact that it seems to follow and share similarities to the original trilogy, particularly A New Hope. I can see how perhaps they played it safe. But in my opinion all they did was improve on it and explore everything on a much deeper level. Star Wars: The Force Awakens contains such great writing and film making so therefore I give it a 9.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens - A Review by Nathan Fischer
review:
Star Wars has never been as huge as it is today. That's saying a lot. The universe George Lucas originally created has only gotten bigger since the release of A New Hope. Now Disney and JJ Abrams brings us the next installment, The Force Awakens. For many fans, this is a way to right what the prequels did wrong. Well fans can breath a sigh of relief. This is the Star Wars movie we have all been waiting for. I'm not going to go in to huge plot details here in case there are readers who have not seen the film. But by no means will this be spoiler free. That is a warning.

Let's start with the story. I found this tale to be classic Star Wars. They definitely took notes for A New Hope. I don't think the intention is to reboot anything, I think it's the idea that the past repeats itself This is a familiar theme in the Star Wars universe. JJ Abrams has done a wonderful job at making the story feel personal on a large scale. We have colorful, charismatic characters running in to each other through unforeseen circumstances.

There is a new evil power trying to run the Galaxy called The First Order let by General Hux and Kylo Ren who is our new dark side badass. Our heroes Rey, Finn, Han, Chewy and more embark on an adventure to join The Resistance and stop the new order after they find a piece of a map inside the droid BB-8 that could lead to the last known Jedi, Luke Skywalker. The mystery surrounding Luke is wonderful because we share it with the characters in the film. No one in the movie knows where he has gone or what he's been doing, and neither to we.

Finn and Rey have the most screen time, and their chemistry is undeniable. It almost bummed me out when they separated for a while in the middle, but I guess that means it works. Han and Chewy feel right at home without being overwhelming or forced. And BB-8 is just as charming and adorable as the ads would have you believe. I really loved how crucial he was to the plot. Then there is Kylo Ren, our villain. He surprised me. At first, he is all badass. Powerful, confident and driven by the dark side. But as the movie continues, we learn who he is and realize this is not a one note character. He is torn and haunted. The writers really did something I would have never thought of. While in all other Star Wars movies, the characters are trying to fight off the dark side, Kylo Ren is trying to fight off the light side. It keeps creeping in to him, seducing him to leave the dark side. I love that. The dark side has always come across as stronger then the light, but that is simply not true. No side is stronger then the other, the dark side is just more manipulative.

JJ Abrams has done a fantastic job of integrating practical effects and CGI. This feels like the original movies because we feel like we are there. Real sets, real costumes, real actors. Sure, there are some CGI characters. Some I liked (the owner of the bar) and some not so much (Supreme Leader Snoke). The battle scenes are also spectacular. All of it is easy to understand and puts you right in the action. I liked the light saber fight scenes as well, slowing down the pace and making it a little more choppy and brutal. These are not well trained Jedi fighting here, they are just starting to learn.

the film is not perfect. There was a lull here and there, and perhaps a little too much throwback, but that is totally forgiven. This was the movie I wanted to see. This is the Star Wars people have been waiting for. Through the film I cheered, laughed, teared up, dropped my jaw, and giggle in excitement. A movie hasn't done that to me since...well...I can't remember.

title: A fantastic action film whatever anyone says.
review: An extremely entertaining film. I was completely captivated. I already can't wait for the next instalment. It is filled with non stop action all the way through. It has everything you would want in an action film; explosions, flight scenes, good VS evil (or put another way the light side of the force VS the dark side) as well as some laughs. Yes, it can be argued, that the storyline resembles the past films and yes it has some cliques in it (such as Hans Solo's son being called Ben) but that didn't take anything away from my enjoyment. As a side note, if it turns out Rey is Luke Skywalker's daughter or some other clique like that, that will be disappointing as it would be nice for her to have more of an original back story. Despite this, I can't say much bad about this film. I really loved it and will definitely be buying the DVD when it comes out.

title: Completely unoriginal albeit entertaining enough
review:
When I first found out JJ Abrams was helming this ship I set my sights a little lower. And I'm disappointed to say I was not disappointed. As a moviegoer I don't mind Abrams, he's especially good at making entertaining and well-crafted movies that make money. But as a fan of an existing "movie universe" I knew the end-product would be unoriginal. If there were such things as a conveyor belt / assembly line that could manufacture movies Abrams' model would surely be the very top of its class.

I will not go in to detail to avoid spoiling anything. It's a shame because the movie had a lot going for it. The cast of new characters and the actors that played them (particularly the female lead) were excellent and refreshing to watch. Also, it was a treat to see many of the original actors back to reprise their roles... though even this seems uninspired. The production-value was great, as expected. The special effects were great, as expected. Even the script was fine. But the story was so completely unoriginal, that I found myself going over it again and again afterwards trying to find some originality in it but there was little to be found. It was like they took the original episodes, changed a few variables around and recycled it for the 21st century audience.

On the bright-side perhaps using the same formula which made the original episodes work so well will adopt a whole new generation of young enthusiast fans.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens... again
review:
SPOILER ALERT! If you are one of the ten people who have not yet seen Star Wars: The Force Awakens, stop reading now. If you are one of the three people who have never seen Star Wars at all, this movie will leave you seriously wondering what just happened.

You have been warned. Discussion begins in 3... 2... 1....

Okay, "Awakens" is a lot of fun to watch, and probably worth watching twice. But don't expect a single original thing in the entire movie. What you will find instead:

* A desert waif by the name of Luke... uh... I mean Rey... who despite living on the edge of survival in the middle of a desert still looks like a supermodel, falls in with a droid named R2D2... I mean BB-8... that shows the desert waif some top secret information. (This plot line is about as original as a Star Trek movie.)

* Rey, has been abandoned by her parents (there's a twist!), and we have no idea who her father is (coughLukeSkywalkercough) and she has no idea she is very strong in the force, and we of course have no idea why that is the case (coughLukeSkywalker'sdaughterrcough).

* He... SHE... goes into a space bar on Tatooine... I mean whatever planet it is this time, where a fight ensues (honest!... a bar fight) and in which Han Solo did not shoot first (probably because he wasn't there this time yet, but he shoots a whole lot later on).

* Our desert-waif meets Yoda... uh... no... Maz Kanata (wow, this does get perplexing)... a tiny, small-eyed wise person who tries to help start her path to the Force but who fails because Rey gets distracted and upset (cough justlikeherfatherLuke cough). Storm Troopers... she narrowly escapes on a junky spacecraft named The Millennium Falcon (no seriously, she really does) so that she can get R2... BB-8, who is carrying top secret information, (that she tells like everyone she meets what it is) to the Rebel Alliance-- evidently for the sole plot purpose of allowing the Death Star... I mean... DeathMOON (really, an actual moon this time) to track them and wipe out five planets with a single blast. (Hmmm maybe Rey is Leia's long lost orphan daughter instead.) Because other than that, there really is no reason at all the Rebel Alliance needs that information. I mean, who really gives a rat's behind about WhineyWalker's whereabouts anyways?

* There is a really bad guy named Darth Va... er... Kylo Ren... (who has a father/son relationship with one of the main heroes. Seriously, I'm not kidding) and he wears a black mask and talks in an odd voice and wears a black suit (but he really isn't Darth Vader honest). He does a lot of bad things and blows up planets but his light sabre looks like a cross instead of a single blade so he's not Darth Vader. Okay?

* The DeathStar... DeathMOON is a huge super-weapon that can only be destroyed by shooting an amazingly unprotected and wide-open thingy in the side that, if only a few dozen X-wing fighters attack it, will cause a chain reaction and the entire place will blow up. Because DeathThingy engineers are total idiots.

* During the battles, Kylo Ren... who was a former student of Obi Wan Ke... Luke Skywalker... but then turned into a bad guy... kills Obi Wan... I mean ... well he kills someone really important. The dead body falls down a really, really, really deep shaft that looks amazingly similar to the one that The Emperor fell down (no... that Darth Maul fell down... no, that Luke fell down... okay ALL of them). Anyway it's a neat effect. Again.

* So when everything gets blown up and the DeathMoon basically turns into a supernova but none of the escaping X-wing fighters are caught in the blast... everyone goes home and has a party. Except then there's an ending that leaves us hanging for part 2. Which is really part 8. Because in charge of plot development, Yoda is.

There is much more that I could review, but for a full plot synopsis of this movie you can watch Star Wars episodes 1-6. There's not much here that wasn't in those already.

Except Obi Wan... I mean Max Von Sydow... uh... someone we don't know who he is at all... gets killed really early in this one (kinda like a ship Captain in the 1st / 4th movie). But it's Kylo doing the killing this time, not Vader. Really, it's easy to get them confused. Kylo's the one without the breathing problem. He's just the one with the whiney problem that he got from his uncle Luke.

Go see it! It's all brand new and exciting. George Lucas didn't write this one. Well, he did write the original scripts, which Disney Inc. kinda borrowed from. A LOT.

At least the DeathMoon blows up a lot better. That alone is worth several rating stars.

(Now let's watch the ratings of this review and see just how much hard-core Star Wars fans are able to poke fun at their favorite franchise. I'm guessing not much. "OH BEST MOVIE EVER!")
