title: Exceeds the Miserable Episodes I-III But Doesn't Top the Original Episode IV -- Relies Heavily on Elements from IV
review:
After I viewed Star Wars VII: The Force Awakens with family and friends, I asked one of my cousins how she liked these as compared with Episodes I-III which I indicated in no uncertain terms were bad additions to the series, with Episode I being a truly convoluted and confusing film and Episode III being mediocre at best. She replied she was surprised I didn't like them, saying she loved the run on the Death Star and Empire Strikes Back. Turned out she hadn't seen Episodes I-III; she was referring to what are now called Episodes IV-VI which were produced long before Episodes I-III. This confusion has plagued the Star Wars saga since Lucas decided to add the miserable prequels which are now called Episode I, II, and III. The first film from the late 1970's, now re-digitized, is Episode IV: A New Hope.

As for the new installment, Star War VII, it is far better than any of the prequels. Not surprising, it doesn't top the original, now Episode IV. If there is a criticism of the new film, it relies heavily on elements of Episode IV. Back in Episode VI, the Empire was essentially destroyed, and the Rebellion created a new galactic government called the Republic, a resurrection of the Old Republic disintegrated by the Empire before the events of Episode IV. However, a new threat called the "First Order", a totalitarian regime which has arisen from the ashes of the Empire, threatens the Republic, and a military group called The Resistance leads the battle against them. The First Order is a cross between German Nazism and North Korea. A horrible looking deformed creature whose appearance rings of the Emperor of Episodes V and Vi, with a countenance which makes Darth Vader seem like a cultured gentleman, is the "supreme leader". His top henchman is Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), who wears a black mask like Darth Vader.

Without giving too much away, the story thread involves two new lead characters who are much better and more memorable than any presented in Episodes I-III, and a supporting character who nearly steals the show. Rey (Daisy Ridley) is a scavenger on the desert planet Jakku. Fin (John Boyega) is a storm trooper in the First Order seeking defection. Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac) is cracker-jack fighter pilot aboard a Resistance vessel captured by the First Order. In his possession is a digital map with the whereabouts of Luke Skywalker. Both sides seek Skywalker: the Resistance/Republic for a renewed order of Jedi Knights, and the First Order to squash this possibility. Dameron hides the map on the equivalent of a flash drive in a droid which ends up on Jakku, Rings a bit of Leia's encrypted message to Obi-wan Kenobi who resides on Tatooine, also a desert planet from the original film. Fin who has turned from the First Order helps Dameron escape from the First Order military ship.

On another front the First Order has developed mega-weaponry which can turn several planets simultaneously into the galactic equivalent of cream of wheat. Rings again of the Death Star of Episodes IV and VI. Fin and Rey through pure happenstance become intertwined with the droid carrying the information on Skywalker. Also, added to the mix, Kylo Ren was with the Republic/Resistance but left to join the First Order. Han Solo (Harrison Ford) and Chewbacca reappear midway, and become involved in the Resistance. They solicit the help of Maz Kanata (Lupita Nyong'o) who reigns over an intergalactic cantina. She was my favorite character of the film, said to be over 1000 years old. She tries to help Rey and Fin better understand their destinies and how the Force can aid in their missions. Princess Leia (Carrie Fisher), now General Leia, is head of the military forces to combat the First Order.

Generally, a very good film. I wouldn't call it the best of the series, but far better than the horrid Episodes I-III. I wish the filmmakers would have considered a different storyline than the old cryptic message hidden in a droid who ends up on desert planet. And the baddies are always blowing up planets, as if there's nothing else they can do to threaten the galaxy. But it more or less works. Overall I give it a B+. Maybe an uncut version on Blu-ray will have a bit more character development, particularly of Maz Kanata and Dameron.

title: An archetypal epic story, retold (but not remade)
review:
JJ Abrams entered that Dark Side cave in Dagobah and came out alive and in one piece. Being a Star Wars fan himself, he knew it would be impossible to reboot the most popular franchise of them all and please everybody, no matter what he did. Too much nostalgia would throw off the uninitiated newcomers; too little would appear as treason to the crowd that has memorized every single line from the original trilogy. On top of that, JJ and his team faced the challenge of introducing new characters the audience would care for, catch up with what the "legacy" ones had been doing over the last 30 years, quickly explain what the Force and this galaxy are all about, and at the same time set up the narrative context for two more movies to follow. All in 135 minutes, where exposition, character development, drama, comedy and action would have to be balanced perfectly.

Of course The Force Awakens borrows heavily from the beloved Episodes IV-VI. Imagine the backlash if it didn't. But a remake? Definitely not. There are so many new elements in the story, which echoes not only the entire Star Wars saga so far, but also every epic narrative ever written. Back in 1977, there were quite a few people who dismissed Star Wars for the same reason; oblivious to the fact that the Arthurian legends or even Homer's Iliad and Odyssey had also incorporated older storytelling elements, probably facing criticism for being unoriginal too in their time. Haters gonna hate, from the dawn of mankind till its end...

Yes, I also wouldn't like to see another Death Star blown up by X-wings in the next two episodes; yes, I'd be disappointed if Rey proves to be Luke's daughter, electrocuted near death by Snoke until her cousin Kylo Ren turns to the light side and throws him down a shaft. Luke sacrificing himself in a duel with his former apprentice and becoming a Force ghost would be pretty cheesy also. But none of this has happened yet, and chances are we are in for a few surprises.

--serious spoilers ahead--

Han being a tormented father that forgives his son the moment he is murdered by him is in no way a repetition of any previous Episodes. Finn being a stormtrooper with a conscience is neither. Rey being the "chosen one" who grows in a desert planet sounds familiar, but she is a very different character from whiny and pampered young Luke, and we still don't know where she came from or how she can be so powerful without training. Kylo Ren is no Darth Vader, and -thankfully- Adam Driver is no Hayden Christensen either. We've never seen such a complex villain before, one who is both merciless and fragile at the same time. Poe Dameron is a cocky top pilot without being Force-sensitive, and he doesn't seem to be the Han Solo charmer type either. Maz Kanata is not Yoda, even if she is small, wise and wrinkled. Snoke remains a mystery, and I doubt it he'll prove to be just a copy of Palpatine in the rest of the story. As for Luke, he has failed as a teacher (and perhaps as a father too, even though I think his -too obvious- connection with Rey is a red herring). And we still don't have a clue if he will behave like Obi Wan or Yoda in training the first female main lead ever to become a Jedi.

Over all, I found The Force Awakens both touching and entertaining, successfully shuffling the cards to create something both new and familiar. Perhaps it's not a cinematic masterpiece, but none of the other movies were either (no matter how popular they have been for generations of fans). And it's certainly not a typical Disney money-grabbing blockbuster with paper-thin heroes and fake-looking digital effects. It's an archetypal epic story, retold (but not remade). And it's also a rare case of a movie that makes grown men and women cry and rejoice from opening crawl to ending roll.

The Force is strong on this one, and it's not simply an excellent marketing campaign that makes it crush box office records.

title: What's up with the bad reviews - This movie is FUN!! Like the originals.
review:
One to four stars? I don't think so. I think fans of the books may be upset that this doesn't follow that cannon. Since I'm oblivious to the books, none of that mattered to me. The first spoken line sums up how I feel about this movie: "This begins to make things right" And TFA does just that. Heart. Humor. and Fun!!! Fun characters, lots of visual candy. Not too much CGI.

I was 17 when New Hope came out, and TFA joyously reboots the franchise. I've already seen it twice and will go again soon (I can count on one hand movies I've seen more than once in theaters, but three times? Maybe never). Welcome back, Star Wars.

title: Powerful Force of nostalgia
review:
The fans have waited for over three years to see this movie. They were praying for the creators not to destroy their childhood passion, again. Fortunately that did not happen and "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" is the perfect return to the original trilogy with plenty of action, humour and very interesting and eye-absorbing new characters. There is no spirit of Jar-Jar Binks in any of them and we are thankful.

I will not delve deeper into the plot to discuss what is going on in the movie, because plenty of You have already seen it, or will see it and I do not want to destroy the fun of experiencing the story for yourself. The action is set 30 years after the events in the "Return of the Jedi". The Empire has fallen, but its idea survived and a new vengeful power rises: the First Order. They spread their influences, but are strongly opposed by the rebellion under the command of General Leia Organa.

This is an action-packed movie with so much humorous interactions and dialogues that it would be categorised as the 'comedy' in the 'genre' section. The most comic lines are from the new 'Star Wars' characters: Finn, played by John Boyega, Oscar Isaac's Poe Dameron and Rey, played by the debuting Daisy Ridley. They all play their parts very well and I have nothing to suggest them at the moment.

Some people may have some problem with the great resemblance to the 'New Hope' plot line and they are right, but let's not forget that the recurring and 'as father as son' moments were in the franchise for as long I can remember. Take the movie as it is - the epic adventure, with the new characters and the old ones. Enjoy the ride again in the Millennium Falcon.

title: Don't listen to the nitpickers, this film is a thrill ride
review:
After reading reviews on here, it stuck me that the majority are negative?? I saw TFA last night and I have to say I loved it!

I loved the original trilogy as a kid, couldn't really care either way for the prequels but found TFA a non stop thrill ride!

I've read reviews on here saying that they got bored?? WHAT!!!..the film rarely stops for a breath yet still manages to focus on characters and build on relationships.

I've read that the return of classic characters was forced and wooden??? WHAT!!! These guys are a lot older and are'nt playing their 30 year old versions of themselves, and in a sense I like this, because as great as it was having these in this it didn't over shadow the newcomers.

I've read people saying how pathetic the villain (Kylo Ren) was?? I think this was kind of the point, the depth to him is his fear of not being a great as Vader and I like this angle , rather than bringing in a cheap rip off of Vader , they went for a different approach and in some sense almost honoured the fact that nobody will ever be as great as that character yet still leave the film winding up knowing there is a LOT more to come from both Rey and Ren in terms of their powers!

For me TFA is what Star Wars should be intense/conflicted/humorous/dark/emotional and yeah Im going to say thisgreat effects, seriously.some of the action scenes in here, wow! TFA fits perfectly in todays cinematic world with todays audience with enough filling to please older audiences also Don't listen to the negatives on here, go in expecting to be entertained by a great movie..simples! The only reason I give this a 9 instead of 10 is a few continuity errors, but this is nitpicking and certainly doesn't detract from the awesomeness of the film.

BTW , I am 35..and I went with my eldest son , who is 10, and my dad, who is 60 and we all came out with beaming faces giving it a thumbs up!

title: A triumphant, goosebump inducing hair raising journey back to what we all love about Star Wars
review:
I'm in my 30's, brought up on the original trilogy and I try to pretend the prequels don't exist so I (and my brother and dad) had such high hopes for this film. We left deliriously happy.

Yes, the story doesn't stray very far from what has gone before but that doesn't matter at all. The new cast are all excellent and spar off each other brilliantly, BB-8 is a joy in every scene and the film just delivers everything you want ... capable acting, a strong lead, drama, action, lore and fan service ... everything that the prequels failed to do. It feels and sounds like a star was movie should with CGI never taking centre stage over practical effects or more importantly, the acting. The original cast are used well, again with the focus clearly being on moving forward in the saga. One thing I really liked is that the First Order were a credible and real threat, something that needed to be stopped with urgency.

As a stand alone film it's great. As an addition to the Star Wars universe it breathes new life and washes away the stink of I, II and III.

title: Awesome to watch
review:
This is not going to be a long review, in fact, I will keep it simple:

This was a great return for me, I had my doubts about this movie, but it really came through for me.

People are saying that it's just a lot of stuff taken from older Star Wars movies, and to an extent, they are right. But, I really didn't mind. The acting was great, the visuals were brilliant and the story, even though it is similar to what we've already seen, left me with the true feeling of Star Wars.

This was one of those movies I'd like to watch again some time.

9 / 10

title: The Force is strong with this one. Stays (mostly) true to classic Star Wars tenets.
review:
I recall watching the release (and re-release) of Star Wars, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi, as an all-day matinée in '83 when RotJ was first released. The thing i remember, as clearly as if it happened just yesterday, is the buzz, anticipation, and adrenalin rush i had knowing i was about to see all three movies at once. Now, how many people (outside cinema staff) can say they got to see all three originals, in one day, on the big screen? But i digress.

For the most part, The Force Awakens, delivered on the promise of the original three movies, where the later three movies that started with Phantom Menace, mostly failed. With the three middle movies, i found a lot of the material, plot lines, and sub-plots were either tacky, cheesy, or just plain average. I found The Force Awakens to have pretty much returned some great classic/fundamental, old Star Wars flavor, cleverly blended in with the new. No mean feat.

Incidentally, i never got to see the first movie (A New Hope), as i was only eight at the time (in '77) - and i'm still envious of my three older brothers who were all old enough to see it during their high school years, at the time.

In all honesty, for those new to the Star Wars universe, on the big screen, trust me when i say, this movie is an excellent introduction to it.

So it's like this: if the following Star Wars movies are anywhere near as well thought out, produced, and filmed as The Force Awakens is, than die-hard Star Wars fans (like myself), old and young, should just about get the same buzz, anticipation, and adrenalin rush i had, all those years ago, back in '83.

title: Don't bother with the waffling reviews, see the movie and judge for yourself
review: Having watched SWTFA several weeks ago now, I have given myself sufficient time for consideration of an appropriate reply. However, I think as a 47 year old who was around for the original trilogy, I would like to leave only one simple piece of advice. Watch the film for the enjoyment factor first and foremost, save the analysis to the posters here who have 2 hours to spew blah on the comparisons to previous films, directors, themes etc etc, ad infinitum. I wanted to feel like an 8 year old again and did. The rest is just cornflakes. The opening credits, the X wings on the horizon across the water and Solo on the bridge of the falcon should be enough to jog the emotion cells of anyone who has an imagination. Don't bring baggage by reading 50 reviews, just get blown away by the feel good.

title: A Worthy Continuation of the Original Trilogy
review: Star Wars: The Force Awakens is by far the best Star Wars film we've gotten since Empire Strikes back. It's a love letter to fans, from fans This movie was made with absolute love and it shines throughout every corner of the film - from the practical effects to the returning characters to the NEW ones we've now been introduced to. Daisy Ridley as Rey is absolutely fantastic. She's bad ass, independent, and the strongest female lead I've seen in a long time (save Jessica Jones), and Daisy Ridley gives a PHENOMENAL performance. John Boyega as Finn is strong, likable, and you cheer for him from the moment you see him try to save Po. He's relatable and always asks the hard questions, and by far has an extremely strong arc, from Stormtrooper to resistance fighter. Adam Driver as Kylo Ren is villainous but EXTREMELY sympathetic. Kylo Ren is memorable, scary, but torn between the light side and the dark, making you question whether he is truly evil. Up there with Darth Vader, I expect awesome things from him in the next movie. The Story itself is fast paced, break-neck action combined with truly heartbreaking AND heartwarming twists throughout it. From the opening attack on the village to the final battle, it never stops, and it never lets you go. Even the quiet moments are so gripping you sometimes forget to breath.

title: Why all the hate?
review: I really liked this movie! Yes it's plot is similar to "A New Hope", but the execution is different enough to make it feel fresh. I've seen it twice. In Theaters in 2015 and today. I wanna quickly mention, that the cinematography by Dan Mindel is extremely underrated! It should at least have gotten an Oscar nomination. The score by John Williams is great as always, though not many original cues. "Rey's Theme" and "March of the Resistance" are however exceptions. Overall a really great experience, great characters, dialogue and a flowing pace delivered by J. J. Abrams. A 4/5 stars from me.

title: Hated it
review: To be honest since TLJ came out I now hate TFA. In itself the film was just an ok-ish film. If it wasn't starwars it would just be an unknown film. JJ did good, it was somewhat original but it lacked interesting storytelling.

title: 'Awakens' is Forced
review:
Okay, let's get the fangirling out of the way, shall we? Ahem. "OHMYGOSH! A STAR WARS MOVIE! BY J.J.ABRAMS! I'M SO EXCITED! THE ORIGINAL CAST?!! DREAM COME TRUE! I LOVE HAN AND LEIA AND Luke!"

Now for the review: This movie was, not a huge disappointment, but it didn't wet my whistle in the same way the originals did. Or even the way the Star Trek reboot did. There was SOMETHING missing from this movie, but I'm not 100% sure what that is. It starts off promising, with the new pilot character teasing at the fact that he works for Princess, er, I'm sorry, General Leia. And then BOOM! Kylo Ren comes and you get to see the new Sith apprentice in all his glory, but then the movie kind of loses it from there. It spends way too much time with the new characters; getting to know them, seeing where they come from, and all of that is fine, but a little later on please. You know who I came here for. And When you finally get to see one of the three that you paid $16.50 to see you learn something that doesn't sit well. But you have to accept it and move on. Then you're in for two out of three characters and you're still hoping that magic will formulate and you will get the fourth Star Wars movie you've been waiting for. But alas that doesn't happen either.

The movie is just too conscious that it is a Star Wars movie and that the prequel series didn't sit well with the fans. Hearing that the prequels were too heavy and lacked a sense of fun this film is over saturated with jokes, making the characters seem not lighthearted but immature or just plain dumb. And the movie wants to show you that it respects its Star Wars history by paralleling the very first Star Wars movie, but it takes too much and it seems like a revamped more modern remake of the original instead of its own original story.

The new trio of heroes don't have the same feel as the original three, and I respect that. These are new characters, they should feel new. But they also don't seem to work too well together, yet. And I look forward to seeing them grown into a good team. But first they have to meet, because Poe and Rey don't during the film. They also tried a bit too hard to make Rey a bad-ass and to make Finn "worthy" or "redeemable." Giving us reasons to love them in black and white instead of letting us make up our own minds about them.

Kylo Ren was also a disappointment. The only character in the whole of the Star Wars Universe that has not only two loving parents, but quite literally a platoon of extended family that loves him, and he turns into the wimpiest baby bad guy ever. Trying to live up to a ghost of the past that he doesn't fully understand. Ugh. Side note: Captain Phasma was awesome! Now there's a bad guy I can get down with!

The three heroes of our youths-- Luke, Leia and Han are never together on screen at the same time, in one place and that is a huge slap in the face! They're who I came to see!!

Overall, I can see what The Force Awakens was trying to achieve, but it just didn't make it all the way there. I still have faith that the next installment will be better. 7/10

title: Better than the prequel trilogy
review:
The good:

  • Harrison Ford


  • Chewie


  • Droids


  • Harrison Ford again


  • The writing really felt like Star Wars again, for the most part. The introduction of the Millennium Falcon was a particularly nice segway.


  • Rey is less annoying than Luke from Episode IV. Seriously hope she continues to grow as a character.


The bad:

  • Harrison Ford's death scene sucks. It has no real purpose, and really comes off like the death scenes TV actors have to film in case they negotiate for too much money. Bringing him back would be total non-canon and probably garbage, but try it anyway.


  • Harrison Ford was being set up as a latent force user, especially with that blind "force shot" with the blaster, and the strength of the force in his son. This foreshadowing of a potential storyline could have been incredibly interesting. Is lost opportunity.


  • Kylo Ren appears to be following the Hayden Christensen school of acting/writing. This is not good. The prequel trilogy was horribly written, and following it will only yield bad things. What's most notably bad is the entire franchise seems scared to write a relatable bad guy, starting with the prequel trilogy. In the original trilogy, even a Sith Lord (Vader) who chokes out generals for incompetence has some good in him (saving Luke). Kylo could very easily be one dimensional and trash the entire sequel trilogy, but we haven't seen enough of him to be sure.

title: Decent movie, can't live up to the hype
review:
I watched the trailers roughly a hundred times leading up to the day I saw the movie. To be honest: To me, the trailer was better than the movie.

The reason for this is, that there is something missing in the movie. I just can't quite put my finger on it. The acting was good, there were a lot of scenes that referred to the earlier movies, making me smile and get that star wars feeling and some witty dialogs that had me laughing out loud. At the end of the day however, there is no "best scene" that could be burned into my memory and never let me forget the force awakens. (Well, now that I think about it maybe there is one, but in hindsight it feels like that particular scene was forced into the movie to create that memorable moment, so it's more like 1 frame that the movie could be summarized in) Furthermore, a big part of the plot feels just like some sort of variation of something that happened in the other movies.

What we are left with is a nice movie that comes nowhere close to what I had hoped for.

title: A nostalgic and fresh (yet not flawless) start for a new trilogy
review:
First off, was this movie good? Yes it was, and I can say that after I had left the cinema I wasn't disappointed. But was it a great movie?

To begin with, I'd like to say a few words about the technical aspects and the overall look of the movie. The CGI looks amazing and combined with the smart use of many practical effects this makes for some truly stunning action sequences. Especially the flight scenes involving the Millennium Falcon, particularly the one on Jakku, had me on the edge of my seat.

A small aspect of the movie I personally enjoyed was the use of the old-school wiping transitions from the original trilogy that add a very nice nostalgic feeling to all the use of modern filmmaking methods in this movie.

Furthermore, I have to say that all these new formerly unknown actors really convinced me, especially Daisy Ridley does an amazing job in my opinion. The idea of casting unknown actors, as George Lucas did with his first Star Wars films, also helps to create compelling and believable characters.

I would also like to mention that another great aspect of this movie for me was its humour. There are some truly hilarious moments that got me and the audience in the cinema burst out with laughter, most of which involved BB-8, the cute little droid that is something in between R2-D2 and Wall-E. In the first half of the movie he constantly provides for some extremely funny comic relief that, however, never felt forced or annoying.

But now lets dive into the story and its characters, because that is what makes a great Star Wars movie, and basically any movie. So, does it hold up compared to the original trilogy?

I can understand when some people complain that this film is too much like the original trilogy and it is true: many aspects of this movie are essentially A New Hope all over again. We basically have a new Death Star (although the idea of it using the power of a nearby sun is a nice new approach; it doesn't, however, change the fact that the general idea stayed the same) and a shield that needs to be destroyed (here we even have Episode VI) in order for the X-Wings to attack the one weak point of this ultimate (or rather not so ultimate) weapon.

However, for me the movie still offered many new aspects that made it feel fresh and the whole story around Starkiller Base was never the main focus of this movie. I see it rather as an homage with which J.J. Abrams tried to pay tribute to the old Star Wars movies. Considering that Abrams had to please a wide range of audiences that reached from the ones who grew up with the old movies and wanted something exactly like that to the ones desiring something completely new I believe that he did a really good job.

Although, I have to say that this choice of adapting certain iconic plot points of A New Hope (and even Episode V and VI) while putting main emphasis on the new (and old) characters did also create a problem for me. And that is the fact that I just didn't really care for Starkiller Base, I never really felt its impact. It is just there and for me at least it never has this daunting menacing aura that surrounded the original Death Star. In addition, that makes the destruction (while visually absolutely stunning) kind of impactless from an emotional point of view and it doesn't help that Leia does not seem too upset about Han Solo's fate.

But as I said, in my opinion this movie is much more than just a remake of A New Hope, which is why I can appreciate the homage, but still enjoy the main focus of this movie - and that lies on the new characters it introduces. So lets talk about them. I liked the idea of Finn's character, emotionalising a Stormtrooper is something totally new and something that has been left untouched. Carrying on, I already mentioned how abundantly entertaining BB-8 is and with Rey we finally get to see a girl become a Jedi!

Most importantly I need to talk about Kaylo Ren for he is another thing that may leave some people disappointed. Judging from the trailers, he seems to be this really cool new villain, though it turns out that his whole demeanour is merely a false front he built up. However, while I was at first a bit thrown off when he took off his mask and his true character and his struggles became apparent, I really like this choice as it gives his character room to develop. We aren't just given another super villain, but a human being who we can understand. This will make for a much more compelling villain when we see how his character evolves and the death of Han Solo was the first part of that. This scene has so much emotion in it and gives the character of Kaylo Ren so much more depth.

In conclusion, I think they did a really great job with all these new characters, yet there is one that left me disappointed and that is Supreme Leader Snoke. He just doesn't do anything in this movie and just says a few lines because we need to see Ren has a superior. He is simply a joke compared to the Emperor. Even the visuals in the scenes involving Snoke didn't convince me.

All things considered, I believe that The Force Awakens is a highly entertaining movie that pays tribute (maybe a tad too much) to the original trilogy. And while it certainly isn't flawless, it is a great fresh start for a new trilogy that makes me want to see more!

title: The Force is back, but not with a bang.
review:
I know, I know, Please don't kill me, although I see that some of you agree.

I will say this, I actually loved the new characters that were made for this generation of Star Wars. Fin acts a lot like a Star Wars fan trapped in a Star Wars movie and his origin was pretty cool. His chemistry with Rey was dynamic and to be blunt, it's good to see a strong female character in a Star Wars movie other than Princess Leia(who I loved in this movie as well).

Poe Dameron was a great character as well. He looks like a carbon copy of Hon Solo and that would have been the case if it were played by anyone one else other than Oscar Issac. I even like Adam Driver as the Dark warrior Kylo Ren.

I could go on and on with the many supporting characters, but I won't. Let's just say they all were developed well from the biggest to the trivial.

And speaking of Trivial, the attention to detail was amazing. It was not just quick scenes in the movie that would make Star Wars fans eyebrows raise when they realize the Easter egg they caught, but it looks like they add cool stuff that would make new fans go ga ga twenty years from now.

And the movie has an very epic appeal to it, as a good Star Wars movie should. the Visual effects are as stunning as the original trilogy.

Now here's the problem. The movie is not tight enough. I went into the film trilled at the fact that it was only going to be 16 mins over two hours instead of taking up half my day, but in reality this movie could have been two hours flat. Number seven had a lot of cool images but a lot of it dragged on a minute too long in an attempt to get dramatic effect.

And that's the other thing. All the images were cool, but I felt no emotion in it, and that's an important factor with the Force Awakens. a lot of stuff is going to happen that's suppose to make you tear up and suppose to make you clap for joy, but the only parts that connected with me emotionally were the parts that made me laugh. I noticed a lot of those fun moments were when the movie was poking fun at the franchise, which is easy to do, while the other emotions are not.

Bottom line, JJ Abrams' reboot of the Star Trek franchise was far better than his sequel to Star Wars. Everything he did that made me love that movie only made the Force Awakens OK. Something tells me this whole new trilogy will just be OK if I go by episode seven.

title: It's Our Fault, We Asked For This!
review:
After 10 years - or 32, depending on your regard for the legitimacy of the prequel trilogy - Star Wars is back, and, in the spirit of times, as Giuseppe DI Lampedusa would have put it, it was necessary for everything to change in order for it to remain the same: new studio, new team, new characters... new expanded universe even (more on that later). It's funny then, and sadly not at all surprising, that so many things remain the same as in 1977.

The Empire has survived, in the form the The First Order, and the rebellion is now the Resistance, led by General Leia Organa. A soul-searching stormtrooper (Boyega) saves ace resistance pilot Poe Dameron (Isaac) and important info stored in a droid and stages an escape to a desolate desert planet... Well, if echoes of Episode IV are already a bit startling, it gets worse. It quickly becomes clear why so many directors turned down this dream assignment, as Episode VII isn't as much a chance to play in George Lucas' sandbox as a remake of his original opus. Blame Disney. Blame J. J. Abrahms, he's certainly done this before... the fault, it turns out, is yours.

After the dismal prequels, chock-block of new ideas, some good, some bad, most of them executed horribly, we've howled for movies that resembled the originals more that Disney would have been suicidal to approve anything more original than this, and history will judge Episode VII on how much it emboldens the studio to be more daring, or whether it just confirms the need to just "give fans what they want", more of the same. Time will tell, but, to quote our heroes, I have a bad feeling about this.

What is annoying this time, after the utter cluelessness of Episodes I-III, is the very real talent on display here. The old characters could have stood silently in the background, paychecks safely cashed, but they make a mark, particularly Harrison Ford as Solo, more touching and involved here than he has been for at least a decade. The new characters are just as involving and appealing, particularly John Boyega's Finn and Adam Driver's Kylo Ren. Andy Serkis also makes an impression. Otherwise, the humor is back and it's a thrill to see J.J. Abrams work a scene after the inane telenovela-like blocking of the prequels.

And still, this could have been much more, and our only consolation will have to be that it could have also been worse. The greatest question is, what comes next?

Tonally, we are squarely back in original trilogy mode, the only limit will be the appeal of the characters (mostly successful here) and the caliber of the stories (not so much). It is a bit worrying that Disney has jettisoned all the expanded universe, both because it might set an ugly precedent, and because it does show a fear of risk and cynical approach to a very valuable brand.

And yet... we might be wrong: what little transparency has been displayed so far might be completely honest. It was George Lucas himself who, in an interview, said Disney had rejected all his outlines saying that they wanted to make "one for the fans". Well, this describes Episode VII perfectly. If we could have some fresh ideas with our next helping, we'd truly be thrilled.

title: "I see your eyes...I know your eyes"
review:
The portrayal of each character in this film makes excellent use of this concept. Maz Kanata has lived for over a thousand years and can learn the essence of an individual just by seeing there eyes. I believe that this idea was used throughout the entire film. Such vivid expression is used by each of the actors that it helps the watcher to really feel that they are looking into that character's life and the essence of who they really are.

When we first meet Rey, she is isolated on Jakku. Her facial features are stern and give the read of someone who has had to live their life constantly on their guard living from meal to meal. She then meets BB-8 and, during her explanation of waiting for her family to return for her, she develops a half-smile with sadness and false hope in her eyes. And from the moment she boards the Falcon she develops a sense of fear, excitement, and uncertainty as she really starts to test her own abilities as a pilot in a life-or- death situation as she and Finn escape from the ties. And so you have Rey. This tough, hardened, and resilient person that is still sweet and yearning for family and unsure of herself all at once. Daisy Ridley did such an excellent job at showing this that you really feel that you know Rey by the end of this film.

This can be said for all of the actors. Whether it's during Han's close up as he explains that the force is indeed real to Finn and Rey, or during Finn's confession of his own past to Rey. Each character is extremely well presented through their facial expressions, sincerity, and genuine representation that you know and love these characters. What an excellent way to bring Star Wars in for a new generation of viewers and for long time fans alike.

This is what these films were always about to me. Likening to the people you see on the screen and developing a connection with them so that you really want to learn what happens to them next and go through it with them. That is what makes a film great and what makes Star Wars generation spanning.

This is definitely the Star wars I was hoping for, and I highly anticipate the next films to come.

title: The Force is ALIVE!!!
review: It took me a long time to write reviews again, which is fair, because I have been going through a bit of a block lately. Since it's the first day of a new year, I guess it's fair that the first review I write of this year is last year's (actually, it came out three weeks ago) biggest hit. To be honest, I didn't expect "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" to crawl deep inside my brain and bring me back into the world of space that I remembered when I was a kid. Mainly, because I lost touch of it for a while. I wasn't born in 1977, but I remember seeing two of the three original "Star Wars" movies with my dad when it was re- released in 1997. Now after re-watching all 6 episodes of the Star Wars saga after seeing "Force", I realized that this was a world (or worlds) I couldn't leave behind. So, what's new this time? Well, Disney took over Lucasfilm, George Lucas is still retired, and it looks like the beginning of the new trilogy can definitely return to the flavor of the much-loved original trilogy (the prequel trilogy still remains quite divisive among fans). Now taken over by J.J. Abrams (director of "Star Trek" and its following sequel), "The Force Awakens" is a wonderful, exhilarating, funny, triumphant, sometimes tragic and beautifully imaginative adventure that reminded me and a lot of people who have already seen it how much we've loved and missed "Star Wars". We cheer for the heroes, hiss at the bad and we feel for the ones that are in-between. Plus, we get to experience worlds that Lucas and company has created 39 years ago and it still remains as vibrant and colorful and thrilling as ever. Whether you missed out or live in a cave (I don't think you're one of those people, because you've already seen the movie more than once), let me try to explain a bit of the plot without spoiling it. Set three decades after the events of "Return of the Jedi", a fellow Jedi that we all know and love has disappeared and the evil Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) is hell-bent on finding him and getting rid of him. Meanwhile, we get to meet some impressive new characters. Rey (Daisy Ridley) is a scavenger from Jakku who has been for looking for her family ever since she was a little girl. Finn (John Boyega from "Attack the Block") is a Stormtrooper who has been ripped from his family and has been sent to kill but manages to turn the other corner, as it is. Finally, there's Poe (Oscar Isaac from "Ex Machina" and "Inside Llewyn Davis") who's a pilot. Oh, wait, there's also a new droid on the scene. Its name is BB-8, who is quite friendly and helpful in every way. Joined together quite late in the process, they team up with returning characters Han Solo (Harrison Ford), General Leia (Carrie Fisher) and, of course, our favorite Wookie, Chewbacca (Peter Mayhew) in order the find the missing Jedi and to take down the First Order led by Supreme Leader Snoke (Our mo-cap superstar Andy Serkis), Ren and General Hux (Domhnall Gleeson, also from "Ex Machina"). I was ever so reluctant to see another episode of "Star Wars", but after seeing it, it renewed my interest in the world of both filmmaking and "Star Wars". It looks as if Abrams has accomplished what Lucas did in the past, recreating the magic as if it still existed. Characters, galaxies, secrets, epic battles and plentiful twists and turns that never diminished of what Lucas had envisioned before. The only glue that remains as a big piece of the puzzle is the always unforgettable score done by John Williams. With the iconic opening theme and a few additional themes added in there as well, Williams once again creates another bit of lightning in a bottle. Nothing moved me more as I got to see Solo and Leia together again, as well as our original droids, C-3PO and R2D2. (Mark Hamill is also in here as well, but I can't reveal where he's at.) Plus the new characters are brilliantly cast. Newcomer Daisy Ridley is a star I definitely should keep my eye on. I even liked her chemistry with John Boyega, who is both heartfelt and humorous at certain turns. We don't get to see much of Poe in the movie, but Oscar Isaac brings a warm and dashing impression. But the standouts are definitely Adam Driver who brings a lot of terror and emotional depth as Kylo Ren and (obviously) Harrison Ford as Solo. This character that we loved for so long is charming, energetic and ruggedly laid-back as ever and Ford continues to make that character totally rewarding. This is a movie event I will never forget (next to "Jurassic World", it's easy not to overlook this). All I can say is this: I can't wait to see what Rian Johnson (director of "Looper" and "Brick") and Colin Trevorrow (director of "Jurassic World") can do with Episodes 8 (coming 2017) & 9 (coming 2019), because this is a fantastic saga that shouldn't be forgotten. The "Star Wars" saga still remains a amazing group of films that if you watch from the very beginning (I always start with Episodes I-III then Episodes IV-VI), you can see that the story still connects one way or another. I certainly hope to see this movie again. Probably because I want to pick up on some of the hidden secrets that are hinted at. Also, I want to be overwhelmed by the amazing visuals, memorable characters and incredible worlds. Another ingredient to add into this is that the Force has been passed down from one generation to another. With "The Force Awakens", it just shows that the force is definitely with us, forever and always. And I'm glad that I got to be a part of it again.

title: Great Addition to the Star Wars Family
review: After waiting to read all reviews before watching it myself, I am disappointed in all the negative user reviews from so many would be Star Wars fans. Really, 1 out of 10...really!!! That seems a little extreme. Was it really that bad to you? Is there any pleasing you; glad you're not paid to write reviews. I feel some of these user reviewers would have rated it badly no matter what was placed on the screen in front of them. Now, I will step off my soap box and begin my user review. I grew up watching Star Wars on VHS over and over again and playing with Star Wars action figures (yes, I took them out of their boxes), and The Force Awakens was the first of the new generation of Star Wars movies that I can't wait to watch again. It held Forcefully true, pun intended, to what makes Star Wars great. JJ made a movie that took Star Wars back to its roots in a galaxy far way, but one with which we are all very familiar. It made me feel like a 5 year old kid watching A New Hope for the first time in my living room all over again. I love the new characters and can't wait to see where JJ is going to take us.

title: JJ Abrams delivers on high expectations with a true Star Wars movie!
review:
Star Wars is back, as JJ Abrams achieves a small miracle in creating a movie that respects its original material, brings in a ton of new characters, makes it appealing for new viewers and sets up a story to build a new Star Wars trilogy on.

Without giving away too many spoilers, the story revolves around a scavenger(Rey), a renegade stormtrooper(Finn) and a fighter pilot(Poe) in their quest to defeat an enemy with the power to endanger the galaxy. To be honest, superb acting has never been a strong point in any of the previous Star Wars movies. This trend has thankfully been broken, as the stellar cast give great performances throughout the whole movie. The newcomers Daisy Ridley and John Boyega, playing as Rey and Finn respectively, prove themselves more than capable of carrying the load in continuing the saga. They both show great chemistry together and give us extremely likable characters, with Rey bringing the heart of the film and Finn the abundant energy. Oscar Isaacs, who plays Poe, is the veteran among the young cast and pulls of a cool and smartass X-wing pilot. And finally, the old cast returns to give this film a true Star Wars feel to it. Harrison Ford returns as Han Solo and has not seemed to skip a beat since 1983, as he is as cheeky and badass as ever. His witty banter with Chewbacca is a pleasure to watch, but Ford also brings a strong emotional performance this time too. Carrie Fisher as Leia also returns, in a rather small role, and delivers some sweet scenes with Han and the new cast. However, the most complex character with the best arc in this movie, is the antagonist Kylo Ren. Ren, played by Adam Driver, gives us an extremely intimidating villain with a troubled past we are eager to discover. Ultimately, he serves us more than a Darth Vader wannabe.

JJ Abrams, alongside Lawrence Kasdan and Michael Arndt, wrote a fun and entertaining screenplay with plenty of emotional plot twists and content. Each main character has its own background and motivation, which develops over the duration of the film. A pleasant surprise to see is the humor used in the movie. The comedic relief in the film was used very effectively in developing chemistry and sympathy for the characters. It is also a sign that the movie does not take itself too seriously as the prequels did.

The Force Awakens is filled with exhilarating action and moves with great pace during these scenes. Yet, Abrams knows to slow it down during scenes conveying intense emotion giving the audience time to process all that is thrown at them. These combined make it easy to understand the main characters' motivations, making the emotional investment so much better.

As is typical of Star Wars, the movie is full of awe inspiring visual images and astonishing sound editing, creating new sounds for laser beams, light sabers, and alien noises. The cinematography is equally impressive, showing beautiful landscape shots of new planets reminiscent of the original trilogy. The cinematographer, Daniel Mindel, also shows us a diverse array of shots, giving heart-pounding POV shots inside the cockpit and nice long shots of the battlefield giving it a great scope while avoiding confusion caused by the numerous explosions.

John Williams makes a welcome return to the Star Wars franchise with a bombastic new score, but also with nicely timed inserts of his famous original music to bring up emotional heartwarming feeling among the old- school fans.

In conclusion, The Force Awakens is a return to form for the Star Wars franchise, as JJ Abrams gives his tribute to the original Star Wars, leading to a fanboys' dream. This beautiful reunion of old characters combined with the introduction of promising new characters results in a nostalgic and emotional adventure trip that left me excited for what is coming next. To quote Jimmy Kimmel, this movie was probably "the most anticipated sequel since the New Testament". So expect this movie to be under the most intense scrutiny by reviewers as they dissect the movie to its core to find the tiniest flaws. Nobody wants to be "Phantom Menaced" again. In the end, The Force Awakens delivers as a fantastic Star Wars film and a worthy addition to the franchise. It is definitely the best Star Wars movie since 1983 and, in my opinion, the best one since The Empire Strikes Back.

title: Ray of Light
review: As much as I love the prequel trilogy, I must admit that Star Wars needed this reboot. I was initially worried that it would be Disneyfied,but George Lucas and J.J Abrams didn't step a foot wrong. I have nothing critical to say and I believe anyone who does is either simply not into star wars or a wannabe critic. The new characters were (as always in star wars films) very welcome on screen and came organically with the story line. The film didn't feel 'forced' or over dramatised, it was all kinds of light hearted and at the same time action packed and thrilling. I felt there was a perfect balance between familiarity and new and exciting characters. They didn't try to replace Darth Vader directly and addressed his absence head on. But what impressed me most about the film (of which I have already watched twice) was its stand alone quality...by which I mean, even if I had never seen a Star Wars film, I still genuinely believe I would have fallen in love with it. To conclude, It does the original trilogy every bit of justice and anyone who hasn't watched this film yet and perhaps fears it won't live up to your childhood memories of A new hope... empire strikes back and return of the jedi... trust me...it will.

title: Slumber Earthquake.
review:
There really is no point trying to do an in depth review of this, it falls in line with a number of series blockbusters that are guaranteed to garner rabid responses, pro and con.

The Force Awakens is a film of many flaws, it has a pungent whiff of safeness about it, the charges of it being a glitzy remake are fair enough, while certain plot strands are frustrating and set to be big talking points for years - and years - to come.

Yet what about its worth to someone who is not obsessed with every finer detail? Someone who just loves the Star Wars universe as a spectacle prism of entertainment, and has just wanted a Star Wars film worthy of being fit to sit alongside that original trilogy?

This made me feel 11 again, took me back to a time in 1977 when I queued for three hours to see such wonders on the big screen. The Force Awakens is, in spite of the recognised flaws, a loving homage to a past love. It's sly with humour and nods to foundations, a blitzkrieg of effects and sound work (my Blu-ray viewing had my sub-woofer doing a jitterbug in the lounge), and it doesn't shy from surprise or the dangling of the carrot.

The makers have big heart and technical invention, the cast vibrant, spunky and strongly committed to the cause - the old hands a very reassuring presence - Yeah, so it's not sci-fi perfection, or any Star Wars geeks' idea of the perfect Star Wars movie (oh J.J. Abrams you devil you!), but it made this middle aged guy shed a tear of happiness. A moment to reaffirm why - as a young lad - I fell in love with film in the first place. 9/10

title: An Elegant Movie for more Civilized Times
review:
***This review may contain Spoilers ***

JJ did it. It is true Star Wars all over again. And I must say, i like the prequel trilogy a lot, specially Revenge of the Sith. Yes it reminds of Episode 4, but at the same time it contains the freshness everybody wanted so bad. I must say the only part thou that it hits me was in the cantina scene. (But I admit, the droid carrying the piece and Death Star ok) But just when the opening Crawl goes away and the ship covers all the light on screen, I knew I was in for quite a ride. Poe character is very likable, BB8 is fun, the action is so well done. No overuse of CGI, just the right amount. Isn't that what everybody wanted? Kylo Ren is menacing and powerful, and yes we have character depth in him. His bashing and trashing computers, and not being able to keep it together, was a home run. We see how he struggles. Or do we really needed another Darth Vader?? People tend to complain about his actions, come on guys, if we had another Vader wouldn't all be complaining as well? Kylo Ren has a lot to show in the following Episodes. Finn is a great character with just the right amount of humor in it. I must say I find it strange his abilities with the light-saber, he should be disposed more easily by Kylo and should not have injured him. But in the overall is a great character. Rey is a gem, she is golden, everything about her is perfect, JJ did a great Job on casting Daisy on this one, she has charisma, talent, her acting is great, the way she develops in the force is well done. Many people say it is too fast, but I believe it's well done, she should become much more powerful from now on. Seeing Han and Chewie when they pop in the Falcon, I must say I let a giant smile come out. It was joyful. Harrison Ford carries the movie brilliantly, with his way better approach of Solo displayed on Empire quite the same on this one. Leia was great, and although I thought Carry Fisher would not bring such a great performance, I was wrong, she was very good in it, and her chemistry with Ford was still there. It was a joy to see them together again. I must say seeing Han ***HUGE SPOILER ** die was heartbreaking, but the scene was so well done, very tasteful. Seeing Chewie lost over the death of his friend is heartbreaking. And seeing the falcon cockpit without Han. equally heartbreaking. I admit I could see more of Luke, he was AWESOME, and I must admit I thought he would come for Finn and Rey rescue at the end. But it does not bothered me at all. The hint of Luke, works perfectly. We could only Imagine how Luke will be on Episode VIII. Star Wars is back for those who complain, for me, it never got away. I Like Star Wars very much, even the prequels, they are all great pieces of a wonderful story which everybody loves. Episode VII is a wonderful addition, It has emotion, it has power, comedy, great action, terrific acting. Once again JJ did it. I remember watching this movie in the opening night, and by the first time I hear Kylo Ren speaking I thought in my mind – JJ you certainly did it. !!! I wasn't worried anymore, I knew the movie would deliver up until the end, and it did. I must say tears drop in more than one scene. This movie is a great addition to the SW universe. It is a must see. Go see this in the theaters, don't wait for Blu-ray, it will not be the same. Nothing compares hearing John Williams score and the Star Wars logo exploding in the theaters, this feeling is one of a kind 10/10.

title: Close to perfect
review:
To put it simply, I feel like if this movie was released on its own, without any of the former Star Wars universe in existence, it would have blown people away. It really is that good. But, let's face it, we're all just being so overly critical about every detail of this movie (myself included). So, I'm going to give it the rating it deserves as a stand alone film but the critique it deserves as an epic saga.

The beginning half felt invigoratingly new and was paced beautifully. It actually put me in a wonderful trance-like state. The last half was more nostalgic Star Wars with seemingly faster pacing but still parts that slowed down so you could enjoy them. I did feel like the last few minutes were drawn out a bit much to show that it will be continued- but nothing to complain about.

My only real critique of this beautiful film would be that it could have slowed down a bit. But realistically, I'm sure that would have been an incredibly difficult feat with J.J. trying to get in as much as he was trying to in such a short amount of time.

My wife's main complaint was that there were too many tight and constantly moving camera shots. This makes for a feeling of a lot more action. Now, this could be amazing in some scenarios, but too much is overkill and it becomes slightly unnerving at times.

Some people feel like Kylo was too whiny. I happened to like this and felt it was realistic for his circumstances. He is a young and confused immature kid trying to make very difficult decisions while still trying to figure himself out.

Although I've mainly only mentioned some negative points, this is really a great movie! Not perfect, but art never is. I think I'm more critical of things that are closer to perfection. And this movie is really close.

title: TFA is Marvelous in both Fan Service and Plot
review:
When the credits rolled, my immediate reaction was hell yes! That was a fun mesmerizing, immersion into the most beloved franchise in history. After 12 hours of letting this sink into my nerd IT brain I am ready to throw in my $.02. I have some thoughts on the negative fan reviews that are currently sweeping the galaxy...

1. The haters are gonna hate, no matter what. Period. There is no winning here no matter who/what/how it was done.

2. If Star Wars is your religion, you will not be happy, no one likes it when there idea of canon is wrong and worshipers always hate what God "dictates" to them.

Now that we got that out of the way. I was a 9 yr old boy in 1977 when I saw my first scroll on opening weekend of this movie called Star Wars. My father took me to see it and told me that I was going to love it. He was not only right, I became obsessed over it and it sat high above as my favorite movie as a child. I got all the toys, even the preorder 4 figure set from Kenner that I got for Christmas and had to wait 8 weeks to receive in the mail. Wish I hung on to that one!!

Jump forward 39 years, and I had the privilege of taking my 9 year old son to our local luxury multiplex here complete with reserved seats and cocktails and food to see his first Star Wars movie in the theater. We were not disappointed at all, from the glorious second the music blared and the words Star Wars enveloped the screen to the credits rolling we were both mesmerized and transported to the Star Wars universe.

The movie sets out to refresh and reboot the franchise and the script, plot, and all the trimmings hit the mark on all cylinders. Many are complaining that it is "A New Hope.1" and I can not deny that the formula is there, but isn't that how every Star Wars movie has always worked? " I got a bad feeling about this?" sound familiar? A major character dies? Interesting dysfunctional family twists? That is not Abrams ripping off a New Hope, that is him continuing the Star Wars we all know and love. Don't hate the player, hate the game. This is the grand space opera, the stories and characters all connect. It is a story about good versus evil, morality vs. selfishness and most of all it is about family. It tells us that our family is not just our blood relatives, but those that share our beliefs and faith in goodness through the light side of the force.

Abrams makes an entertaining and marvelous achievement in his treatment of TFA, but more than that, he sets up the storyline that we all knew was coming.....the story of the Post Trilogy has always been the restoration of the light side of the force to return the balance and order to the Galaxy that once existed. It is just not coming so easily as we all might have expected after Episode 6. Luke is the last remaining Jedi Knight and the hope of the galaxy rests on him to restore order by training a new legion of Jedi to maintain balance in the Galaxy. It his destiny....TFA, just gives us a heck of a familiar ride in setting up that inevitable journey to restoring order.....and it does so with all the trimmings, action, humor and twists that every true normal Star Wars fan wants and expects.

They killed it with this movie. It is thick with all kinds of interesting things that happen quickly and that will require many return viewings to get all the chunky detail out of it. This is a triumph to the most beloved franchise in history. Star Wars is back and there are many new stories coming in Rogue Squadron and Young Han Solo that all Star Wars fans should be looking forward to enjoying for years to come!!

Thank you Disney for bringing back Star Wars for us, for our kids and our children's children to enjoy. The hype is real!

P.S. John Williams crushed the soundtrack. Best work he has ever done for the franchise.

title: I liked it more watching it at home
review: I saw this with my son on opening day and again a couple days later, thought it was pretty good, funny, exciting and nostalgic. At the time I would have given it a 7 out of 10 stars but to be honest most of that rating was because it was star wars, I expected a little more in the theaters. I saw the first one when I was 8 years old back in '77 at a little theater on university in Ann Arbor which is now a mall I think. Been a star wars fan ever since. The opening credits are the same; 'a long time ago ...' looks exactly the same, 'Star Wars' with the john williams theme looks exactly the same, a planet with a star destroyer silhouette at first looks like a paper cutout, all of it I expected more. I think that I carried this disappointment for the next couple of hours and it affected my opinion of the movie. Of course I bought the movie the day it came out on DVD, watched all the bonus features and then the movie on blue ray and DVD, it's even playing now as I type this, I really wish there were more bonus features, which is something that I rarely say. Now having seen it several times I give it a solid on it's own 9 out of 10, the extra point is just because it's star wars. The actors are engaging, emotional and complex, much better than the original star wars, even Han Solo is better 'I never ask that question 'till after I've done it' the look on his face is awesome. The main character in this movie carries it better than Luke did, she has a great deal of depth and charisma whereas Luke was more a whiny kid 'but I was going to toshi station to pick up some power converters' even at 8 years old I thought he was whiny. A lot of little things they put in there I was happy for; the sound of the millennium falcon not going into hyper drive, Han Solo being captured (they really should make a figurine with his hands on his head) the look on Chewy's face in the copilots seat near the end of the movie, that they found a role for Simon Pegg, loved Daniel Craig's part and that a couple of star wars nerds had made a droid and they were given a role in the movie. No idea why but I like seeing admiral ackbar. One of my favorite little things was the millennium falcon scraping a piece of metal during the first spaceship fight. Originally I was kind of agreeing with bad reviews that I was reading about all the similarities with the other star wars movies but some of them go a bit too far; there's tie fighters in this movie, there were tie fighters in the others, they talk about the force in this movie ... just shut up and watch it on it's own, it's an awesome movie. The bad guy is full of anger and rage, the heroine is full of hope and promise, that's the only similarity that matters, a fight between the dark side and the light side, that's what all these movies are about and they did a wonderful job at it. It's beautiful, fun and nostalgic.

title: Well, if no one is going to defend this movie from the haters below I guess I will
review:
Apparently the people below me decided to take their pen and clipboards to the theater to judge the movie while they watched it instead of just watching it and enjoying and judging it the second time around. I saw the movie three times and all three were just as equally fun.

The whole story of the movie is Luke Skywalker has gone missing and in his absence a new dark order called the First Order has risen to power spreading fear across the galaxy. A map is found by an old ally of princess, now general, Leia that leads to Luke. She sends Poe, the best pilot of Leia's Resistance, to retrieve the map. But village where Poe meets the ally is ambushed and he captured, but Poe gives the map to his loyal droid BB-8 and sends him far away from the attack as possible. BB-8 meets a scavenger named Rey and a run away storm trooper named Fin. They help BB-8 get back to the Resistance before the First Order gets the map.

While the summary sounds like a kids film the real story revolves around Fin and Rey. I won't go into full detail because the site has a word limit. First special effects were amazing. The blaster fire, the fighter dog fights, all were amazing. I was especially pleased to see the return of organic sets to the franchise after the prequels went full green screen and ruined just about everything. Next, the acting was certainly the best there has ever been in Star Wars. The emotion felt real and the brand new cast that came out of no where did a fantastic job. I bet they spent months getting into character before actual shooting began. The story was really good. A lot of people said that it was "too predictable" and all events were scene from a mile away. Well that's only half true, while some of the events are easily predictable, most of the events that catch you off guard. I.E. Han Solo's death. The thing I love most about this movie is how it leaves you with unanswered questions. This may confuse you but I love that they left you wondering what next. I really appreciate that feel from a franchise that isn't based on anything from a book or a comic. It leaves you with endless possibilities for world building. As a writer I really love this.

Overall I really enjoyed the movie and I think that the people below are just the people that don't know how to enjoy a good movie. This isn't a remake, it isn't a knock off, this is the next episode in the series. 32 years of waiting have finally paid off.

One last note: to the people who a trashing JJ, I hope you realize that he is just as big of a Star Wars fan as y'all. He may not have met any of your expectations but he has made the expectations of 8.4 stars worth of fans. Enjoy the being in the minority.

title: Thank you Lucas for selling SW to Disney...The Force Awakens = Awesome!
review:
Can't believe how good this was. Disney did a great job keeping to the original appeal and premise of the original. OK, learning how to fly a spaceship or use a lightsaber on the first try is a little hokey, but who cares?! They incorporated the old cast in brilliantly. The new ships and technology are awesome despite their Star Wars-ish impossibility.

And most importantly, they created such a good story and did it without the venerable Lucas...oh thank god considering how bad I, II & III were. But all was not lost thanks to Disney. I thought the waiting for VII was tough...now the waiting for VIII is unbearable already. So good the Force Awakens was!

title: Revisited the movie for Rise of Skywalker
review:
I started watching the sequel trilogy again so I could go watch rise of Skywalker with good knowledge of the story. So onto my thoughts about the movie.

This movie Is just boring.I can't find any other word for it. It's not a bad movie, but it's not a good one either. Some of it's characters, like Finn and Kylo, are pretty compelling. But some, like Rey, are completely boring and uninteresting to watch.

The movie uses a lot of nostalgia to get old fans hooked without making much sense. Also the dialogue and the acting can be infuriatingly idiotic at times. And after the 3rd act the movie just goes full Disney, meaning that It uses stupid jokes at every chance they get.

Overall, a mildly entertaining movie. As I said, not bad, not good.

title: Not exactly a sequel when it's so familiar to a new hope.
review:
Check out my reviews at http://moviereviews51.wordpress.com

When I heard that Disney had bought the rights to the Star Wars franchise and there were plans for episode 7,8 and 9 I was disappointed, I mean lets all remember the disappointment we felt when George Lucas made episodes 1-3. If there was anything to make those films bad it was the introduction of Jar Jar Binks, then again George Lucas did need to create someone dim witted for the Senator Palpatine to trick into giving him all the powers of the senate to create the First Galactic Empire, anyway I'm getting off topic I do just like a rant about that bloody Jar Jar Binks. I was disappointed about the decision to make 7,8 and 9 until I learned that JJ Abrams was on board for episode 7, we have all seen what he done with the Star Trek reboot.

Star Wars: The Force Awakens did tend to disappoint though, it was more of a reboot of A New Hope than it was a sequel, there were just too many similarities, for example the star destroyer that was just a bigger version of the death star, a robot with something both sides want, storm troopers searching a village and killing everyone, Kylo Ren being similar to Vader. I was disappointed with the story line that could have been so much better if it didn't go so similar to A New Hope, one thing that could have made it better was maybe mentioning that Jar Jar Binks was no longer with us just to make sure he doesn't make an appearance.

Having said I was disappointed with the story line I did still enjoy the film, it revolves around finding Luke Skywalker who hasn't been seen since one of his apprentices turned bad and killed all his Padawan learners, and blaming himself he left, there is a map that leads to him though and that's where the movie begins. A young pilot Po Dameron (Oscar Issac) receives the map from an old man on a settlement village, which then gets invaded by storm troopers, Po gives the map to his trusted sidekick BB-8, (who everyone seems to love, my fiancé included), Storm troopers destroy his ship and BB-8 escapes, this is when Kylo makes his first appearance, having not found the map he orders the whole village murdered and takes Po. Only one of the storm troopers doesn't follow orders.

Kylo Ren gets the information out of Po regarding the droid and then comes the storm trooper Fin to rescue him, similarities to episode 4.

Now its time to introduce Rey (Daisey Ridley), a scavenger who is good with droids and mechanical parts and can fly a ship (Anakin and Luke), she rescues BB-8 who has been taken by another scavenger and she takes him with her, the droid carrying vital information on the whereabouts of Luke Skywalker, again similarities to episode 4.

The First Order, the new version of the empire, are looking for the droid and send storm troopers down after it only to fail, Rey gets into a little bother with people trying to steal the droid, she manages to fight them off then the droid notices Fin wearing Po Damersons jacket, which he took after there ship crashed and he is presumed dead, after a brief talk they are chased by storm troopers and they manage to escape on an all too familiar ship.

They escape on the ship only to be captured by the ships original owner, the one and only Han Solo and they become friends, as expected though everything eventually goes wrong and Rey is captured, not before she has an encounter with Luke and Anakins lightsaber and has a vision. The rescue is on to save Reay and destroy the Star Destroyer, having got BB-8 back to the rebellions camp they find out the map is incomplete, no shock there.

With a plan to destroy the Star destroyer and save Rey, Han Chewbacca and Fin set off, Rey on the other hand is being tortured by Kylo Ren, who is getting nowhere as she can use the force without any training necessary. She manages to escape by using mind control on a storm trooper and eventually bump into Han, Fin and Chewy. For anyone who hasn't seen this I wont say what happens next but as you would expect the Star Destroyer is destroyed.

Once it is all over we find out that R2D2 has the missing piece of the map and Rey sets off to find Luke, we do get to see Luke and all I can hope for in the next film is, I hope he isn't still a whiney little brat as he does look like an impressive Jedi Master, maybe he will take after the comics and be Grand Master Jedi.

Now to look forward to Rogue One when it comes out.

title: Recycled plot
review:
This movie feels like a remake of a previous episode. The development in the abilities of the protagonist happens way, way too quickly for my taste and it leaves me with the impression that the galaxy is safe even though there are still two more movies left.

There are lots of humorous elements that play nicely with the atmosphere of the movie. There are many references to the previous episodes, so I can definitely recommend re-watching these if its been long since your last viewing.

I did find it enjoyable and easy to watch, regardless of the (in my opinion) recycled plot, but it is nowhere near the 8.6 rating it is currently sitting on.

title: Good, not great
review:
The movie is entertaining and occasionally funny, the action sequences and special effects are great, but the plot is convoluted, shallow and forgettable. Is it just me or does it appear that movies have evolved into just one long mishmash of action and explosions punctuated only by brief periods of meaningless dialog?

Not that the original Star Wars trilogy was a work of deep philosophy, but they had structure to their plot, and more gravitas overall.

What I find particularly disappointing is the shallowness of the evil characters in this movie. They just completely lack the depth of someone like Darth Vader, in particular Adam Driver (Kylo Ren) to me just comes across as a mediocre actor. I found Domhnall Gleeson (as General Hux) much more convincing in his role.

Daisy Ridley (as Rey) also offered a lackluster performance, a whole league below of what you would hope for in a big production like this.

title: Media Res Redux
review:
So this movie starts out just like the original - media res.

We get the middle first.

If you ever watched an episode of Alias - you know this is JJ's favorite plot device.

And then there is Lucas' own decision to begin with Episode IV.

With 30 years of in-between, my bet is number eight will not be a carbon copy of TESB but a major series of flashbacks telling the untold stories of Han and Leia, Luke, and how C3P-O has a red arm.

It remains obvious that a significant contribution to this film was the research and mining of the original for subtleties which made it so endearing - (incredible scale of ships - throwaway appearances of nocturnal creatures - the little empire bot that zips around the floor) these I personally appreciate and do not scorn.

Thank you all for not spoiling the plot points until my own viewing with family - more surprised that I did not know what would happen than with what did happen.

Haters gotta hate - and lovers are blind.

If you really want to get excited - bring back the Cooper and true 70 MM.

With all the other indulgences we afford ourselves, why can't we have a great theater anymore?

It was good yarn and at times comfort food - did miss the 20th Century theme but even I can add that later.

Expecting to retire around Episode 12 or so - which should be about half way through the franchise.

Media Res Redux

title: Beautiful and stunning visuals accompanied by a pretty average script
review: I have been waiting to write this review since around 2012 when it was announced to the public that LucusFilm had been sold to Disney and that a Star Wars new movie was going to come out in 2015. So as soon as I could, I hopped into the next open IMAX Theater (which was at 530 in the morning) and saw the film. The movie was pretty much what I expected it would be. The visuals were stunning and crisp. The editing flowed together with the movie very beautifully, so did the sound mixing and editing. The acting was great. The movie was shot in real JJ Abrahams fashion with a lot of lens flares and unique camera angles. The cinematography was stunning as well. Daniel Mindel, who also did the cinematography on Star Trek, did a very good job at setting up shots that capture how well the visuals team revitalized the beautiful landscapes from the previous films. This was a very good remake of the old films and I really think the cast really revitalized the Star Wars franchise. However, I didn't expect it to be perfect and it wasn't. Most of the issues I had with this film, surprisingly, had to do with the writing. The way this film was written was like it was pretty much just a remake of the original movies. Within a couple of minutes into the movie, it started to become obvious that JJ was playing it safe with this movie. I would say that the overall tone of the movie was "Hey, remember this? How about this? This was really cool right? This is a Star Wars movie!!" While it's not bad enough to ruin it as a stand- alone movie, it is enough to call it unoriginal and unimaginative. I wouldn't argue with anyone who had that opinion of it. However, I also wouldn't argue with anyone who says that this is a well a great remake. Overall, my feelings about the movie were pretty mixed. While, it isn't as bad as the prequels, it also isn't as creative and visceral enough to compete with the original movies. It doesn't seem that JJ even wanted to do that though. It seems that he caught a bad case of 'fanboy' when he started working with Ford, Hamill, and Fisher. Also I blame Lawrence Kasden a bit for not going "Ok, we need to come up with something new for this movie. The new characters have to be memorable and engaging. The plot shouldn't copycat the movie me and Lucas wrote in 77'. We should take out the scene where they hide under the floorboards of the Millennium Falcon and every other scene that has that kind of unoriginal feel to it. Let's move forward not backward." But to be honest. I don't there is too much to complain about. It actually felt good to visit those places over again. I don't think that a lot of other audience members mind it either. It wasn't the most revolutionary piece of art to hit the screen. As a matter of fact I would say that the script was pretty average. It just felt like it was another fan remake that has been done a billion times. However, it does get the job done. It isn't a huge disappointment and anyone that thinks so should keep in mind that it was marketed and built-up for more than two years. The expectations for a lot of people shot through the roof. If the anticipation for a movie matched its quality, then 50 shades of Grey would have been the next Casablanca. I give this movie a decent 8/10.
