title: Best Star Wars since Empire, welcome back Lawrence Kasden and thank you JJ Abrams.
review:
It was worth the wait, that's the first thing I'll say about STAR WARS: THE FORCE AWAKENS, the very highly anticipated sequel to the original trilogy. J.J. Abrams and Lawrence Kasden clearly have dug deep and come up with a story that logically continues the STAR WARS saga into a new generation, one that brings back iconic figures beloved by millions of fans, while at the same time, introducing new characters with whom the audience can fall in love. Those who say this is the best STAR WARS film since EMPIRE are right on point, if for no other reason than there is not a hide nor hair nor scale of an Ewok or Jar Jar Binks to be seen. In short, there is none of George Lucas's ill-conceived attempts at being cute.

The thing, which makes this STAR WARS ring so true, is the way Abrams and Kasden remind us that at its heart, STAR WARS is only a space opera, but also the story of a most dysfunctional family. The original trilogy centered on a father who had turned to dark side and opposed by his children who followed the light; FORCE AWAKENS simply reverses the dynamic, where now we have two good parents who must try to save a son seduced by the Dark Side. They make it very plain that there was no truly happy ending after the final scene in JEDHI.

Another thing I loved about THE FORCE AWAKENS is the way it truly brings back the STAR WARS universe, a place that was often dirty and very lived in, filled with vivid and distinctive creatures and worlds that were not always what they appeared to be to the viewer. We see crashed and derelict Imperial cruisers and Walkers, the remains of battles past and an implication that war is a constant in this place. The Millennium Falcon is discovered in a junk yard after being stolen by smugglers years before.

One of THE FORCE AWAKENS great strengths is the way so many of it's scenes are clear echoes of what has come before: Obi-Wan and Darth Vader's final encounter, the cantina on Mos Eisley, the medal awards at the finale of the first movie, are among the very many that are not just simply recalled, but are improved upon in ways that will hit with a deep emotional wallop for many fans. I'm so glad I made a point of not hearing about any of the numerous plot twists and revelations in the script; also happy Abrams and company did not try and explain everything by the final scene, which actually raises many questions and sets up the fan anticipation for the next movie.

Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher and Mark Hamill are back as Han Solo, Princess-now General-Leia, and Luke Skywalker; so is Chewbacca, C-3PO, R2D2 and host of other familiar faces, even Admiral Akbar turns up and gets to say a few more lines this time besides, "It's a trap." The new faces belong to Daisy Ridley, John Boyega and Oscar Isaac as characters who blend seamlessly with the old pros; Boyega's Finn, a deserter from the Imperial Storm Troopers, is the everyman through whom the audience sees the action and intrigue unfold. Ridley's Rey is the best kind of heroine, resourceful and brave despite the fact that she's terrified to be confronting the worst evil in the galaxy. That evil being personified by Adam Driver's Kylo Ren, a disciple of Darth Vader and follower of the Dark Side; truth told, Driver's Ren is my favorite character in the movie, but I'm a sucker for a good bad guy and Ren is a character with so many interesting possibilities. Domhall Gleeson, Gwendoline Christie and Andy Serkis round out the formidable villains whom we will be seeing much of in future films. And Max Von Sydow shows up, not looking that much older than when he played Father Merrin in THE EXORCIST all those years ago. J.J. Abrams is the George Lucas for whom we have been waiting, especially after the original proved he simply didn't have anything more to offer; he, with the help of many others, have revitalized the most beloved franchise in the history of movies and given it new life in the 21st Century. We are home indeed.

title: Appeal for Justice for Non-Jedis and Ordinary people
review:
The creators of the story should have done a little more justice to the character of Han Solo. As I could see Han Solo had a very troubled life. Most part of his life was spent in fighting. To me he seems to be the real hero of the story rather than the great Jedi's or Dark warriors. Didn't he deserve a better ending. He was an ordinary man. He never seemed to get the treatment he deserved from his wife. But that's OK most relationships in real life are like that. No father should ever have to die by their son's hand especially when he loves his child. Han Solo was never strong with the force although he had witnessed its usage and power. He didn't even know the way to come back from dead. Like the great Jedis Anakin, Obiwan, and Yoda. They had found a path to commune with the living men and disciples even after their death.

And what about Padme why couldn't she come back? What about all the uniformed and un-uniformed army, the resistance, first order and earlier the soldiers of the empire. They were all ordinary people. They didn't know what dark or light was. They were all just following orders like everyone does until they realize. Doesn't each member of the white armored men and women deserve to loose their disguise and know their individuality and uniqueness like Finn did?

And what is this gross escapism and cowardliness about the great good Jedis who always escape when faced with the dark. Yoda, Obiwan and now Luke escaped from the dark when faced with it with an explanation that they are trying to find strength. Is it wise to just escape and go into exile when faced with hard reality and abuse of power. You might say its all just fiction but Star Wars for me is serious stuff. Its how I understand life. There is no light, There is no dark side, All force is one. May the force be with you guys.

title: It's plot lacks originality but the characters are magnificent
review:
The new Star Wars movie continues reboots the Star Wars universe, but at some cost.

The plot, which is the weakest since the Star Wars Episode I, is badly executed imitation of A New Hope. A heroic figure who was abandoned by his/her parents in a deserted planet, who is unaware of his secret powers which he/she later uses to destroy a super weapon which can destroy planets. Sounds familiar? It almost seems that the producers were playing it safe, using an equation that has entertained fans a decade ago.

But, there is a but in this movie. The characters presented in the movie could be my newly favorites in the Star Wars universe. Compared to the original trilogy, these characters are more "human" and complex. I love how they present Kylo Ren as an individual struggling with his sense of self, not knowing his true position in the force. I can wait how this character will evolve in the following movies.

To conclude, The Force Awakens is a gutless movie (in the sense of plot) which introduces amazing characters that will be superior in the following films.

title: The old hope reawakens
review:
I will not say the movie was bad, it wasn't, it fulfilled its purpose, it kept me interested in what I was watching

So, had this been a standalone movie, it would've scored 8 to me But it wasn't, it's a sequel to a longstanding franchise Unfortunately, a sequel that feels more like a retelling of Episode IV. Is that what they were really gunning for? Because it is a retelling. Maybe they thought it worked all those decades ago, just tweak the same story and it might work again

Only now is not even half as captivating, nor does it have a truly menacing, commanding villain, do you remember someone mocking Darth Maul? Whiny Kylo Ren is taunted like thrice in this movie and almost equaled by the janitor stormtrooper

You again have a droid with a hidden message, sent to an arid planet to be located by a loner with no family to keep her in Only difference now is that she never had a family to begin with, didn't lose it to stormtroopers, so she didn't cry before she left, big deal

Then, again, you have the couple of heroes on the run who are saved by Han and Chewbacca and granted flight, in the Millennium Falcon, into a supposedly secure location Only difference now is... nope, no difference at all, same stuff, just older Han and Chewbacca, further broken down MF and new pair of heroes

You witness the destruction of life by the Starkiller Base only differences between the Death Star is that this base is bigger, wow, and can destroy planets, not just a planet, from one shot Fantastic, guess they didn't want to get their hands tired from having to pull the switch more than once

Same base, only bigger, same weakness you contemplate how they carry out the same plan to bring about its destruction, probably devised from a napkin Leia produced with base- destroying notes taken over 30 years ago, did you gobble up your popcorn in excitement at this point?

And finally... once again you see the death of a beloved character by lightsaber, only difference now is that the character that cries "No!" this time after the killing blow is Chewbacca, in a language you can't understand

Not a remake, just a retelling Despite how criticized the prequels were, at least they told an original story This one is just... there

But also... no medals for the remaining heroes at the end? Damn Just place one over comatose Finn, old Han's or at least a pin or something, some appreciation

Jaime A. De la Garza

title: Room For Improvement
review: There seems to be a lot of negative, low rated reviews which are unfair and unjustified in my opinion. People focus only on the plot similarities of this films predecessors. They expect too much from a franchise which is desperately wanted. If you don't enjoy or appreciate the efforts to bring it back, it's very simple; don't go to see the next one! I know i will be going! We know history can repeat itself and the same logic applies to this story. Yes there's a lot of episode IV in here, but its ironic to love that plot, yet hate this one. The inspiration of The Empire is exactly what determined this. They could have brought some new ideas, but i think they're saving them for the next one. This was a good film. The quality of filming, special effects, music, editing and character development: all excellent. The casting was pretty good although Driver(Kylo Ren) just doesn't have that villainous feel to him and looks young for the role despite being 32. May sound harsh but he's too pale and skinny for me, he also needs a haircut. Too late to change now i suppose, maybe some Sith eyes would up his scare-factor. Abrams did disappoint me with the predictable death of Solo, and his inclusion of Leia was weak. Some parts did feel rushed and i thought they could've maybe dragged it out. Its more about the story for me and not all the action. They'll find it hard to make a good Star Wars film without Solo as his character just brings so much to the film, but i have faith in this team. People seem to have trouble with Ren being beaten by Rey so easily. Maybe you didn't notice his abdominal injury sustained by Chewies' crossbow blaster... however i do agree he was pretty weak and unconvincing. Struggling against a Stormtrooper in a lightsaber battle, It was not mentioned whether he's a Sith lord or not, but surely has training to that of at least a Jedi knight from Luke. Cannot vouch for Snoke as i have no idea of his understanding or teaching of the dark side. I have a suspicion about who he is though, won't say just in case i am correct. I am a big fan of Star Wars, even Episodes I, II and III. I read character bios and invest time and interest into understand the thoughts of Lucas and what he was trying to achieve, i'd like to think i know what i'm talking about when it comes to Star Wars. Hopefully they can make Ren more of a threat and beef up the plot to make the next one satisfying for all. They don't have to cram it all into one film, they should take their time and deliver what i suspect will be Reys training by Luke, Rens training by Snoke and the revival of the battle for balance of the force which the whole story has ultimately been about. By all means, demand more from Disney and Abrams, they can only get better with criticism, but remember credit where credit is due. Have faith, fear is a path to the dark side.

title: The force Awakens did what it had set out to do (MEGA Spoiler Alert!!)
review:
There seems to be a polarizing consensus on IMDb regarding Star Wars the Force Awakens. One one hand, we have the average rating of 8.6 based of 262,316 reviews this far (28/12/2015). On the other hand we have IMDb's own users mostly writing reviews where they are negatively criticizing the film's overall tone, targeted age group, story-line decisions and the borrowed story elements from IV. In this review I would like counter the in my opinion unfair criticism to bring balance back to the force on IMDb, this film deserves it.

The film-crew of this film had one mission: Maintain the great things about what made the old Star Wars movies great( IV-VI ) so the old fans would love it, while also introducing enough new elements to a new generation of fans. I have to admit that they took a risk by widening the target audience, making the characters emotions and dialogue not as complex or philosophical as the complex philosophical viewers would like. But one has to remember that this film is the first part of a trilogy. They wanted to show the old characters and old elements, but also new planets and locations and enough new interesting characters that will star in the next two films. I believe this leaves little room for complex explanations and refined character emotions. But again, this is not the job of the first film in the trilogy. The interest of the viewer needs to be grabbed, and enough questions need to be raised so you want to see the second movie immediately after viewing the first one. This film does this so well, that I bet you that Star Wars will have a fan-base of a size like never before.

Rey is the mystery girl of this film. Old force tricks are simply not as hard to learn for the new chosen one, as they were for Anakin or Luke. The spirit of the Light-side(good) versus the Dark-side(bad) is explained very well in this film. Maz (Yoda's spiritual successor) does most of the explaining, when she holds dialogue with Rey. The physical light is also used symbolically. When the last light of the sun being absorbed disappears on both Han and Ben, leaving them into physical darkness, the Ben whom wanted to side with Han then struggles with his emotions once more and turns into Kylo once more. This is the perfect example of how the force is symbolically linked to the physical realm. While the dialogue might seem simplified, there are enough little moments that need to be puzzled together in order for them to be fully understood. How does the movie does this? This film has many, many perspectives and fast scenes, and it is a challenge to keep up with the fast editing sometimes. This makes this film highly re-watchable for a second or even a third time, like I did.

The Millennium-Falcon is introduced as a piece of junk but boy can she still fly. The chase sequences in the Falcon have extraordinary camera movements and are choreographed excellently by the VFX artists. The other aerial scenes are incredibly well animated and all have memorable perspectives (like the killing spree Poe went on in a 20 second shootout). Boy that's one helluva good Pilot, Finn screams. I also want to salute the VFX team for creating authentic looking VFX that are as artistic as visually stunning. This movie has many, many little iconic star wars perspectives and moments. From the camera pans, to the background activity of characters, to general screenplay moments which all scream positive Nostalgia. The old cast are individually revealed, and these moments are spread out enough throughout the film, so the new characters get enough time to be developed as additional new main characters.

Lastly, the acting is phenomenal. There is something to love about all the new main characters. Finn and Poe for their strong willpower, high energy and comical moments. Rey for her mysteriousness and her epic ability to learn new skill-sets. Maz for her calming deep emotion(she did need more screen time though, just like Phasma). Kylo for his frightening dark side acts(excellent sound design with his force actions by the way, just amazing) yet the conflicted state he portrays without his helmet(great facial expression from Adam Diver). General Hux is also interesting as he and Kylo rival each other with their dark choices, and the speech Hux delivers before all the stormtroopers is every bit as epic as it can be. BB8 is my favorite new Droid. It is truly a main character as it is presented in all scenes, at all times(where it is present) and makes this film all the more perfect for all age-groups. My mother was laughing throughout this film because of the droid. All the other characters with minor appearances all carry the Star Wars theme people have come to love of the previous films. The acting is always delivered passionately while still being realistic. This is not the perfect film for everyone, but is a fantastic film for anyone, if you allow it to be. My favorite films mostly consist out of deep films like Waking Life, The Prestige, Mr. Nobody and the Tree of life for example, but the complex viewer should not watch this film to fuel all their philosophical needs like those movies did. And the hardcore Star Wars fans decoding the story elements, have to come to terms with the fact that this is a new Star Wars Trilogy with many new elements to the force and to the universe of Star Wars that have yet to be introduced in the upcoming two films. Let go of what this film not is, because it is exactly the film it should be. THIS IS Star Wars at its best. This is the fantasy film from a galaxy long ago and far far a way that both the old and new fans deserve. The force has been Awoken.

title: Possible Improvements on a Already Good Movie Plus a Fix for the Basic Big Boom at the End
review:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens (2015): After reading others reviews I will not nitpick the minor plot holes or praise TFA's many good points which would repeat what most have already covered. I enjoyed the movie and was pleasantly surprised that it was not the anticipated Abram's reboot that overlooks canon but is a story that fits nicely as chapter VII in the SW saga. I will however, IMHO, do an improved but moot rewrite of the Starkiller's (SK) destruction scene to avoid Star War's threadbare "big bada boom".

As the Republic fleet hammers the SK's shields and move asteroids and bombs between the SK and the sun to impede charging the weapon, the Millennium Falcon jumps under the SK's shields and lands as close as possible to the command bridge to stop the weapon from firing. A squad of 30 commandos along with expected main characters unloads and gets trapped outside the command bridge following Finn's plan ("It's not my fault" Finn says). In the MF, Chewbacca opens fire on the command bridge surprising everyone. Finn having worked sanitation and guarding engineering work crews recalls that the Techno Union have their own nearby control room to test the SK's systems and is accessible. Captain Phasma is captured accidentally by Finn and used to gain access to the engineering control room ("I don't know, I'm making it up as I go along", says Finn). In the control room they cannot stop the weapon firing but using resistant Techno Union workers, CP3O, R2D2, or BB-8, to trigger a simple plasma containment field calibration program. The program quickly cycles through hundreds of containment fields used deep within the SK to contain plasma. Since the SK is now full of plasma from the sun when charged, the containment field calibration causes multiple plasma leaks which slowly eats away at the inside guts of the SK. The incredulous command bridge soon realizes that they are now sitting on a small sun and will fry long before they can fire at the targeted Republic sun. After quick arguments, General Hux misfires the weapon and vents any remaining plasma out the ports thus saving their lives but the SK is now an unstable smoldering husk (no big boom). Captain Phasma is dumped down a garbage chute, Kylo Ren hacks his way into the control room just as everyone runs away. Lots of fighting and heroes dying getting off the SK as the Republic fighters swoop in to deliver the coup de grace. Kylo Ren is shocked/chuckles/irate when he receives injuries (i.e. losing toes by a dropped lightsaber) from people who do not know which end of a lightsaber to hold (AKA never fight an amateur). After the battle General Hux receives a message from the departing Techno Union congratulating Hux on turning their SK into scrap. Then the banking clan calls to confirm what the Techno Union wrote and Hux is called to an update meeting with Supreme Leader Snoke about his shiny new toy. A new base commander is quickly promoted (Hux dies) or Hux becomes the SK's permanent decommission officer for life. A reeking Captain Phasma is recovered from the rubbish bin and escorted for questioning and joins Hux's fate.30 years later the misfired beam hits another galaxy and they respond.

Watched TFA some more and a nice twist would have the First Order being anti-religion anti-force (after both Jedi and most Sith) because of the death toll of the "ants" during the Force wars.

title: Underwhelming, but competent, Star Wars sequel.
review:
I would argue that 'The Force Awakens' has been the most highly anticipated, and therefore hardest to make, Star Wars movie thus far.

With so much riding on the success of the movie, bringing back estranged fans etc, JJ played it safe in a number of ways. The movie is filled with visual references to the original trilogy, essentially fan service, and it shares a story line almost identical to A New Hope. The latter isn't necessarily bad, unlike the prequels we understand the villain's motivation & goals, we are given a clear idea of the events that will take place in movie, and we have a clear main character. We are also given likable characters, in particular Poe and Finn, and intriguing villains, Kylo Ren + Snoke. Also the film is incredibly fast paced, and when watching the movie for the first time i was never bored or distracted.

However, by having the film share so many similarities to the original trilogy & A New Hope, it is slightly underwhelming and lacks a true amount of new ideas (vital for this new trilogy to be good). Snoke is a carbon copy of the emperor at this point, The First Order is essentially the empire and the back story in regards to the new republic is quite vague. The Starkiller base too was essentially a death star, and i was taken aback by lack of a twist or surprise in regards to it.

Overall the movie is competent, the plot holes are few and less detrimental to the story (not at all akin to episode 2 for instance, and the strange/illogical assassination choices made on Padme). I would struggle to find anybody who goes into this movie and doesn't enjoy it, however it does little to embellish the mythos and universe the film is set in. Perhaps JJ played it too safe.

title: Good but not great
review:
The main issue with Force Awakens is the storyline. It's a reboot of Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi. It doesn't continue the storyline but instead reverts it back to bring Harrison Ford's dream of Han's death to fruition. Ford so desperate for Han Solo to die lacks the vision to see how it destroys the franchise and characters established in the originals.

I consider this a clear reboot attempt, though I'm curious as to why. Almost everyone enjoyed the original 3 films and the story elements involved. The idea of re-structuring it makes no sense as it just creates more work.

The sad fact is Han, Luke and Leia are far to out of character to relate with so we're left wondering what happened to cause such absurd rifts in their relationships. Luke would never have become a mind-numbing hermit fleeing to the outer reaches of space, he'd already met the greatest challenge ever by facing Vader. Han's son though special is not more important than his own father was, so betrayal by him wouldn't have been so devastating. We also should expect Luke was prepared by then for any of his students turning to the darkside of the force, there is no logic involved with Luke's actions.

Han would not be so stupid as to approach his son and fall for a trap such as we see here. Yes it's his kid but also a murdering psychopath which Han knows full well if it drove Luke to flee. Also killing him off was done SOLELY because Ford asked (again) or from some nostalgia JJ Abrams had in wanting to follow his previous wishes.

Leia would not have been so stand offish with Han, no way. She acted like a complete wall of stone, no love or passion. Far from the original character we came to know.

Over-all this film is entertaining, worthy of an 8/10 but absolutely not a sequel or improvement on any of the films before it, including the prequels. I am 100% confident anyone that's a true fan could've written a more compelling story than what this turned out to be, maybe Disney should've had an online submission process for fresh ideas.

title: The force is strong with this one
review: Episode VII picked up where Episode VI left off (pretty obvious :D) and it is like 20-30 years ago after the original trilogy. I was surprised that this movie did not rely much on CGI, but instead JJ Abrams relied mostly on practical effects which is awesome. Now to the characters: the original characters have returned like Leia, Han, and Chewbacca. Among them, Han pretty much changed. He is still cocky, yes, but he has matured since the original trilogy. Leia, well, she is a general now ha! (Not a surprised though) And Chewie is still the same. The characters are also good. John Boyega's Finn is likable and there is also Daisy Ridley's Rey. The two have great chemistry despite the fact that they are both unknown actors. Then there comes Oscar Isaac's Poe Dameron. He is like the best big brother you never had. Kylo Ren is the most bad-ass of the cast and he is the villain. Wew. Judging the from the trailers alone, it looked like he was gonna be another Vader but surprised to say that he is not. He is more human than you think. And then there the dick space Nazi and other characters that I'm not gonna reveal because SPOILERS! The soundtrack and the sound effects will give you goosebumps because it's too nostalgic! grin emoticon The only gripe I have about this movie is the story and some elements of it. This film feels exactly like the original which is a plus and not.There are scenes that you know will happen because I feel it was copied from the original. Just wait and listen to Han's joke about the Death Star- like system.

title: Better the second time
review:
I must admit that I was a bit disappointed when I first went to the cinema but I went again today and liked it more than I thought.

OK so the story isn't exactly original but the special effects are really something and the acting seemed more believable the second time. I thing it is probably because I was so intend on wanting the story to work the first time that I didn't really give it a proper chance. For all those saying, Lucas come back all is forgiven are talking nonsense! I watched a bit of the phantom menace this weekend and it's simply terrible! Truly awful! The effects are like a poor computer game and the characters are soulless and annoying.

While this film is a long long way off the originals, it was always going to be. I enjoyed it, thought it funny in parts and loved the effects, especially on the iMax 3D.

Give it a chance and don't compare it to the originals and I think you will like it more. M

Solid 8/10 for me. Has the falcon and X-wings in so what's not to like.

title: People Need To Lighten Up. It Wasn't Great, but it was Fun.
review:
I am old enough to have seen every Star Wars film in their original runs and have been a fan of the franchise from the beginning. Seems like everyone wants to be a professional movie critic these days. I read reviews where people just want to complain at a level that tells more about how unhappy they are rather than taking a movie for what it it. Then you have the movie studio shills writing ridiculously positive reviews that makes this film comparable to Citizen Cane. Finally you have the hard-core fans that will not complain about this film under any condition. My message is simple...Lighten Up.

I took my 9 year old to see his first major Star Wars film in a theater for the first time that he will remember and spend as much time observing the movie from a child's perspective rather than a cynical adults that spends as much time looking for the flaws than enjoying the ride. My son cheered when the good guys prevailed, cried when Han Solo died and has spent the last several days speaking of the film.

As Yoda said: "Truly wonderful the mind of a child is."

Now from the cynical adults perspective: It wasn't perfect. This was certainly a "Passing of the torch" movie where you have to deal with the aging original cast while incorporating the new cast of characters. I knew this was going to be troublesome giving ample screen time to everyone. To be honest, the way Carrie Fisher and Harrison Ford have aged, they can no longer carry a Star Wars and sell the sizzle like they used to. Father time has caught them.

I didn't have much of a problem re-treading some of the original concepts, but the film certainly went too far. The new Death Star plot was weak. The film did not need another "Ultimate Weapon". The Villains were not particularly meaning. I would call them almost comical. You will have a hard time finding a kind word about Kylo Ren. My biggest disappointment was they made this weenie to be the offspring of Han Solo/Leia and of course the grandson of Anakin Skywalker. I would have preferred this character to have been a non-related Jedi recruit that went rogue rather than a descendant of Skywalker.

Although the new 3 main actors were obviously cast by race, sex and national origin I must say I liked them and they had really good chemistry.

I am going to take the perspective that after ROTJ, the Sith and the Jedi were pretty much wiped out and were are not catching them at their prime. I am hoping the next film cleans up some of the plot shortcomings.

For now, enjoy the ride.

title: It may be a reboot, but it's a joyously enjoyable one
review:
The new Star Wars film must be good - only one person got their phone out during the entire running time!

Definitely a hit, SWTFA has a joyous, celebratory feel and it's a delight to see Han Solo (or Hun Solo as most people seem to call him now) et al on the big screen again. The 3D IMAX looks and sounds fantastic (a full screen shot of a Star Destroyer in particular is awesome), the John Williams score as iconic as ever, the new characters are great and the story zips along. JJ Abrams has done a superb job bearing in mind the weight of expectation and the need to match the tone to the classic trilogy.

The film is virtually a reboot in places. So much is the same as episodes IV-VI, including Stormtrooper armour that still can't protect the wearer from anything other than a light slap, and inexplicably noisy ships in the vacuum of space. A few minor changes include the fact that even small craft like the X-Wing apparently now come fitted with hyperspace drives. Well, this is set 30 or so years after ROTJ I suppose. I think JJ was wise to use so much of the iconography to be fair, it's what people were expecting. There should be a lot more scope in the subsequent instalments to break away from the template a bit more, and they ought to be even better films as a result.

Another great decision was the one to use physical sets so much; it makes the movie so much more solid and believable than episodes I-III. Hopefully this starts a trend that other blockbusters follow. There were still plenty of visual effects shots of course, but they were seamless apart from the big hologram geezer that looked like a cross between Thanos and Bill Nighy.

The script is a lot more human than probably any of the other episodes and the humour hits far more than it misses. My only slight criticism of it is that multiple characters deliver the same brand of dry wisecracks, making it too obvious they'd all come from the pen of the same writer.

Talking of criticisms, I only have a few:

  • I craved a little more backstory to understand the main character's motivations and mindsets - but at least I cared.


  • The plot is enjoyable and contains some mystery, but is ultimately lacking real drive or tension compared to the very best sci-fi. We're essentially just along for the ride.


  • Apparently everyone can just pick up a lightsaber now and kick butt straight away. Really?


The other little niggle was that despite certain grown men claiming otherwise, these are essentially family films and aimed at kids of all ages from about 8 to 108. So for the sake of cutting a couple of seconds of injury detail, why press ahead with a version of the film that needed a 12 certificate?

What a relief though hey? Far from being a disappointment, Star Wars: The Force Awakens is a triumphant must-see, and the wait for Episode VIII is already way too long!

title: Saved by good new actors and good technical execution
review:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens is one of the better movies of 2015... as a standalone film. I can imagine people seeing Star Wars for the first time, really liking this one and developing an itch to see more of the Star Wars universe.

The sad part comes when you realize why the movie probably does that to new viewers: this is a reboot of Star Wars IV. They took 0 risk of making the mistake that the prequels made and that in itself was another mistake. If I had shown this movie in class, I would have gotten a 0 out of 10 and a punishment for plagiarism. It's not even hidden well! As soon as I realized that I had seen it all before, it started to annoy me.

There are positives as well. The movie is visually stunning, the villain is written really well and every new character has an amazing actor/actress in support. The fun of the movie is (for me) in its details: humour, the way certain scenes are filmed... and it would deserve more like an 8 or 9 out of 10 were it not for the recycled story.

In short: visually stunning, great new actors/actress, incredibly well directed, but lacks originality in it's story and tries to purely rely on nostalgic feelings of old fans and the amazement of new, younger fans.

title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens Review
review:
After watching Star Wars: The Force Awakens I feel like it had a lot to prove because the previous episode (Return of the Jedi) and its amazingly high reputation in the film industry. So I think J.J. Abrams did a great job in rebooting a franchise that is close to fans hearts.

The film it self was very enjoyable to watch and was great to see the original actors playing the much loved iconic characters of the Star Wars franchise. The Run time was not at all too long and I think the story of the new characters flowed well. Although the original characters were in The Force Awakens they didn't have a big part and it was more about the new story and I'm excited to see what it might lead to in the episodes to come.

When first hearing that J.J. Abrams was going to direct the next episode In the series I was quite sceptical. But after realising some of the films he is affiliated with such as Super 8, Star Trek and Armageddon. It made me feel better of what the outcome may be for The Force Awakens. And with a budget of $200 million you knew it was going to be a visually impressive film. But even with such a large budget its not gonna matter if you don't have a director capable of pulling off such a big movie.

So I think Star Wars: The Force Awakens was a great film and has amazing potential to develop into something that even the most dedicated Star Wars fan would be proud of but there is a long way to go until we see the conclusion to the new trilogy in episode 9 and if its anything like the previous trilogy's its gonna go off in a bang.

title: A great start
review:
It's good, lets get that out of the way (phew!). It overcomes all of its most unenviable challenges confidently. I can't recall another franchise tasked with conjuring up a cast of insta-classic, original characters like this - pretty much every blockbuster we see now is based on existing material. Even the Star Wars prequels relied mostly on stock characters (sorry padme). The nearest comparison I can make to The Force Awakens success in this regard is 1999's other sci-fi franchise starter, The Matrix, which went on to squander the appeal of Morpheus and Agent Smith.

Finn, Rey, Poe, Kylo and BB-8 are all fantastic. Adam Driver as Kylo Ren stole this movie for me; his performance is threatening, playful, vulnerable, casual, tragic... and he even gets a couple of laughs! This is the film's principal villain I'm talking about! He's brilliantly conceived and equally compelling inside and outside of the helmet. John Boyega as Finn is as charismatic as they come, funny and natural even with an affected American accent.

I'm a little more cautious about newcomer Daisy Ridley (Rey), who I found slightly clunky in places; but luckily the movie adores her, and the whole thing pivots around her character's journey, creating many of the most memorable moments, including my favourite scene (that recalls a sequence from Harry Potter - you'll know when you see it). On the subject of Rey; Lucasfilm has beaten everyone to the punch by creating a franchise leading female action hero with absolutely no romantic connections. Female X-wing pilots and Stormtroopers also on show - not just Gwendoline Christie's headline grabbing Captain Phasma, but regular troopers too. Equal opportunities abound.

If the film falters at all it's with the simpler challenges. A basic action adventure plot is enough to hang the trappings on for this first instalment, but this feels directionless in places (Like the rescue mission that's not principally a rescue mission and in the end doesn't really require a rescuer) and there are a few odd contrivances when you think about it afterwards and some obvious echoes of the original Star Wars story that would be better off avoided. So maybe a little rushed on the screenplay front, but hey, I was tired when I saw it. Our midnight showing started 30 minutes late due to the sheer number of people in the multiplex. 10 screens, all showing star wars, absolutely packed. That tells its own story.

title: Has character and a sense of fun, but needs its own voice
review:
The amount of one star reviews on here are baffling, though not surprising. Of course, this film was never going to live up to everyone's impossible standards and ridiculous expectations, especially considering that not everyone was pleased with Disney buying out Star Wars or J.J. Abrams's involvement to begin with; however, what we got was a marvelously entertaining and emotional, if a little too safe, film.

The plot does appropriate a lot from the original 1977 Star Wars: a droid carries plans that the good and bad guys want, the heroine is a dreamer on a crummy desert planet, the main villain is a fallen Jedi in a cloak and mask, and there is another huge doomsday device which must be taken out of commission in a space battle. I admit it disappointed me a little, all this familiarity, especially the resurrection of the Death Star concept, which was terrible back in 1983, let alone in 2015. The moment when the Resistance explains that THIS Death Star is planet rather than moon sized, I groaned aloud in the theater. The movie needed to make its own iconic moments instead of appropriating images and lines from the older films.

Aside from a sometimes too fast pace (I really do miss the slower pacing of the original, which gave us forty minutes to set up its universe and main character, though I suppose that is not fashionable these days), this blatant fan servicing is really the film's biggest problem, lingering on nostalgia imagery for much too long; however, is this enough reason to claim the film sucks and should only have one star? Of course not, for the film's greatest strengths are its sense of fun, chemistry between actors, and mythic resonances. The new heroes, Finn, Rey, and Poe, are all likable and flawed, given much more depth than even the Golden Trio in Episode IV were allowed back in 1977. When Harrison Ford isn't on screen, John Boyega and Daisy Ridley steal the show as Finn and Rey, earnest and vulnerable, plus sharing palpable romantic chemistry. Basically, they're the sort of heroes you love watching and cannot wait to watch more of in the next two movies. I was also relieved that Harrison Ford didn't phone his performance in and that he and Carrie Fisher still had a great deal of chemistry.

If there's anything weak with the story, then it's the villains. While Kylo Ren gets more depth and interest as the film goes on, lifting him up from being another uninspired Darth Vader stand-in, the "Big Bad" Snoke is not so interesting. I know no one would ever be able to be as memorable as Emperor Palpatine, who was both threatening and gleefully wicked, but Snoke is just dull, as dull as any ominous, humorless villain in modern Hollywood cinema. There's an overabundance of action scenes as well, but at least writers Abrams and Kasdan allow for character moments in between them. Plus there is genuine tension in them and the light saber fights are emotional and natural-looking again, thank the Lord above.

Overall, the movie does have a little too much fan service, but it is a loving and entertaining flick, with humor that arises from character and not flatulence or blatant theft from masters like Buster Keaton or Harold Lloyd, romance that is sweet and understated, and action that never forgets it isn't worth a thing unless we care about the people involved in the chases and big battles. Here's hoping the next film will continue to focus on character and swashbuckling, while also finding its own voice.

title: Is this a galaxy far, far away, or somewhere we've already been?
review:
You don't need to trawl too far into the internet to realise this film has polarised fans. People are either defending its magnificence to their last breath, or calling it a 'remake in all but name.' A 'bland rehash of already overused ideas.' It doesn't take a genius to realise that Star Wars: The Force Awakens does indeed borrow heavily from A New Hope, and some elements from The Empire Strikes Back. Entire story beats, set-pieces and locations are lifted from the original and moulded into this new story, or even given new names as if we wouldn't notice (Tatooine/Jakku).

If you were looking for a bold new direction for the Star Wars story, there will no doubt be a tinge of disappointment. It seems J. J. Abrams and team tackled this from the angle of 'history is repeating itself in the Star Wars universe,' and no doubt wanting to ignite nostalgia in fans by replicating so much from Episode IV. To put this into perspective, if you haven't seen any of the original trilogy in years, that sense of nostalgia might well work for you. But if you're one of those who likes to binge watch the Star Wars saga in chronological order, Force Awakens may feel like too much of the same too soon.

So you may now be wondering, with all of that said, why have I scored it an 8/10? Because, despite its flaws, Star Wars: The Force Awakens was the most satisfying experience I've had at the cinema for a very long time. I laughed, I was excited and I was moved. At no point did I feel disappointed. And more than that, for everything that this film lifts from ANH, it has something fresh and original to counter it with. I was peripherally aware of the similarities to A New Hope as the film played, but I was also aware of some fantastic new characters, emerging mysteries and an interesting plot line for the franchise to continue which was (in true ESB fashion) left on a cliffhanger for us to ponder until the sequel arrives.

What's most important to me though, is that J.J Abrams clearly understood the core and soul of what makes Star Wars what it is. It isn't the titular 'wars' themselves, or space politics or CGI saber-fests. It's the characters themselves and their relationships. Abrams has preserved this for another generation. If you consider that George Lucas himself failed to deliver that core and soul in his own Star Wars prequels, it becomes clear what an accomplishment this is.

title: Phew ...
review:
I went into the movie almost fearful.Wasn't sure at all, if this baby could possibly be rocked. I was relieved to say the least.

Considering the notion, that more sequels are to come, the movie doesn't give away too much with TFA, after all, there needs to be a bit flesh left for the next ones. Although the movie is on some levels completely NOT-Star Wars, I loved the fact how it bridged nicely to the older movies, which in turn turned it into Star Wars as we remember it.A few surprises, yes, and one big one for me personally, I see no reason to be harsh on the writers for using known plots from 4 and 6. TFA in my eyes is clearly to be understood as a way to give us older fans of SW a reconnecting straw to our memories from back then as well as way for new generations to feel and connect to the thrill of SW but on this new level. TFA is the entry point for the next ones,they HAD to build it somehow.. On the business side I have to say they managed extremely well, to continue a well established franchise with so much passion for the feel of SW.And knowing that our favorite actors of SW like CF, HF and MH are getting older they did a great job to introduce the new characters and let us viewer accept them. And let's be real, one day the old stars will be gone forever but we have accepted the new ones. I understand the mixed feelings about Adam Driver. During the movie I myself was puzzled why they chose him. But the longer I was watching him, I could see why they chose him. And they picked the perfect one. What I liked very much in the TFA is, that for once it was not the dark side tempting a character but the good side. A really new thing in Hollywood. And a welcome change, I have to say. I've kind of had it with the good always being tempted by the bad. It's VERY refreshing to see the bad being tempted by the good. Overall, I clearly feel a paradigm shift happen in Hollywood and thus in SW. TFA is not the only one that has this strange new feel to it. Almost as if Hollywood forces us into new habits we don't really want, yet, Like forcing us to drink water when we are used to sirup. I am VERY relieved it turned out as good as it did. Thank you for not messing this up.

title: A return to form.
review:
A very familiar, but solid film, and a solid return for Star Wars.

Director J.J. Abrams hits all the right notes in this film, and if you're a Star Wars fan, it will bring out the "feels" in you.

While at first I was nervous of how the new faces will be portrayed, without revealing too much I'm happy to report that they are all interesting and juggled very well. Daisy Ridley as Rey carries the whole film on her shoulders as does John Boyega as Finn. I really liked the diverse leads J.J. had in this film, and those two have a potential career ahead of them. A strong female character who isn't a damsel in distress and an African male lead who also kicks some ass but is able to show vulnerability. Oscar Isaac as Poe Dameron, the galaxy's best pilot brings some cool swagger, a bit Han Solo in him I might add. Adam Driver is superb as Kylo Ren, he's not a Vader ripoff, he's quite effective in the role and his overall appearance is very cool. The foursome will definitely have more significant exposure to them in the next chapters and I can't wait to see them on screen again.

The new cast also gels well with the older cast. It's great to see Harrison Ford as Han Solo once again. He plays it effortlessly and he seems to be having fun doing so. Ford gets the most screen time of all the original cast and he's got a lot of great moments through and through. He has a great father-figure chemistry between the two leads and his banter with Chewbacca is just as good. Carrie Fisher, this time is General Leia and she's in charge of the Rebellion, and she's under a lot of pressure and a little more broken-hearted. As for Luke, well you'd have to see the movie to find out, but that is the part where I was just a tad bit letdown on, but it'll only make you more excited and anticipate to see what's to come in the future. Not to mention BB-8, what an adorable little droid. BB-8 will definitely be a favorite among children.

The qualms and issues I had in the film was the absolute lack of Captain Phasma, she hardly does anything at all. I'm sure she will be explored a little more in the future, but here she was a complete waste. I really wasn't feeling Domhnall Gleeson at all. Not particularly his acting per say, but his character. He just seemed to be there as General Hux. In fact he's pretty much every other evil General in the original trilogy. He doesn't bring too much to the table either. Andy Serkis is Kylo Ren's master, Supreme Leader Snoke. There's a shroud of mystery in his character and he is a powerful Dark Side figure, I hope to see more of him in the future as well. Lupita Nyong'o's character Maz Kanata also provides some decent moments. She disguised her voice quite well, to be honest I was kinda shocked it was her performance.

J.J. Abrams also captures the aesthetic look and feel of the original Star Wars trilogy. It's not like the prequels where the technology looks way better than the technology of the original trilogy. Everything is put with attention to detail, the way Jakku looks, the way the Millennium Falcon moves, the sounds the TIE Fighters make, the sounds of the lightsabers clashing, just about everything, it feels like the original Star Wars. Also give credit to sound designer Ben Burt. He never fails to create iconic sounds in each film, and do I have to tell you John Williams, the living legend, arguably the greatest film composer in history does a magnificent job in the film?

Abrams also shoots action with a lot of flare. They're thrilling and exciting. He's always able to make you feel tension within the fight as the stakes do matter. With that being said, the lightsaber fights are incredible. Any positive in a Star Wars film is a lightsaber battle, even the prequels(except for Attack of the Clones) have some decent lightsaber duels, but in The Force Awakens, it feels authentic, because it's not heavily choreographed. Making the scenes much more grasping and more engaging. The X-Wing and TIE Fighter scenes rock as well, although I did feel the finale involving those two space ships to be a tad bit rushed and a little too easy.

It absolutely does parallel A New Hope and it can feel a bit like a Star Wars: Greatest Hits every now and then, but it offers new elements into the narrative without it feeling completely like a carbon copy, kinda.

J.J. Abrams resurrects Star Wars in great fashion and sets up the future very well for directors Rian Johnson and Colin Trevorrow(he's the one I'm nervous about). I think it's safe to say Mr. Abrams matches most of the expectations and solidifies the film's own hype.

7/10

title: Passionate Homage
review:
Continuing the Star Wars saga can be both an exciting and tough decision. Aside of the fans' disappointment from the prequels, it is a serious task to make a new trilogy as good or even better than the original. And what The Force Awakens chose is to start with sheer nostalgia. The result of the new story is rather more intriguing than it is great. But the greatest feat of the whole is how downright fun it is. Whether you're a Star Wars fan or not, you'll just find this as an ultimately entertaining movie. And since this is only the first movie of this reborn franchise, it is already pretty good to what it is.

Before we get to the stuff we loved, there are few problems that we should point out (hopefully, these would be nitpicks if the sequel payed off with better answers.) Mainly is the fact that most of these characters feel like a retread of the original. Rey might as well be Luke, BB-8 is definitely Artoo, Poe Dameron is Han Solo in the making and Han Solo is Ben Kenowbi. Gee, I wonder what equivalent Kylo Ren, Hux and Snoke are supposed to be. The only one who doesn't seem to have his own match is Finn, who was a Storm Trooper found awareness and now seeking for some sort of redemption. But instead of doing exactly everything all over again, it takes these elements to challenging, often mysterious, twists. The thematic focus of this franchise, while it does have a light and dark side, is basically having these characters face their complex choices. The movie doesn't go deeper to that, at least not yet. But it's still all about introduction.

And as an introduction, it's just an adventurous blast. The movie never really hesitates its plot. It just keeps moving, having our heroes being chase from a number of enemies, cherishing every place and character they stop into and that's the type of fun we were missing in the last films. The fan service doesn't stop there, even the craft follows its own nostalgia. There's a mix between CG and practical effects and the result is just magnificent. The love for the franchise is immediately defined from this homage of filmmaking. The action is also downright exciting, specifically the Millennium Falcon chase and a lightsaber fight with a storm trooper.

As for the acting: Daisy Ridley fares better physically, where we see this protagonist's sense of danger and adventure from her expressions and action. John Boyega brings the energy and charisma as one of the lead heroes. Harrison Ford bounces perfectly with these two kids. Adam Driver gives compelling angst as Kylo Ren. The other villains are being a little campy and that was never bad and actually rather entertaining, anyway. Oscar Isaac and Gwendoline Christie gave enough intrigue from their short roles that we'd hope to see more in the sequels.

Star Wars: The Force Awakens is the Star Wars everybody always wanted to see in years, maybe not entirely. Yeah, it's basically a series of questions that may be answered to the next one, but if the next movies manage to give us impressive answers and twists, then maybe the flaws here would be easily forgiven. For now, it's still a pretty good movie. The action is enjoyable, the homage is terribly beautiful, the acting is very entertaining. Nothing exactly groundbreaking to it, but the amount of enjoyment around is undeniably tremendous.

title: A Monument to a Legendary Franchise
review:
What was it that captivated so many back in 1977 when Star Wars was first released? Was it the revolutionary advancement in practical and CG effects? The idea that space was so large and new, yet we care for these amazing characters like they were our neighbors? Was it the lightsaber? Or was it the simple line between good and evil, the Dark Side and The Light? To me, the answer is all of the above, and then some. After a shift in ownership, and a 32 year wait for a true sequel, Star Wars returns to the world in the form of Episode VII - The Force Awakens (TFA), and returns the legendary name to its rightful glory.

The main plot of the film echoes from a time of simpler storytelling, that line between good and evil, a story that is easy to grasp while being able to invest deeply into the events that transpire in and around it. The pacing of the film is terrific, leaving room for breathtaking action sequences while bringing the speed down to give you time to digest and invest in everything. Director and writer J.J. Abrams overcame every ounce of skepticism by delivering a true Star Wars story, comprised of powerful themes, incredible dialogue, and exhilarating action while traversing your mind through the endless boundaries of the Star Wars galaxy. While there has been negative feedback regarding the film's similarities to Episode IV, the feeling of nostalgia and a new adventure come together to appeal to every generation of Star Wars fans. The overall story of Episode VII is genuinely amazing, from the simple premise to the deeper roots of each and every character, it's a nod to what made Star Wars so wonderful to begin with, and there's no better feeling than getting lost in a Star Wars story that has you on the edge of your seat.

At the core of The Force Awakens, is the outstanding cast of characters, both old and new. We get to see Han Solo (Harrison Ford), Princess Leia (Carrie Fisher), Chewbacca (Peter Mayhew) and even Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) for the first time since 1983, and their return to the franchise is just the start of a much greater path for Star Wars, paving the way for a new generation. Not a lot has changed since the original trilogy, in the fact that Harrison Ford steals the show in nearly every scene he's in.

Maybe even more important than the original cast, we are introduced to the new faces of Star Wars in the form of Rey (Daisy Ridley), Finn (John Boyega), Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), Poe (Oscar Issac) and the lovable new droid, BB-8. These new characters are exceptional, with each one bringing life and depth to the Star Wars universe, with each and every actor displaying magnificent emotion in their role, almost forcing you to care for them and their story.

Kylo Ren is an exciting and ravenous new villain, and although he resembles Darth Vader almost too much (yes he is a Vader-worshiper so to speak), Kylo Ren is now a household name due to his fierce nature, relentless motives, eye-popping costume and his instantly recognizable fiery, red cross-guarded lightsaber. Ren is a welcomed new antagonist to the Star Wars lore. Among the other new characters we have Rey, the strong, beautiful and incredibly likable scavenger, the new lead character in Star Wars. Rey is a spectacular example of how you can relate and so easily be captivated by Star Wars characters, with her mysterious origins, tough demeanor and willingness to do whatever it takes. Daisy Ridley was phenomenal in the role, and she will only continue to grow as an actress and with this role.

John Boyega is arguably the most invested in his role as Finn, a fantastic new addition. BB-8 rolls around and grabs your heart, making you laugh and love him throughout the film, and while Oscar Issac's Poe isn't given enough screen time or development, he's a blast to watch when he's up on the screen. Along with the main cast there are several other smaller characters, both new and old, that help make TFA feel like a real living, breathing story. There's always been the epic space setting and iconic weapons, but what makes Star Wars so indisputably amazing is the characters that fill the space, and Episode VII gives long time and new-coming fans spectacular characters to love.

The Force Awakens wasn't nominated for 5 Oscars for no reason, those Oscars involving sound mixing, editing, and original score along with visual effects and film editing. Much like "A New Hope" back in '77, TFA brings Star Wars back to the forefront of technological advancements in film, with jaw-dropping CGI, the return of stunning practical effects, and the simply majestic score of John Williams, who without, Star Wars would't be the same. The visual effects help make every action scene enthralling, as iconic lightsabers clash and you watch the Millennium Falcon soar on screen like never before through gorgeous set pieces and atmospheric beauty keeping your mind lost in the film. Episode VII is a visual and audible masterpiece, simple as that.

Monuments are erected to pay tribute to someone or something, to preserve a legacy and to carve a path for the future of all that see it, and dream to accomplish what it did. That is Episode VII. A monument to the original Star Wars saga, a piece of art that brings total justice to the illustrious Star Wars name, and a beacon of hope and assurance for the future of the franchise. The Force Awakens pulls your heart and mind into its world with an engaging story, sensational characters, heart-racing action and visual, audible and practical effects that leave you breathless. It's old and new, coming together to craft a generational milestone. Star Wars is back, and I couldn't be more overjoyed.

9/10

title: Star wars is back!
review:
I'm a huge fan of the original trilogy and was dismayed by all but the last half of Return of the Sith when it came to the prequels. Making a film that was better than the prequels was easy, the question would be how close to the originals could a new Star Wars film get? Could it even be better than them?

Well, it gets close and I would argue it is even better than Jedi, perhaps as good as A New Hope. Empire Strikes Back is still my favourite. There is just so much to like with this newest instalment. The acting is great. All the main characters do a really great job. The effects are wonderful. Gone are the computer game like images of the prequels and now we get a nice mix of models and CGI. The sounds are fantastic - from John Williams' new score (peppered with some of the classic old stuff) to the sounds of the lightsabers and blasters. Bliss. It's funny. Actually, I could go on and on about what I liked for a long time. That's not what you want to know though. You'd like to know what I don't like, right? Here are my issues with the movie (WARNING - SPOILERS galore here)

1) It is too much like A New Hope and Return of the Jedi!!! There is another death star. They have to take out the shield, again. Etc. etc.

2) As soon as Kylo Ren stepped out onto the bridge near the end of the movie I knew Han would follow him and I knew he would be killed. I just knew it. I had avoided all such speculation before seeing the movie so I wasn't expecting Han to be killed off. But I just knew it.

3) Why did Chewie walk right past Leia after he lands the Falcon and Han has died. It is clear that Leia knows Han is dead and the camera cuts to her "feeling it" as he dies. So why would the two most important people/creatures in Han's life NOT console each other?? WTF? Leia goes straight to Rey, who she has never met and consoles her? Was this just a massive mistake?

4) Why are lightsabers suddenly like the ring from Lord of the Rings. Calling to people etc.?

5) The pacing was just too fast. I would have liked to draw breadth a little.

My biggest gripe is the first one. This was just a stupid idea. I mean come on. Off the top of my head here is a better way they could have done it and not re-made an old star wars movie. Just have a rescue mission to save Rey on some planet (keep all the tension and lightsaber battles etc.) and create a distraction by having a space battle with Poe. Done. Wasn't hard.

Even given these gripes I give it 8/10. It was still a fantastic movie.

BTW I saw it twice. Once in normal 3D and once in iMax 3D. Wow, the difference is spectacular. If you can see it on an iMax screen then make sure you do so.

Go see it, if you haven't already, and enjoy!

title: It's Star Wars
review:
It is Star Wars - what did you expect? A lot of folks are bashing this film, but it is a pretty good movie. Again, it is Star Wars: it is the bad, almost non-existent plot; the horrible acting that feels wooden; the ridiculous dialog; and the over-the-top special effects. Star Wars was always a mindless, action adventure with a ridiculous storyline and terrible actors (except for Harrison Ford).

The Force Awakens is the same thing: just by chance a droid lands on a planet with important information and runs into a member of the Skywalker family; who than just happens to run into Han Solo; who just happens to be the sire of another bad Skywalker; who just happen to fight another death star. The story is bad - the script is bad - the question is: does the eye candy and action make it at least watchable? The answer is - yes. This is on par with the original and "The Empire Strike Back".

Daisy Ridley is as bad of an actress as Mark Hamill is as an actor. They kept that same parallel of terrible actors playing the main Skywalker.

Folks are complaining about John Boyega, but aside from Han Solo and Chewbacca, I felt that he was one of the better characters in the movie. Oscar Isaac was the other new character that was entertaining to watch.

I didn't like Adam Driver as the villain. If the villain is supposed to be Solo and Leia's child; I would have expected a more charismatic actor who looked more like he could have been their child rather than someone who looked like Adrien Brody. He lacks the charisma and looks laughable rather than dangerous.

The idea that someone can grab a lightsaber for the first time and beat a trained sith is typical Abrams garbage.

There are a lot of bad things in Star Wars - most as a homage to the bad things in the original three - but it is a fun adventure worth seeing. At least George Lucas wasn't involved to make something worse than Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones and Return of the Sith - three of the worse movies in the history of film-making.

title: The Force Has Awaken
review: A long time ago in a galaxy far awayÂ… It really has been a long time ago if you are a Star Wars fan. The big question is "Has the Force Really Awaken? Since the prequels?", no puns intended. This movie starts with this big question and yet it left you with a sense of awes and discoveries. The biggest fears going into this movie for us are managing expectations, too much fan services, and the handling of the new characters. In delight, this film has diminished all of those doubts and fears and instill a new light into this new saga where JJ Abrams (the director) and Lawrence Kasdan (the writer of the empire strikes back) who brought back the nostalgia and magic of the original saga without compromising the plot of the film. There were so many positive points about the film from the castings to the practical effects which bring this movie to life. The movie team has done many things right, from marketing the trailer without spoiling the film to the last scene of the movie. Thus, leaving the audience wanting MORE after the movie is over. This is the beginning to new saga with characters whom you care about as the plots propel along. A point to be noted is that this is a fast pace moving film with enough exposition that keeps you entertained and informed throughout. Going back to the portrayals of the new characters Daisy Ridley, John Boyega, Oscar Isaac, and Adam Driver as Ray, Finn, Poe, and Kylo Ren respectively were very well executed and were given more than just role to play but role to be supported and sympathized with. The Force has awaken as the saga continues as it picks up where it was left off. In conclusion, Star Wars Episode VII: The Force Awaken is an excellent film and is highly recommended for not just Star Wars fan but for movie lover in general. May the force be with you.

title: It's great for what it is. A Star Wars movie.
review:
In comparison to other movies, this won't win any awards for Best Picture of the Year, but it's awesome for what it is - Star Wars. It's just like the original trilogy, and as some people complain, it might be too much like the originals. There are obvious plot devices that are re-used for nostalgia, but I appreciate them as a fan. My only gripe is the Star Killer Base - C'mon, seriously. THREE TIMES?!? WHY?

Besides that, the acting from all the new characters were charismatic and it was a pleasure to see the OG crew as well. I only wish that the score was used more effectively - it's John Williams for crying out loud! He should be front and center of the movie.

Some people might think that are too many plot holes, but that's because we are thrown right into a new story. Many things need to be inferred by the audience, and that's because the writers trust that we, the audience, are intelligent enough to figure it out.

title: A generally enjoyable film
review:
The film manages to capture the essence of Star Wars, and has decent production values. It also provides the audience with intriguing questions about the characters of this film.

However, this films relies heavily on the overall feel of the Original Trilogy, evident in its plot that resembles that if A New Hope.

In conclusion, this is a fun and interesting film to watch, however, it's dependence on the Original Trilogy material may be limits to the creativity and rewatchability of the film.

title: Not Bad... Certainly Not Extraordinary... Better than the Prequels
review:
The movie was fun to watch, especially after 10 years since the last film. The new leads, played by Boyega, Ridley, and Driver, are much better than Christensen and company. And... Thank Goodness... NO tag-along "comic relief" aliens.

The plot is so-so, but it does appear to be leading up to something which could make for an excellent sequel and finale in this trilogy. Kylo Ren is the most interesting character so far, so I hope that he sticks around for whole trilogy. Something happened between Ren, Leia, Han, and Luke... and I think it's going to be a lot of fun watching that story unfold. Plus, Adam Driver has the character "Nailed".

The first two trilogies started off with a big "We Won!" in the first film, but that was not the case in Episode VII. I like where that is going. This seems to be a big setup for a very "Dark" Episode VIII, which would be awesome. The release date for VIII has already been pushed back, perhaps because the writers and director see an opportunity to really make it the darkest "middle" episode of the whole saga.

The acting by Driver is exceptional, and both Ridley and Boyega are above average, although Boyega was stuck in some places where the dialog didn't quite seem to meet the situation. Gleeson (General Hux) does some decent work, although he doesn't have many lines in the film. Word is that Gleeson and Isaac (Poe Dameron) will have bigger parts in VIII. I think that would be a good thing.

I saw the film in IMAX, which was definitely worth it. If you haven't seen it yet, and don't have easy access to an IMAX cinema, I'd wait for the Blu-Ray.

title: star wars The Force Awakens
review: This movie had a lot of scenes that were similar of the other movies in the franchise. title: ''The force is strong with this one''
review:
The Force Awakens was a blast to watch and an emotionally thrilling ride filled with adventure, story, characters and a lot of heart. The film has exceeded my expectations for the Star Wars film franchise. I expected a good movie but what i did not expect was a great one. I am casual Star Wars fan. I love the original trilogy, but i can also appreciate the prequels as well, though to a lower degree because when there are so few Star Wars films, you kinda have to. What this film does is it eliminates the overly complicated story-lines of that set up the prequel trilogy in favor of a much simpler old fashioned way of story telling reminiscent of the original. Which is a refreshing breath of air for Star Wars fans.

The film pays homage to what made the original so great. The wonder of an age long forgotten, a novelty of discovery and the age-old tale of good vs evil. Exciting battles and unlikely heroes seemingly destined for greatness. And the story with characters that feel much more natural and likable added with the much absent humor aspect thrown into the mix. The result is adventure that many will want to revisit time and time again. I left the movie theater satisfied with the ending and with hopeful expectations for its bright future.

title: Galactic romp with a minor Rey of doubt
review:
Ah yes, the difficult seventh installment.

Let's be honest: how many franchises have got to seven installments and still been good? Cards on the table now, I reserve the right to use this line again when I come to watch the upcoming Creed.

But this is no underdog story. This is a heavyweight. This is Star Wars. This is a franchise that's now 39 years old and counting. Equipped with the punching power of Disney behind it and with an armada of super-fans queuing for midnight screenings worldwide, this is a movie with every chance of standing tall at the end of round seven.

It's a movie that will be emotive to a lot of people. This will be as spoiler-free as possible.

The first point is the casting, which I think JJ Abrams (Armageddon, Lost and Star Trek) got just about right. John Boyega was fantastic as lovable Stormtrooper turned rebel, whilst the better known Lupita Nyong'o (12 Years a Slave) and Domhnall Gleeson (Harry Potter) suited their roles perfectly.

What raised my eyebrows was Daisy Ridley's appearance as female lead Rey. I didn't find her believable, I didn't empathize with her plight and ultimately I wasn't that bothered about her prevailing. I don't think it was her fault; the role was not well written and the character too naive to be taken seriously. There are repeated attempts to shroud her in mystery that failed to intrigue.

One talking point amongst people I've spoken to was the role of Kylo Ren, played by relative unknown Adam Driver. I think he excelled: playing the role with an intriguing vulnerability. Not every villain can be a cold-hearted bad-ass.

It's an interesting change in direction: where in Episodes 1-3 and 4-6 the bad guys have traditionally had a flawless, confident villain here we see a villain lacking conviction. This is a character that will develop across the next two installments. Kylo Ren intrigues me more than his protagonist counterpart.

In plot terms, I'm happy here. We all know the drill: band of misfits group together to take out the bad guys and save the galaxy. It's the same much-loved tried and tested principle as the episodes that came before. It works. Not much else to say.

Structurally it's sound too. The film begins with a nod to previous films (scrolling yellow intro text the best example), there's sufficient action immediately following. We then meet our major cast, understand them, and the story goes from there

Without giving too much away, this is where the beloved cast of installments 4-6 reappear. This won't be a spoiler, the likes of Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher are here as most will have suspected, expected and demanded.

The movie flies to its conclusion at lightspeed, with gorgeous visuals aplenty en route. At no point does the film feel slow nor rushed. You learn and see enough to maintain a happy medium of interested and absorbed. The ending is an action-packed, gloriously visual finale that will gratify casual moviegoers and die hards alike.

There's not much more that can be said whilst remaining spoiler friendly. Go and enjoy this movie for what it is, a swashbuckling sci-fi that pays sufficient homage to its predecessors.

title: The Force Has Indeed Awakened
review:
Reviewed by: Dare Devil Kid (DDK)

Rating: 5/5 stars

J.J. Abrams and his crew have restored the shine to our beloved story, and then some. Packed with action and populated by both familiar faces and fresh blood, "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" successfully recalls the series' former glory while injecting it with renewed energy.

The film begins three decades after the defeat of Darth Vader and the Galactic Empire, when a new threat known as the First Order has arisen and attempts to rule the galaxy once again with tyranny and ruthlessness, just as the Empire had done many decades ago. Enter Rey, a scavenger from the planet Jakku, who finds a BB-8 droid that knows the whereabouts of the long-vanished Luke Skywalker. Along with a rogue stormtrooper and two well-known smugglers, the rag-tag group of heroes team up with the Resistance to stop the daunting legions of the First Order.

What works the most in favor of this latest entrant to the space saga is the dexterity, fluency, and zip with which each scene flows, and seamlessly blends with all the exhilarating action, smart humor, and indelible dialogues; nothing ever feels out of place - Abrams delivers a tour-de-force in the act of pure storytelling. Another highlight is the crop of new characters - well-written and fleshed out with intrigue and promising back stories without revealing too much in one go. They play well with and against each other as also with some of the grizzled veterans now ready to make way for younger blood to take over the mantle.

And it all climaxes with the right elements (though many die-hard fans will be left fuming or at least inconsolable at one shocking development that transpires toward the denouement), tantalizing us and setting things up brilliantly for the next installment. Secret threads on social media are already picking their nits and debating theories; it's going to be a tough wait to see what happens next.

title: A safe return to the Saga

This is hardly a new revelation: critics and fans made that point when it was first released. The plan was to make an entertaining if safe film to win back fans who displeased with the Prequel. The Force Awakens manages this with ease: it was a fun, popcorn film with excellent special effects and action sequences. When compared to J. J. Abrams' Star Wars work Rise of Skywalker, The Force Awakens actually had some build-up and invested in the characters.
