The new republic didn't start any military to counter remnant threats all these years?

title: Flawed but highly enjoyable
review:
Star Wars Episode VII : The Force Awakens, directed by JJ Abrams, has its flaws which can quite obvious at times, but the film makes up for it in every other way.

The seventh movie in the Star Wars movie franchise (if you exclude the animated "Clone Wars" movie ) is the first Star Wars film I had the opportunity to see in the movie theater/cinema, and boy did I enjoy it. Abrams perfectly concocts a mixture of humour, action, drama and mystery. From start to finish you hardly have a chance to go to the toilet in case you miss something. The movie is perfectly paced, with the first few scenes setting up the rest of the movie.

In contrast with George Lucas' prequel trilogy, Abrams focuses more on the use of practical effects, while seamlessly incorporating CGI that makes the film look incredibly realistic and beautiful ( Bar the characters of Maz Kanata and Supreme Leader Snoke , who do tend to stick out ever so slightly ) .Beautiful locations like the desert planet of Jakku, the forests on Starkiller Base or the ending scene filmed on Skellig Michael make for a film that is incredibly pleasing on the eye.

Daisy Ridley and John Boyega steal the show as the newcomers to the Star Wars films. Both Rey and Finn are extremely well acted characters, no thanks to their acting skills and the great dialogue that was missing in the Prequel trilogy. Oscar Isaac and Adam Driver also put in great performances as Poe Dameron and Klyo Ren respectively. Poe,Finn and Rey all play off each other brilliantly and there is a believable relationship that they all form with one another ( Although I believe Poe and Rey are yet to meet ) The trio from the Original trilogy, Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher and Mark Hamill reprise their rolls in TFA as Han Solo, General Leia Organa and Luke Skywalker. Ford is in the film for much more than the Skywalker twins and he definitely steals the show. He seems happy to back playing Han Solo again and his ((( SPOILER ))) and his final scene with Kylo Ren//Ben Solo was incredibly emotional. Fisher returns to play Leia and although she does a fine job, there isn't much more you can say about her. Her acting feels slightly stiff at times but thankfully she isn't in the movie as much as Ford. Hamill on the other hand shows up for around 20 seconds at the end of the movie and has no dialogue, so...I can't really say much about him

I loved Kylo Ren as a villain . He has so much depth after one movie. He puts on his mask to appear threatening but underneath that mask he is a conflicted and impetuous . Abrams does a great job of showing that although he is an extremely powerful user of the dark side of the force, he is still a young boy with feelings and emotions. He even has a few lines that made me chuckle along the way.

The Lightsaber fight at the film's climax is dark,gritty and realistic. Kylo Ren, Finn and Rey look like they are actually fighting to survive rather than just dancing with flashy laserswords in an over-choreographed duel. No, these guys are hacking at each other, trying to land a fatal blow to their opponent. It is definitely one of my favorite duels of the 7 movies.

My biggest gripe with the movie is that it tends to re-use plot elements from A New Hope eg. Droid with vital information,another Death Star that can be blown up if hit in the right spot etc. I wish they would have gone in a slightly different direction with this film. Another nit-pick is that I feel Captain Phasma was underutilised, but hopefully we'll see more of her in Episode 8.

In conclusion, The Force Awakens is a very very good movie that will not only entertain you for a few hours, but also get you emotionally invested in the universe that is unfolding in the continuation of the Star Wars franchise. There are so many enjoyable aspects of this film that far outweigh the negatives. Star Wars Episode VII : The Force Awakens is a great movie that puts Star Wars back on the map.

title: This trilogy is going into right direction
review:
There are not so much CGI. Prequels were ruined by that along with bad acting. I liked it very much that creatures were made for real and not by CGI. I'm not going to write long review so I just list things. First good things. + Rated PG13. + old characters return + acting is good + feels more like old star wars + one surprise Game of thrones style

Bad things - feels a bit a remake of episode IV - Some characters doesn't have enough screen time - Characters can fight with a lightsaber even when not trained - Not enough background information why things are like they are

All in all I feel like this trilogy is going into right direction!

title: 'Star Wars' is finally restored to its former glory.
review:
For those of you who have doubts about the ratings that are being given to this film - keep doubting them. Let the fanboys give their 10/10s, and let the haters give their 1/10s. But let me say this - having rewatched all the episodes, 'The Force Awakens' stands as the third best 'Star Wars' film in the franchise - just behind the original 1977 'Star Wars' and 'The Empire Strikes Back'.

There are a lot of similarities between this film and the Original Trilogy - both in terms of characters and plot points. I'm not going to go into much detail about it, but all I can say is that I was reminded a lot of what took place in that trilogy. I personally love the fact that Abrams and Kasdan took the story in a familiar direction, yet also added just enough new elements to keep the film from going stale. It's been a long time since we've seen a PROPER 'Star Wars' film, so anything that felt too new might have just have been harder to accept.

Once I got over my hype of seeing this film, I also realized that the story contains quite a few of problems - mainly plot conveniences. Some of the major events that propel the plot forward just kind of 'happen'. In addition, I felt that the plot reveals certain details a little too early - thus killing the suspense of some of the more dramatic parts of the film. I also had some issues with the pacing of the action sequences (especially during the dogfights); the editing jumps to different characters more times than necessary. It's not disorienting, but those scenes certainly could have been tightened up a bit more.

Every actor tries their best to bring life to their characters - and the overall effect is amazing. This is, by far, the best acted 'Star Wars' film since 'Episode V'. Many of the major players in the new cast - including Ridley, Boyega, and Issac - are not only convincing in their roles, but have rightfully earned their places in the existing pantheon of 'Star Wars' actors. I am sure that their characters will eventually be as famous as Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and Princess Leia.

All of the technical factors in this film are done to near perfection. Both the VFX and SFX departments deserve to be commended as usual (possibly with Oscars). The cinematography is reminiscent to that of the Original trilogy (with plenty of awe-inspiring wide shots thrown into the mix). The editing is consistent and helps this epic adventure feel more accessible. And the score by John Williams is... what more do I have to say about this godly composer!?

In my opinion, Disney could not have picked a better director than J.J. Abrams (okay, maybe Ridley Scott) to bring us 'The Force Awakens'. Everything he did with this film just felt 'right'. Sure, he made some mistakes here and there, but the experience that he crafted for all of us to enjoy just drowns those mistakes out.

I personally had a great experience watching 'The Force Awakens' (and I'm not that big of a fan either), and I'm sure anyone who even remotely likes 'Star Wars' can have a great experience watching this epic film.

title: Watch the film first Spoilers ahead. Best crawl ever
review:
First of all, like many of you, I was a 5 year old when my dad took me to the largest cinema in town to see Star Wars A new Hope. But my fondest memory comes from watching over 10 times the second installment The Empire Strikes Back, so the expectation for Return of the Jedi was equal or above The Forcé Awakens.

Remember it was an era with no internet, social media, you tube, memes, etc. So our imagination and amazement capabilities were in another level.

Now I'm over 40 with an 11 year old son, who already watched the OT and PT, and with a high level of excitement. For my son, the thrill was to experience his first Star Wars movie in a theater, actually the same one where I watched the OT back in the eighties, and for me it was the fact that the next chapter of my favorite saga was about to begin.

Yes I wanted this film to be the most incredible experience with my son, travel the nostalgia lane and feel amazed in every way a movie can do while meeting my expectations as a geeky sci fi fan.

Now the theater looks smaller, the screen is old fashioned unlike our new IMAX and the rows or seats are too close from each other. Even though I'm aware of this, as soon as the blue letters appear on the screen, I'm 10 years old again. The big yellow logo appears and I still can't believe it, here comes the opening crawl ( for me the best of the 7 episodes)

So here it comes my positive finds

  • great introduction to new characters ( Finn, Rey, Kylo Ren, Poe and BB8 ) - great sense of humor, goofy lines without sounding silly - new perspective for the bad guys, conflicted villain, seeing the first order behind the curtains, including female characters. - best acting since Empire, also better dialogue - good rhythm and pacing - chemistry between new and old characters, even the droids and creatures - ending scene and cliffhanger - although the soundtrack is not iconic like the OT, there are some themes and cues that stand out - lightsaber duels, well balanced.


Now my spotted áreas of improvement that do not necessarily annoyed me,

  • the score did not resonate through the film, with the exception of two scenes - I think at times General Hux was a little overacted - Captain Phasma was underused - Supreme Leader Snoke CGI design, however the hologram size looks neat - the whole rathtars chase CGI moments - the x-Wing attack on Starkiller Base climax


I do not share the whole this is a rehash of A New Hope thing, yes there are crowdpleasers, there are lots of parallelism to the original story line, even direct references, there could be more original twists on the plot, however this feels like Star Wars, it introduces new developments and questions to this universe. title: The Special Effects Awaken
review:
A long time ago in a galaxy not so far away, George Lucas created a simple movie that would blossom into one of the biggest franchises in history. Over 40 years, Star Wars has managed to work its way into numerous media that keeps fans screaming in glee. After a corporate buyout, Disney has set their sights on reviving the movie franchise in the form of Episode 7: The Force Awakens. Yet with the mixed response to the prequels and dry movie spell, is the Force still strong enough to keep us entertained? Hi, I'm Robbie K and I'm here for another review on the latest Sci Fi Blockbuster, spoiler free.

From the trailers, there were three questions I wanted to address in this review: 1. Is it action packed? 2. Is the acting better? 3. Does it feel like Star Wars. To answer the first question, Yes The Force Awakens is an action packed adventure that gave us a taste of nearly everything we loved from the preceding films. The strongest piece was the ship/space warfare that finally stepped back into the shoes of the original trilogy. Exciting dogfights on multiple fronts kept things diverse as both factions' ships flew about in a chaotic slew. The editing impressively brought you into the cockpit, maximizing the thrill of flying into battle against the enemy. Ground combat wise it felt similar to the original trilogy, skillful blasting with a touch of suspense to keep things exciting. As for the lightsabers, well they are off to a good start, but this movie lacked the finesse style the prequels saber fights held, sometimes being a little hokey and drawn out. Regardless, there are few dull moments in Episode 7, which may be the biggest strength of this film. Now what about the acting? You'll be happy to hear that the Episode 7 has improved on this aspect as well. This should be no surprise when regarding the prequels lack of chemistry between the leads, however in regards to the original trilogy this installment has managed to reach the same quality of acting. Our seasoned actors (Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher, and Anthony Daniels) once more bring their characters to life, just with a few more wrinkles and some digital editing for looks. Ford in particular steals the show, maintaining that charismatic, live strong attitude that we fell in love with all those years ago. Fisher's lost the majesty in her voice, but makes up for it in facial expressions and body acting that bring the feel of Leia with it. As for Daniels, well the man has not let age wear down his quirkiness, making the most of his screen time. Our new cast has stepped up to the task placed on their shoulders, and created new characters that fit into Lucas' world. Daisy Ridley leads the charge of the new generation, a nice balance of strength and vulnerability to craft a dynamic character. John Boyega drives the story and provides comedic relief to ease the tension of this movie. As for Adam Driver, he certainly has the arrogance and regality of his character down, but there are some qualities that need tweaking (either by him or the writing staff) to capture the ominous tone his predecessors had. Finally, does the Force Awakens feel like Star Wars? Yes. The Force Awakens takes the best of both proceding trilogies and mixes them into an adventure of spectacular quality. The opening crawl gets the nostalgia started, as Star Destroyers, alien creatures, and beautiful worlds emerged in high-definition graphics. I found myself laughing at the multitude of references to the classic adventures, primarily in the clever placing of small trinkets here and there. This installment also expanded the galaxy further, adding a variety of new planets, species, and technology to the mix that fit well in Lucas' world. While the nostalgia and classic references are a welcome attribute of this film, it is also the biggest issue I have with the movie. The Force Awakens has little originality to it in terms of story, essentially using recycled plot elements in this story. To me this plot felt more like a remake with much of the original story amped up to a grandiose scale that sometimes was a little too big for me. In addition, I felt this movie tried to stuff too many things into one movie, and the new additions to the film (many scrapped from the expanded universe books) felt rushed or greatly underdeveloped. Perhaps more details will come in the next movies (both main film and side stories), but for now their stories remain very shallow. I greatly enjoyed this new adventure and felt that The Force Awakens was a Star Wars tale worth the wait. It provided the whole Star Wars experience, especially in terms of the design of the worlds and the action packed plot. While the lack of originality is annoying, I think this movie sets a solid ground for any future films, one I hope to see flourish in the next five years. I definitely recommend a trip to the theater for this one, whether in 3-D or regular is your choice.

My scores for this tale are: Action/Adventure/Fantasy: 8.5 Movie Overall: 8

title: Ignore the naysayers - this movie is excellent
review:
REVIEW CONTAINS SPOILERS

The Force Awakens is a fast paced, family movie that delivers in every way you want a fantasy movie to deliver - you forget the world you live in for 2 hours and enter into another less realistic but altogether more enjoyable one. It lacks originality but makes up for it with big enthusiasm, great casting and wonderful execution.

If you are reading the poor reviews of this film, those who are VERY down on this film have missed the mark on The Force Awakens in several ways.

1. Many people are criticising some of the moments in the force awakens that are not 'realistic' IE Rey picking up the force so quickly and defeating Kylo Ren. If you find this the most difficult thing to believe about a world with AI Robots, light speed vessels and elite trained soldiers that miss every target, perhaps The Force Awakens is the least of your problems. Star Wars requires you to suspend belief, so suspend belief and enjoy yourself. There are no hard and fast rules about anything when everything is impossible anyway.

2. Kylo Ren is not a weak villain, he is a deliberately weak villain. He will rise from the flames to become ruthless and terrifying. This is the start of his story arc and will give him more texture for the future. Removing his helmet shows us the weak and vulnerable boy he currently is. Once his training is complete I doubt the mask will be removed to show either his vulnerability or face again.

3. The Force Awakens is a new hope revisited. Yes it is. And this provides the perfect opportunity to introduce new characters to the Star Wars universe. I believe the story will now take new and interesting paths that The Force Awakens has opened the door to. They needed to mount the new beginning within a familiar framework to help us associate the new with Star Wars. I understand exactly where they are coming from with this. As a grown man taking his own children I appreciated the nostalgia and throwbacks, and although they may have been overdone they were well executed.

The new casting was exceptional, John Boyega and Daisy Ridley both excelled whilst Adam Driver was perfect in the role of angst ridden bad guy. Oscar Isaacs played a throwback hero and was a personal favourite.

Harrison Ford nailed an older Han Solo. Perhaps the only slight let down for me was Carrie Fisher, who didn't feel like the same person.

Effects, scenery and music all excellent. I give this film 8 stars with hope that the next films in this sequence will bring more originality.

title: This is not a reboot
review: I feel like this movie was treated like a total reboot of the franchise instead of being a sequel. And it is a sequel. It's a direct continuation of the story, although it feels completely unnatural and not true to the original trilogy's ending what-so-ever. The new characters are cool at the start. I mean watching the first few scenes of the movie is almost orgasmic. As a Star Wars fan, that's everything I could have asked for. However, the movie changes during its course. It's one thing to be mysteriously powerful, but a whole another to just completely destroy anything in your path. There is no build-up of anticipation after a certain point is reached. You can just assume the main character is always going to prevail no matter what, and despite all odds, without even breaking a sweat. It would be fine if someone had to work for it, but the characters are just handed everything they need, and buffed to meet their opposition whenever it's required. No character arcs, just immediate power changes. It's almost funny. Still a great watch and much better than its sequel. Its effects are astonishingly well done, but the fight scenes need better choreography.

title: An unnecessary remake of Star Wars: A New Hope
review:
This is not a Star Wars sequel. This is primarily a remake of Episode 4. It is so jam-packed with original trilogy references and direct plot ripoffs, all trying to ram the nostalgia down our throats It gets to a point where it's actually overbearing and distracting from the movie. If you can look past that, it's a decent movie.

My least favorite aspect of the movie is the total abandonment of the prequels. There are no scenes showing the full scope of the battle or any battle sequences occurring with non-main characters, which were easily the best aspects of the prequels for giving us a taste of the bigger picture.

My favorite aspect was almost Kylo Ren, but his reveal happened far too soon. A character with potential to be extremely cool was turned into an angsty teenager. It almost seems as if he is a poor Sith because he mistakes his angst for the rage that a Sith requires. So instead, my actual favorite part was the lightsaber duel. Both of the characters involved have no reason to be experienced with a sword, and their lack of experience is really obvious on screen.

title: It took a long time for me to accept it, but this is a remake
review:
I have defended this title against all the possible critics it has. I have tried to justify director's choices and the validity of the plot. But what's on screen can't be denied. This movie is a remake.

I find the attempt to remake a movie so revered as 'Star Wars' a disloyalty to its legacy. Homages can be made in other media, but if you have the responsibility of extend a story that millions of people love, you have to do your best to create new elements, in one direction or another, but the worst thing you can do is to repeat what has been done, and what is considered to be unbeatable. I find in that an excess of pride or a lack of courage, or at least a terrible mistake, but repeating a movie is not a tribute. I found the first paralelism before the first scene ended. The plot copies are so many that they exceed the reference to become a mistake. Specially, I find the 'copy climax' in everything involving the new Death Star, but you can choose: main character's mysterious parentage, rebels in a hidden base, cantina, old mentor who lived the events of the past, etc.

And I feel so sorry for saying that, but the most hyped movie of history is far away from the expected level.

I won't join that hate wave that has grown through fans, because the movie has its positive elements. I find interesting the new ones. Kylo Ren is a good idea of villain, because, as J J Abrams said himself, you can't do anything better than Darth Vader. Also the character of Rey finds her own pace with a skilled and hard cover, but with a vulnerable heart. That idea of main characters who have grown up influenced by myths of the past suppose a resemblance with the viewer. Also Finn and his noble decisions are interesting elements. Finally, the lightsaber battle in a dark forest is a very good environment never seen.

But stop counting new elements there. And I won't speak about other details and problems, because I have argued about all of them for a long time. The movie has its own excuses to explain why Rey won the duel. The fail is greater than that. Why everything managed in 'Return of the jedi' is now destroyed, just to start from the same point, in a sand planet, with a plan in a droid....? We expected other things in Ep. VII. A Luke settled as a Jedi Master, a Leia leader of the New Republic, a new jedi order with new characters, two or three children of Han and Leia. What a wasted opportunity...

To mention it, because I find it fair, it's so good to see Star Wars back to the top of VFX effects, John Williams back to his saga, and one of the best cinema moments I had in this decade: watch the Star Wars title over the stars again in the big screen.

I find my 6/10 in those details and the fact that this can be an interesting title to those people who have never seen Star Wars. Because this is not a bad movie, is a bad Episode VII.

title: This Made Star Wars Fun Again!
review:
The Force Awakens isn't perfect entertainment and we should all stop pretending Star Wars movies as a whole have to be flawless(The Prequel Trilogy also gets held up to that kind of scrutiny, as well as The Original Trilogy). They're not THE films by which ALL movies must be compared to; films like Sunset Boulevard or Citizen Kane are more suited for that purpose to compare movies to because they were benchmark films that set the stage for Hollywood movies then onward, even though they weren't films driven by special effects. Cinema is an evolving art form and it's bound to repeat some things. Is that really a bad thing especially when the film in question is only a 'soft-reboot' and not a shot-by-shot remake of the original? I say no: it isn't. The Force Awakens is a blockbuster that's derivative but progressive, familiar but fresh. It's not perfect but it's Star Wars through and through.

Star Wars Episode VII: The Force Awakens was finally released in 2015 to audience, critical and commercial fanfare: it was named one of the AFI's Top 10 Films of 2015, grossed $U.S.2.07 billion at the global box office and was credited with revitalizing the Star Wars franchise. However, there were some ardent fans who criticized the film for its redundancies they wished weren't featured in the film, and I can understand those criticisms; I just don't agree with those who hold those issues against the film. The Force Awakens is an overdue visit from an old friend that you've been wanting to see again for years. And you find that the friend has made some notable changes since the last time you saw him. You see what was there before but you can also feel and embrace the new stuff as well; and that's very true for the story of The Force Awakens.

The Force Awakens is a blast to watch: it's intergalactic fun that honors the previous movies beautifully and manages to feel new while strictly being a self-aware Star Wars romanticist's film made for people who grew up on The Original Trilogy.

The Force Awakens gets 5/5 stars.

title: Loved it
review:
Being born in the 70's I'm part of the generation that grew up with the original trilogy. It was basically my childhood, the movies, action figures, magazines. I know the original trilogy inside out. I still watch the originals every two years or so, they still work for me, haven't lost any of their charm. I was almost 30 years old when the second coming was, and while I did see them at the movies once, I never really returned to those movies. I tried to watch them before Force Awakens, but didn't get past The Phantom Menace. I remember the two following movies were better, but still never got around watching them again.

I was waiting forward to seeing The Force Awakens like any other Star Wars fan. I'm not a huge fan of JJ Abrams and have been disappointed by quite a few reboots, prequels or late sequels like Indy 4, Star Trek and Prometheus, so I went to the theatre open minded. I was eager to see it, but I wasn't thinking if it would be good or bad, tried to stay neutral and thought that I don't HAVE TO like it at this age anymore.

But I loved it, totally loved it. It was quite close to being perfect in my opinion. Sure the story is a bit recycled, things happen quite conveniently and sometimes rushed, but the movie feels Star Wars. It feels very familiar without being tacky. It's just what Star Wars franchise needed in my opinion. It's difficult to know how new generations feel, but for those of us who lived the original trilogy, this was like coming home. Meeting old friends and immediately getting on like back in the days.

I had three major concerns before seeing this, even tho I tried to stay neutral. First being that it would be overly complicated, clever and tricky like I feel Abrams likes to do his TV and movies. Instead we got quite a straight-forward story without any unnecessary complexities or trying to be overly creative. Star Wars doesn't need a mind-boggling plot that pushes the boundaries of storytelling.

The other concern was that it would be made too violent and realistically grim. This is what has happened a lot of times with reboots and since movies and TV are completely different today in terms of violence than they were back in the day, I was fearing the worst. The first 10 minutes made me feel even more concerned as they may be quite intense (for the younger audience), but luckily the rest of the movie is quite tame. I have a son who is still a bit too young to see this, but who really waits forward to seeing it and this is the main reason I was a bit worried about how harsh they had made it. I'm happy they kept it the way it is.

The last concern was that it would feel forced, unnatural and cringe-worthy in terms of the acting and the old crew getting together. I was quite sure Harrison Ford could pull off his role as Han Solo, but Carrie Fisher as Leia and Mark Hamill as Luke were and are somewhat wildcards. We had no idea how they would do. Stop reading here if you don't want to read spoilers. Harrison Ford really IS Han Solo, he did absolutely perfect job. Carrie Fisher was still surprisingly Leia, I was a bit worried having watched a few of her interviews on youtube and not really seeing her act since The 'Burbs (1989). The scenes with her and Harrison are slightly on the stiff side, but they work OK, given they're characters past. Mark Hamill on the other hand. Well, we still have to wait and see.

The new cast is good. I especially enjoyed Adam Driver acting as Kylo Ren. Daisy Ridley is good too. Oscar Isaac is a capable actor as seen before, his scenes are quite brief here, but I'm sure there's a lot more to come. John Boyega was OK, but for some reason his character is not quite as interesting as the others. Domhnall Gleeson makes a great bad guy. Interesting to see if Max Von Sydow will be featured more in the next two episodes. It's amazing how long his career is as I just watched him on an Ingmar Bergman movie from the 50s!

Visually the movie is amazing. It works great, the places feel real. There are a few surprisingly CGI looking characters. Even one quite major character. Not saying they don't look good, but they look as if they are CGI, which is rarely a good thing.

Lot's and lot's of references to old trilogy. Never out of place tho. I'm going to see this again in the movies, and that's the first time watching the same movie twice in a theatre since the Return of the Jedi. One great thing about this new Star Wars episode is that it made me want to watch the original trilogy again, even tho I've just watched it last summer.

title: Great Movie, Period.
review:
First off, all the people giving this film low ratings just because their particular idea of what Star Wars 'should' be wasn't followed are all crazy. Crazy and wrong. There are legitimate criticisms to be made about The Force Awakens, but any reasonable analysis should see it for what it is -- a damn good Star Wars movie.

Yes, Rey is a Mary Sue. She just is, and all the people arguing against that point are just as wrong as the people who think the movie sucked. There's no real way to argue that she's not a perfect character who picked up on her skills a bit too fast to make sense. Rey is indeed a Mary Sue. It doesn't matter.

Yes, the film follows the same template as A New Hope. Same beats, same general storyline, same overall goals. Definitely. It doesn't matter.

Yes, the leads were chosen mostly because of a politically correct desire to get a woman and two minorities into the hero roles. This is also pretty obviously true. It doesn't matter.

What this film has going for is are characters that are genuinely likable, a story that is interesting while also being fun and whimsical, and cinematography, set design, and special effects that are absolutely brilliant which build a universe that you have no problem buying into. This -- above all -- is a fun movie, and it's true to the original Star Wars narrative a hundred percent.

The fact that the overall plot echoes so closely to A New Hope is actually a strength, I believe. It shows that history always repeats itself, and children are destined to walk in the footprints of their parents. It's a powerful message and I think it's one that is totally consistent with the entire story of Star Wars, with it's focus on the inescapable father/son/family dynamic and how there's really no escaping your destiny. I have no complaints there.

Rey being a Mary Sue was frankly only something I picked up on after I left the theater and gave it some thought. The fact that I didn't think of it during the movie is a testament to how great the writing was, but even now that I've come to the realization I just don't care. She was a very likable character, and frankly I can see explanations for most of her skills. It was established early in the film that she was resourceful and could handle herself in a fight, that she was good with machines, and that she could easily climb and scale the walls of massive starships. And I think her force powers came to her when Kylo Ren was attempting to enter her mind -- himself nowhere near as skilled or disciplined as a true Jedi master, and it backfired on him. Instead of Kylo entering her mind, she entered his and learned all about the force in that one instant. I can buy that, I just wish it was made a little more clear on screen.

J.J. Abrams had ONE overall job here -- to make Star Wars fun again. And he accomplished that beautifully. After the dreadful prequels, we needed a group of characters that everyone could enjoy and care about and a story that actually took you for a magical ride. We got that here. It was fantastic and I look forward to the next films.

title: An Awakening of the Star Wars Franchise
review:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens is the seventh entry in the Star Wars franchise. The Force Awakens is directed by J.J. Abrams, and stars Daisy Ridley, John Boyega, Adam Driver, Oscar Isaac, Harrison Ford, Carrie Fisher, Andy Serkis, Domhnall Gleeson, Mark Hamill, and a lot more people. The Force Awakens as I said is the continuation of the Star Wars saga, where a new menace is facing the galaxy, and only our old heroes with the help of some new ones can stop them from conquering the galaxy.

If you are like me you would know the huge amount of hype around this movie, everyone and I mean everyone was excited to see this movie. I remember watching the very first teaser trailer on Thanksgiving with my brother and being overwhelmed with pure excitement for the release of this movie, and wondering what Abrams was going to do with Star Wars. My excitement only grew as new trailers were released and the release date got closer. I went to see this movie with my two younger brother, on the opening day, and being blown away by this movie.

This movie showed me why I love Star Wars, when George Lucas made Star Wars back in the 70's, I don't think he knew what kind of cultural phenomenon he was creating. What I love about Star Wars is that there are an infinite amount of possibilities of things you can do in the Star Wars universe. What Abrams did with this movie was recapture that feeling of infinite possibilities within this universe. How he was able to recapture the feeling of the original trilogy, and put to shame the prequel trilogy. Know I know most people don't like the prequels, and I am one of them, but I don't think that they are that bad. But what Lucas failed to do in those films was to recapture the feel of the originals films, and he made them feel fake and artificial.

What I love most about The Force Awakens was its characters, new comers Rey, Finn, Poe Dameron, and Kylo Ren are greatly written and well realized characters. They bring new depth to the Star Wars universe and set up very interesting characters. The old comers Han Solo, Chewbacca, Leia, C-3PO, and R2-D2 are also well written, but other than Han Solo and Chewbacca the other original cast members don't get enough screen time. Some other new characters like Supreme Leader Snoke, Captain Phasma, Maz Kanata, and General Hux also have limited screen time, and I hope that in the next two episodes they get more screen time and character development.

Another good thing about the movie is the action scenes. Abrams is a really good director of action, as shown in Mission: Impossible III and the Star Trek movies, and he directs and shows the action very well. The light saber fight at the end of the movie is well handled and not giant and bloated, like the prequel era light saber fights. The aerial dogfights are also very well visualized, and very entertaining to watch. Another thing that deserves praise is the use of practical affects, the prequels are known for using mass amounts of CGI, and this movie knows how to use CGI as a tool and fill everything else in with practical affects, which really warmed my heart. Because I love when big blockbusters are reliant on practical affects and not CGI.

Negatives with the movie was as I said before were some of the characters who get pushed to the back and aren't given much screen time. But this could be fixed in the future installments in the franchise. Also the big super weapon in the movie, Starkiller Base was just another Death Star, and I thought that maybe Abrams and Kasdan could have come up with something better. Other than that it's just small nit-picks here and there.

Over all Star Wars: The Force Awakens is a fun enjoyable movie, with great characters, great direction, great action scenes, some not well realized characters, and a kind of cliché super weapon, and left me with pure excitement for the next two movies. I give Star Wars: Episode VII – The Force Awakens an A.

title: J.J. Abrams Has Restored Hope to the Star Wars Universe (no spoilers)
review:
I purposely waited 24 hours before writing my review because I wanted to digest the film that long to truly take it in and reflect before I actually reviewed it. I wanted the euphoria of seeing the next chapter of the saga on the big screen to subside some so that I can make an objective review, but alas the euphoria has not subsided and the childlike excitement is still at an 11! This is plain and simply a great Star Wars film! In fact, I feel it is the second best offering of the franchise (behind 'The Empire Strikes Back'). From the opening crawl to the epic and somewhat moving final scene the movie kept you on the edge of your seat.

Even now, 24 hours later, I'm still left in awe of what Abrams has done. He has ignited a passion in me that has lied dormant for a decade thanks to the dreadful prequel trilogy. After Episode III I vowed never to see another George Lucas Star Wars film ever again. The prequels were cheesy (and not in a good way) and lacked imagination. They borrowed heavily from the expanded universe (which flies in the face of his original assertion that he had planned out the prequels before Episode IV was even made) and spat in the face of Star Wars fans everywhere. Lucas is now (thankfully) out of the picture and in steps admitted Star Wars fan boy J.J. Abrams who is quickly establishing himself as this generations Steven Spielberg. Abrams intention was to reignite the franchise and call upon his own boyhood wonderment when seeing the original trilogy for the first time and try to recreate that with the sequel by meshing old and new to weave a new chapter in the saga. What Abrams has done so well here is he's managed to keep the older cast members relevant while also creating new characters who feel like they've always been part of the story. He's been able to expertly bridge the generation gap and bond the older cast members with the new ones to create a cohesive story that is not only enjoyable to watch, but really FEELS like a Star Wars film from the epic battle scenes, music, costumes, sets - every part of the film, even down to the bits and pieces that Rey scavenges oozes STAR WARS and it is fantastic.

I won't delve into the plot for fear of spoiling it, but the film obviously revolves around a core of new characters in the Star Wars Universe - Rey, a young scavenger who lives on the desert planet of Jakku, Finn a former Stormtrooper who is desperate to escape the clutches of The First Order, Poe Dameron the top fighter pilot of the Resistance and his trusty droid BB-8, and Kylo Ren, a member of the First Order and a wannabe Sith who acts as the main antagonist of the film. There are other supporting cast including General Hux, a First Order General, Captain Phasma, the leader of the Stormtroopers, Maz Kanata, a pirate and collector of artifacts, and Supreme Leader Snoke who is the leader of the First Order. Several former characters are weaved into the film with Han Solo and Chewbacca seeing the majority of the screen time from that group. The connection between old and new is a constant theme in the film and it is pulled off masterfully. The film is an emotional roller-coaster from beginning to end and is a movie that I will always cherish thanks to it's re- ignition of my love for the franchise. There isn't much more that I can say other than if you are even remotely a fan of the Star Wars Universe you owe it to yourself to see this. Even if you are not, there is a lot to keep you entertained here and you never know, it may turn you into a fan of the franchise if you're not careful, regardless quit reading this and go see it!

title: Loved it. Will be seeing multiple times while in theatres.
review:
I don't think this review will contain plot spoilers, but just in case...

Yesterday: I ranked the movies from best to worst - V, IV, VI, III, I/II (tied for last).

I'll start by saying this: I am a huge star wars fan. I've read many of the canon and non-canon books, have seen all of the films dozens of times, have watched them in various orders (nod to machete cut), and have collected trading and decipher playing cards. I named my dog Obi Wan Kenobi. I love star wars.

I was hugely disappointed by the hollow prequels. My buddies and I lined up in front of the theatre on Eglinton in Toronto at 2 in the afternoon for the midnight showing on the eve of episode I's release and were crestfallen when the movie was garbage. And then the rest of the prequel trilogy stunk too. Jar jar Binks, metichlorians, weak sith apprentices (Maul was cool but would have been cooler if he hadn't croaked in the first film), whiny dark lords and half-assed attempts at romance et al. So I was apprehensive about this film, especially since it's been hyped up so much (like episode I had been).

Lo and behold, for me the film lived up to the hype! It was a two hour nod to the original series, and I loved it. I've read other reviews and seen how disappointed others have been. "It's predictable", "Events in the film occurred needlessly", "It was funny when it shouldn't have been", "Characters weren't what they should have been", "It's not a sequel but a remake", and the list goes on.

In my opinion, this film is everything that J.J. Abrams an the writing team meant for it to be. Conflicted characters WERE MEANT TO BE CONFLICTED. It was meant to recycle the plot devices of A New Hope. "Events" (wink) that occurred achieved precisely what they were meant to achieve and created traction for plot events that I'm sure will occur in VIII and IX. It ended just the way it needed to. Awesome.

Effects: the dogfighting (aerial battling) was the best I have ever seen in film. The use of 3D was the best I have seen on the big screen. They used just the right balance of CGI and costumed characters. The lasers and lightsabres looked better than they ever have. The decision to film on site made the locations look lived in and real (such a relief after I, II and III). Perfect.

I'll just stop there because I don't think I am saying anything that hasn't been said already. Go see this film, it is definitely worth it.

Today: V, VII, IV, VI, III, I/II (tied for last).

title: Feeling 9 years old again. (spoilers)
review: Yes. I get it some of the old fans are disappointed. The feel that to much things were to obvious. Fact is many of those fans didn't go to the first movie in 1977. The Force Awakens had one daunting task to begin with, bring back the magic. JJ Abrams delivered. The FA makes it painfully clear that although George Lucas came up with the best science fiction story ever didn't really get what made it good. Just because he could look at it from a healthy distance. If he would have all the technology of the 90ties available he would probably never had so much success. He is a creator great at imagining all of it. But all as not so good at portraying dialog and emotions. JJ Abrams was first fan. He could feel what made his heart beat faster. Therefore he could make the right decisions of what to put into the FA. I hear many complain about the plot but all of them are crazy about part 4,5 and 6. All of those plots are pretty thin and repetitive. If I would be really rude to those plots I could summarize them as: a battle between good and evil and at the end of the movie, good wins by destroying the death star. Everybody was fine with it. Of course good and bad also happened to be family but guess what that's also the case in 7. In fact this movie is the perfect sequel if you look at the pattern of 4 5 and 6. Each time a death star is destroyed the empire rebounds with a new bigger better and stronger weapon. It fits perfectly that the Republic opted for a death planet. Now everybody who complains about similarities in storyline do not include the possibilities that can evolve from the cast of characters and their backgrounds. The FA needed to serve the older fans but also the newbies. I think that 10 to 20 percent have not seen the part 4 5 and 6. For them nothing is familiar. Rey is awesome. She is a genuine believable strong female character. With a both muscular yet appealing physic. She displays the right kind of emotions. The fact that she learns to do the Force on her own isn't a bad thing for me. It fits her character. As a scavenger she is used to try and do things herself. She is not a Luke who was raised in the warmth of a family. It was for that reason that Luke was firstly a kid that was spoiled a bit and got through most of his time wining. Rey doesn't wine. She does what needs to be done on her own. Poe is basically the pilot that Han Solo was. Witty and full of himself. He has all the potential to be better than Han in terms of character. Finn is interesting because he is basically scared as can be but has the inner sense for justice and will fight for if it needs be. My gut feeling says that he has the force. What makes Kylo Ren so interesting is the level of instability. He is more mentally instable than most of the serial killers in any other movie. Which could lead to interesting developments in the sequels. Of course the sequels will have a more elaborate part for Luke who will most likely act as a mentor for Rey. JJ Abrams did an excellent job in reviving that good old feeling. I think now and only now the franchise is ready for more ingenious plot-twists. If he had done that now we would be lost in space ourselves.

title: The Force is Back! Quick No Spoiler Review
review:
The Force Awakens, and it is back! J.J. Abrams has erased the mistakes of episodes I-III and has brought us a gem.

Both fans and non-fans alike will like this movie. There are enough shout outs to the originals to keep the traditionalists happy. There is plenty of humor, but its not campy humor. It works. And that's how the movie is. It works. It's Star Wars as we remember it from the originals. The world id grimy and gritty. It is real. Not some green screen abomination.

The actors are great. You will love Boyega as Finn. I had my doubts but he quickly grew to be a favorite character. And Daisy Ridley in my opinion should be a contender for best actress.

Bottom line is that if you are a Star Wars fan you will not be disappointed. Not one bit. I put this episode right behind Empire Strikes Back. That says a lot. 10 out of 10 for me. Perfect? Almost. This is Star Wars at its best.

title: Not another angry review
review: I must say that people need to calm down about calling this movie a rip off of the first one. Yes, the movie does take the structure of the plot from the Star Wars: A New Hope, but summing up a movie in 5 sentences and based on that saying that they are the same is just plain ignorance. The characters are different, they have different views, different goals and the character development goes very nicely in hand with that. Instead of a the mighty antagonist, that was Darth Vader, we have someone who is driven to the dark side by the fear from the lack of his own skills. If you know a little bit about the extended universe, you know that this is often the driving force behind turning to the dark side. Also the view from the point of a stormtrooper adds a lot to the story and finally we see them as more than just objects to be killed. Rey, which is the force sensitive main character, comes completely from a different background than Luke and feels much more mentally grown up, than he was, when we met him. Also this time the main character does not go to save someone just because he likes her appearance. All in all the movie has a similar STRUCTURE as the old Star Wars movies but it also feels different and fresh. I have left the cinema with a smile on my face and looking forward to watching it again.

title: Force is Strong with This One
review:
I saw the last chain in the Star Wars series with my wife yesterday. It has been a while since the last Star Wars movie hit the theaters and "a long" while since we saw a "good" Star Wars movie.

As a huge fan of Star Wars this movie is a solid next link in the most expected film series - and is the first step on the right direction since (sorry Lucas)those terrible prequels with the exception of Revenge of the Sith.

When I saw the negative comments I was upset but after seeing the movie my hopes were replenished for ahead. I strongly recommend you to see this movie, it is a must for any fan of Star Wars or Sci-fi, and a great watch for any cinema enthusiast.

I won't talk about positive aspects (And Believe me there is a great deal of them) but I have to address some so-called negatives, because I feel there is a lot of unjust criticism going on. There will be mild spoilers Beware.

***Spoilers Ahead***

This film follows in the footsteps of the original trilogy, especially "A New Hope". There is again two military factions with different names, there is again a sand planet and again a super weapon capable of destroying entire planets. Well all of these sound familiar but this film is the start of a new story. Remember going on a familiar road at the start is something many of us do in our lives when we embark upon a new journey. Many say there isn't enough depth to the history between this film and Return of The Jedi, why the republic didn't prevail, why there are no jedis, why Kylo Ren is lost? Well it is impossible to put all those background stories into one film, remember we didn't learn until prequels why there is a galactic empire in the first place so patience is the key.

Again this film is "A Renewed Hope", go and see it.

title: Review from a Fan and Realistic Point of View
review:
First of all, I created this account entirely to review this movie and give an explanation that most die-hard Star Wars fans should understand, as well as those who enjoy Star Wars in general and were looking forward to an excellent movie.

Without spoiling any details of the movie or revealing anything, I would like to touch on one of the most fundamental aspects of the movie that most people have varying opinions on.

"Heavily influenced by the old trilogy"

This movie has a high influence from the old trilogy, especially because of the actors we know from the previous films. Some people say it is way too much influenced, such as Kylo Ren being a masked villain with a cool voice, or there being similar references to the past such as a giant base that has a huge destructive power, etc.

But think about it from this way. If we had a completely new storyline, with only new characters, no influence from the old trilogy, and a bold new way to show Star Wars. We would most likely have the same disappointment as some people have with the Prequels. Too new ideas, concepts that seem weird, within more complaints.

What I am trying to say is, that with this film, and the way it ended as well as some events in the middle that had a huge impact on viewers.. This was by far the best way to give a continuation of the old trilogy, whilst tying in a new story yet to come, with new characters, new concepts, new villains, and an even more possibilities. We would never warm up to those new characters as easily, unless we had the old actors reprise their roles to give meaning to this galaxy.

In regards of screen writing and directing, this was the best anyone could've done with a Star Wars sequel, as it gave a perfect balance of old and new. The entire movie can be seen as a trailer to a universe yet to come, not as a just a sequel. It is a stepping stone for a future for Star Wars fans.

title: I cant believe nobody "gets" it .....#Spoliers
review:
****POTENTIAL SPOILERS*****

Just returned from the theater, and decided to come to IMDb to see what everyone was saying, and I am appalled by how many people just don't get whats going on here.....

So many people saying its a reboot, and a bad one. They are clearly mistaken, and clueless as to how the Star Wars universe works. So may comparing it to Episode 1, and with good reason, BUT its NOT a reboot, and its not a re-hash. Sure there are similarities but they were all used for good reason, and to bring the new story to light. JJ himself said it was an homage to the original trilogy, and it completely was. Sure a lot was the same, but "from a different point of view"

Lets discuss the similarities.....

1. Desert planet that a lone force force user is on alone. This is VERY poignant to the story and shows us that everyone dreams of being in the stars. This is a very big part of the Star Wars universe, always has been, even in the post trilogy books. Clearly anyone who understands the Star Wars universe, or is a real fan will understand this.

2. Starkiller Base is a massive "Death Star".... what did you really think that this would change? Why? its still the Empire, and they clearly feel they have the upper hand being able to destroy entire star systems. It's the intimidation factor, same tactic they have used in all the movies, books, and comics.

3. Father vs Son - This is the ultimate struggle in the universe. Everyone wants to be better then their father, everyone fights with their father, and everyone at times wishes they were dead. Why would this change? It's been the same story for years... IT Is THE STORY OF STAR WARS!! It wouldn't be a STAR WARS movie without this struggle.

Clearly those of you reviewing this movie badly do not understand Star Wars or the Star Wars universe. The movie was amazing, had great plot points, and a terrific ending. The throwback dialog was great, and really dragged you into the Star Wars universe, the similarities between the new characters and old made it FEEL like Star Wars, and the story, although slightly re-hashed MAKES IT a Star Wars movie.

For true fans of the the Star Wars universe this is the PERFECT sequel, and it makes you feel at home.

title: Awesome
review: It's better than you'd expect. Lots of twists, and LOTS OF NOSTALGIA. You get to see everything, and i mean EVERYTHING you want in a star wars movie. The graphics are certainly a lot better, everything is much more advanced. The whole movie in the end would want you to wait for the next one, however, it's great. New characters are great, actors are okay. Ray was spectacular, Finn was good as well. Harrison Ford had a big role in the movie, unlike what the trailers suggest. Disney has certainly added it's good touches, unlike what I expected. The sith had a good role, actor was okay, It was the general sith stories, what you'd expect to be honest. However, lots of unpredictable questions came up.

title: A Good Start to a New Trilogy
review:
Looking at the trailers for this film, I was worried The Force Awakens would have a tone closer to an original JJ Abrams film than to the original Star Wars movies. Boy was I wrong. This film has all the quip and action of the original trilogy, making it an enjoyable ride for this viewer. The only differences in style are actually improvements: the cinematography and the image quality.

However, this movie is not without its set of flaws. I suppose when you're expecting a full trilogy you should expect the story to set up elements that will be revisited later in the trilogy. However, looking back at the original Star Wars (now titled A New Hope) we received a strong stand-alone film, and I would have liked to see that with episode 7 rather than ending the film on somewhat of a cliffhanger.

I was also a little disappointed with the new villain Kylo Ren, to be honest. It is pretty cool when you find out who he actually is, but that does not make up for the fact that he is susceptible to temper tantrums and there seems to be no real reason for him to wear the mask aside from the fact that it pays tribute to Darth Vader and gives him more of a threatening presence. Also, just like Vader having the emperor above him, we see Lord Snoke communicating with Kylo Ren and the other "leader" of the First Order (Domhnall Gleeson) but we don't yet know much about him. Hopefully we will get more of an explanation with the next installment of the trilogy.

The new cast members bring new life to the series in a positive way. Finn, Rey, and Poe are the main characters (aside from Kylo Ren) that are made up of these newcomers, and Poe is played by Oscar Isaac, who has had great performances in Inside Llewyn Davis and Ex Machina, which released earlier in 2015. Finn is the stormtrooper gone good who you can't help but root for as he tries to impress Rey. Rey essentially has the same role as Luke did in the original Star Wars, and she does a fantastic job at being a bad-ass character. We don't see as much of Poe as I would have hoped, but the story in the film could not have started without him. I hope they don't throw Oscar Isaac under the bus in the next installments; he has great potential.

This film is good fun, but one can't help comparing The Force Awakens to Star Wars (A New Hope) in a number of different ways. 1) A droid with important information is the MacGuffin of the film. 2) Rey is from the desert planet of Jakku, lacking adventure in her life. 3) The First Order is basically The Empire with a new name. I'll stop there to avoid revealing too much.

The Force Awakens is a decent way to start this sequel trilogy, and while this installment nearly lived up to the original trilogy, I am hoping the next installments will succeed at doing just that.

3.0/4.0

title: Brilliant film! Star Wars is BACK!!!
review:
Firstly, a note to the haters of this film, who refer to themselves as 'die hard fans' who have been bashing and nitpicking this film...the expanded universe is gone. Let it go. Also, the Thrawn Trilogy is gone too, and will not be made into a film. Let it go.

*breathe out. calm.*

This film absolutely blew me away. After the prequels debacle, I held strong reservations about any modern Star Wars film. I was wrong this time. Star Wars The Force Awakens is a brilliant, fast paced, exciting film.

The two leads, Daisy Ridley and John Boyega shine as Rey and Finn, much to the chagrin of the minority of'die hard' (read 'stubborn, conceited) old fans, I feel. They do an excellent job of picking up the mantle. They have a real chemistry on screen, not bogged down with romantic rubbish.

Harrison Ford and Peter Mayhew are on top form as Han Solo, and Chewbacca, adding a fun nod back to the originals.

Another welcome return is Carrie Fisher as General Leia, who comes across as war weary, and wracked with guilt (not saying why)

Finally, we have the two polar opposites. Oscar Isaacs as the heroic Poe Dameron, and Adam Driver as the evil Kylo Ren. Both are outstanding in their respective roles.

The action scenes crackle with almost tangible energy, the music is amazing, and there is a surprising amount of humour.

JJ Abrams has nailed it with this one, and I highly recommend seeing it with family, as these are the intended audience.

Destined to be a classic!

title: The Force is back....but a little too familiar
review:
Months before I entered the packed theater to witness history in the making, I avoided any and all contact with the trailers and social media, because I don't have social media. I went in with all my knowledge of the old films. And I will admit, I was quite impressed with what Abrams had to offer.

The original characters hadn't changed a bit and the new ones were introduced very smoothly. Had your good ole Star Wars action scenes and famous character lines. The music was just right and the effects were phenomenal. Disney didn't seem to bother restraining from the violence either. The problem? Throughout the whole film, I was like "that happens in Episode IV, and that, and that, and that , and that." A bunch of the scenarios in the story were recycled; recycled to the point when you knew what was going to happen next. Of course some material from the classic movies was going to be brought back, but Abrams went a little too far in this department. As if he ran out ideas and decided to just use some stuff from the old movies.

Overall, it succeeds as a Star Wars movie. I'm glad I wasn't mind blown, for the strict purpose of the next film being a step up. 3/4*

title: Too much of a loving homage to the originals, too afraid to be its own film
review:
I wasn't really interested in seeing this after the prequels turned me off of the Star Wars universe as a whole but I went with a friend who wanted to see it, so that was my attitude going in.

The second 1/3 of the movie was more or less able to be called original but the first and last portions were basically a carbon copy of A New Hope with an extra light-saber battle thrown in.

As expected, the visuals were top-notch but without a decent story or good characters or at least well-acted ones, a film cannot captivate. This was not the problem for a majority of the film but for a few minor characters. The newcomers portraying Rey and Finn were terrific, they should be credited as capably carrying the film but for the stakes in this story it seemed unfitting that they were so young, at least without being accompanied by someone older from the start.

It was hard feeling the nostalgia of anyone other than Chewbacca because all the returning cast look so much different than they did in the original trilogy, but they did perform adequately. The character Kylo Ren's performance was slightly below average.

Overall I would have preferred more information during the opening crawl, a lot of things were left unclear as a result and degraded the amount of enjoyment and understanding of the film and story. It's likely that whether unintended or not, this was tailored for younger audiences to enjoy and less so for adults. It's still somewhat fun at parts but there is a bit too much drag and a lot more needless depressing moments than necessary. Darker does not always equal better.

title: A New Hope Part II ????
review:
Whether you're a Star Wars fan or just someone looking for a entertaining movie to watch you will probably enjoy this film. However, being a huge, huge Star Wars fan I had some issues with the film and I rank The Force Awakens fifth in the canon. The Empire Strikes Back, A New Hope, Revenge of the Sith, Return of the Jedi, The Force Awakens, The Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones.

The story was a retread of A New Hope and that was my biggest issue with this film. The story starts out on a desert planet, a droid stranded on a desert planet with a secret mission, the villains are after the droid, a daring rescue at the enemy's base, and a last ditch effort against impossible odds by good guys to destroy the galaxy's most dangerous weapon. Sound familiar? Furthermore, all the characters mirror the New Hope characters, Rey (Luke), Finn (Han), BB8 (R2-D2) Kylo Ren (Darth Vader), Han (Obi-Wan). I really thought with Lawrence Kasdan writing the script that he would have come up with something more original. Not another Death Star (Death Planet) its already been done twice. There's so many other ways they could have gone with this. Not A New Hope again. George Lucas already made that movie and it was perhaps the greatest movie of all time.

Next, Han Solo was just killed and Chewie and company return back to the resistance's base and when he gets off the Millennium Falcon he and Leia walk pass each other and say nothing. Not so much as a look. Han best friend and the love of Han's life who have known each other for thirty five years and they say nothing to each other not so much as a word or even a hug to console each other. Then Leia goes and meets Rey whom she has never met and they hug. What? Now I have a theory that Leia has a bond with Rey on some level, I won't go in to detail, but Leia and Chewie should have had moment.

Then there is Supreme Leader Snork a horrible rip off of the Emperor with really lousy name. Snork really? They couldn't come up with something better. Was he named after the 1980's Saturday morning cartoon? They couldn't have had a younger villain maybe middle age character that was maybe a Dark Force wielding agent who worked for the Emperor or Darth Vader when the events of ROTJ took place. No we get Emperor part two. His age doesn't really make sense. I would think if there was a powerful being with dark force power that he would have been a threat to the Emperor and Vader and they would have eliminated him.

The Star Wars movies have always had a great secondary villain, such as Darth Maul, Grand Moff Tarkin, Boba Fett, and in the Force Awakens they have Captain Phasma, but she is in the movie for like five minutes. I was really looking to seeing Gwendoline Christie and the character she was playing. They should have given her a bigger role.

I hate to say this, but one of my biggest disappointments was the soundtrack. I love John Willliams and if this was some other movie the soundtrack would have been fine, but the soundtrack had no memorable themes. Look back to every Star Wars movie and the soundtracks have been magnificent and have had memorable themes in each one. The Phantom Menace had "The Duel of the Fates" Revenge of the Sith "Battle of Heroes" then there is A New Hope and The Empire Strikes Back. Those two movies soundtracks are so incredible and have so many memorable themes that I would have to list several.

Despite all this the movie was good and it brought back some nostalgic feelings of the originals, even though it was basically a remake of ANH. The movie had good action humor, and some cool new characters (Rey, Finn and especially BB8). Having grown up with originals when they were released I was a little worried that J.J. Abrams would mess this up like the Star Trek Movies, but I must say he did a pretty good job. Abrams really captured the look and feel of a Star Wars movie. Abrams did a great job of mixing in the new cast with the old and I thought that the Cinematography was great. The camera movement was really good and really followed the action well, especially during the Millennium Falcon Tie Fighter dogfight.

Daisy Ridley was awesome as Rey. I'm looking forward to see her become a Jedi and follow in the footsteps of Luke and Anakin...hint, hint previously mention theory. I think from what I saw of her in this film that she'll be able to carry the next two movies.

The best thing about this movie was Harrison Ford's performance. He did fantastic job carrying this movie and had a lot of funny moments in the film. Han Solo has been sorely missed and will be sorely missed moving forward with the new series. Looking back if you look at all the movies he was in and wasn't in the saga Harrison Ford really had or was part of most of the funny moments throughout the saga. They are going to have a big challenge moving forward without him in the films.

I give the film eight stars out of ten and I can't rank it any higher than fifth in the Star Wars saga due largely in part to the retread of the story line taken from A New Hope and the other issues I mentioned. It was a good movie and I would certainly see it again, but it was a flawed Star Wars movie.

title: A very enjoyable film
review:
First of all, this is my first review, sorry in advance for my English.

I'll have to start with the criticism this film gets. You have to read one other review in IMDb and you'll see. title: Best Star Wars Movie, Not the Best Movie
review:
I came into Star Wars 7 with hesitant excitement, hyped over the prospect of a new Star Wars movie and cool looking footage which seemed to have a more serious vibe, and dubious over the villain. After seeing the movie, I feel both satisfied and disappointed, but looking forward to the next stage of this new trilogy.

The things that I liked/loved about the movie. I liked the main characters, Rey and Fin, the different personalities, backstory and relationship. Rey, a woman living on the desert planet Jakku who dreams of more (the shot where it shows the old woman opposite her cleaning the junk while she also does it was particularly symbolic and subtle)and Fin, a rogue storm trooper who makes the decision to go against the First Order. Harrison Ford's Han Solo was great and didn't feel forced, and the general atmosphere of the movie was great, with practical sets, dialogue and realism of the Original Trilogy Star Wars. BB-8 is probably my favourite droid, the perfect combination of cuteness and usefulness (the scene where he gives Fin the thumbs up with the light!).

However, the film suffers from the "Abrams Effect", where a rebooted or soft rebooted film franchise has to try bridge the gap between the old fans who don't want the new movie to be different to the movie they love and the new generation who don't care and just want an exciting experience. Abrams did this rather well with 2009's Star Trek, getting rid of a lot of the smaller Star Trek details, going back to the original Spock and Kirk, and adding in the action and explosions that the general audience crave for these days. Abrams once again did, and succeeded, with his direction of Star Wars 7, but I believe goes too far.

Firstly, the plot is a complete recycle of Star Wars (A New Hope) and has elements from Empire and Return which seems propelled by coincidence rather than human intervention. A droid is carrying information vital to the Resistance (Rebellion) that the First Order (the Empire) and a Sith Lord (Darth Vader) want. Along the way the droid encounters an unknown named Rey (Luke) on a desert planet called Jakku (Tatooine) with hidden Force abilities which they use to stop the First Order, meeting Han Solo and Chewbacca and also having to destroy the new StarKiller Base (Death Star) by destroying the shield reactor (Return of the Jedi). At least George Lucas tried to make an unique story with the prequels, this story had little originality and makes me want to know what Lucas had in store with his new trilogy (not that I want them to be movies that is). The story took me out of the movie completely and at the end left me more disappointed.

Secondly, the dialogue, although for the most part excellent, just had too many Marvel-like quips. For me, the beginning jokes landed for me such as the BB-8 thumbs up, the Millennium Falcon reveal and Fin telling himself not be nervous and Poe getting confused, but these jokes happen too much for me and also took me out of the film. They may have made me chuckle, but it seemed less Star Wars and more catering to the new post-Marvel generation (which I am becoming quickly sick of the one liners and quips).

Thirdly, the CGI, which is 95% great, was particularly noticeable in the Falcon and two of the CGI characters we are introduced to, Maz Kanata(?) and Snoke, although this is probably due to how much practical sets are in this movie and that contrast.

Now BIG SPOILERS talk such as Kylo Ren and big reveals. Skip to the last paragraph if you don't want these (although most people have probably seen the movie by now).

Kylo Ren is a mixed bag for me. When I came out of the cinema I hated him, as I expected, but now I'm just not sure. He is introduced as this ultimate badass character who can read minds, stop blaster shots and is seemingly pro with his lightsabre and has a distraught past with his parents Han and Leia. But as soon as his face is revealed (which I am disappointed by the lack of anything memorable on his face) he is turned into a wimp, who has temper tantrums, gets easily beaten by someone who just learnt they were force sensitive and needs more training. Although this is good for a character development standpoint, I just dislike this sudden change of character, make him either badass or an apprentice, not both.

Han Solo's death was rather obvious, making you say "I knew that was going to happen!" rather than "Oh no!". His death tries to parallel the Obi Wan Kenobi death in A New Hope, succeeds to a certain degree (the grazing of Kylo/Ben's face was touching, no pun intended), I am left ultimately feeling like it didn't matter.

Captain Phasma was wasted, Poe Dameron didn't do anything for me, and Luke's 15 second end shot seemed forced in for the Star Wars fans who wanted Mark Hamill to be in it (including me).

If I seem to so many gripes with the movie, then why am I giving it 7/10? Because despite of its flaws, I have seen it twice and I am excited to see the next two in the trilogy, and Abrams did a great job of incorporating the best of the Original Trilogy, more or less discarding the Prequels and adding in the action and humour touches that the modern audience want. Star Wars The Force Awakens, in my opinion, is the best Star Wars made, it just leaves too many different sequel bait moments and "rhymes" too much with the Original Trilogy to give it the 10/10 I hope that it would get.

title: A tiny bit disappointed, but a great Star Wars experience!
review:
In my opinion, this is a solid 7,5/10 movie,but Mr.IMDb doesn't let us give half-ratings, so i'm giving Force Awakens an 8/10. Here's why:

First of all, i'd like to acknowledge that every single review that gives this film a rating below 6/10 is just a try to get the attention of others, with the author being a drama queen that just wants to rant over everything.

And let's begin with the review. First and foremost, PRACTICAL EFFECTS for god's sake. The aesthetics of the old trilogy is back! Beautiful practical beings in every scene. This gave the opportunity to every hater in the world to post irrelevant reviews about the movie. I've even seen people that put The Force Awakens in the same group with Holiday Special. Oh boy...
