title: Not flawless but very satisfying.
review:
First of all, how everyone seems to forget that Kylo Ren was shot with a weapon that kills armed stormtroopers with one shot? That's why Finn and Rey managed to fight with him. It was seen earlier in the movie that Rey can fight, so is it a big surprise that she could keep up with a wounded Sith apprentice. Rey was connected to the force which gave her an advantage. I have to admit the one scene where Kylo acted like a teenager, was a disappointment for me. I'm talking about the one in which he destroyed the room with his light saber (again). It ate away Kylo Ren's credibility. But in this case, the Sith in this movie is really a person you wish would die. J.J Abrams made you hate the villain, because of Han. The former villains, especially Vader, were admired. Hating the villain might turn out to be a good thing in the upcoming films.

Han Solo dies. That sucks, but it's not a secret that Harrison Ford himself wanted Han to die in either episode V or VI. In addition Ford told the press that three movies were enough for him. Maybe this is how they got Harrison to star in this film!

Visually the film is excellent. It has no flaws or too much CGI. Dialogue between the new characters, especially Rey and Finn is brilliant. The movie even has great humor in it. I would have liked to see more of the old stars, especially Luke. Han and Chewie were excellent, the new droid was funny and likable. Leia wasn't quite so determined and strong as in the old trilogy. C-3PO had it's moments again.

The movie definitely gave audience wonderful moments of nostalgia, thats what I expected the most.

The plot was quite a surprise being so similar to episode IV. Wonder if that ever crossed the minds of the makers of the script. Nevertheless there was so much good and new in it that you shouldn't be mad about a little similarity. The other movies in the making are most likely not gonna be similar to V and VI at all?

It wasn't flawless. The Han-Leia-son-storyline wasn't as deep as it could've been. It lacked motion. Some more gaps in the storyline should've been filled in my opinion. For example the Kylo Ren's turning in to the dark side. New music in the film wasn't anything out of the ordinary, nothing stunning. There's still a lot to improve, but this is a great start for a new saga! The actual rating might around 8.2-4, but I'll give it a Star Wars bonus!

title: Good attempt at nostalgia
review:
I think this was definitively a good attempt at nostalgia, however I believe they most certainly recycled way too much of the original 1977 Star Wars IV- A New Hope, only with a new filter.

Excellent special effects and CGI, however, it seems to me that JJ Abrams was a little too afraid of not getting it just right. So in order to play it safe for Disney, he simply reused what worked from the original, or better yet, originals.

Films in my opinion are about gambling with new attempts and different ideas, and just like with actual gambling, there can never be a sure way in film industry, and when filmmakers use too much of by the boom methods, something get's lost.

Hence because a few gambles were made, I believe in my opinion, that it somehow missed the mark.

title: Way, way better than the prequels...review from a huge fan
review:
I'm almost 40, which means I saw two of the original three movies in the theater as a kid. I had all of the old toys, stupidly threw them all into the bathtub and wrecked them and constantly begged my parents for my own light saber.

Take all of the annoying garbage from the prequels and toss them out. The horribly sappy dialogue, the horrible acting, constantly changing outfits every scene and annoying characters (Jar Jar) that refuse to go away. You'll thankfully get none of that this time.

When I saw that JJ Abrams was in charge, I knew at the very least we'd get a solid attempt with this new trilogy. We definitely got that, and a little bit more. Just a little. It felt like he knew what the old die hards wanted to see. He also managed to find some really good actors. I knew Oscar Isaac would be good, but I didn't know the Rey or FIN characters at all. All three did a great job, but I was particularly impressed with Adam Driver. Being a great goof-off on Girls doesn't necessary mean you can be a key character in a Star Wars movie, but he did a super job. It's a grittier, more human movie with far more interesting characters.

For the most part Abrams played it safe, nailing the action scenes and adding some quirky CG animal characters. But he did try a few things that worked. For example, we've never seen a non-Jedi handle a light saber, and I thought that was very cool. There could have been more light saber action, but what you do see is very well done and believable.

The real test was taking my six year old daughter to the movie, the most exciting part for me. She hasn't watched any of the old movies yet, but she spent most of the movie with her eyes half-covered. That's always a good thing. She loved it, and now she's asking me to play the first movie for her to see. So thanks Disney, you passed the test.

title: A good, if flawed, film.
review:
It's finally here! Yes, this film does exist and isn't just a figment of everyones imagination. The most anticipated film of all time has finally landed. So, the question on everyones mind is, how good is it? (No, the question isn't, is it any good?) I think that by now everyone is convinced that This film will be good. But how good is it? The answer to this question is, it is perfectly adequate. Now, don't tear me to pieces quite yet. Here me out first and if you still want my head on a silver platter, that's fine. 'The Force Awakens' takes place roughly thirty years following the events of episode six or 'Return of the Jedi'. But this time we follow some new faces.

Yes, the central protagonist of the original trilogy (Luke) is long gone. And we are left with two new faces. Rey, played by Daisy Ridley and Finn, John Boyega. Finn is a stormtrooper for a new empire called The New Order. Who seems to be following in the very large footsteps of Darth Vader. Needless to say, these are bad dudes. And Finn recognizes this very early on and escapes to Jakku.

This is where we met Rey. A scavenger that roots through wrecked star ships to try and survive. These two join together in an attempt to escape Kylo Ren and the first order. It's a fairly simple story that has some great twists and turns. Twists that I will refrain from spoiling in this review.

Aside from an interesting story 'The Force Awakens' offers some of the best sequences in any Star Wars movie. Thanks to careful direction from Abrams and spectacular set pieces we get some of the coolest action scenes of the year. It's easily the best looking and feeling Star Wars in the franchise. It's gorgeous to look at and a blast to watch.

Not to mention it has a great cast and compelling characters. This is what I loved about this film. As the film moves along we see sides of the old characters that we never have. And the new ones are given their own distinct identities. The film wisely doesn't go to far though. It gives them just enough for us to care about them but not so much where the next films will lack new development. This allows Boyega and Ridley to shine in their respective roles.

But this is not a perfect film. The most noticeable flaw was the lack of one central character. In the original trilogy there is certainly a slew of characters but there is no doubt that Luke Skywalker is the lead. 'The Force Awakens' doesn't have anyone like that. It takes so long introducing everyone that is going to be in the films, that no one becomes the actual star until the bitter end of the movie. We jump between so many different character subplots that it's sometimes hard to keep everything in line.

There are other flaws like Gleeson feeling severely out of place, clashing between VFX and practical effects, and a handful of continuity errors but I will only touch on one more. Kylo Ren. While he himself is not a mistake, but the way the film handles him is. He is easily the most complex character in the entire film. This is because the film gives him (as I felt) a full, three film arc. By the end I was unsure where the next films could go with him because he feels like he has already reached his full arch. ​ 'The Force Awakens' is far from a perfect film. It's bloated, melodramatic, and sometimes even clumsy. But there is no denying that it's a blast to watch. It's able to introduce new characters into its universe with ease. While, simultaneously, being one of the coolest, sleekest films to release this year.

title: As expected
review:
This movie was very, very, FUN. It was not perfect; but then again, I don't think any of the Star Wars movies are perfect.

This movie definitely pays homage to the original movies in more ways than you can count. While some people think of it as a cop out, or a bad reboot of the series, I think of it as a way of paying respect, and giving people who love these movies exactly what they want. They want Star Wars. They want light saber battles, storm troopers battling it out with the good guys, stupid cheesy dialogue, giant weapons of mass destruction of ungodly scales, and guns that go 'pew pew'.

The best part of the movie, at least imo, ancient, crusty, hints at the original movies. The obvious Star Destroyer that we see in the trailer; plus a few others that I won't spoil.

Speaking of spoilers; it takes a certain person, or persons, with a heart of coal, to seriously go and spoil major parts of the movie for everyone else. Sadly that's what I, and I'm sure everyone else (because I'm still sadly seeing the same spoiler thrown out) had to deal with. Even while waiting in line just to get into the movie.

That aside, the movie was still fun, and tugs hard at the heart strings. This movie did exactly what I wanted it to do. It made me smile, clap, and want more.

title: Fun for the whole family
review:
I understood what J.J. Abrams and company were trying to do. Move forward, but pay as much homage to the original trilogy as possible AND connect this last film to Return of the Jedi in a way that would make sense.

I don't know why the story was so cloak and dagger at times. It's not like we don't have a clue as to what is going to happen. Star Wars is one franchise that has always went in one direction. I think that might have been to the detriment of this film. There isn't supposed to be much in the way of a surprise and it seemed at time that this film wanted to have some sort of surprise climax through out the whole film.

I thought that the character of Finn was somewhat poorly written and that Fey was under developed but I get it. This was an attempt to be a politically correct as possible. A diverse cast, African American represented in a mostly White ensemble cast, and a strong female character as the actual lead.

So I get it. Pay respect to the original story-line, move forward with a continuation of the last film AND try to appease the masses with a politically correct film. The film unfortunately falls short of that "political correctness" with the character of Finn. In spite of that John Boyega does what he can with what little he has to work with and I applaud him for it. He is still very entertaining to watch. As always.

This is a great film for the whole family to see.

title: The same as my first ever YouTube Review... Worth a watch!
review:
Fans have waited too long to see if the Franchise can survive without Lucas.. So is the film any good?

Well, Lets deal with the Critics first and look at the bad points.

The film is a re-skin of Episode VI: A New Hope ... A little unfair from critics but yes there are many similarities.

So is this a bad thing? George Lucas tried to experiment with the Prequels, look how that turned out!!! Long an the short, if it ain't broke - DON'T FIX IT!

Poor Acting - I saw this on another reviewers comments here... And yes some of the acting is quite "Stilted" - But hang on - The Original Trilogy which I LOVE AND ADORE had really poor acting, some really cheesy lines and they are declared MASTERPIECES!?

I have to disagree... John Obayga as Finn is AMAZING and worthy of an Oscar for giving a full range of emotions in a retentively short space of time... He won't get one as Fantasy films NEVER do...

Its a Bad Script - Again! So was the Original Trilogy!!!

Its predictable... Sadly, this is one major downside - It is... This is not just because of the story but the Disney/Lucasfilm Marketing campaign which gave way too much time for leaks and spoilers!!!

The Good... Effects are amazing, the story is EXACTLY what Fans wanted... Its fits the overall feel of the Original Trilogy without being "Too Good" - And for all those moaning about the stilted acting, if they had been BETTER than the OT, Truly Oscar Worthy... It would have gave Disney the power to REMAKE THE ORIGINAL TRILOGY!!!

THAT MUST NEVER HAPPEN!!!

Ignore the hype, go in expecting a good Fantasy/Action movie without the Internet japes and you will enjoy! No its not perfect - Its not supposed to be either or it would truly destroy what we have all loved for so long!

title: The force has really awoken !
review:
This is the true face of Star Wars! This indeed is STAR WARS !

Astoninish, Breathtaking, Striking, Brilliant, Sensational, Wondrous, Heart-stirring movie that everyone should watch. It's not only just a Star Wars sequel, It's more than that. This movie is about friendship, (old) love and a lot more. You just can't stay calm when you see Han Solo entering the Millennium Falcon for the first time in 30 years, you just can't. This is one of the most heart-warming moments in movie history. J.J. Abrams succeeded in offering us Star Wars as we know it, yet with some witty and jocular moments.

I have had more than 10 goosebump periods throughout the movie. This movie just smashes you to the seat and won't let you even think of moving your head to some other direction rather than the screen that's in front of you.

Ravishing performance by the actors! The Star Wars movies don't boast with popular actors, yet directors still manage to find the the ones that suit to their role utterly perfect.

J.J. Abrams has really accomplished not to ruin this everlasting and enthralling movie.

title: It's not groundbreaking new cinema, it's not a steaming pile of poop...It's Star Wars!!
review:
I enjoyed this movie a bunch!! I feel that this film captured everything we loved about the previous star wars films and added some new stuff!! Though, as you may have seen in other reviews, it's not a perfect film.

First off, there are parts of the film that could be better. I feel that as far as pacing goes, there are parts that felt rushed. Parts where we needed to be in the moment just a few seconds longer, but were rushed to keep the plot going. But that's a nitpick.

Second, this film sticks with the cookie cutter formula that each Star Wars trilogy has. Here is where I'm going to get into the spoilers:

  • The token "tainted" character: Star Wars has to have that character that is good but goes bad. Because we don't have Anakin Skywalker any more, we have to have his grandson, Ben Solo (AKA Kylo Ren), be the guy who was seduced by the darkside.


  • "Bad Guy Fortress is Not So Impenetrable" - Remember how the Death Star was the empire's base/greatest weapon? And remember how simple it was to blow it up? Villains haven't learned their lesson. The Starkiller base, though a bit more guarded, still too easy to blow up. There are more similarities, but I'll let you see them yourself.


Now, this next thing is the biggest problem I have with the film....HOW DID THEY FIND LUKE'S LIGHTSABER??? One of the sacred items in the film is that blue lightsaber Luke acquires in New Hope that was originally Anakin's. But last time we saw that saber, it was hurling into the abyss below Luke and Vader at the end of the duel, clutched in Luke's severed hand. I'm sorry but that lightsaber was from there on gone. It was forever lost in the depths below Cloud City. Vader cutoff that hand that was holding it, and it fell to be forever lost. So no way that alien lady found it and kept it so she could give it to a perspective jedi one day.

All in all though, I really liked this film! Finn is great hero, and I can't wait to see him in the next two. JJ Abrams did fantastic with directing and bringing the Star Wars universe back to life.

title: If you like the Star Wars series as a whole, go ahead and watch this one too
review:
First of all it was a great movie!

It had action(stormtroopers were somehow better at shooting rebels and planets down this time).

It had good character development for Fin and Rey as a team (don't try to say otherwise, nobody knew about Anakin's/Emperor/etc past in A New Hope).

Building the Starkiller was not the most inspired plan the First Order could come with but it did its job and blew up pretty nice. Not mad about that, anybody could see that it's going to get blown to pieces by an X-wing squad.

It was good to see that the Skywalkers, Han Solo, Chewie, C-3PO(without his original hand though, found that funny) and R2D2 came back to the Force universe.

For there is no movie that is without mistakes or wrongdoings here is my opinion !

Kylo Ren was presented as the next Darth Vader, cold and remorseless, even seen asking his grandfather to show him the dark side's power (obviously none has told him that his grandfather wasn't evil and his story) but the deeper the movie goes the more he looks like Linguini from Ratatouille (not just physically but the attitude as well).

Rey and Fin are pretty good at handling light sabers from the beginning but Rey becomes a master somehow and defeats Ren in one-on-one combat? She should of barely escaped, like the other way around but she did a good job nevertheless.

All in all I for one give it a 9, because it is a fantastic movie, the stormtroopers are better at shooting, nice to see new faces for each side and good acting from everyone, old and new cast!

review:
I Loved this movie, not because of the old trilogy making a comeback but because of it's new tone and characters! Finn and Ray are amazing choices for not only good characters but of their personalities and roles in this film. title: An enjoyable, if not entirely original night at the movies
review:
Star Wars episode 7 is the most disappointing thing since my son....

OK, OK, so it was pretty good. Visually it was flawless. The movie mostly contains recycled elements of A New Hope and seems to be banking on the idea that a new generation of Star Wars fans aren't old enough to truly remember or appreciate the significance of that movie (probably true) and the old generation will watch and appreciate it anyway for nostalgia's sake (probably also true.) **WARNING some spoilers below** The macguffin is again some vital piece of information contained on a droid, that hides away on a desert planet where it encounters our protagonist who will be led on a quest across the galaxy. The rebels again have to blow up a planet-destroying superweapon with X-Wings. Again an elder mentor to our protagonists is slain by a Sith's lightsaber. And Snokes is basically a CGI version of Palpatine, while Kylo Ren a slightly more conflicted but also by extension a slightly more interesting version of Darth Vader.

Whereas GL's prequel trilogy frequently overdid it on the boring exposition, this movie could've perhaps used some more explanations. That's not to say the movie suffers from any egregious plot holes, but it is very rapidly paced, leading from one plot element into the next at breakneck speed with minimal clarification on the details. I often found myself wondering what was happening and why it was happening before I made up some satisfactory explanation in my head (or I remember back to A New Hope and foisted the plot machinations of that movie on this one.) For example: Why did Finn betray the New Order and what makes him different from any other stormtrooper (i.e. are we to believe he is the only trooper to ever develop a conscience)? Why were those other space pirates hunting Han Solo? If they're outlaws why are they informing for the New Order and how do they know the New Order is hunting for that specific droid? Why was Han Solo carrying around three deadly space Octopi? What happened to the Chrome Trooper (Gwendoline Christie's Character)...did she make it out of that garbage chute they were threatening to throw her down before the planet was destroyed? Why was Rey waiting on Jakku? Why did that little orange yoda equivalent give Luke's Lightsaber to Finn when Rey is the one who found it and by all indications the one who actually has strong Force abilities? Why did R2-D2 suddenly wake up at the end other than to Deus ex Machina reveal where Luke is hiding? These are just of the top of my head. Some of these may or almost certainly will be clarified in upcoming installments. Some of them probably won't.

I will say the idea of a rogue stormtrooper was a good one, and probably the most original twist in the film. I was a bit disappointed they didn't explore stormtrooper culture and conditioning a little more. It would've been a more interesting plot to slowly see Finn become more and more disillusioned with the empire, and switch sides at some point later in the movie, rather than seemingly randomly right at the beginning, but I suppose we wouldn't have had a reboot of A New Hope in that case.

*MASSIVE SPOILER below* I felt Harrison Ford/Han Solo carried large portions of the film with his presence, whereas the new characters (Finn and Rey) have not yet entirely come into their own they do seem to have some potential for growth in upcoming installments and this was a fine introduction for them. Han's death scene was the strongest scene in the entire movie for me. Although it felt epic, it was also saddening, not just because it was the death of a beloved character at the hands of his own son, but also in the sense that they killed off the character that was basically carrying the movie by that point. Obviously the actor himself wanted to end his involvement with the franchise also, and I think he did so on a high note. The success of the sequels now hinges on the new characters stepping up, although I am also looking forward to seeing what Mark Hamill will do in the future, considering his role was basically reduced to a cameo in this movie.

Even though Disney played it entirely safe with this movie, they still managed to produce something enjoyable and I am looking forward to seeing the sequels and hope they take some more risks with the writing then, and make the plot a little less action-driven and little more original.

title: Star Wars: The Reboot
review:
Star Wars: TFA updates the franchise with beautiful 3D, excellent casting, familiarity, and more than a little nostalgia. By and large it is a solid, entertaining movie that will please all but the most jaded of fans. For better or worse, this iteration asks to be judged on the qualities of earlier films due to the return of characters, visuals, ideas, music, and themes.

Breathtaking visuals! This movie absolutely glows, and everyone involved with the look, style, special effects, and presentation should be proud of their achievement. The Force Awakens delivers some of the best use of visual 3D ever to hit the big screen. Incredible depth, memorable vistas, amazing sense of scale, and a wide variation of organic vs artificial environments are gifted to those lucky enough to see this film on the best screens cinema can offer.

The famous Star Wars sound effects are intertwined with a commendable music score - it is nice to experience bold music that doesn't demand attention, yet is fully present in the total experience. The score is not on the level of the original trilogy, perhaps due to the lack of complete originality.

The casting is borderline brilliant. One of the best traditions SW has maintained is casting relative unknowns into major roles. I feel this takes bravery and skill in casting and directing. It is easy to envy and fall in love with the main characters, and like those involved in post production - these young actors should hold their heads high, and accept the well earned praise.

Writing and Story - Eh... this is where I have to unfortunately hold my own fanaticism accountable. Very average. Especially the writing. There are moments of real humor, timing, and sequences one can get lost in, but there is no wit. Many of the places where intelligent dialog should have occurred come off as silly, generic, even idiotic. I'm not a stickler for the lack of science in SW - light speed travel around the galaxy, noise in space, and bad motivators are not my problem. But cliché dialog during the build up to a war, and adults speaking like children is disappointing. Reader, please refresh your memory with classic dialog from the original trilogy: "Thank the maker, this oil bath is going to feel so good...", "Hokey religions and ancient weapons are no match for a good blaster at your side kid.", "The circle is now complete. When I left you, I was but the learner; now I am the master." - There isn't one line in TFA that stands along side the many timeless lines from A New Hope, the movie The Force Awakens tries so hard to emulate. For those who have so quickly forgotten the lyrical wizardry of the original trilogy, "I find your lack of faith disturbing."

Originality? This is a reboot by the numbers. Elements chopped and remixed like bad stir fry do not taste good, and insult the palate of the seasoned Star Wars fan. We have all seen the original trilogy too many times. Because it is brilliant! Because of the originality! Because it does something wonderful to the mind and senses. The arc of The Force Awakens comes off like a blast of MSG, but instead of fooling the senses, the obviousness of the ripoff lacks perhaps the most important ingredient in the SW formula: a soul.

Yes, this movie is orders of magnitude better than episode I, II & III. Yes, it is a fun movie full of wonderful qualities, and well worth the price of admission. But no, this is not truly great film making and not the work of a master. I'm glad that JJ did his homework this time, and didn't tarnish an entire franchise with sloppy research and entertainment at all cost production. He succeeded in this project, but the sights were set too low.

This generation's kids deserve better - they deserve a fresh IP, new characters, and a new story - not a mix of old and new in a fashionable attempt to appease generational fans. In my heart of hearts, I really wanted to believe that SW:TFA could be completely fresh, new, intelligent And still Star Wars - but not from this film maker, not with this story, not with this writing.

While it may seem as though this old fan did not like this movie, actually I did. It was just so beautiful, and fun to experience with a large audience. I hope many people share my experience - but I also hope many more crave fresh ideas like me, and will support the next great film maker, with truly new and exciting science fiction ideas.

an optimistic and fanatical - 7 out of 10

title: The Jurassic World syndrome
review:
In a year in which throw backs from the yesteryear were the norm, oh how I hoped that this would be the one where I would not want to get up from my seat, the one that would give me the joy and chills of excitement that make cinema the greatest of art forms. How I wished to be moved by emotion and feel that special something, that on screen magic that touches the soul and makes you grateful that in spite of everything that is wrong in the world, you were born in a time when you can witness stories like the ones happening a long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away.

While the Force has indeed awakened, it did so with a lot of the magic feeling manufactured. There were so many throw backs to the original trilogy that to me it didn't feel like it stood on its own feet as a movie. Although it was clearly not, it felt like a remake throughout, it felt like "Nostalgia: the movie" because of not only plot points and visuals (the desert planet, the snow planet and more) but also entire scenes taken from the original trilogy.

The characters on the light side of things were all enjoyable to watch, easy to relate to and understand. And they were not completely what the trailers led you to believe. The motivations although kind of finicky in some cases, worked as a whole. The old cast was great and the new faces were even better.

On the dark side of things, I found that a lot did not work. While most characters (the ones from the trailers) are visually appealing we do not get to understand what they are about. Not a lot of motivation is given and this makes the scenes that are supposed to be very emotionally charged, a lot less so.

The direction is on point, the pace of the plot keeps you engaged, the acting is great, the humor does not feel forced. The soundtrack is inspired, although lacking anything with the impact of Duel of the Fates or Battle of the Heroes which stayed with you in spite of what you actually thought about the movies that featured them.

So can a good movie feel like a disappointment ? In my case, the answer is yes. We got just what we asked for and nothing more. I wanted it to be great so badly, that good enough wasn't actually... enough. It made me want to see Lucas' version. It might have been bad, but it also might have been great. It certainly would have not been safe.

title: A little rough, but some diamonds inside
review:
First I'll point out that if you're trying to return to the universe in the original Star Wars, that's a futile wish. That film was a product of many things: 1977, a low budget, the burden to invent a new universe, and a young George Lucas to name a few. This film cannot be what that film was because it is not a product of any of those same things. That's not inherently a good or bad thing, just know that it means this movie is different and the next ones will be, too. I consider this review to be spoiler-free, but everyone seems to have their own definition as to what this means. I will speak broadly about characters and themes, but not specific events. Proceed as you see fit.

For the backdrop of the film we have some beautifully realized planets and space settings, and there are simply amazing visuals throughout. I don't just mean the digital and practical effects (although each of those more than gets the job done), but the use of color, of framing, of setting and location. The areas all feel distinct from one another, and each is given time for you to appreciate them fully and holds their own self-contained chapter of the story.

Over the backdrop we have writing that mostly gets the job done. When the writing is at its peak, this film is funnier, cleverer, and potentially more meaningful than any Star Wars before it. The characters are well written, the interactions are natural, there are seamless transitions from one beat to the next, and there is a wit that is so good it almost feels out of place in this franchise. Sadly, though, that is not the case for the entirety of the film, and where the writing falls flat it falls flat hard. Some exchanges are prequel-quality pieces that are shoe-horned in awkwardly purely for expository purposes. Also much of the pacing falls apart in the final act of the film where characters make sudden, unwarranted leaps in their development. The very end of the film needed to get the characters to a specific point in setup for the next movie, but it feels incredibly out- of-place and forced.

The characters themselves again mostly get the job done. Newcomers Finn and Rey are by far the bright points, even outshining the likes of Harrison Ford's Han Solo. Each character is distinct from one another and very well performed. Their motivations feel sincere and their development is natural (again with notable exception in the last act). Poe Dameron fills out the trio and his character is incredibly fun, but also criminally under-utilized. His character arc doesn't have anywhere to go thus far, but that might be remedied in future installments. The best scenes in the entire film have to do with the interactions between each of these three. When it comes to capturing youthful energy and the exuberance of new adventure, no other Star Wars film has done so well and so naturally. Over on the other side, Kylo Ren is an interesting direction for the film. His character is menacing and powerful, yet also revealed to be broken and scared. In many ways he is designed to be the inverted Luke Skywalker, which is a refreshing take. His motivations, though, remain unclear and there is much that is still a mystery about him. That is probably intentional, but so far the Star Wars series still hasn't been able to explain properly why people are seduced to the Dark Side. General Hux is acceptable, but not very fleshed out and Captain Phasma has about as many lines and screen time as Greedo from the original Star Wars. I'm really not sure why she was featured so heavily in promotional material. Snoke is also in the film too briefly to have any opinion about. From the old characters I won't discuss Luke as that would venture into spoilers. Han Solo is believable as being the same character as before, but having experienced a great amount since. In fact he is shown to be more tender than ever before, and it is a good addition to his character. Leia? Well, that gets into my final point about the film.

One weakness that the film suffers from is constraining itself too tightly to replicating the original. In some cases this results in cameos that are nothing but meaningless fan service. This is the case with the characters of Leia, C-3PO, and R2-D2. None of these characters help move the story along or, in fact, do anything that couldn't have been handled just as well without them. As such their involvement is forced and weighs down the rest of the film. This is also true in the inclusion of Starkiller Base, i.e. Death Star 3.0. It's hard as an audience to feel menaced by something that you're so familiar with, and the struggle against it not only feels unoriginal, it is also devoid of any of the emotion and character development that made the original's trench run so riveting. In fact no matter how the film tries to suggest that the First Order and Rebellion are not just the Empire and Rebellion all over again, they really are and it retreads worn-out areas.

In summary, if the entire film maintained its highest points it would be the best Star Wars film to date, but it sputters out of originality and quality. Fortunately, in spite of its flaws it does introduce characters that are brilliantly conceived, and that provides me hope for their continuing stories in the following installments. Sorry to say it, but I'm happy to see the directing and writing pass into new hands for Episode VIII and I will be anxiously awaiting that film. Overall, I give this a 7/10. I would place it beneath Episode IV and V, and more on the VI and III tier, perhaps between those two.

title: Definitely didn't disappoint, though there still was some potential for improvement
review:
In this review I want to purely focus on the aspects that are not relevant to the story in any way, so this is going to be SPOILER FREE.

From the beginning until the end of the movie several motifs and situations can be found that just remind too much of Episode IV. The more you think about it, the more you notice the movie "borrows" from its predecessor. This doesn't necessarily have to be a bad thing, as when I was watching the movie I couldn't tell what the precise outcome would be solely by having seen Episode IV. Further, especially the older Star Wars fans might feel some nostalgia due to these slight parallels. Nevertheless, the ending is predictable to some extent, by modern movie standards.

There was a lot of critique regarding the prequel trilogy having made too extensive and intensive use of CGI. While watching the movie I noticed it was somehow strange and familiar at the same time, because Episode VII makes use of CGI when it's appropriate and not more. Remember those awful scenes on Kamino, Geonosis etc. ? You won't see anything like that in Episode VII. Most sets make use of natural terrain and tangible requisites. The movie takes place in a many natural environments, which has this old-school-feeling to it.

The only thing I wished for the movie to do is to explain one minor plot-hole and the background of one of the more central characters, but we still have two more movies to expect.

All in all the movie was very entertaining, even funny at times.

May the Force be with you.

title: Quick paced adventure, not a dull moment but some plot devices are repeated
review:
The same thing that happens in "a new hope" happens in "return of the Jedi" so why should that matter when it's practically the same thing that happens again in this film.It doesn't make it any more less entertaining. no! The film is good, really good. but yes we have seen it before, it's part of the franchise. The acting is excellent, the visuals are spectacular, and you can tell there are more practical effects (with puppets) rather than silly cgi- characters. But there is a difference. It's more gritty than before. When a laser blaster is fired it's more like a real rifle than a children's toy. They have more stopping power than we used to. When a planet is destroyed we get to see the effect from the eyes of the soon to be exterminated. When Disney took over they didn't go for more child friendly approach, that's for sure.

Star wars is no Sci-fi, and if you start to think about the technical explanation of the "first order"s new super weapon it would be very unpractical to aim not to mention load as it takes it energy from the nearest sun (until it's gone) . But never mind that (family guy will surely make a parody) Star wars is a fantasy, period.

We get to see all the old actors from the original films, which is nice. Han Solo mostly.

And yes there are some "who is related to whom" (spolier alert in the end it will surely turn out that they all are inbreed) which will be important. But i don't think the main objective of this film is to tell a story it is more to introduce the new actors and watch what events that occur that lead them to develop.the film is more character driven.

A nice thing is that we get to see a little glimpse of how a life as a storm-trooper might be. And oh, the empire has finally come around to hire females. nice to see that even evil can be p.c.

title: It's just part one of a 3 part trilogy, keep that in mind.
review:
(Spoiler Free)

Episode 7 is nothing more than an introduction to what will inevitably become a new Star Wars trilogy. Just when the film started to get good, it ended! The main characters never really developed, and the the supporting ones had little screen time. BB-8 was adorable, and I did like Kylo Ren, he's going to make for an interesting villain, despite his goofy boy next door looks. Note how I said, "Going to make" So far, we got too little of him to judge. But he's a promising villain. Harrison Ford acted well, and Hans Solo seemed like the same Hans Solo of the past. Ray and Finn were also good. They put a lot of heart into their performances, but, their story is only just beginning. It's easy to say that this film had little plot, but after all, didn't episode 4 have little plot? We didn't get to find out that Vadar was his father until the next film!

Okay, so as the end credits rolled, I felt like I wanted more, but I'm not complaining. I gave the film an 8 after all, and even though it sounds like I'm disappointed, I did like a lot of things about this film. I docked two points because I felt myself wanting more and we will indeed get more once the other movies are made. It just stinks that we have to wait so long to see this story through. Don't get me wrong, this film was well acted. The dialogue was very good, it was funny too, and the nostalgic elements had me teary eyed a few times.

I thought that the film almost felt small, at least it did when you compare it to the prequels because this film was made in the image of the original trilogy. Bigger sets, less green screen and more props. I'll take it over CGI any day, but the prequels still felt bigger and grander overall because they the CGI did all the work. And I can't help but find myself disappointed in the score for this film. John Williams is getting old...its no secret now after hearing the music in this film. No memorable pieces...no music on par with the old stuff.

The light saber battles were not as impressive as the ones in previous episodes either. Yes, I understand that JJ didn't want the sword fights to look like ballet dancing, and JJ went for a more realistic approach, but we don't go see Star Wars movies for realistic sword fights. I missed the elegant choreography from the previous films. Remember how dramatic the light saber battles were in the other six films? They all were shot with no background music. No dialogue. Just the sound of light sabers. Well, JJ did leave out music for the final battle, but it just didn't have any wow factor. The sabers looked too damn heavy! Perhaps its because the final light saber battle was fought by 2 people who were newly acquainted with the force. If you look at it that way, then, perhaps JJ made the right choice after all!

8/10 for the excellent pacing, direction, dialogue, action and more importantly, the nostalgia!

title: The force had a big nap
review:
In 1977 I was 17, I attended a Cinema in Sydney Australia and watched the new release of "Star Wars (1977)" now with the added words "A new Hope" ... Already a fan of Sci Fi I found the movie to be excellent fun.

On the 17th Of December 2015 I went to the Cinema here in Sydney and watched what I consider to be a revamp of that 1977 movie.

This new offering was fun and visually exciting.

The thing I found myself thinking during the movie were, couldn't we have a new plot with our new actors?

Yes, as I said, good fun, and I did enjoy it a lot, though the fact that I had thoughts that I'm sure many others had and will express here means that for all the $ spent of the movie a completely original plot was not worthy of such spending, and this meant I was noticing those things instead of being absorbed in the movie, so my hope to find 2hrs 15min of total escape from my mundane life did not happen.

So, we have a promise of more movies, this plot line can no longer be used again ... I hope, surely the next movie will not be based on "The Empire Strikes Back"!

title: In JJ we trust
review:
A typical Star Wars recreating the spirit of the originals. The new cast look as though they are going to take the franchise forward, with the help of the more established faces.

The film leaves you with a number of questions, you will want to watch it again to spot things you missed first time round which may offer clues (one scene in particular requires multiple viewings to capture all of the information on offer).

Whist there are definite nods to the Star Wars of old, you mustn't forget that this films primary goal is to welcome you back to that Galaxy Far Away and win back some of the love that had been tarnished because of the prequels.

review: I grew up watching all the star wars saga, i've seen it dozens of times and still can't get bored of it. 10 years ago i heard rumors and even saw a picture o a possible episode VII but as I said, rumors.Finally these year I got the privilege of this great sequel. title: Force Awakens Spoiler free review!
review:
"I will finish what you started" a promise made by Kylo Ren to Darth Vader, a mission reflected to that of Director JJ. Abrahams who has now taken over the reigns from George Lucas in continuing the legacy of the Star Wars Universe and in this film he has definitely recaptured the magic of what made the trilogy such timeless classics.

As soon we are introduced to the 'Force Awakens' we find ourselves on familiar ground, a path laid out in 'A New Hope' in which Abrahams follows its beats very closely. His understanding of the spirit of Star Wars is never in doubt though as Oscar Issac's Poe Dameron makes an electric entrance as an elite star fighter on a covert mission. He jump starts the path to us meeting the rest of new characters such as John Boyega's Finn whom he shares great banter and energy with. Boyega really brings a charismatic and emotional weight to his role as a stormtropper who is desperately trying to break free from the shackles of fate forced upon him.

Harrison Ford reprises his role as Han Solo and perfectly slides back into the character that made him a star, he scenes with Peter Mayhew returning as Co-pilot Chewbacca really bring a welcomed nostalgia, this is turned up even higher when we meet Leia and old sparks fly.

Kylo Ren the antagonist of this new era played by Adam Driver brings a multi layered performance to the table, successfully avoiding the one dimensional trope of villains that run rampant on our screens. His actions undoubtedly questionable but with motives that you will perhaps even sympathize with.

Who really shines brightest though is Daisy Ridley as Rey, a scavenger on the planet of Jakku who longs for adventure and there isn't a scene I can recall where I felt she missed her mark. Every part of performance is believable and this perfectly complemented by her companion, the superb and comical BB-8 Robot. The studios choice to rely heavily on practical effects as opposed to CG really pays off here as Rey and Finn are able to interact with BB-8 and the many other characters without any notion of being pulled away from the reality of the film but with this achievement does come instances where two important CG characters feel out of place, its a shame they were not fully realized using costume and prosthetics as the rest of the supporting cast.

The world of 'Force awakens' is beautifully filmed, from the wide angle shots showcasing the amazing set design and location choices to the tight aerial acrobats of the Millennium Falcon. The action is fast paced both in its dogfights and within its narrative. Any paused moments of fluidity help the emotion and humour pour out from its wonderful cast, we are never left with overly long scenes with clunky exposition that plagued the prequel films.

So has it been worth the wait? Yes, Abrahams's and co have been able to re-kickstart the Star Wars universe which is hugely pushed by the stellar new cast which will dazzle a new generation of fans of those of old, the returning players bringing a story that feels like a true sequel even if it does fly too safe at times and not diverging from what has come before, hopefully in the following sequels we will have a more confident approach in telling a new saga.

👎Overly familiar story paths 👎Use of CG on certain characters

👍Wonderfully filmed 👍Brilliant new cast 👍Fast paced action
